qs.e: Profit per unit = P - ATC = 30 - 25 = 5. Total supernormal profit = 5 * 100 = 500 Naira.

qs.q: If a country population grows at an annual rate of 3 percent while its real GDP grows at 2 percent, real per capita GDP will
qs.e: Growth in per capita GDP approximately equals GDP growth minus population growth = 2% - 3% = -1%.

qs.q: A specific tax of 5 Naira per unit imposed on a good with perfectly inelastic demand will be borne
qs.e: When demand is perfectly inelastic, buyers purchase the same quantity regardless of price, so sellers pass 100% of the tax to consumers.

qs.q: If a specific tax of 5 Naira per unit is imposed on a product with perfectly elastic demand, the economic burden falls
qs.e: When demand is perfectly elastic, price to buyers cannot rise without demand dropping to zero, so sellers bear 100% of the tax burden.

qs.q: In a 3-sector Keynesian model where Y = C + I + G, C = 50 + 0.8(Y - T), I = 100, G = 100, and T = 50, equilibrium income Y is
If the reserve requirement for commercial banks is reduced from 20 percent to 15 percent, the simple credit multiplier increases from
qs.e: Initial multiplier = 1 / 0.20 = 5. New multiplier = 1 / 0.15 = 6.67.

qs.q: An increase in structural unemployment across an economy is best addressed by
o: retraining programs and labor mobility schemes
expansionary monetary policy and lower interest rates
reducing import tariffs on consumer goods
qs.e: Structural unemployment stems from mismatch of skills; retraining and relocation assistance match workers to new industries.

qs.q: In an economy experiencing demand-pull inflation, the appropriate monetary policy action is to
o: lower the central bank discount rate
sell government securities in the open market
qs.e: Selling securities (OMO) absorbs cash from commercial banks, shrinking liquidity and dampening aggregate demand.

qs.q: Which situation causes cost-push inflation in a developing economy reliance on imported industrial inputs?
o: A surge in domestic consumer credit grants
A rise in government foreign exchange reserves
Substantial currency depreciation increasing import costs
A decline in statutory corporate income tax rates
qs.e: Depreciation makes imported raw materials and machinery more expensive in local currency terms, pushing up production costs.

qs.q: The opportunity cost of holding cash reserves rather than holding interest-bearing government bonds is the
o: transaction fees charged by commercial banks
rate of capital depreciation on physical assets
face value of the currency notes
forgone interest yield on the bonds
qs.e: Holding liquid cash incurs an opportunity cost equal to the interest that would have been earned on bonds.

qs.q: Liquidity trap in Keynesian economic theory occurs when interest rates are extremely low and money demand is
o: infinitely elastic with respect to interest rate
completely inelastic with respect to interest rate
equal to total government public spending
qs.e: In a liquidity trap, speculative demand for money becomes perfectly elastic, rendering monetary expansion ineffective.

qs.q: A country export prices fall by 10 percent while its import prices rise by 10 percent. The terms of trade index change from 100 to
qs.e: New Export Price Index = 90. New Import Price Index = 110. Terms of Trade = (90 / 110) * 100 = 81.8.

qs.q: An infant industry argument for trade protectionism asserts that temporary tariffs should protect new industries until they
o: generate sufficient tax revenue for government
achieve economies of scale and competitive efficiency
export 100 percent of their output abroad
qs.e: Infant industries need initial protection from mature foreign competitors to scale up and become cost-competitive.

qs.q: The main economic rationale for agricultural price support mechanisms (floor prices) is to
o: lower food prices for urban industrial workers
reduce government budgetary outlay on agriculture
protect farm incomes against price fluctuations
qs.e: Agricultural price supports prevent farm collapse caused by price volatility due to inelastic agricultural demand.

qs.q: Land fragmentation in traditional West African agriculture leads directly to
o: inefficiency in farm mechanization and lost travel time
rapid adoption of commercial irrigation equipment
qs.e: Small scattered land parcels prevent efficient deployment of tractors and modern farm machinery.

qs.q: The crude oil monoculture in an economy increases vulnerability to external economic shocks because
o: national revenue fluctuates directly with volatile world oil prices
foreign exchange reserves remain constantly elevated
qs.e: Over-reliance on a single export commodity exposes government budget and trade accounts to international price swings.

qs.q: Gas flaring in petroleum extraction represents an economic loss because it involves
o: increasing domestic natural gas supply for electricity
lowering foreign oil company operating costs
wasting valuable energy resources and environmental degradation
qs.e: Flaring burns off natural gas that could otherwise generate power or industrial chemical feedstocks.

qs.q: Public debt service burden measures the proportion of national revenue allocated to
o: funding public health and education infrastructure
paying principal interest and loan repayments
qs.e: Debt servicing consumes government revenue required to pay interest charges and amortize debt principal.

qs.q: Fiscal drag occurs in a progressive tax system during inflation when rising nominal incomes
o: push taxpayers into higher tax brackets without real income gain
reduce government total tax revenue collections
lower average tax rates across all households
qs.e: Fiscal drag happens when inflation inflates money incomes into higher tax brackets, raising tax burdens without real purchasing power growth.

qs.q: Economic development differs from economic growth because development includes
o: only quantitative increases in real gross domestic product
qualitative improvements in living standards and institutions
rapid growth in total national population size
continuous expansion in foreign trade import tariffs
qs.e: Economic growth is quantitative output expansion, whereas development embraces structural change, poverty reduction, and institutional quality.

qs.q: A major structural bottleneck in achieving long-term economic development in developing nations is
o: excessive domestic saving rates among rural households
inadequate physical infrastructure such as power and transport
high levels of direct foreign trade surplus
qs.e: Deficits in electricity supply, roads, and port logistics severely constrain industrial growth.

qs.q: When a product has a perfectly inelastic supply curve, an increase in market demand leads to
o: an increase in equilibrium quantity with price unchanged
a fall in equilibrium price and quantity
no change in either equilibrium price or quantity
a rise in equilibrium price with no change in quantity
qs.e: With vertical supply (Es = 0), a demand surge pushes price upward while quantity remains fixed.

qs.q: Joint products are goods where an increase in the production of one good automatically
o: increases the supply of the other good
decreases the supply of the other good
increases the demand for the other good
lowers the cost of raw materials for the other good
qs.e: Joint products (e.g., crude oil and natural gas) emerge from the same production process.

qs.q: The expansion path of a firm in production theory connects cost-minimizing input combinations along
o: indifference curve and budget line tangency points
isoquant and isocost tangency points at different output levels
production possibility curves across different years
qs.e: The expansion path shows optimal long-run factor combinations as scale increases.

qs.q: An isoquant curve represents all combinations of two factor inputs that yield
o: the same total cost of production
equal marginal utility to the producer
the same level of total physical output
qs.e: An isoquant (equal product curve) shows input combinations producing a constant output volume.

qs.q: Under monopolistic competition, long-run equilibrium for a firm occurs where the demand curve is tangent to
o: the minimum point of short-run average cost curve
the upward-sloping segment of marginal cost curve
the downward-sloping segment of average total cost curve
qs.e: Monopolistic competition leads to excess capacity in the long run because tangency occurs to the left of minimum ATC.

qs.q: Which condition guarantees that a price-discriminating firm maximizes profit across two distinct market segments A and B?
qs.e: Profit maximization across segments requires allocating output so marginal revenue in segment A equals marginal revenue in segment B and overall marginal cost.

qs.q: A partnership firm converting into a public limited company achieves the major benefit of
o: eliminating all corporate tax payment liabilities
raising large equity capital by issuing shares to the public
retaining complete secrecy over business operations
qs.e: Conversion to a public company allows access to broad public capital markets.

qs.q: Corporate horizontal integration occurs when two firms merge that operate
o: at different sequential stages of the same supply chain
at the same stage of production in the same industry
qs.e: Horizontal integration merges competing firms at the same production level (e.g., two commercial banks).

qs.q: Vertical backward integration is illustrated by a furniture manufacturing company acquiring
qs.e: Backward integration extends firm ownership into previous supply chain stages (raw materials).

qs.q: The precautionary motive for holding money depends primarily on the level of
qs.e: Precautionary demand for money to cover unexpected emergencies varies directly with consumer income level.

qs.q: Speculative demand for money according to Keynes is negatively related to
o: the price level of food items
qs.e: When interest rates are high, bond prices are low and interest return is high, reducing speculative cash holding.

qs.q: A statutory requirement that commercial banks hold a minimum percentage of total assets in liquid assets is the
qs.e: Liquidity ratio specifies the proportion of total bank assets to be kept in cash or short-term liquid instruments.

qs.q: The canon of taxation which states that tax payments should be convenient in terms of time and method of payment is
qs.e: Adam Smith canon of convenience dictates that taxes be collected when and how it is easiest for the taxpayer.

qs.q: The canon of economy in taxation requires that the cost of tax collection should be
o: small relative to the total tax revenue collected
equal to total government public spending
borne entirely by foreign commercial firms
fixed at 50 percent of total tax receipts
qs.e: Canon of economy specifies that administrative collection expenses must be minimal compared to revenue generated.

qs.q: An increase in government transfer payments funded by public borrowing tends to
o: increase aggregate demand and consumer spending
qs.e: Transfer payments put income in households hands, stimulating consumer demand.

qs.q: If a consumer demand function for commodity A is Qa = 80 - 2Pa + 0.5Y, where Pa = 10 Naira and Y = 200 Naira, the quantity demanded Qa is
For the demand function Qa = 80 - 2Pa + 0.5Y with Pa = 10 and Y = 200 (Qa = 160), the income elasticity of demand at this point is
qs.e: Income elasticity Ey = (dQa/dY) * (Y / Qa) = 0.5 * (200 / 160) = 0.5 * 1.25 = 0.625.

qs.q: If supply function is Qs = -20 + 4P and market demand is Qd = 100 - 2P, an excise tax of 3 Naira per unit levied on producers changes equilibrium price to
qs.e: New supply with tax: Qs = -20 + 4(P - 3) = -20 + 4P - 12 = -32 + 4P. Equating to demand: -32 + 4P = 100 - 2P => 6P = 132 => P = 22 Naira.

qs.q: In the tax scenario above where equilibrium price rises from 20 Naira to 22 Naira under a 3 Naira tax, the price paid by consumers rises by
qs.e: Initial equilibrium without tax: -20 + 4P = 100 - 2P => 6P = 120 => P = 20 Naira. With tax, P consumer = 22 Naira, an increase of 2 Naira.

qs.q: The producer share of the 3 Naira excise tax in the above problem is
qs.e: Consumer bears 2 Naira (price increase from 20 to 22). Producer bears remaining tax = 3 - 2 = 1 Naira per unit.

qs.q: If a firm short-run total cost function is TC = 100 + 10Q + Q^2, average fixed cost at Q = 10 units is
qs.e: Total Fixed Cost TFC = 100. Average Fixed Cost AFC = TFC / Q = 100 / 10 = 10 Naira.

qs.q: For TC = 100 + 10Q + Q^2 at Q = 10, the average variable cost AVC is
qs.e: Total Variable Cost TVC = 10Q + Q^2 = 10(10) + 100 = 200. AVC = TVC / Q = 200 / 10 = 20 Naira.

qs.q: For TC = 100 + 10Q + Q^2, the output level Q that minimizes Average Variable Cost AVC is
qs.e: AVC = TVC / Q = (10Q + Q^2) / Q = 10 + Q. As Q approaches zero, AVC approaches 10; AVC increases linearly with output Q.

qs.q: If a country balance of trade shows visible exports of 600 million USD and visible imports of 750 million USD, the balance of trade is in
qs.e: Balance of trade = Exports - Imports = 600 - 750 = -150 million USD (deficit).

qs.q: If a nation Gross National Disposable Income is 1,500 billion Naira and Final Consumption Expenditure is 1,200 billion Naira, Gross National Saving is
qs.e: Gross National Saving = Disposable Income - Consumption Expenditure = 1,500 - 1,200 = 300 billion Naira.

qs.q: In a 2-sector macroeconomic model, if saving function is S = -50 + 0.2Y, the consumption function C is
If autonomous consumption is 50, marginal propensity to save is 0.2, and investment I = 150, equilibrium income is
qs.e: Equilibrium Y = (Autonomous Consumption + Investment) / MPS = (50 + 150) / 0.2 = 200 / 0.2 = 1,000.

qs.q: When the price of a good rises by 25 percent and total consumer expenditure on the good remains completely unchanged, price elasticity of demand is
qs.e: When price changes do not alter total expenditure, price elasticity of demand equals unity (|Ed| = 1).

qs.q: If the cash reserve ratio is raised from 10 percent to 25 percent, the deposit creation multiplier decreases by
qs.e: Initial multiplier = 1 / 0.10 = 10. New multiplier = 1 / 0.25 = 4. Decrease = 10 - 4 = 6.0.

qs.q: A country export price index rises from 100 to 120 while its import price index rises from 100 to 110. The commodity terms of trade have
qs.e: Terms of Trade = (120 / 110) * 100 = 109.1. An increase from 100 to 109.1 represents a 9.1% improvement.

qs.q: If a monopolist can divide buyers into two separate markets with demand elasticities Ed1 = 3.0 and Ed2 = 1.5, the firm should set a higher price in
o: Market 1 where demand is more elastic
Market 2 where demand is less elastic
qs.e: Price discrimination principles dictate setting higher prices in market segments where demand is less price elastic.

qs.q: The Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution (MRTS) of labor for capital measures the
o: amount of capital that can be replaced by one unit of labor keeping output constant
ratio of total output to total capital employed
rate at which capital depreciates over time
slope of the consumer budget line
qs.e: MRTS_LK = MP_L / MP_K represents the trade-off between labor and capital along an isoquant curve.

qs.q: An indifference curve is L-shaped (right-angled) when the two goods consumed are
qs.e: L-shaped indifference curves occur for perfect complements consumed in fixed proportions (e.g., left and right shoes).

qs.q: If two goods are perfect substitutes, the indifference curves are
qs.e: Perfect substitutes feature a constant Marginal Rate of Substitution, producing straight-line indifference curves.

qs.q: A firm experiencing increasing returns to scale will see its long-run average total cost curve
o: remain horizontal across all output levels
qs.e: Increasing returns to scale mean output grows faster than inputs, pulling long-run average cost down.

qs.q: A deadweight loss in a competitive market occurs when government imposes a tax because the tax
o: reduces total combined surplus of consumers and producers
increases producer surplus at consumer expense
transfers all wealth from buyers to commercial banks
qs.e: Deadweight loss is the net loss of economic efficiency when equilibrium output is distorted by taxation.

qs.q: The Gini coefficient is a quantitative measure of
o: the inflation rate relative to unemployment
the elasticity of supply across agricultural markets
qs.e: Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality), measuring income distribution disparity.

qs.q: A Lorenz curve that lies closer to the 45-degree diagonal line indicates
o: a higher degree of income inequality
a rapid increase in consumer price inflation
a decline in national population growth
qs.e: The 45-degree line represents complete income equality; proximity to this line means lower inequality.

qs.q: Stagflation is an economic situation characterized simultaneously by
o: falling price levels and rapid economic growth
high export growth and budget surplus
high inflation and high unemployment or economic stagnation
qs.e: Stagflation combines stagnant economic output/high unemployment with persistent inflation.

qs.q: The Philips curve in short-run macroeconomics illustrates an inverse relationship between
o: the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment
the interest rate and money supply
export price index and import price index
qs.e: Short-run Phillips curve shows trade-off between inflation rate and unemployment rate.

qs.q: Real interest rate is calculated as the nominal interest rate minus
o: the commercial bank cash reserve ratio
qs.e: Real Interest Rate = Nominal Interest Rate - Inflation Rate.

qs.q: If nominal interest rate is 15 percent and annual inflation rate is 9 percent, the real interest rate is
qs.e: Real interest rate = 15% - 9% = 6%.

qs.q: According to the Quantity Theory of Money (MV = PY), if money supply M grows by 10% and velocity V and real output Y are constant, price level P will
qs.e: In MV = PY, with V and Y constant, percentage change in P equals percentage change in M (10%).

qs.q: Under a floating exchange rate regime, a rise in foreign demand for a country export commodities causes its currency to
o: be officially devalued by central bank
qs.e: Higher foreign demand for exports increases market demand for national currency, appreciating its exchange rate.

qs.q: Dutch Disease in resource-rich economies refers to the phenomenon where a natural resource boom leads to
o: rapid expansion of manufacturing export competitiveness
appreciation of local currency hurting non-resource export sectors
permanent deflation across domestic consumer markets
elimination of public sector foreign borrowings
qs.e: Dutch Disease occurs when resource export windfalls appreciate local currency, making domestic manufacturing and farming uncompetitive.

qs.q: Which policy measure directly mitigates Dutch Disease effects in petroleum-exporting nations?
o: Increasing government domestic spending on import subsidies
Fixing commercial bank interest rates at zero percent
Establishing a Sovereign Wealth Fund to sterilize foreign inflows
Abolishing all corporate taxes on petroleum companies
qs.e: Sovereign wealth funds save windfall oil revenues abroad, reducing domestic currency appreciation pressures.

qs.q: A tariff rate quota allows a specified quantity of a good to enter a country at
o: zero tax, with total import prohibitions beyond the quota
a fixed uniform price set by international treaties
a progressive tax rate determined by importer income
a lower tariff rate, with higher tariffs on imports exceeding the quota
qs.e: Tariff rate quotas combine quotas and tariffs by applying lower duties within quota volumes and higher rates above.

qs.q: Export subsidies paid by government to domestic producers result in foreign buyers paying a price that is
o: equal to total domestic cost plus tariff
fixed by world central banking reserves
qs.e: Subsidies reduce export costs, enabling firms to sell in foreign markets below domestic prices.

qs.q: Which form of regional economic integration eliminates internal trade barriers and establishes a common external tariff for non-members?
qs.e: A customs union combines internal free trade among members with a unified external tariff on non-member imports.

qs.q: A common market goes beyond a customs union by additionally allowing free mobility of
o: monetary currencies through a single central bank
factors of production (labour and capital) among member states
qs.e: Common markets permit free movement of products, labor, and capital across national borders.

qs.q: Under traditional sharecropping arrangements in West African agriculture, land use rent is paid in the form of
o: a fixed monthly monetary cash fee
free labor on non-agricultural estate projects
a fixed proportion of harvested crop output
qs.e: Sharecropping requires tenant farmers to pay landowners an agreed fraction (e.g., 1/2 or 1/3) of the harvested crop.

qs.q: Stabilization funds operated by agricultural marketing boards serve to cushion farmers against
o: increases in statutory direct income tax rates
excess supply of farm labor during planting
qs.e: Stabilization funds accumulate reserves during commodity price booms to subsidize farm prices during downturns.

qs.q: The crowding-out effect of fiscal policy occurs when government deficit spending funded by domestic borrowing leads to
o: lower interest rates that encourage consumer borrowing
higher interest rates that reduce private sector investment
increased commercial bank excess liquid reserves
a decline in overall government national debt
qs.e: Heavy state borrowing pushes up interest rates, squeezing out private enterprise investment.

qs.q: The lump-sum tax multiplier in Keynesian economics is equal to
qs.e: The tax multiplier is -MPC / (1 - MPC), which is smaller in absolute terms than the expenditure multiplier.

qs.q: Indicative economic planning differs from command planning because indicative planning
o: enforces compulsory production quotas on all private firms
prohibits all forms of private foreign investment
operates without setting national economic targets
uses incentives and policy guidelines rather than binding output directives
qs.e: Indicative planning guides private enterprise using economic forecasts and fiscal incentives rather than state commands.

qs.q: Rolling economic plans are designed to be revised annually to
o: adapt targets to changing economic realities and performance
eliminate the need for long-term development forecasting
ensure government expenditure equals tax receipts every year
replace foreign trade transactions with domestic barter
qs.e: Rolling plans maintain a fixed horizon (e.g., 3 years) by adding a new year as each current year ends.

qs.q: A firm shut-down point in the short run occurs when market price falls below minimum
qs.e: If price is below AVC, the firm cannot cover variable costs and minimizes loss by shutting down operations.

qs.q: In the long run, a perfectly competitive firm operates at the minimum point of its
qs.e: Free entry and exit drive economic profits to zero in the long run, forcing firms to operate at minimum LRAC.

qs.q: Cartel agreements among oligopolistic producers are inherently unstable primarily because
o: government regulations prohibit all profit-making activities
demand for oligopoly products is perfectly elastic in the long run
cartel managers receive fixed civil service salaries
individual member firms have an incentive to secretively cheat on production quotas
qs.e: Firms face temptation to undercut agreed cartel prices or exceed output quotas to gain market share.

qs.q: Kinked demand curve model of oligopoly explains why prices in oligopolistic markets tend to be
o: equal to marginal cost at all times
determined solely by government price ceilings
qs.e: Assumes rivals match price cuts but ignore price hikes, creating a kinked demand curve and price rigidity.

qs.q: A public good exhibits which two defining characteristics?
o: Excludability and high marginal cost of production
Rivalry in consumption and price elastic demand
qs.e: Public goods cannot exclude non-payers, and one person consumption does not diminish availability for others.

qs.q: Free-rider problem in public economics arises because non-payers
o: are forced by law to buy corporate equity shares
pay higher indirect taxes than other citizens
cannot be excluded from enjoying the benefits of public goods
qs.e: Non-excludability allows consumers to enjoy public goods without paying, leading to underprovision by private markets.

qs.q: Negative externalities in production, such as industrial pollution, cause competitive markets to
o: underproduce the commodity relative to social demand
charge a price higher than total social cost
overproduce the commodity relative to the socially optimal level
qs.e: Firms ignore external pollution costs, leading private marginal cost to be lower than social marginal cost and causing overproduction.

qs.q: To internalize a negative production externality, government can impose a
o: Pigouvian tax equal to the marginal external cost
production subsidy paid directly to polluting firms
price ceiling set below market equilibrium price
lump-sum grant to commercial bank lenders
qs.e: A Pigouvian tax aligns private costs with social costs, reducing output to the socially optimal level.

qs.q: Under a floating exchange rate, expansionary monetary policy tends to cause national currency value to
o: appreciate due to increased foreign direct investment
depreciate due to lower interest rates and capital outflows
remain completely fixed against gold standards
be devalued by official government decree
qs.e: Lower domestic interest rates discourage foreign capital inflows and spur outflows, lowering demand for local currency.

qs.q: Given the utility function U = X^0.5 * Y^0.5 with prices Px = 10, Py = 20, and income I = 400, the optimal consumer choice of X and Y is
qs.e: For Cobb-Douglas U = X^0.5 Y^0.5, equal expenditure is spent on each good: Px*X = I/2 = 200 => X = 200/10 = 20. Py*Y = 200 => Y = 200/20 = 10.

qs.q: For the utility function U = X^0.5 * Y^0.5 with Px = 10, Py = 20, and I = 400 (where X = 20 and Y = 10), maximum total utility attained is
If demand function is P = 100 - 0.5Q, consumer surplus when market price P is 60 Naira is
If supply function is P = 20 + 0.5Q, producer surplus when market price P is 60 Naira is
Combining the demand P = 100 - 0.5Q and supply P = 20 + 0.5Q (equilibrium P = 60, Q = 80), total social surplus generated in the market is
qs.e: Total Surplus = Consumer Surplus + Producer Surplus = 1,600 + 1,600 = 3,200 Naira.

qs.q: A firm total revenue is TR = 200Q - Q^2 and total cost is TC = 100 + 40Q + Q^2. The profit-maximizing quantity Q is
qs.e: MR = 200 - 2Q. MC = 40 + 2Q. Profit max MR = MC: 200 - 2Q = 40 + 2Q => 4Q = 160 => Q = 40 units.

qs.q: For TR = 200Q - Q^2 and TC = 100 + 40Q + Q^2 at profit-maximizing Q = 40, total maximum profit is
In a open economy national income model Y = C + I + G + (X - M), if C = 100 + 0.8Yd, Yd = Y - T, T = 50, I = 150, G = 150, X = 100, and M = 20 + 0.1Y, equilibrium income Y is
In an open economy model Y = C + I + G + (X - M), if C = 100 + 0.75(Y - T), T = 40, I = 100, G = 110, X = 80, and M = 20 + 0.15Y, equilibrium income Y is
For the open economy above (Y = 600, M = 20 + 0.15(600) = 110, X = 80), the foreign trade balance (X - M) is
qs.e: Imports M = 20 + 0.15(600) = 110. Exports X = 80. Net Exports = 80 - 110 = -30 (deficit of 30).

qs.q: If the foreign trade multiplier in an open economy is 2.5, an increase in exports of 40 million Naira will cause national income to rise by
qs.e: Change in income = Foreign trade multiplier * Change in exports = 2.5 * 40 million = 100 million Naira.

qs.q: The Marginal Propensity to Import (MPM) measures the change in imports resulting from a unit change in
qs.e: MPM = delta M / delta Y, expressing the fraction of additional national income spent on imported goods.

qs.q: If Marginal Propensity to Save is 0.2 and Marginal Propensity to Import is 0.05, open economy expenditure multiplier (1 / (MPS + MPM)) is
qs.e: Open economy multiplier = 1 / (MPS + MPM) = 1 / (0.20 + 0.05) = 1 / 0.25 = 4.0.

qs.q: A monopoly firm faces demand P = 120 - 2Q and cost TC = 100 + 20Q. If government fixes a price ceiling at P = 60 Naira, the firm will produce output Q of
qs.e: Under price ceiling P = 60, the firm acts as price taker where P = MR = 60. Setting P = 120 - 2Q => 60 = 120 - 2Q => 2Q = 60 => Q = 30 units.

qs.q: For the regulated monopolist above facing P = 60 and TC = 100 + 20(30) = 700 at Q = 30, total revenue TR is
If price elasticity of supply for farm produce is 0.4 and farm output prices drop by 15 percent, quantity supplied will decrease by
qs.e: Percentage change in Qs = Es * percentage change in P = 0.4 * (-15%) = -6%.

qs.q: If a country inflation rate is 20 percent and nominal wages rise by 12 percent over the same period, real wages have
qs.e: Change in real wage approx equals Nominal wage growth minus Inflation rate = 12% - 20% = -8%.

qs.q: Hyperinflation leads to a collapse in money function as a store of value because
o: commercial banks increase interest payments on savings
purchasing power erodes rapidly making cash holding costly
the central bank restricts total currency printed
government replaces paper currency with gold coins
qs.e: Rapidly escalating price levels destroy purchasing power, forcing individuals to minimize money holdings.

qs.q: The income velocity of money V in the equation of exchange MV = PY represents the average number of times a unit of money is spent on
o: final goods and services in a year
qs.e: Velocity V measures the circulation frequency of money spent on final national output.

qs.q: If currency in circulation is 500 billion Naira, demand deposits are 1,500 billion Naira, and bank reserves are 200 billion Naira, money supply M1 is
qs.e: M1 = Currency in circulation + Demand deposits = 500 + 1,500 = 2,000 billion Naira.

qs.q: High dependency ratios in West African countries affect economic growth negatively primarily by
o: reducing national savings and capital formation
lowering government spending on basic education
qs.e: High proportion of dependents forces households to spend income on immediate consumption rather than saving.

qs.q: An underpopulated country expanding its workforce through immigration will initially experience
o: diminishing returns and falling living standards
increasing average product and per capita income
a sharp increase in urban congestion costs
a persistent balance of payments deficit
qs.e: Underpopulation means resources are underutilized; additional labor yields increasing returns and higher per capita output.

qs.q: Which land tenure system in West Africa permits absolute individual ownership and transferability of land?
qs.e: Freehold tenure gives absolute ownership rights to individuals, allowing outright sale or mortgage.

qs.q: Commodity marketing boards were criticized for functioning as a tax mechanism because they
o: imposed high import tariffs on farm fertilizer
forced farmers to pay corporate income taxes
sold farm produce below cost to foreign buyers
withheld accumulated trading surpluses rather than paying full market price to farmers
qs.e: Marketing boards extracted surpluses by paying producers less than world market prices and transferring reserves to state budgets.

qs.q: The extraction of petroleum in Nigeria creates an enclave economy when it
o: has minimal backward and forward linkages with local manufacturing
employs the vast majority of the national rural labor force
supplies cheap raw materials exclusively to local craft industries
eliminates government reliance on foreign capital investments
qs.e: An enclave sector relies on imported technology and capital and exports raw output without developing local supply chains.

qs.q: An oil boom causes real exchange rate appreciation primarily through
o: a sharp reduction in domestic civil service wage rates
foreign currency inflows expanding money supply and domestic price inflation
a decline in national consumer expenditure on imported goods
an increase in direct taxes levied on oil companies
qs.e: Export windfalls convert to local currency, pushing up non-tradable prices and appreciating the real exchange rate.

qs.q: Automatic fiscal stabilizers in public finance include
o: changes in commercial bank cash reserve ratios
progressive income taxes and unemployment benefits
open market operations by the central bank
qs.e: Progressive taxes and welfare payments adjust automatically with economic cycles to cushion fluctuations without legislation.

qs.q: During an economic boom, progressive tax structures act as automatic stabilizers by
o: lowering corporate tax rates to encourage investment
increasing public transfer payments to households
collecting a larger proportion of income, dampening aggregate demand
qs.e: Higher incomes push taxpayers into higher tax brackets, withdrawing purchasing power and moderating overheating.

qs.q: In economic planning, capital-output ratio measures the amount of capital required to produce
o: one unit of annual economic output
one unit of exported crude petroleum
a given level of government tax revenue
full employment across rural labor markets
qs.e: Capital-output ratio (K/Y) measures investment efficiency; lower ratio indicates higher capital productivity.

qs.q: If the capital-output ratio in an economy is 4 and target annual GDP growth is 6 percent, required national saving rate according to Harrod-Domar model is
qs.e: Growth rate g = s / k => 6% = s / 4 => Required saving rate s = 6% * 4 = 24%.

qs.q: Strategic import substitution industrialization aims to foster industrial growth by
o: increasing export duties on raw agricultural commodities
prohibiting foreign capital investments in manufacturing
replacing imported manufactured consumer goods with local production
eliminating domestic tariffs on all imported manufactures
qs.e: Import substitution protects local infant industries to produce goods previously imported.

qs.q: Export-led growth strategy contrasts with import substitution by focusing on
o: restricting foreign trade through comprehensive tariff walls
subsidizing domestic consumption of imported food items
producing goods for international export markets based on comparative advantage
qs.e: Export-led growth builds manufacturing capacity targeted at global market demand.

qs.q: A firm experiencing diseconomies of scale sees its long-run average cost curve
qs.e: Diseconomies of scale arise from managerial coordination problems in large firms, increasing average cost as scale expands.

qs.q: Minimum efficient scale (MES) in production theory refers to the lowest level of output at which a firm can
o: achieve monopoly status in the market
qs.e: MES is the smallest scale of plant output where long-run average total cost reaches its minimum.

qs.q: If a firm operates in an industry where MES is very large relative to total market demand, the industry market structure will naturally become
qs.e: When MES requires a vast output, only a few large firms can operate at minimum cost, leading to oligopoly or natural monopoly.

qs.q: Prisoner Dilemma model in game theory illustrates why collusive oligopolists find it difficult to
o: raise financial capital from equity markets
maintain cartels due to individual incentives to defect
qs.e: Game theory shows that non-cooperative cheating is a dominant strategy, breaking down cartel collusion.

qs.q: A price-taking competitive firm short-run supply curve above minimum AVC is represented by its
qs.e: For P >= AVC, the firm chooses output where P = MC, so the MC curve is the firm supply curve.

qs.q: Under price discrimination, a seller charges higher prices in market sub-segments where price elasticity of demand is
qs.e: Lower price elasticity means consumers are less price sensitive, enabling higher profit margins.

qs.q: A public limited company shareholders rights include voting for directors and receiving
o: guaranteed interest returns regardless of profit
qs.e: Shareholders receive dividends declared out of corporate net earnings.

qs.q: Conglomerate merger occurs when two merging companies operate in
o: the same industry at the same stage of production
successive stages of the same manufacturing supply chain
completely unrelated product lines and industries
qs.e: Conglomerates merge firms in diverse, unrelated markets to diversify corporate business risk.

qs.q: Transactions demand for money in Keynesian monetary theory depends primarily on
qs.e: Money held for day-to-day transactions scales directly with personal income and expenditure.

qs.q: Which instrument of monetary policy involves direct central bank guidelines specifying credit growth limits to commercial banks?
o: Credit ceilings or direct credit control
Changes in central bank rediscount rate
qs.e: Direct credit control imposes explicit statutory limits or ceilings on bank credit expansion.

qs.q: High marginal tax rates in a progressive tax system can create disincentives to work by
o: lowering consumer demand for imported manufactures
increasing commercial bank cash reserve holdings
reducing the net reward for additional labor effort
qs.e: High marginal rates reduce net take-home pay on overtime or extra income, substituting leisure for work.

qs.q: A tax is termed ad valorem when it is calculated as a
o: fixed physical sum per unit of quantity sold
flat fee assessed on all adult citizens
fixed percentage of the value or price of a good
qs.e: Ad valorem tax is assessed as a percentage of the transaction value (e.g., 15% VAT).

qs.q: A tax assessed as a fixed monetary amount per physical unit of a product (e.g., 50 Naira per liter) is a
qs.e: Specific tax is levied per physical unit regardless of product market price.

qs.q: National debt burden is shifted to future generations when government borrows to fund
o: long-term infrastructural power and road networks
recurrent consumption expenditure rather than productive capital assets
qs.e: Debt spent on immediate consumption leaves future taxpayers with interest liabilities without output-generating assets.

qs.q: When government funds deficit spending by printing new money, the resulting macroeconomic outcome is
o: a fall in commercial bank cash liquidity
an immediate increase in real per capita output
a surplus in the balance of payments current account
qs.e: Monetizing deficits expands money supply without backing output, driving up prices.

qs.q: Structural adjustment programs (SAP) recommended for developing nations by international financial institutions emphasize
o: expansion of state public enterprise ownership
fixing price ceilings on agricultural food crops
qs.e: SAP focuses on market-oriented structural reforms: removing price controls, shrinking public sector, and opening trade.

qs.q: An indifference curve that is concave to the origin implies
o: zero marginal utility for both goods
qs.e: Concavity means MRS increases as consumption shifts along the curve, violating standard consumer equilibrium axioms.

qs.q: If a consumer preference satisfies transitivity, then for choices A, B, and C, if A is preferred to B and B is preferred to C, then
o: C must be preferred to A
A must be preferred to C
B must be preferred to A
A and C must yield zero utility
qs.e: Transitivity axiom guarantees logical consistency in consumer preference orderings.

qs.q: If the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor is equal to 1, the production function is classified as
qs.e: A Cobb-Douglas production function has a constant elasticity of factor substitution equal to unity.

qs.q: For a Leontief production function Q = min(aK, bL), capital and labor are used as
qs.e: Leontief functions represent fixed-proportion technology where inputs are perfect complements and cannot substitute each other.

qs.q: An increase in the wage rate relative to rental rate of capital causes a cost-minimizing firm to
o: substitute labor for capital along an isoquant
increase labor input while keeping capital unchanged
substitute capital for labor along an isoquant
reduce total output while maintaining factor ratio
qs.e: Higher relative price of labor flattens the isocost line, prompting the firm to substitute cheaper capital for labor.

qs.q: If a firm long-run total cost function is LRTC = 10Q - 2Q^2 + 0.1Q^3, the output Q at which long-run average cost is minimized is
qs.e: LRAC = LRTC / Q = 10 - 2Q + 0.1Q^2. Setting d(LRAC)/dQ = 0 => -2 + 0.2Q = 0 => Q = 10 units.

qs.q: For LRTC = 10Q - 2Q^2 + 0.1Q^3 at minimum average cost Q = 10, the minimum Long-Run Average Cost (LRAC) value is
Under third-degree price discrimination, total output is allocated between two markets such that
qs.e: Equalizing marginal revenues across sub-markets and to common marginal cost maximizes total firm profit.

qs.q: If a monopolist sells in Market A with Ed = 2.0 and Market B with Ed = 4.0, the ratio of price in Market A to price in Market B (Pa / Pb) is
qs.e: MR = P(1 - 1/Ed). Since MR is equal across markets: Pa(1 - 1/2) = Pb(1 - 1/4) => Pa(0.5) = Pb(0.75) => Pa/Pb = 0.75 / 0.5 = 1.33.

qs.q: Excess capacity in monopolistically competitive long-run equilibrium refers to the difference between
o: total potential output and zero output
current sales volume and competitor output
short-run fixed output and variable output
profit-maximizing output and output at minimum LRAC
qs.e: Because tangency occurs on the downward slope of LRAC, monopolistically competitive firms operate below minimum LRAC capacity.

qs.q: In Stackelberg duopoly model, the leader firm chooses its output by anticipating the
qs.e: Stackelberg leader incorporates the follower best-response function into its profit maximization problem.

qs.q: Cournot duopoly model assumes that each firm chooses its output level assuming
o: the rival firm price remains constant
the rival firm output remains constant
the rival firm will shut down operations
qs.e: Cournot competitors treat rival output as fixed when deciding their own profit-maximizing output.

qs.q: Bertrand duopoly model assumes firms compete on price, leading to equilibrium price equal to
qs.e: Under Bertrand price competition with homogeneous goods, price-cutting drives price down to marginal cost.

qs.q: In an IS-LM macroeconomic model, the IS curve represents equilibrium in the
qs.e: The IS (Investment-Saving) curve depicts combinations of interest rate and income where output equals aggregate demand.

qs.q: In the IS-LM model, the LM curve represents equilibrium in the
o: money market where money demand equals money supply
goods market where investment equals saving
labor market where labor demand equals supply
qs.e: The LM (Liquidity Preference-Money Supply) curve connects interest rate and income levels balancing money demand and supply.

qs.q: An upward shift of the LM curve can be caused by
o: an increase in real money supply
a decrease in the real money supply
a decrease in autonomous consumer spending
an increase in government public investments
qs.e: A reduction in real money supply creates excess money demand, raising interest rates for any given income level.

qs.q: Expansionary fiscal policy shifts the IS curve to the right, causing income and interest rates to
o: income to rise and interest rate to fall
income to fall and interest rate to rise
qs.e: Rightward IS shift boosts income but increases transaction money demand, driving up interest rates.

qs.q: Monetary expansion in the IS-LM framework shifts LM rightward, resulting in
o: lower income and higher interest rate
higher income and higher interest rate
lower income and lower interest rate
higher income and lower interest rate
qs.e: LM shift rightward increases liquidity, lowering interest rates and stimulating investment and aggregate output.

qs.q: The compensated (Hicksian) demand curve isolates which economic effect of a price change?
qs.e: Hicksian demand holds real utility constant to measure pure substitution effect.

qs.q: Assuming an economy's total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) stands at $800 million, net factor income from abroad of $20 million, and depreciation of $60 million, calculate Net National Product (NNP) at market prices.
qs.e: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad = 800 + (20) = $820 million. NNP = GNP - Depreciation = 820 - 60 = $760 million.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant generates 100 units of output incurring total fixed cost of $400 and total variable cost of $600. Calculate the average total cost (ATC) per unit.
qs.e: Total Cost TC = TFC + TVC = $400 + $600 = $1000. Average Total Cost ATC = TC / Q = $1000 / 100 = $10.00 per unit.

qs.q: A rational consumer allocates expenditure between Product X (price $4) and Product Y (price $2). If marginal utility of Product X is 24 utils at equilibrium, calculate marginal utility of Product Y.
qs.e: Equilibrium condition: MUx / Px = MUy / Py => 24 / 4 = MUy / 2 => 6.0 = MUy / 2 => MUy = 12.0 utils.

qs.q: A competitive firm sells output at ${p_unit} per unit. With total fixed cost of $100 and variable cost per unit of $7, calculate the break-even output quantity.

A market demand function for a product is Q = 500 - 4P. Calculate the point price elasticity of demand when market price P = $50.
