qs.e: Southern coastal West Africa receives two rainfall peaks following the northward and southward passage of the ITCZ.

qs.q: Which climatic factor is primarily responsible for the existence of cold ocean currents along West African coasts like the Canaries Current?
o: Heavy monsoon rain discharging into the Atlantic
Subtropical ocean gyre circulation driven by trade winds
Melting of Sahara desert sand dunes
qs.e: Global oceanic gyres drive cold polar/subpolar waters southward along West African shores as the Canaries Current.

qs.q: A climate graph for a station in the Southern Hemisphere showing peak summer temperatures in January and December will have its temperature curve
o: U-shaped (dipping in the middle months of June-July)
qs.e: In the Southern Hemisphere, summer occurs in December-January and winter in June-July, giving a U-shaped temperature line.

qs.q: If a coastal weather station records a temperature of 26°C at sea level, what is the expected temperature at a hill station 1,200 meters above sea level?
qs.e: Temperature drop = 1.2 * 6.5 = 7.8°C. Altitude temp = 26.0 - 7.8 = 18.2°C.

qs.q: If a climatic table shows monthly rainfall (mm) as: Jan 10, Feb 15, Mar 40, Apr 80, May 150, Jun 200, Jul 250, Aug 220, Sep 180, Oct 90, Nov 20, Dec 5, what is the total annual rainfall?
The lapse rate of dry air ascending without condensation taking place is known as the
o: Saturated adiabatic lapse rate (~5°C per 1,000 meters)
Dry adiabatic lapse rate (~10°C per 1,000 meters)
qs.e: Unsaturated air cools at the constant dry adiabatic rate of ~10°C per 1,000 m ascent due to expansion.

qs.q: Saturated adiabatic lapse rate is lower than dry adiabatic lapse rate because ascending saturated air releases
qs.e: When water vapor condenses into liquid cloud droplets, latent heat is released into the rising air parcel, slowing its cooling rate.

qs.q: Which of the following is an agent of denudation?
qs.e: Running water, wind, glaciers, waves, and groundwater are the primary surface agents of denudation.

qs.q: Which human activity significantly accelerates the rate of denudation and soil erosion?
o: Deforestation and overgrazing on steep hillslopes
qs.e: Removing tree roots and plant cover exposes topsoil directly to heavy rainfall impact and surface runoff wash.

qs.q: Denudation is a comprehensive geological term that encompasses which sequence of processes?
o: Weathering, erosion, mass wasting, transportation, and deposition
Continental drift, plate subduction, and faulting
Fold mountain building, regional metamorphism, and igneous intrusion
qs.e: Denudation includes all exogenic processes that wear down, sculpt, and lower the land surface.

qs.q: On a climograph, what does a flat temperature line at 27°C across all twelve months signify?
o: Equatorial location with negligible seasonal variation in solar insolation
qs.e: Equatorial locations near 0° latitude experience nearly constant day length and sun angle, giving flat annual temperature curves.

qs.q: The climate table above (all months > 120 mm rain, total 2,420 mm) belongs to which ecological zone?
qs.e: Continuous high monthly rainfall exceeding 120 mm every month indicates an Equatorial rainforest regime.

qs.q: A climograph with temperature lines remaining near 0°C or below for 9 months of the year represents a
qs.e: Polar and tundra climates experience severe extended freezing winters where monthly temperatures stay below 0°C.

qs.q: If monthly rainfall values on a climate graph are equal for all 12 months at 200 mm, the annual total rainfall is
qs.e: Total annual rainfall = 12 * 200 mm = 2,400 mm.

qs.q: If monthly temperatures at a station are: 12, 13, 15, 18, 22, 25, 28, 27, 24, 20, 15, 13 °C, the highest temperature occurs in
qs.e: July records the peak temperature value of 28°C in this Northern Hemisphere temperate sequence.

qs.q: The wearing away and removal of rock materials from one part of the Earth's crust to another by mobile natural agents is called
qs.e: Erosion involves active detachment and transportation of rock debris by wind, water, ice, or waves.

qs.q: A climograph with an inverted U-shaped temperature curve peaking in June-July indicates that the recording station is located in the
qs.e: In the Northern Hemisphere, summer insolation peaks in June-July, producing an inverted U-shaped temperature line.

qs.q: Using the same dataset (Jan-Dec temp: 22, 24, 27, 30, 32, 29, 26, 25, 27, 28, 25, 23 °C), what is the minimum monthly mean temperature?
qs.e: The lowest temperature value listed is 22°C in January.

qs.q: If a climate graph's rainfall bars drop to zero for 8 consecutive months (October to April) in Northern West Africa, agriculture during those months requires
qs.e: An 8-month dry season makes crop cultivation impossible without artificial irrigation supply.

qs.q: If a station's monthly mean temperatures (°C) from Jan to Dec are: 22, 24, 27, 30, 32, 29, 26, 25, 27, 28, 25, 23, what is its maximum monthly mean temperature?
qs.e: The highest temperature in the given monthly sequence is 32°C in May.

qs.q: If a climate graph shows 12 monthly rainfall values of 0 mm, 0 mm, 2 mm, 5 mm, 12 mm, 18 mm, 22 mm, 15 mm, 4 mm, 1 mm, 0 mm, 0 mm (total 79 mm), the location is a
qs.e: Total annual precipitation under 100 mm signifies hyper-arid hot desert conditions.

qs.q: Regolith is best defined as the layer of
o: Unconsolidated weathered rock debris overlying solid bedrock
Molten mantle magma beneath the crust
qs.e: Regolith is the mantle of loose fragmented rock material produced by weathering above intact bedrock.

qs.q: Mudflows differ from landslides in that mudflows contain a
o: Much higher proportion of water and liquid mud
qs.e: Mudflows are fluid mixtures of fine-grained mud and water that flow rapidly along channels like liquid concrete.

qs.q: The rate of denudation is generally fastest in regions with
o: Flat plains, dense rainforest canopy, and low rainfall
Steep relief, high rainfall intensity, and sparse protective vegetation
Frozen permafrost and zero wind movement
qs.e: Steep gradients accelerate gravity flow, heavy rain supplies erodible kinetic energy, and lack of plant roots leaves soil exposed.

qs.q: Landslides are frequently triggered on steep mountain slopes by
o: Prolonged heavy rainfall saturating rock strata and reducing friction
Formation of coral reefs along coastlines
qs.e: Water saturation increases pore water pressure and lubricates slip planes, causing entire rock masses to slide downslope.

qs.q: What feature on a climate graph indicates a distinct dry season?
o: Months where precipitation bars fall below a low threshold (e.g. < 60 mm) or near zero
Inverted scale labels on the vertical axis
Blue color shading on the temperature line
qs.e: Dry seasons are identified on climographs by months with very short or absent rainfall bars.

qs.q: Climographs for monsoon climates (Köppen Am) are distinguished by
o: Uniform low rainfall under 100 mm all year
Zero rainfall in summer and heavy snow in winter
A very high rainfall peak in summer contrast with a short dry season
qs.e: Tropical monsoon climates (e.g. coastal West Africa, India) feature extremely heavy summer monsoon rainfall and a brief dry period.

qs.q: Exogenic processes of denudation derive their energy primarily from the
qs.e: Exogenic forces (weathering, erosion, mass movement) are driven by solar energy and gravity operating at Earth's surface.

qs.q: Endogenic tectonic forces contrast with denudation because endogenic forces
o: Level down mountain peaks into flat plains
Erode river valleys into deep gorges
Build up landforms through crustal uplift and volcanism
qs.e: Endogenic processes (earthquakes, faulting, folding, volcanism) originate inside Earth and construct relief features.

qs.q: In arid and semi-arid regions, wind erosion forms broad, shallow depressions called
qs.e: Deflation hollows are created when turbulent wind currents lift and blow away loose sand particles from arid plains.

qs.q: A climatic graph for Kano, Nigeria, shows a single sharp rainfall peak in August because
o: The Harmattan wind blows strongest in August
The ITCZ reaches its northernmost inland position in West Africa during July-August
Cold Benguela ocean currents flood the inland plains in August
Kano is situated directly on the Equator
qs.e: In July-August, the moist Tropical Maritime air mass extends furthest inland into Northern Nigeria, bringing peak monsoon rain.

qs.q: Which climate graph feature differentiates Tropical Savanna (Aw) from Tropical Rainforest (Af)?
o: Presence of a pronounced dry season in Aw where monthly rainfall falls below 60 mm
Total absence of sunshine in Aw
Higher annual rainfall in Aw than Af
qs.e: Tropical Savanna (Aw) has a distinct dry winter season, whereas Tropical Rainforest (Af) remains wet year-round.

qs.q: Mass wasting (mass movement) differs from erosion primarily because mass wasting is driven strictly by
o: Gravity acting on slope materials without a fluid transporting agent
qs.e: Mass wasting is the downslope movement of rock and soil under the direct force of gravity.

qs.q: If a station's monthly mean temperatures for 12 months sum up to 300°C, what is its mean annual temperature?
qs.e: Mean annual temperature = Total sum of 12 monthly temperatures / 12 = 300 / 12 = 25.0°C.

qs.q: Which rapid mass movement process involves a sudden massive collapse of rock blocks down a vertical cliff face?
qs.e: Rockfalls occur on steep or vertical rock slopes when fractured rocks break free and fall under gravity.

qs.q: Which type of mass movement is extremely slow and barely perceptible except through tilted telephone poles and fences?
qs.e: Soil creep is a continuous, ultra-slow downslope movement of soil caused by freeze-thaw or wetting-drying cycles.

qs.q: In the same temperature sequence (12, 13, 15, 18, 22, 25, 28, 27, 24, 20, 15, 13 °C), the annual range of temperature is
qs.e: Annual range = 28°C (July) - 12°C (Jan) = 16°C.

qs.q: On a climate graph, if rainfall bars exceed 100 mm every month and temperature stays at 26-28°C, the biome represented is
qs.e: Abundant monthly rainfall exceeding 100 mm and high uniform warmth are classic signatures of tropical rainforest biomes.

qs.q: Which month exhibits the highest temperature peak in Northern Nigerian climate graphs prior to the onset of monsoon rains?
qs.e: Northern Nigeria experiences its hottest temperatures in April-May before monsoon cloudiness and rainfall bring temporary cooling.

qs.q: An isolated, steep-sided, residual hill rising abruptly from a surrounding gentle plain in a savanna landscape is called an
qs.e: Inselbergs (e.g. granite domes / bornhardts) are resistant rock masses left standing after extensive denudation of surrounding land.

qs.q: Using the same temperature dataset (22, 24, 27, 30, 32, 29, 26, 25, 27, 28, 25, 23 °C), what is the annual temperature range?
qs.e: Annual temperature range = Max (32°C) - Min (22°C) = 10°C.

qs.q: If total annual rainfall from a climograph is 350 mm and annual potential evapotranspiration is 1,800 mm, the region has a severe
qs.e: When potential evapotranspiration far exceeds annual precipitation, a permanent moisture deficit exists.

qs.q: Which landform is produced at the base of a steep cliff by the accumulation of angular weathered rock fragments fallen from above?
qs.e: Scree or talus consists of coarse, angular rock debris shattered by frost action and collected at the cliff foot.

qs.q: A climate graph showing high summer temperatures, very cold sub-zero winter temperatures, and moderate summer rainfall represents a
qs.e: Continental interiors far from oceans experience extreme temperature variations between hot summers and freezing winters.

qs.q: A climate graph for London shows mild winters (4°C), cool summers (18°C), and evenly distributed rainfall all year round. This depicts a
qs.e: Marine West Coast climates (Köppen Cfb) feature moderate temperatures and year-round rainfall due to prevailing westerly ocean winds.

qs.q: A climograph with rainfall bars concentrated exclusively in winter months (June-August in Southern Hemisphere) and dry summer months represents a
qs.e: Mediterranean climates characteristically receive winter rainfall while summer months remain dry under subtropical high pressure.

qs.q: On a climate graph, if the gap between temperature curve and rainfall bar chart is shaded to represent moisture availability, a period where rainfall exceeds evapotranspiration is called a
qs.e: When rainfall surpasses evapotranspiration demand, water surplus recharges soil moisture and feeds river runoff.

qs.q: Which process converts loose eroded rock debris into solid sedimentary rock layers over geological time?
qs.e: Lithification turns accumulated sediments into firm rock strata through pressure compaction and mineral cementation.

qs.q: A slump is a form of mass movement characterized by the curved rotational movement of a rock mass along a
qs.e: Slumping involves backward rotational slipping of unconsolidated material along a spoon-shaped concave rupture surface.

qs.q: Which index derived from a climate graph measures the thermal comfort or heat stress experienced by humans?
qs.e: THI combines temperature and relative humidity data from climatic records to assess human heat stress.

qs.q: Solifluction is a specialized form of mass wasting common in sub-polar regions where saturated soil slides over
qs.e: In periglacial zones, summer thawing melts topsoil while the underlying permafrost remains frozen, causing mud to flow downslope.

qs.q: The work of denudation reduces high mountain landscapes over geological time toward a gently undulating plain known as a
qs.e: Continuous weathering and erosion erode highlands down to base level, creating a featureless low plain called a peneplain.

qs.q: If a climograph displays two distinct rainfall peaks (bimodal pattern), it indicates that the sun passes directly overhead
o: Only once a year during winter solstice
qs.e: Equatorial and sub-equatorial stations experience two rainfall maxima corresponding to the twice-yearly overhead zenith passage of the sun.

qs.q: If a climate table shows rainfall (mm) for Jan-Dec as: 250, 220, 210, 200, 180, 150, 120, 140, 190, 230, 260, 270, the annual total is
In a climate graph, a steep downward dip in the temperature line during rainy summer months in tropical West Africa is mainly caused by
o: Increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling during heavy monsoon rain
Inflow of Arctic polar air masses
Total loss of solar radiation in summer
qs.e: Heavy summer cloudiness blocks direct solar insolation and rainfall evaporation cools the surface air layer.

qs.q: When comparing two climate graphs, Station X has an annual rainfall of 2,400 mm while Station Y has 450 mm. Station X is most likely in a
o: Tropical Rainforest belt, while Station Y is in a Semi-arid Savanna/Sahel belt
Hot desert, while Station Y is in an Equatorial swamp
Tundra region, while Station Y is in a Monsoon forest
Mediterranean zone, while Station Y is on an Alpine glacier
qs.e: High annual rainfall (>2,000 mm) characterizes tropical rainforests, whereas low rainfall (~450 mm) fits semi-arid Sahelian zones.

qs.q: If a climatic table lists monthly rainfall (mm) as: 0, 0, 0, 5, 25, 80, 150, 190, 70, 10, 0, 0, what is the length of the wet season (months with > 50 mm rain)?
o: 4 months (May, June, July, August, September -> wait, June, July, Aug, Sep = 4)
qs.e: Months with > 50 mm rain are June (80), July (150), August (190), and September (70) = 4 months.

qs.q: Biological denudation includes rock breakdown accomplished by
o: Freezing water expanding in rock joints
Growth of tree roots in rock fractures and burrowing animals
Salt crystal growth in arid soils
qs.e: Tree roots grow into rock cracks, exerting immense mechanical pressure that wedges rocks apart.

qs.q: A river divide or watershed is defined as the elevated land ridge that
o: Marks the deepest point of a river bed
Forms the submerged mouth of an estuary
qs.e: A watershed (drainage divide) is a highland perimeter separating precipitation runoff into distinct river basins.

qs.q: Weathering differs fundamental from erosion in that weathering involves
o: Disintegration and decomposition of rocks in situ without transportation
Active transportation of sediments by running water
Deposition of sand dunes in deserts
Movement of mudflows down mountain channels
qs.e: Weathering is a static, in situ breakdown of rocks; erosion involves active movement of rock debris.

qs.q: Which feature forms where a river drops its sediment load upon entering a quiet lake or ocean body?
qs.e: When river velocity drops abruptly upon reaching standing water, suspended silt settles to build a delta.

qs.q: Which denudation process involves the chemical breakdown of minerals inside rocks without moving them?
qs.e: Chemical weathering alters the mineral composition of rock in situ through reaction with air and water.

qs.q: The principal agent responsible for transportation of denudation products to ocean basins worldwide is
qs.e: Rivers carry the vast majority of weathered continental debris to the oceans as dissolved and suspended load.

qs.q: The total volume of water discharging from a river basin per unit time past a gauging station is called river
o: Discharge (measured in cubic meters per second / cumecs)
qs.e: Discharge = Cross-sectional area of channel * average stream velocity (m³/s).

qs.q: A drainage pattern that develops on uniform rock strata resembling the branching twigs of a tree is described as
qs.e: Dendritic drainage patterns form on rocks of uniform resistance, developing tree-like tributary branches.

qs.q: Which stage of a river profile is characterized by steep gradients, narrow V-shaped valleys, waterfalls, and dominant vertical erosion?
qs.e: The upper stage has high kinetic energy focused on vertical bed-cutting, forming steep V-shaped valleys and rapids.

qs.q: River regime describes the
o: Seasonal variation in a river's discharge volume over the course of a year
qs.e: River regime reflects annual flow fluctuations driven by seasonal rainfall or snowmelt patterns.

qs.q: Corrosion (solution) in river erosion refers to the
o: Chemical dissolution of soluble rocks like limestone and chalk by stream water
Physical collision of boulders on channel beds
qs.e: Slightly acidic river water dissolves carbonate minerals in limestone beds.

qs.q: Rill erosion develops when sheetwash concentrates into
o: Tiny well-defined micro-channels on exposed soil
qs.e: Rills are small temporary channels formed when runoff collects into streamlets; if unchecked, rills widen into gullies.

qs.q: An oxbow lake is formed in the lower course of a river when a
o: Waterfall retreats upstream leaving a gorge
Meander neck is cut through during a flood, isolating a curved loop
River captures another stream across a divide
Glacier melts in a mountain corrie
qs.e: Flooding cuts across narrow meander necks; deposition seals the cut-off loop into a crescent-shaped oxbow lake.

qs.q: The River Niger delta is classified as an arcuate delta because of its
o: Fan-shaped or triangular coastline curved outward toward the sea
Finger-like long extensions resembling a bird's foot
qs.e: Arcuate deltas (like Niger, Nile, Rhine) have smooth, outward-curving triangular shoreline margins.

qs.q: The Mississippi River delta in North America is a classic example of a
qs.e: Bird's foot deltas feature distributary channels extending far into open sea bounded by natural levees, resembling bird toes.

qs.q: Saltation as a river transport process involves small pebbles and sand grains
o: Floating in suspension near the water surface
Bouncing along the river bed in a series of short hops
Rolling continuously without leaving the bed
qs.e: Saltation describes the hop-and-bounce movement of medium-sized bed load particles pushed by turbulent currents.

qs.q: Exfoliation (onion-skin weathering) is a denudation process caused by repeated
o: Freezing and thawing of water in rock pores
Dissolution of calcium carbonate in acid rain
Daytime heating and nighttime cooling of rock outer layers
qs.e: Differential expansion and contraction of outer rock layers under high diurnal temperature ranges causes surface shells to peel off.

qs.q: Sheetwash (sheet erosion) occurs when rainwater flows over a smooth land surface as a
o: Continuous unchanneled layer removing a uniform film of topsoil
qs.e: Unchanneled surface runoff during heavy rain sweeps away topsoil evenly across exposed slopes.

qs.q: The sharp bend where a capturing river diverts the captured headwaters is known as the
qs.e: The sudden right-angled diversion point where headwaters switch channels is called the elbow of capture.

qs.q: Alluvial fans are fan-shaped deposits of sediment formed where a steep mountain stream
o: Emerge abruptly onto a flat plain, losing velocity and dropping its load
Drains into a underground limestone sinkhole
qs.e: Abrupt reduction in slope gradient at a mountain foot reduces stream velocity, spreading sediments into a fan shape.

qs.q: Corrasion (abrasion) by a river occurs when the river's bed load of sand and gravel is
o: Dissolved chemically by weak acidic water
Lifted vertically into the atmosphere by wind
Haptically scraped against the channel bed and banks like sandpaper
qs.e: Abrasion is the scouring action of transported rock tools scraping channel floor and walls.

qs.q: Pot-holes on a bedrock river floor in the upper course are circular depressions drilled by
o: Swirling pebbles rotated by turbulent eddy currents (abrasion/corrasion)
qs.e: Eddy currents trap stones in bedrock hollows, swirling them around to grind circular pot-hole depressions.

qs.q: Natural levees are low embankments formed along lower river banks during floods through the
o: Deposition of coarse sediment when overbank floodwaters lose velocity
Erosion of bank clay by lateral corrasion
qs.e: When a river overflows its banks, water velocity drops immediately at the bank margin, dropping coarse silt to build levees.

qs.q: Wave-cut platforms along rocky coastlines are landforms created by coastal denudation through
o: Wind deflation in coastal sand dunes
Deposition of river silt in estuaries
Undercutting of sea cliffs by wave abrasion and hydraulic action
qs.e: Waves batter cliff bases, eroding a notch that forces cliff collapse and leaves a flat wave-cut rock platform exposed at low tide.

qs.q: Gully erosion represents an advanced stage of water erosion where channels become so deep that they
o: Refill automatically with pure organic compost
Cannot be removed by ordinary agricultural tillage equipment
Turn into navigable ocean shipping routes
qs.e: Gullies are steep-sided ravines carved by flash floods, destroying arable farm fields.

qs.q: Interlocking spurs are a landform characteristic of upper river valleys created as a youthful river
o: Cuts straight lines through soft coastal mud
Forms massive deltas into deep ocean gulfs
Winds around obstacles of resistant rock strata
qs.e: Youthful rivers lack energy to cut straight through resistant rock spurs, weaving left and right around them.

qs.q: Which agent of denudation is primarily responsible for creating U-shaped valleys and hanging valleys?
qs.e: Glaciers gouge out V-shaped river valleys, widening and deepening them into steep-sided, flat-bottomed U-shaped troughs.

qs.q: Which landform is an undulating ridge of glacial till deposited at the margin of a melting glacier sheet?
qs.e: Moraines are unsorted glacial debris accumulations left behind along edges or terminus of glaciers.

qs.q: A radial drainage pattern is formed when streams flow outward in all directions from a central highland such as the
qs.e: Radial drainage features rivers originating from a central elevated dome or volcanic peak and flowing outward in all cardinal directions.

qs.q: The base level of erosion refers to the lowest elevation to which running water can erode the land, which is ultimately
o: Bottom of the deepest oil well
qs.e: Rivers cannot erode their beds below the level of the sea or lake into which they discharge.

qs.q: Centripetal drainage occurs when rivers flow inward from surrounding highlands toward a central inland basin such as the
qs.e: Centripetal drainage develops in interior depressions (like Lake Chad) where rivers drain inward from surrounding rim highlands.

qs.q: Which process of river erosion involves the sheer mechanical force of moving water dislodging loose joint blocks from the channel bed?
qs.e: Hydraulic action relies on water pressure and surging currents forcing air into joint cracks to break rock beds.

qs.q: Braided river channels feature multiple interconnected sub-channels separated by temporary sandbars; they develop when a river carries a
o: Heavy bed load far exceeding its transport capacity
Zero sediment load in clear water
High volume of icebergs in polar seas
qs.e: When river transport capacity drops below its heavy sediment load, silt bars deposit within the channel, splitting the stream.

qs.q: Which process of river erosion involves rock fragments carried by the stream colliding with each other and breaking into smaller, rounder pebbles?
qs.e: Attrition is the self-grinding collision between bed load particles, reducing their size and sharpness.

qs.q: A trellis drainage pattern typically develops in regions underlain by alternating hard and soft rocks where folded strata produce parallel valleys; tributaries join the main stream at
qs.e: In trellis drainage, short tributary streams cut through soft rock bands and join main valley streams at right angles.

qs.q: A knoll or kopje is a small residual hill formed during the denudation of a
qs.e: Kopjes are residual granite block piles created by deep subsurface chemical weathering followed by stripping of regolith.

qs.q: Which type of chemical weathering turns feldspar minerals in granite into kaolin clay?
qs.e: Hydrolysis involves hydrogen ions in water reacting chemically with feldspar to yield kaolin (china clay).

qs.q: In karst topography, the collapse of cavern roofs after extensive underground chemical denudation produces
qs.e: Carbonic acid dissolves subterranean limestone, enlarging caverns until the ceiling collapses to form sinkholes and dolines.

qs.q: River terraces are step-like benches on valley sides representing former floodplain levels left elevated after
o: River rejuvenation and renewed vertical erosion
qs.e: Rejuvenated rivers incise new lower floodplains, leaving remnants of older floodplains as paired or unpaired terraces.

qs.q: Gorges and canyons are narrow, deep valleys with near-vertical rock walls created by rapid river bed-cutting in
o: Broad, gentle floodplains near ocean mouths
Arid or resistant rock regions where vertical erosion far outpaces lateral weathering
qs.e: Where climate is dry or rocks resistant, valley sides do not collapse easily, allowing steep vertical gorges to form.

qs.q: Estuarine deltas develop where river mouths are drowned by rising sea levels or tides, such as the mouth of the
qs.e: Estuarine deltas form where sediment fills submerged river estuaries rather than projecting out into open sea.

qs.q: Knickpoints on a river profile are break-points in slope (often marked by waterfalls or rapids) formed as a result of
o: Excessive silt deposition in lower estuaries
Rejuvenation of the river caused by crustal uplift or drop in sea level
Formation of natural levees on floodplains
Growth of mangrove vegetation across river channels
qs.e: Rejuvenation gives a river renewed erosive energy, creating a headward-eroding knickpoint step along its longitudinal profile.

qs.q: Which term describes the maximum slope angle at which loose, dry rock debris remains stable without sliding downslope?
qs.e: The angle of repose is the maximum steepness loose sediments can sustain before gravity causes down-slope sliding.

qs.q: Badland topography (such as in dry clay regions) is characterized by dense networks of steep gullies and ravines produced by
o: Glacial ice movement across granite bedrock
Volcanic lava flows sealing surface soils
Severe water erosion on soft, unprotected rocks in arid/semi-arid regions
qs.e: Occasional violent rainstorms on soft, vegetation-scarce clays carve intricate ravines and ridges known as badlands.

qs.q: A stream flowing in a valley that is far too large for its current small volume (often below an elbow of capture) is called a
qs.e: Deprived of its headwaters by river capture, the remaining stream appears under-sized (misfit) for its existing valley.

qs.q: Salt weathering (haloclasty) is common in coastal and arid zones where salt crystals grow in rock pores, causing disintegrating stress through
qs.e: Evaporating saline water leaves salt crystals that expand upon heating, fragmenting porous rock walls.

qs.q: Spheroidal weathering is a form of chemical weathering where jointed rock blocks become rounded into spheres because chemical attack is fastest at
o: Corners and edges of joint blocks
qs.e: Water penetrates joint planes, attacking block corners from three sides simultaneously and rounding the rock.

qs.q: In cold alpine environments, frost shattering (freeze-thaw weathering) operates efficiently because water expands in volume by about what percentage when it freezes?
qs.e: Water expanding by ~9% upon freezing exerts up to 2,100 kg/cm² pressure, splitting fractured rocks apart.

qs.q: River capture (stream piracy) occurs when a powerful stream with greater erosive power breaches a divide and diverts the upper headwaters of a weaker neighbor; the dry valley left behind below the elbow of capture is called a
qs.e: The abandoned valley segment below a capture elbow where water no longer flows is called a wind gap.

qs.q: In desert landscapes, pediments are gently sloping bedrock surfaces formed at the foot of mountain fronts through
o: Parallel retreat of slopes (scarp retreat) and sheetwash erosion
qs.e: Scarp retreat and sheet erosion shave back mountain slopes, leaving behind smooth, rock-cut pediments.

qs.q: In West Africa, the high forest belt featuring broad-leaved evergreen trees, layered structural strata, and extensive lianas is termed the
qs.e: Tropical rainforests feature tall trees forming continuous canopies and buttress roots for stability.

qs.q: A rural settlement whose buildings are clustered closely around a central market or water source is described as
qs.e: Nucleated settlements feature buildings grouped tightly around a core central point like a market or well.

qs.q: The vertical section of soil from the ground surface down to the underlying parent bedrock is referred to as the soil
qs.e: A soil profile exhibits distinct horizontal layers known as soil horizons from topsoil to parent rock.

qs.q: The rotation of the Earth on its axis from west to east is directly responsible for causing
qs.e: Earth rotates eastward on its axis once every 24 hours, creating the regular sequence of day and night.

qs.q: An industry whose final manufactured product weighs significantly less than the raw materials used is a
qs.e: Weight-losing industries locate near raw material sources to minimize transportation costs of heavy inputs.

qs.q: Coal deposits mined in Enugu State, Nigeria, are primarily associated with which geological rock class?
qs.e: Coal is formed from ancient plant material compressed within sedimentary rock strata over millions of years.

qs.q: The warm ocean current flowing poleward along the east coast of North America in the Atlantic Ocean is the
qs.e: The Gulf Stream carries warm tropical water northward along the eastern coast of North America.

qs.q: The main ecological reason trees in the Sahel savanna possess small thick leaves and deep taproots is to
o: Minimize transpiration loss and reach deep groundwater
Resist high wind pressure during tropical cyclones
Prevent soil erosion caused by heavy flash flooding
Enhance rapid photosynthesis during short dry spells
qs.e: Xerophytic adaptations such as small leathery leaves and deep taproots enable plants to survive severe drought.

qs.q: Mangrove vegetation along the Nigerian coast thrives primarily in which specific aquatic habitat?
qs.e: Mangrove trees feature stilt roots adapted to saline and brackish intertidal muddy coastal ecosystems.

qs.q: Settlements aligned along a major transportation route such as a railway line or highway are classified as
qs.e: Linear settlements extend in a ribbon-like pattern along linear infrastructure or physical lines.

qs.q: Which physical site factor historically encouraged the establishment of hilltop settlements in West Africa?
o: Protection against enemy invasion during inter-tribal warfare
Easy access to deepwater ports for ocean vessels
Proximity to fertile alluvial floodplains for swamp rice
Direct connection to regional transport networks
qs.e: Elevated hilltops provided strategic defensive vantage points against military attacks in historical times.

qs.q: In soil science, the removal of soluble minerals from topsoil down into subsoil layers by water is called
qs.e: Leaching occurs when heavy rainfall causes downward movement of dissolved minerals through topsoil.

qs.q: Which soil horizon is richest in dark organic humus and active microbial activity essential for crops?
qs.e: Horizon A (topsoil) contains the highest concentration of decomposed organic humus and biological activity.

qs.q: If local solar time at Greenwich Meridian (0 degrees) is 12:00 noon, what is the solar time at longitude 45 degrees East?
qs.e: 45 degrees divided by 15 degrees per hour equals 3 hours ahead of GMT. 12:00 noon plus 3 hours is 3:00 p.m.

qs.q: Footloose manufacturing industries are characterized primarily by their freedom of location because they
o: Require large amounts of heavy iron ore and coal at port sites
Are not tied to specific localized raw material or energy sources
Depend exclusively on water transport along major navigable canals
Generate zero electronic waste and require no electricity
qs.e: Footloose industries produce lightweight components and can locate independently of raw material sources.

qs.q: Columbite and tin ore (cassiterite) in Nigeria are historically extracted from basement complex rocks of which plateau?
qs.e: The Jos Plateau is famous for placer and alluvial deposits of tin ore (cassiterite) and columbite.

qs.q: Cold ocean currents flowing along western tropical coastlines contribute significantly to coastal aridity by
o: Increasing sea surface evaporation rates to produce heavy rainfall
Stabilizing atmospheric conditions and inhibiting cloud formation
Generating powerful tropical cyclones that blow rain clouds inland
Warming adjacent air masses to cause intense convectional rain
qs.e: Cold currents chill the lower atmosphere, creating temperature inversions that suppress convection and rainfall.

qs.q: Granite and basalt are classic examples of which major group of rocks formed by cooling magma?
qs.e: Igneous rocks form through the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava.

qs.q: The physical disintegration of rocks into smaller fragments without chemical alteration of minerals is called
qs.e: Mechanical (physical) weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces without altering their chemical composition.

qs.q: Which vegetation belt forms a transition zone between the tropical rainforest and Guinea savanna in Nigeria?
qs.e: Derived savanna is created by anthropogenic deforestation and bush burning along the rainforest margin.

qs.q: In equatorial rainforest ecosystems, epiphytic plants such as orchids obtain structural support by
o: Parasitizing water from host plant vascular tissues
Growing attached to high branches of taller forest trees
Forming thick prop roots directly into swamp mud
qs.e: Epiphytes grow on host branches purely for structural support and access to sunlight without harming the host.

qs.q: A settlement pattern where individual farmsteads are widely separated across agricultural land is termed
qs.e: Dispersed settlement patterns consist of isolated farmsteads separated by large expanses of farmland.

qs.q: In settlement geography, a wet-point settlement is established primarily to secure immediate access to
o: Dry land elevated above flood-prone valley floors
A reliable year-round water supply in dry regions
Rich deposits of industrial iron ore and limestone
High-speed rail nodes connecting administrative capitals
qs.e: Wet-point settlements are sited close to water sources in arid or semi-arid zones where water is scarce.

qs.q: Soil texture is fundamentally determined by the relative proportions of which primary mineral particle sizes?
qs.e: Soil texture depends on the relative percentages of sand, silt, and clay particle size fractions.

qs.q: Lateritic soils in hot humid tropical regions develop their reddish hue primarily from high concentrations of
qs.e: Intense tropical leaching removes silica, leaving insoluble iron and aluminium oxides that color the soil red.

qs.q: The Earth completes one full orbit around the Sun in approximately how many solar days?
qs.e: The revolution of the Earth around the Sun takes 365 and 1/4 days, producing our solar year.

qs.q: During the June solstice, the overhead rays of the midday sun shine directly vertical over which line of latitude?
qs.e: At the June solstice, the Northern Hemisphere tilts closest to the Sun, placing the noon sun over Tropic of Cancer.

qs.q: Which major industrial cluster in Nigeria is renowned for petroleum refining and petrochemical processing?
qs.e: The Niger Delta coastal belt around Port Harcourt and Warri houses Nigeria's major oil refineries.

qs.q: The spatial concentration of interconnected industrial firms in a single urban region to share infrastructure is called
qs.e: Agglomeration economies occur when factories cluster to reduce costs through shared suppliers and utilities.

qs.q: Crude petroleum in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria is trapped predominantly within deep sandstone layers of which era?
qs.e: Niger Delta crude oil reservoirs are located within Tertiary sedimentary rock formations.

qs.q: Limestone deposits in Ewekoro and Sagamu serve as essential raw materials for which major manufacturing industry?
qs.e: Limestone provides calcium carbonate necessary for producing Portland cement in Nigeria.

qs.q: Which cold ocean current flows southward along the northwest coast of Africa, influencing the Sahara desert climate?
qs.e: The cold Canaries Current flows along northwest Africa, reinforcing aridity in the western Sahara region.

qs.q: If a feature measures 8 cm on a map with scale 1:50,000, what is its length on a map drawn at 1:25,000?
A mountain peak has an elevation of 750 m and a valley base is at 150 m. If horizontal map distance is 6 cm on a scale of 1:50,000, what is the slope gradient?
Baobab trees with water-storing trunks and acacia species with modified thorns characterize which vegetation belt?
qs.e: Baobabs store water and acacias reduce transpiration as adaptations to dry savanna conditions.

qs.q: A dry-point settlement is intentionally located on elevated ground within low-lying regions primarily to avoid
o: Arid dust storms blowing from desert regions
Extreme cold temperatures at high altitudes
Geothermal activity near volcanic rift valleys
qs.e: Dry-point settlements are built on elevated terrain to protect residents and structures from seasonal flooding.

qs.q: The spatial transformation of multiple adjacent towns merging together into an unbroken urban region is called a
qs.e: A conurbation forms when expanding cities and towns merge geographically into a continuous urban zone.

qs.q: The sequence of different soil types down a hillside slope from ridge top to valley floor is termed a soil
qs.e: A soil catena represents a series of distinct soil profiles along a slope under similar climatic conditions.

qs.q: Waterlogged soil conditions in low-lying anaerobic depressions produce greyish-blue soil colouration through
qs.e: Gleying occurs under waterlogged anaerobic conditions where iron compounds are reduced to blue-grey ferrous forms.

qs.q: When traveling eastward across the International Date Line (180 degrees longitude), what calendar adjustment is made?
qs.e: Crossing the International Date Line going eastward moves into time zones that are behind, so one day is subtracted.

qs.q: The apparent deflection of global ocean currents and wind systems caused by Earth's rotation is known as the
qs.e: The Coriolis effect deflects moving winds and ocean currents to the right in Northern Hemisphere and left in Southern Hemisphere.

qs.q: Open-cast or strip mining method is chosen over deep underground shaft mining when mineral seams are
o: Buried thousands of metres deep beneath thick granite overburden
Dissolved in deep subterranean thermal groundwater aquifers
Concentrated exclusively under deep ocean floor trenches
Located near the Earth surface in flat horizontal layers
qs.e: Open-cast mining is economically preferred when mineral deposits lie shallowly beneath topsoil and overburden.

qs.q: The meeting zone of warm and cold ocean currents off Grand Banks creates world-famous commercial areas for
o: Coral reef growing with high salinity
Permanent ice shelves blocking all transport
Fishing due to plankton nutrient upwelling
qs.e: Mixing warm and cold ocean currents generates nutrient-rich waters supporting dense plankton and rich fisheries.

qs.q: A map distance of 5 cm represents an actual ground distance of 10 km. What is the Representative Fraction scale?
A nature reserve measures 4 cm by 6 cm on a map with a scale of 1:50,000. What is its actual ground area in square kilometres?
qs.e: 1 cm = 0.5 km. Width = 4 * 0.5 = 2 km. Length = 6 * 0.5 = 3 km. Ground Area = 2 * 3 = 6 sq km.

qs.q: In ecological succession, how does human-induced bush burning transform high forest into derived savanna?
o: By increasing soil nitrogen through ash to favour coniferous seedlings
By lowering ground temperatures so that sub-alpine mosses dominate
By flooding topsoil to select for floating aquatic angiosperms
By eliminating fire-sensitive rainforest trees and allowing light for drought-tolerant grasses
qs.e: Repeated burning destroys fire-sensitive evergreen forest trees, allowing fire-resistant savanna trees and grasses to take over.

qs.q: The environmental phenomenon of acid mine drainage occurs when exposed sulphide minerals react with water and air to produce
o: Methane gas explosions in shallow quarries
Thermal volcanic plumes in adjacent streams
Sulfuric acid and toxic heavy metal runoff
qs.e: Pyrite oxidation in mining wastes produces sulfuric acid, which dissolves heavy metals and contaminates water bodies.

qs.q: How does the warm North Atlantic Drift influence the winter climate of coastal ports in Western Europe like Norway?
o: It causes severe blizzards and permanent pack ice formation
It reduces ambient winter air temperatures to sub-zero desert levels
It completely dries up coastal rainfall during winter months
It keeps ocean ports ice-free throughout winter despite high latitude
qs.e: The warm North Atlantic Drift moderates winter air temperatures, keeping Western European ports navigable year-round.

qs.q: If two contours on a 1:25,000 map are separated by a vertical interval of 100 metres and a map distance of 2 cm, what is the slope gradient?
Chemical weathering through carbonation is most pronounced in landscapes underlain by which rock type?
qs.e: Dissolved carbon dioxide in rainwater forms weak carbonic acid, which readily dissolves calcium carbonate in limestone.

qs.q: Rocks formed directly from the cooling and crystallization of molten magma or lava are classified as
qs.e: Igneous rocks originate from cooled molten mantle material either beneath or on the Earth surface.

qs.q: The rapid and uncontrolled growth of urban population exceeding available infrastructure and employment is called
qs.e: Overurbanisation occurs when urban population growth outpaces economic development and municipal infrastructure.

qs.q: The physical process of soil removal by running water forming narrow channels across bare slopes is known as
qs.e: Rill erosion creates small, well-defined streamlets and channels on exposed sloping topsoil.

qs.q: The exchange of goods and services between different independent sovereign nations is defined as
qs.e: International trade involves commercial transactions across recognized national borders.

qs.q: Which mode of transport is generally most cost-effective for carrying bulky, non-perishable goods over long overseas distances?
qs.e: Maritime shipping offers the lowest per-ton-kilometre cost for heavy long-distance international freight.

qs.q: The movement of water through the atmosphere, land surface, and underground reservoirs is called the
qs.e: The hydrological cycle describes continuous water circulation powered by solar energy and gravity.

qs.q: Total population of a region divided by its total land surface area gives the population
qs.e: Population density measures the average number of human inhabitants per unit area (e.g. persons per sq km).

qs.q: Metamorphic rocks such as marble and slate are formed through the transformation of pre-existing rocks under extreme
qs.e: Metamorphism alters rock texture and mineralogy using intense heat, pressure, and hydrothermal fluids.

qs.q: Exfoliation or onion-skin weathering occurs predominantly in arid desert environments due to intense daily
o: Temperature fluctuations between day and night
Freezing and thawing of trapped groundwater
Chemical reaction with rainwater carbonic acid
Biological activity of deep tree root systems
qs.e: Repeated diurnal heating and cooling causes outer rock layers to expand and contract, eventually peeling off.

qs.q: Which major factor drives massive rural-to-urban migration in most developing West African nations?
o: Search for employment opportunities and modern social amenities
Desire for high-altitude cooler mountain weather
Abundance of free fertile agricultural land in cities
Avoidance of industrial noise and traffic congestion
qs.e: Rural residents migrate to urban centers primarily seeking higher-paying jobs, education, and healthcare.

qs.q: Gully erosion represents an advanced stage of soil erosion characterized by the formation of
o: Deep steep-sided ravines that cannot be removed by normal tillage
Uniform thin layers of topsoil removal across flat plains
Microscopic pores in sandy topsoil layers
Smooth round pebbles along river bed margins
qs.e: Gullies are deep, wide channels cut by torrential runoff that severely dissect and ruin farmland.

qs.q: A trade deficit occurs in a country's balance of trade when the total monetary value of its
o: Visible imports exceeds its visible exports
Visible exports exceeds its visible imports
qs.e: A trade deficit arises when a country spends more on imported physical goods than it earns from exported goods.

qs.q: Which mode of transportation is uniquely suited for continuous bulk transport of liquid crude oil and natural gas?
qs.e: Pipelines provide reliable, low-cost, continuous movement of petroleum fluids over long distances.

qs.q: The boundary line separating two adjacent drainage basins or river catchment areas is called a
qs.e: A watershed (or divide) is elevated ground separating waters flowing into different river systems.

qs.q: When it is 8:00 a.m. local time at Greenwich Meridian (0 degrees), what is the local time at longitude 60 degrees West?
qs.e: 60 degrees West is 4 hours behind GMT (60/15 = 4 hrs). 8:00 a.m. minus 4 hours equals 4:00 a.m.

qs.q: On a map drawn at a scale of 1:100,000, two towns separated by a ground distance of 25 km measure how many cm?
qs.e: 1:100,000 means 1 cm = 1 km. Therefore, 25 km ground distance equals 25 cm on the map.

qs.q: A key advantage of railway transport over road transport for heavy bulk industrial freight is its lower
o: Flexibility for door-to-door urban delivery services
Energy consumption and cost per ton-kilometre over long distances
Initial capital expenditure required for track construction
Speed when negotiating tight city residential streets
qs.e: Railways excel at moving massive bulk loads over long distances at low energy and operational costs per ton-km.

qs.q: Which agricultural system in West Africa involves clearing a forest plot, farming it briefly, and abandoning it to recover?
qs.e: Bush fallowing allows soil fertility to regenerate naturally through fallow periods after temporary cropping.

qs.q: The demographic transition model indicates that high birth rates combined with rapidly declining death rates leads to
qs.e: When death rates fall due to healthcare improvements while birth rates stay high, population increases rapidly.

qs.q: Sedimentary rocks formed from the compacted mineral fragments of pre-existing rocks are classified as
qs.e: Clastic sedimentary rocks (e.g., sandstone, shale) consist of mechanically weathered fragments cemented together.

qs.q: The process of chemical weathering where atmospheric oxygen reacts with iron-rich minerals in rocks to form rust is
qs.e: Oxidation converts ferrous iron compounds into reddish-brown ferric oxides, weakening the rock matrix.

qs.q: Suburbanisation refers to the movement of human population, industry, and commerce from
o: Rural villages directly into high-density city slums
Central urban areas into surrounding outer suburban fringes
Coastal fishing ports into inland desert oases
Highland farming settlements into river delta marshes
qs.e: Suburbanisation expands outer residential ring development as people leave overcrowded city cores.

qs.q: The preventive soil conservation technique of planting alternating strips of row crops and dense cover crops along contours is
qs.e: Strip cropping slows surface runoff and traps eroded soil particles between dense vegetative barriers.

qs.q: Invisible trade in a country's balance of payments accounts includes international transactions involving
o: Raw timber, cocoa beans, and crude petroleum
Refined gold bars, coal, and iron ore
qs.e: Invisible trade covers non-physical service transactions such as tourism, insurance, freight, and banking.

qs.q: A trellis drainage pattern typically develops in regions characterized by
o: Uniform horizontal granite batholiths on flat plains
Isolated volcanic cones with radial slopes
Alternating bands of hard and soft rocks folded into parallel ridges
Limestone caverns with collapsing subterranean sinks
qs.e: Trellis drainage features primary streams flowing in parallel valleys joined at right angles by short tributaries.

qs.q: Two points A and B have elevations of 900 m and 300 m. If map distance between them is 12 cm at scale 1:50,000, calculate the gradient.
A topographic map symbol consisting of closely spaced hachures or concentric closed contours with tick marks pointing inward indicates a
qs.e: Contours with inward-pointing hachures mark natural depressions, volcanic craters, or sinkholes.

qs.q: An optimum population is achieved in a country or region when the human population size
o: Exceeds the total carrying capacity causing widespread famine
Is far too small to utilize available natural resources
Maximizes per capita income given available resources and technology
Matches the exact land area in square kilometres
qs.e: Optimum population balances population with available natural resources and technology to yield maximum standard of living.

qs.q: In West Africa, commercial palm oil production is concentrated heavily within which ecological belt of Nigeria?
o: Niger Delta and southern rainforest belt
qs.e: Oil palm requires high temperature and heavy rainfall, making the southern rainforest belt ideal for plantations.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through solution is most dominant in regions underlain by soluble rock types like
qs.e: Soluble mineral salts dissolve directly in groundwater without requiring complex acid reactions.

qs.q: On a map with a scale of 1:25,000, six consecutive contours with an interval of 20 m span a distance of 4 cm. What is the gradient?
qs.e: 5 intervals * 20 m = 100 m VI. On 1:25,000 scale, 4 cm = 1,000 m HD. Gradient = 100 / 1,000 = 1/10 or 1 in 10.

qs.q: Which type of internal migration involves seasonal movement of pastoral herders and livestock between summer and winter pastures?
qs.e: Transhumance is the seasonal herd movement between upland pastures in wet season and lowland valleys in dry season.

qs.q: The lowering of the Earth surface through the combined processes of weathering, mass wasting, and erosion is termed
qs.e: Denudation encompasses all destructive exogenic physical and chemical processes that wear down landforms.

qs.q: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) over West Africa shifts northward during the Northern Hemisphere summer, bringing
o: Dry dusty harmattan winds from the Sahara Desert
Cold polar easterlies from the Atlantic Ocean
Moist maritime south-westerly winds and monsoon rains
Sub-zero freezing blizzards across savanna plains
qs.e: The northward migration of the ITCZ draws humid Tropical Maritime air masses inland, initiating the wet season.

qs.q: On a climate graph, a station displaying double rainfall peaks in June and October separated by a short dry spell in August illustrates an
o: Equatorial climate zone with an August break
qs.e: Southern Nigeria experiences a bimodal (double peak) rainfall regime with a minor dry spell in August.

qs.q: Thermal expansion and contraction in rocks composed of different minerals with varying expansion coefficients causes
qs.e: Unequal expansion of coarse mineral grains under daily heating causes individual mineral grains to pull apart.

qs.q: The economic concept of 'primate city' in population geography describes a leading national city that is
o: Located exclusively along an international maritime boundary
Dedicated entirely to single heavy raw material processing
Disproportionately larger than any other city in the urban hierarchy
Populated exclusively by government administrative personnel
qs.e: A primate city is more than twice as large as the second-largest city and dominates national economy and culture.

qs.q: Wind deflation in arid desert regions creates shallow landscape depressions known as
qs.e: Deflation hollows form when wind currents scoop out loose fine sand down to the underlying water table.

qs.q: Which international trade bloc was established to promote economic integration and free movement of goods across West Africa?
qs.e: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) fosters regional economic cooperation among West African nations.

qs.q: A radial drainage pattern characteristically develops on which specific landform structure?
o: Isolated volcanic dome or central highland peak
qs.e: Radial drainage occurs when streams flow outward down in all directions from a central elevated dome or peak.

qs.q: A map drawn on a scale of 1:25,000 is reduced to one-half (1/2) of its linear scale. What is the Representative Fraction of the new map?
qs.e: Halving the linear scale means 1 cm represents twice as much ground distance (2 * 25,000 = 50,000 cm), giving RF 1:50,000.

qs.q: In map reading, a dip slope on a ridge is distinguished from a scarp slope by having
o: Steeper and extremely crowded contour lines
Vertical cliff face symbols with zero contour spacing
Circular closed contours with inward tick marks
Gentler and more widely spaced contour lines
qs.e: An escarpment features a steep scarp slope (closely spaced contours) and a gentle dip slope (widely spaced contours).

qs.q: An age-sex population pyramid with a broad base and rapidly tapering top signifies a population with
o: Low birth rate and high life expectancy
Declining fertility rate and aging workforce
High birth rate and high infant mortality
qs.e: A wide pyramid base represents high birth rates, while rapid narrowing indicates high mortality across age groups.

qs.q: Groundnut (peanut) production in Northern Nigeria is centered primarily around which semi-arid state region?
qs.e: Light sandy soils and dry savanna climate in Northern Nigeria (Kano, Sokoto) provide ideal conditions for groundnuts.

qs.q: Which major transport project connects West African coastal capitals from Lagos to Dakar to facilitate regional commerce?
qs.e: The Trans-African Coastal Highway (TAH 7) links West African coastal capitals to boost intra-regional trade.

qs.q: The chemical process of hydrolysis in rock weathering involves the reaction of hydrogen ions in water with mineral silicates to form
o: Insoluble quartz crystals and basalt magma
Clay minerals and soluble silica compounds
qs.e: Hydrolysis breaks down feldspar and silicate minerals in granite into soft clay minerals like kaolinite.

qs.q: In river morphology, the formation of a braided stream channel pattern is caused by
o: Intense vertical downcutting through hard igneous basement rock
Dissolution of soluble limestone beds along deep fault fractures
Rapid ocean wave refraction along steep rocky cliff coastlines
Heavy sediment load exceeding river transport capacity during fluctuating discharge
qs.e: Braided channels split into multiple interconnected channels separated by sandbars when sediment supply exceeds energy.

qs.q: The concept of 'demographic dividend' refers to an economic growth potential created by
o: A sudden surge in crude birth rates following national industrial expansion
Massive emigration of skilled professional workers to developed nations
High infant mortality rates that reduce overall national food consumption
A higher proportion of working-age population relative to dependent children and elderly
qs.e: Demographic dividend occurs when declining fertility reduces child dependency, expanding the productive labor force.

qs.q: In map interpretation, intervisibility between two designated points on a topographic map is obstructed when
o: The slope between the two points is perfectly concave throughout
The two points share the exact same contour line elevation
A broad flat valley floor lies continuously between both points
A ridge, high contour crest, or convex slope intervenes between them
qs.e: High intervening landforms or convex slopes block the line of sight (intervisibility) between two map locations.

qs.q: The Volta River Project in Ghana was constructed primarily to generate hydroelectric power for processing which mineral resource?
qs.e: The Akosombo Dam on the Volta River was built to power the Valco aluminium smelter using Ghanaian bauxite deposits.

qs.q: Dense evergreen vegetation adapted to saline coastal lagoons and muddy river estuaries in West Africa is called
qs.e: Mangrove swamp forests grow in saline or brackish tidal coastal environments with aerial prop roots.

qs.q: A rural settlement pattern where houses are constructed in an isolated manner across wide farm holdings is described as
qs.e: Dispersed settlements feature widely scattered homesteads separated by large agricultural fields.

qs.q: The measure of acidity or alkalinity of a soil sample expressed on a scale from 0 to 14 is the soil
qs.e: Soil pH indicates the concentration of hydrogen ions, measuring soil acidity or alkalinity.

qs.q: The movement of the Earth in an elliptical orbit around the Sun every 365 and 1/4 days is termed Earth
qs.e: Earth revolution is the orbital motion around the Sun responsible for seasonal changes.

qs.q: Industries located near urban consuming centers because their finished products are bulky, fragile, or perishable are called
qs.e: Market-oriented industries locate close to consumers to reduce distribution costs of fragile or perishable items.

qs.q: The primary metallic ore from which aluminum is extracted commercially through smelting is
qs.e: Bauxite is the principal sedimentary rock ore refined into alumina and smelted into aluminium metal.

qs.q: The cold ocean current flowing equatorward along the coast of Namibia and western South Africa is the
qs.e: The Benguela Current brings cold Atlantic water northward along the southwestern coast of Africa.

qs.q: Fine-grained extrusive igneous rocks formed when volcanic lava cools rapidly at the Earth surface include
qs.e: Extrusive volcanic lava cools quickly on the surface, producing fine-grained basalt or vesicular pumice.

qs.q: Frost action or freeze-thaw weathering is most active in physical landscapes characterized by
o: High-altitude mountain peaks with daily temperature fluctuations around freezing point
Lowland equatorial rainforest valleys with high relative humidity
Arid desert sand basins with permanent zero moisture
Deep underground limestone caves with constant temperatures
qs.e: Freeze-thaw occurs when trapped water in rock crevices repeatedly freezes, expands, and melts.

qs.q: The rapid spread of urban development onto surrounding rural agricultural land on the edges of major cities is known as
qs.e: Urban sprawl refers to unrestricted outward geographical expansion of cities into suburban areas.

qs.q: Sheet erosion removes topsoil in thin uniform layers across broad unvegetated land areas primarily through
o: Unchannelled surface runoff following heavy rainfall
Glacial ice movement down steep mountain valleys
Thermal expansion of surface quartz grains
qs.e: Sheet erosion occurs when overland flow sweeps evenly across bare topsoil without forming distinct channels.

qs.q: A trade policy where a government levies high tariffs on foreign imported goods to protect domestic industries is called
qs.e: Protectionism uses import duties, quotas, or subsidies to shield local industries from foreign competition.

qs.q: Air transport is preferred over maritime transport for exporting valuable low-weight items because of its superior
o: Speed and transit security over long distances
Low freight cost per ton-kilometre for bulk commodities
Immunity to all atmospheric weather disturbances
Unlimited cargo carrying capacity per single vessel
qs.e: Air transport delivers high-value, perishable, or urgent goods rapidly despite higher operational costs.

qs.q: A meandering river channel typically cuts deeper into its outer bank during flood flow because of higher water velocity and
o: Deposition of coarse sand bars along the outer bend
Reduction of hydraulic action near river bends
Growth of dense mangrove roots holding the outer bank
qs.e: Swifter current on the outer bend exerts maximum hydraulic action, scouring out cut banks.

qs.q: What is the local solar time at longitude 90 degrees East when it is 10:00 a.m. at Greenwich Meridian (0 degrees)?
qs.e: 90 degrees East is 6 hours ahead of GMT (90 / 15 = 6 hrs). 10:00 a.m. plus 6 hours is 4:00 p.m.

qs.q: A map drawn at a scale of 1:100,000 is enlarged to four times (x4) its linear scale. What is the new Representative Fraction?
qs.e: Enlarging by x4 means 1 cm on the new map represents 100,000 / 4 = 25,000 cm ground distance (RF 1:25,000).

qs.q: A circular lake has a map diameter of 2 cm on a map with a scale of 1:50,000. What is the actual ground radius in kilometres?
qs.e: Map diameter = 2 cm -> map radius = 1 cm. At 1:50,000 scale, 1 cm = 500 m = 0.5 km.

qs.q: Plantation agriculture in West Africa is distinguished from traditional subsistence farming primarily by its
o: Use of simple hand tools and land fallowing practices
Large scale, monoculture of cash crops, and capital investment
Dependence exclusively on family labor without chemical fertilizers
Production of diverse food crops for immediate home consumption
qs.e: Plantations operate as large commercial estates producing single perennial cash crops using modern inputs.

qs.q: The crude birth rate of a national population measures the total number of live births occurring per year per
qs.e: Crude birth rate (CBR) expresses live births per 1,000 mid-year total population.

qs.q: Foliated metamorphic rocks characterized by distinct parallel mineral banding formed under high-grade metamorphism include
qs.e: High-grade regional metamorphism aligns platy minerals into distinct banded foliation layers in gneiss and schist.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through carbonation occurs when atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in rainwater to form weak
o: Sulfuric acid that dissolves igneous quartz grains
Carbonic acid that reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone
Hydrochloric acid that neutralizes saline coastal soils
Nitric acid that decomposes organic humus layers
qs.e: Rainwater absorbs CO2 to yield weak carbonic acid, which converts insoluble limestone into soluble calcium bicarbonate.

qs.q: The spatial model of urban land use featuring concentric rings of residential and commercial zones around a central business district is the
qs.e: The Burgess model describes urban growth in concentric rings expanding outward from the central core.

qs.q: Mass wasting processes involving slow, imperceptible downward movement of soil and rock debris under gravity are called
qs.e: Soil creep is the extremely slow, steady downhill movement of soil driven by gravity and freeze-thaw cycles.

qs.q: Entrepot trade in international commerce refers to a specialized commercial operation where goods are
o: Bartered directly for crude oil without currency exchange
Imported, stored, and re-exported without paying import duties
Sold exclusively to domestic state-owned enterprises
Manufactured entirely from indigenous raw materials
qs.e: An entrepot acts as an intermediate import/export transit hub where goods are re-exported to other countries.

qs.q: A dendritic drainage pattern resembles the branching structure of a tree and typically forms on land surfaces with
o: Alternating bands of steeply dipping hard and soft strata
Uniformly resistant horizontal rock strata or massive flat terrain
Radial volcanic slopes ascending to a central peak
Rectangular fault joint networks in crystalline granite
qs.e: Dendritic drainage develops where rocks offer uniform resistance to erosion in all directions.

qs.q: Two contour lines on a topographic map with a scale of 1:50,000 are 4 cm apart. If elevation difference is 100 m, what is the gradient?
A map feature indicated by concentric closed contours with increasing values toward the innermost circle represents a
qs.e: Closed contours with values increasing inward represent elevated landforms like hills or conical peaks.

qs.q: Underpopulation in a geographical region occurs when the total number of human inhabitants is
o: Exceeding the carrying capacity causing food shortages
Concentrated entirely in a single primate city
Too small to fully exploit available natural resources efficiently
Growing at an exponential rate of ten percent annually
qs.e: Underpopulation means an area has insufficient labor force to fully develop its rich natural resources.

qs.q: Cacao (cocoa) cultivation in Nigeria is concentrated predominantly within which region due to favorable climate and soil?
qs.e: South-western states (Ondo, Osun, Oyo, Ogun) have fertile well-drained soils and high rainfall ideal for cocoa.

qs.q: The climate region characterized by hot dry summers and mild wet winters controlled by shifting pressure belts is the
qs.e: Mediterranean climates (e.g. Cape region, southern Europe) experience winter rainfall and summer drought.

qs.q: A climate graph showing high uniform monthly temperatures around 27°C and heavy rainfall exceeding 2500 mm annually indicates an
qs.e: Equatorial climate stations display high year-round temperatures with minimal monthly variation and heavy rainfall.

qs.q: Biological weathering is accelerated by living organisms primarily through
o: Solar radiation absorption by plant leaves
Condensation of atmospheric dew on grass blades
Root wedging in rock crevices and burrowing animal activity
Photosynthetic absorption of oxygen by tree roots
qs.e: Growing roots exert physical pressure expanding rock fractures, while burrowing animals loosen rock fragments.

qs.q: The agricultural practice of contour ploughing along hillside slopes reduces soil erosion primarily by
o: Increasing topsoil temperature to accelerate crop growth
Eliminating weed seeds through deep soil inversion
Creating horizontal ridges that slow surface water runoff
Compacting subsoil layers to prevent root penetration
qs.e: Ploughing across slopes following contour lines creates mini-terraces that break the velocity of runoff water.

qs.q: The Kainji Dam on the River Niger in Nigeria was constructed primarily to serve which multi-purpose development function?
o: Nuclear waste storage and deepwater shipping
Petroleum refining and natural gas liquefaction
Hydroelectric power generation and flood control
Desalination of seawater for urban supply
qs.e: Kainji Dam generates hydroelectricity for Nigeria and regulates downstream flooding along the Niger valley.

qs.q: Solution weathering in karst topography creates distinct underground caverns containing stalactites that grow downward from
o: Cave floors through upward silica deposition
Subterranean stream beds through gravel compaction
Cave ceilings through calcium carbonate precipitation
Surface sinkholes through wind-blown dust accumulation
qs.e: Stalactites form as water dripping from cave ceilings deposits dissolved calcium carbonate in hanging structures.

qs.q: In Central Place Theory, the minimum market population required to support a central commercial service is termed the
qs.e: Threshold is the minimum demand or consumer base needed to make a specific business or service profitable.

qs.q: In coastal geomorphology, longshore drift transports beach sediment along a coastline through
o: Direct offshore currents carrying sand into deep ocean trenches
Vertical wave oscillation lifting sand particles straight up and down
Zigzag movement of swash angled to shore and backwash perpendicular to shore
Subterranean tidal currents moving parallel to deep continental shelves
qs.e: Waves approaching at an angle push swash diagonally up the beach, while backwash pulls sediment straight down.

qs.q: The balance of payments account of a country records all financial transactions between domestic residents and
o: Domestic commercial banks and central bank
Regional state governments within the federation
The rest of the world over a specified period
Manufacturing firms operating in free trade zones
qs.e: Balance of payments encompasses all monetary flows including imports, exports, investments, and transfers.

qs.q: An oxbow lake is formed along a river valley through the sequential processes of meander neck narrowing,
o: Deep vertical downcutting into basalt bedrock forming vertical gorges
Tectonic faulting creating graben basins across river channels
Subterranean cavern collapse trapping surface stream runoff
Cut-off during flood stage and subsequent deposition blocking the former loop
qs.e: Floods breach meander necks, cutting a straight channel; deposition then seals off the old loop into an oxbow lake.

qs.q: A topographic map displays contour lines that merge into a single line along a steep hillside. This symbol indicates a
qs.e: When contours merge, it signifies a vertical cliff face where multiple elevation levels occupy the exact same horizontal coordinate.

qs.q: Demographic dependency ratio measures the ratio of economically dependent citizens (aged under 15 and over 64) relative to
o: The total female population of childbearing age
The total number of employed government civil servants
The gross national product in national currency
The working-age population aged 15 to 64 years
qs.e: Dependency ratio compares dependents (children and elderly) to the productive working-age age bracket.

qs.q: Irrigation agriculture along the Hadejia-Jama'are river basin in Northern Nigeria facilitates the cultivation of
o: Cocoa, rubber, and oil palm throughout winter months
Timber trees, tea leaves, and cinchona bark on mountain slopes
Root crops, coconut palms, and mangrove wood in tidal estuaries
Vegetables, wheat, and swamp rice during the dry season
qs.e: Irrigation schemes in dry northern river basins enable intensive dry-season cropping of vegetables, wheat, and rice.

qs.q: The heavy rainfall recorded in the Niger Delta area of southern Nigeria is predominantly convectional and
o: Frontal polar rainfall caused by cold Arctic air surges
Cyclonic blizzard precipitation coming from Mediterranean lows
Sub-tropical katabatic wind precipitation from desert plateaus
Orographic relief rainfall influenced by Tropical Maritime air masses
qs.e: Warm humid Tropical Maritime air brings abundant convectional and coastal rain to southern Nigeria.

qs.q: The Trans-Saharan trade routes historically connected West African savannas with Mediterranean ports primarily across the
o: East African rift using steam trains
qs.e: Caravans crossed the Sahara Desert exchanging West African gold and slaves for Mediterranean salt and manufactured goods.

qs.q: Which major mineral deposit mined at Itakpe in Kogi State supplies raw materials to the Ajaokuta steel complex?
qs.e: Itakpe deposits supply high-grade iron ore deposits required for steelmaking at Ajaokuta.

qs.q: Chemical weathering by hydrolysis is exceptionally rapid in tropical rainforests because of high ambient temperatures and
o: Low atmospheric humidity preventing moisture condensation
Freezing night temperatures causing frost shattering
Lack of organic acids from decomposing vegetation
Abundant hydrogen ion concentration in warm percolating rainwater
qs.e: Abundant warm water accelerates hydrolysis, altering feldspars into kaolinite clay.

qs.q: In coastal geomorphology, wave refraction along an irregular indented coastline concentrates wave energy primarily against
o: Submarine trenches, causing deep crustal subsidence
qs.e: Refraction bends incoming waves toward headlands, concentrating destructive wave energy and eroding cliffs.

qs.q: The spatial distribution of world population is most severely constrained in high-latitude polar regions by
o: High atmospheric humidity and tropical infectious diseases
Dense tropical rainforest canopies blocking agricultural machinery
Excessive soil salinization from ocean storm surges
Extreme permafrost, low solar radiation, and short growing seasons
qs.e: Sub-zero temperatures, permanently frozen permafrost, and lack of solar warmth prohibit agriculture and dense settlement.

qs.q: The Jos Plateau in Nigeria experiences cooler temperatures than surrounding lowlands primarily due to the influence of
o: Cold ocean currents flowing along the Benue river channel
Sub-polar jet streams descending from northern Europe
Extensive evergreen coniferous forest canopy cover
Environmental lapse rate associated with high altitude
qs.e: Temperature decreases with altitude at approximately 6.5°C per 1,000 metres (environmental lapse rate).

qs.q: The thermal equator experiences maximum annual solar insolation during equinoxes when the midday sun is directly overhead at the
qs.e: During March and September equinoxes, the midday sun is directly overhead at 0° latitude.

qs.q: The thin upper layer of the Earth crust capable of supporting plant growth through mineral and organic matter is
qs.e: Soil is the naturally occurring unconsolidated mineral and organic material supporting terrestrial plant life.

qs.q: The permanent displacement of people from rural farm areas into growing urban centers is defined as
qs.e: Rural-urban migration describes people moving from rural farm areas to live and work in urban cities.

qs.q: The atmospheric condition of a specific place over a short period of time (hours or days) is called
qs.e: Weather refers to short-term day-to-day state of the atmosphere including temperature, rainfall, and wind.

qs.q: The agricultural system where crops are cultivated primarily for family consumption rather than commercial sale is
qs.e: Subsistence agriculture focuses on growing food to meet immediate household consumption needs.

qs.q: Which major transport mode is most suitable for rapid door-to-door delivery of light cargo within an urban region?
qs.e: Road transport offers flexible routes and direct door-to-door accessibility for intra-urban deliveries.

qs.q: The natural boundary line separating land and sea where coastal wave processes operate is called the
qs.e: The coastline marks the dynamic boundary zone between marine wave forces and terrestrial land margins.

qs.q: The foreign trade of a nation involving physical tangible commodities such as raw minerals and crops is termed
qs.e: Visible trade involves physical, tangible imported and exported goods that pass through customs ports.

qs.q: Rocks formed through the compaction and cementation of mineral sediments over long periods are classified as
qs.e: Sedimentary rocks develop through lithification of accumulated mineral or organic sediment layers.

qs.q: The chemical weathering process where minerals absorb water molecules into their crystal lattice to form new compounds is
qs.e: Hydration involves the chemical addition of water to mineral structures, causing volume expansion and rock weakening.

qs.q: A mega-city is defined in urban geography as a continuous urban agglomeration with a total population exceeding
qs.e: UN urban definitions classify metropolitan urban areas with over 10 million residents as megacities.

qs.q: Wind abrasion in arid desert environments sculpts standing rock outcrops near ground level through the impact of
o: Wind-borne sand grains acting like natural sandblasting
Dissolved rainwater acids etching granite faces
Gravitational slope sliding shearing soft sandstone
qs.e: Wind-driven sand particles blast lower sections of exposed rocks, carving undercut yardangs and mushroom rocks.

qs.q: A balance of trade surplus is achieved when a national economy records
o: Higher monetary value of exported goods than imported goods
Higher monetary value of imported goods than exported goods
Equal value of visible imports and invisible services
Zero collection of foreign import customs duties
qs.e: A trade surplus occurs when export revenue from physical merchandise exceeds import expenditure.

qs.q: Inland waterway transport in West Africa is constrained during the dry season primarily by
o: Permanent sea ice formation along river channels
Low water levels, sandbars, and seasonal rapids
High ocean wave swells crashing into river sources
Excessive water speed exceeding engine capabilities
qs.e: Seasonal reduction in river volume exposes sandbars and rocks, hindering navigation during dry months.

qs.q: A delta forms at a river mouth when river velocity slows upon entering a sea or lake, resulting in heavy
o: Vertical downcutting into submarine granite bedrock
Deposition of fine sediment load exceeding marine wave removal
Dissolution of coastal limestone cliffs by freshwater
Erosion of river mouth sand spits by ocean waves
qs.e: Deltas build up where river sediment supply exceeds the rate of removal by ocean waves and currents.

qs.q: If local solar time at longitude 30 degrees West is 7:00 a.m., what is the local solar time at longitude 45 degrees East?
qs.e: Longitude gap = 30 W + 45 E = 75 degrees (5 hours gap). 45 E is east, so 7:00 a.m. + 5 hrs = 12:00 noon.

qs.q: A map with an original scale of 1:50,000 is reduced to one-fifth (1/5) of its linear size. What is the new scale?
qs.e: Reducing linear scale to 1/5 means 1 cm on the new map represents 5 * 50,000 = 250,000 cm ground distance.

qs.q: Two railway stations are separated by 18 km ground distance. On a map with scale 1:50,000, what is their map distance in cm?
qs.e: At 1:50,000 scale, 1 cm = 0.5 km. 18 km ground distance / 0.5 km/cm = 36 cm on the map.
