qs.q: Sedimentary rocks composed of accumulated plant remains compressed in ancient swamp environments are classified as
qs.e: Coal and lignite are organically derived sedimentary rocks formed from compressed plant material.

qs.q: Natural increase in population growth is calculated as the difference between total
o: Immigrants and emigrants entering a country
Births and deaths in a population over a given period
Urban workers and rural agricultural farmers
Adult citizens and dependent school children
qs.e: Natural population growth equals crude births minus crude deaths, excluding net migration flows.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through hydrolysis dissolves silicate minerals in granite rocks, converting feldspar into soft
qs.e: Hydrolysis attacks potassium feldspar in granite, transforming it into kaolinite clay and soluble compounds.

qs.q: The Hoyt sector model of urban land use asserts that high-class residential areas develop along
o: Concentric circular rings isolated around industrial factories
Major transportation corridors and high-elevation ridges outward from the city core
Scattered isolated clusters away from all city roads
Low-lying marshy river floodplains near waste dumps
qs.e: Hoyt argued that urban land use grows in sector wedges along major transport arterial routes.

qs.q: The accumulation of loose rock fragments and scree debris at the foot of a steep cliff face is produced by
qs.e: Scree (talus) slopes form as frost action breaks rock fragments off cliff faces, which fall under gravity.

qs.q: Tariffs, import quotas, and foreign exchange controls are policy instruments employed by governments to manage
qs.e: Trade barriers like quotas and tariffs regulate foreign import volumes to manage national trade balances.

qs.q: A rectangular drainage pattern typically forms in geographical landscapes characterized by
o: Isolated conical volcanic domes with steep uniform slopes
Strongly jointed or faulted rock structures intersecting at right angles
Soft uniform marine clay plains lacking structural faults
Parallel mountain ridges separated by broad gentle valleys
qs.e: Rectangular drainage develops where streams follow intersecting master joint systems or fault lines.

qs.q: A slope rises from an elevation of 200 m to 600 m over a map distance of 8 cm on a scale of 1:50,000. Calculate the gradient.
In map reading, a saddle or col is identified on a topographic map as a low pass between two
o: Adjacent mountain peaks or elevated hill summits
qs.e: A col or saddle is a low dip or pass along a ridge line separating two higher peaks.

qs.q: The Malthusian theory of population posits that human population grows exponentially while food production increases
qs.e: Malthus argued population grows geometrically (1, 2, 4, 8) while food output increases arithmetically (1, 2, 3, 4).

qs.q: Which major river basin in Nigeria provides extensive alluvial floodplains (fadamas) ideal for dry-season rice and vegetable farming?
qs.e: Fadama lands along the Rima and Sokoto river valleys retain moisture for dry-season rice and vegetable cropping.

qs.q: Tropical continental climate (Sudan climate) in West Africa is characterized by high summer temperatures and a distinct
o: Double rainfall peak with continuous winter snow
High year-round rainfall without any dry month
Single wet season and prolonged dry winter season
Sub-zero freezing winter temperatures and permafrost
qs.e: Sudan climate features a marked single summer rainy season and a long dry winter under harmattan influences.

qs.q: A climate graph displaying monthly temperatures between 30°C and 40°C with near-zero precipitation all year round illustrates a
qs.e: Hot desert climate stations exhibit high summer temperatures and extremely low, erratic rainfall.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through hydration causes rock expansion because water molecules
o: Freeze into ice crystals inside microscopic rock pores
Dissolve surface quartz grains into clear liquid silica
Combine chemically with mineral crystals, expanding their volume
Boil into high-pressure steam within deep rock fissures
qs.e: Hydration integrates water into mineral crystal structures, causing swelling that disintegrates rocks.

qs.q: Terrace farming along steep hill slopes conserves topsoil primarily by
o: Inverting deep subsoil layers using heavy motorized tractors
Flooding slope fields with saline coastal water
Constructing stepped flat ledges that reduce surface runoff velocity
Removing all vegetation cover to expose bare bedrock
qs.e: Terracing builds stepped flat platforms along hillsides, slowing downhill runoff and trapping eroded topsoil.

qs.q: Which major hydro-electric power station in Nigeria is situated along the Kaduna River to boost national electricity grid supply?
qs.e: Shiroro Dam is built across the Kaduna River in Niger State to generate hydro-electric power.

qs.q: Nomadic pastoralism in the semi-arid savanna of West Africa is practiced predominantly by which ethnic group?
qs.e: Fulani pastoralists practice transhumant livestock herding across semi-arid West African savannas.

qs.q: Biological weathering is accelerated in humid tropical soils through the action of nitrifying bacteria and organic acids produced by
o: Decomposing plant humus and leaf litter
qs.e: Humic acids released during organic decomposition dissolve soil minerals and attack underlying rock faces.

qs.q: In Harris-Ullman multiple nuclei model of urban structure, cities develop around several independent growth nodes rather than a single
qs.e: The multiple nuclei model posits that modern cities expand around several functional nodes (e.g. ports, airports, industrial parks).

qs.q: In wind geomorphology, yardangs are streamlined wind-carved ridges formed in desert landscapes where alternating bands of
o: Soluble limestone beds collapse into waterlogged sinkholes
Loose sand dunes shift across flat coastal mudflats
Hard and soft rocks lie parallel to the direction of prevailing winds
Volcanic basalt columns cool inside deep crater lakes
qs.e: Yardangs are carved by wind abrasion where hard and soft rock strata run parallel to prevailing wind direction.

qs.q: The terms of trade index for a developing country measures the ratio of its export price index relative to its
o: Total gross domestic product in national currency
National foreign currency reserves in commercial banks
Total agricultural production volume in metric tons
qs.e: Terms of trade = (Export Price Index / Import Price Index) * 100, indicating purchasing power of exports.

qs.q: An antecedent river drainage system is one that maintains its original course across a rising landform because the river cut down at a rate
o: Much slower than the rate of volcanic ash deposition
Driven entirely by ocean wave action breaking against mountain bases
Controlled exclusively by subterranean limestone cavern collapse
Equal to or faster than the rate of tectonic uplift
qs.e: Antecedent streams erode downward fast enough to cut gorges across uplifting ridges without changing course.

qs.q: On a topographic map, a spur is distinguished from a valley by contour lines that point V-shaped vectors toward
o: The exact center of a crater lake
qs.e: Contour V-shapes pointing toward lower elevation indicate a spur, while V-shapes pointing uphill indicate a valley.

qs.q: Push factors driving rural depopulation in agricultural regions of developing nations include
o: High industrial wages in countryside villages
Abundance of modern university hospitals in rural hamlets
Low cost of urban housing in metropolitan city centers
Rural poverty, land scarcity, and lack of basic infrastructure
qs.e: Push factors are negative rural conditions like poverty, land shortages, and lack of amenities driving emigration.

qs.q: The Jos Plateau tin mining industry in Nigeria created severe environmental degradation characterized by
o: Widespread oil spills contaminating mangrove estuaries
Atmospheric acid rain from heavy sulfur coal combustion
Extensive open pit mine ponds, abandoned tailings, and soil erosion
qs.e: Decades of open-cast tin mining on the Jos Plateau left massive excavated pits, spoil heaps, and eroded land.

qs.q: The tropical maritime air mass (mT) originating over the South Atlantic Ocean brings high humidity and heavy rainfall to West Africa during the
qs.e: During summer, the onshore Tropical Maritime air mass moves inland, bringing moisture and rains across West Africa.

qs.q: In map projection theory, a conformal map projection preserves true feature
o: Distances along all map directions simultaneously
qs.e: Conformal map projections (like Mercator) preserve correct local angles and shapes at the expense of area distortion.

qs.q: Which major limestone cave complex in Cross River State, Nigeria, exhibits spectacular karst topography including stalactites and stalagmites?
qs.e: Ogbunike Caves in Anambra/Cross River borders are famous limestone karst formations with solution caverns.

qs.q: Hydrolysis of orthoclase feldspar in granite rocks chemically alters potassium silicate into kaolinite clay, releasing soluble
o: Insoluble gold nuggets into river beds
Solid basalt lava flows onto volcanic slopes
Gaseous methane plumes into lower troposphere
Potassium carbonate and silica into groundwater
qs.e: Hydrolysis converts orthoclase feldspar into kaolinite clay while releasing soluble potassium compounds and silica.

qs.q: In fluvial geomorphology, the base level of erosion represents the lowest elevation to which a river can deepen its valley, governed globally by
o: The crest of the highest mountain peak in the catchment
The depth of the deepest underground mine shaft
The top of the nearest hydro-electric power dam
qs.e: Sea level is the ultimate base level below which rivers cannot erode their valleys vertically.

qs.q: Demographic momentum causes a population to continue growing even after fertility rates drop to replacement level because of
o: Massive net immigration of retired elderly citizens
Sudden increase in national infant mortality rates
Complete cessation of all international air travel
A large proportion of young people entering childbearing age
qs.e: A youthful age structure ensures high numbers of future parents, sustaining growth despite lower birth rates per woman.

qs.q: The Benue Trough in Nigeria is a major geological structure formed through
o: Quaternary glaciation and ice sheet carving
Cretaceous rifting and continental crustal extension
qs.e: The Benue Trough is an intracontinental Cretaceous rift basin filled with sedimentary rocks and mineral deposits.

qs.q: The thermal inversion layer in coastal desert climates inhibits cloud formation and precipitation because warm air aloft overlies
o: A superheated surface sand layer generating updrafts
A subterranean volcanic gas plume bursting through topsoil
A high-pressure hurricane vortex pulling moisture downward
A cooler dense air layer chilled by cold ocean currents
qs.e: Cold ocean currents chill air near the surface, trapped under warmer upper air, preventing vertical convection and rain.

qs.q: The organic matter component formed by the decomposition of plant and animal residues in soil is
qs.e: Humus is the dark decomposed organic matter that improves soil structure and nutrient retention.

qs.q: A cluster of urban settlements expanding until their outer boundaries merge together is defined as a
qs.e: A conurbation forms when adjacent urban areas merge geographically over time.

qs.q: The scientific instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure at a meteorological weather station is the
qs.e: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure in millibars or hectopascals.

qs.q: The system of farming involving the cultivation of food crops alongside animal husbandry on the same farm is
qs.e: Mixed farming combines crop cultivation with livestock rearing on a single agricultural holding.

qs.q: Which mode of transportation requires no physical vehicles and is used exclusively for fluid commodities?
qs.e: Pipelines transport liquid petroleum, natural gas, and water continuously without vehicles.

qs.q: The coastal landform created when wave deposition builds a narrow sand ridge connecting an island to the mainland is a
qs.e: A tombolo is a sand depositional ridge linking an offshore island to the mainland coast.

qs.q: The total financial value of all goods and services produced within a country in a single year is the
qs.e: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) quantifies total economic output generated domestically per year.

qs.q: Metamorphic rocks formed when limestone undergoes intense heat and pressure recrystallization are classified as
qs.e: Marble is a non-foliated metamorphic rock produced by thermal metamorphism of limestone.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through oxidation is easily identified on rock surfaces by the development of a distinctive
qs.e: Oxidation transforms iron minerals into ferric oxide rust, giving exposed rock surfaces a reddish hue.

qs.q: Counterurbanisation in developed countries describes the net population movement from major cities into
o: Rural villages and small country towns
qs.e: Counterurbanisation is the migration of city dwellers away from metropolitan areas into rural communities.

qs.q: Wind deflation in desert environments lowers land surfaces by selectively removing fine particles of
o: Sand, silt, and dust leaving coarse gravel behind
Heavy granite boulders and basalt blocks
Solid limestone bedrock and quartz veins
Wet mud and waterlogged clay slurry
qs.e: Deflation scoops out fine dry dust and sand grains, leaving behind a stony desert pavement (reg).

qs.q: A trade tariff is a government tax levied specifically on physical goods during
o: Domestic retail sale in local markets
qs.e: Import tariffs are custom duties applied to imported merchandise to generate revenue or protect local producers.

qs.q: Sea transport is preferred for international trade of heavy raw minerals because of its very low
qs.e: Ocean shipping provides unparalleled economies of scale for transporting heavy bulk raw materials.

qs.q: An oxbow lake is formed when a river cuts through a narrow meander neck during flooding and seals off the old loop by
o: Volcanic lava cooling across river channels
Silt and sediment deposition at both ends
Glacial ice dams blocking upstream flow
qs.e: Sediment deposition seals off both ends of the abandoned meander loop, creating an oxbow lake.

qs.q: When local time at Greenwich Meridian (0 degrees) is 2:00 p.m., what is the local time at longitude 120 degrees West?
qs.e: 120 degrees West is 8 hours behind GMT (120 / 15 = 8 hrs). 14:00 minus 8 hours is 6:00 a.m.

qs.q: A map scale given as 2 cm to 1 kilometre has a Representative Fraction (RF) scale of
A rectangular farm measuring 2 km by 3 km ground dimensions is drawn at scale 1:25,000. What are its map dimensions in cm?
Metamorphic rocks formed from sandstone under intense heat and pressure recrystallization are classified as
qs.e: Thermal or regional metamorphism of quartz sandstone recrystallizes quartz grains into hard quartzite.

qs.q: Demographic transition theory models the historical change from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates during
qs.e: Demographic transition links falling birth and death rates to economic development and industrialization.

qs.q: Biological weathering by plant roots exerts pressure inside rock fractures, causing mechanical breakdown known as
qs.e: Growing tree roots expand within rock joints, exerting mechanical leverage that wedges rocks apart.

qs.q: In central place geography, the maximum distance a consumer is willing to travel to purchase a commercial good or service is the
qs.e: The range of a good represents the spatial limit beyond which consumers will not travel to buy a service.

qs.q: Mass wasting involving the rapid downhill sliding of a cohesive block of rock and soil along a well-defined curved shear plane is a
qs.e: Slumping occurs when a block of land slips downhill along a concave curved failure surface.

qs.q: Free trade agreements eliminate tariff barriers between member countries while allowing each nation to maintain its own
qs.e: A free trade area removes internal tariffs between members, but each nation sets independent external tariffs.

qs.q: A radial drainage pattern characteristically develops where streams flow outward down in all directions from a central
o: Volcanic cone or elevated structural dome
qs.e: Radial drainage radiates outward from central topographic high points like volcanic domes or inselbergs.

qs.q: A hill slope drops 400 m elevation over a map distance of 8 cm on a map scale of 1:25,000. Calculate the gradient.
On a topographic map, contour lines that are spaced widely apart represent land surfaces characterized by
qs.e: Widely spaced contours indicate low elevation change per horizontal unit, representing gentle or flat terrain.

qs.q: Overpopulation occurs when a geographical region contains more human inhabitants than can be supported by its
o: Total physical area in square kilometres
Available natural resources and technology at an adequate standard of living
qs.e: Overpopulation exists when population exceeds carrying capacity given current resources and technology.

qs.q: The Niger Delta region in Nigeria accounts for over ninety percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings from exporting
qs.e: Niger Delta crude oil and natural gas exports generate the overwhelming majority of Nigerian foreign exchange revenue.

qs.q: The harmattan wind blowing across Nigeria during the dry season originates from which high-pressure desert region?
qs.e: The harmattan is a dry, dusty North-East Trade wind originating from the Saharan high-pressure cell.

qs.q: A climate graph exhibiting high monthly temperatures and zero rainfall for nine consecutive months represents an
qs.e: Desert stations display prolonged dry spells with zero precipitation during most months of the year.

qs.q: Chemical weathering through carbonation dissolves calcium carbonate in limestone rocks, converting it into soluble
qs.e: Carbonic acid in rainwater reacts with insoluble calcium carbonate to produce soluble calcium bicarbonate.

qs.q: Afforestation and re-vegetation conserve vulnerable topsoil along sloping hillsides primarily by
o: Increasing ground temperature to evaporate rainfall instantly
Compacting subsoil clay layers to block root penetration
Binding soil particles with roots and reducing surface runoff impact
Inverting topsoil layers using heavy bulldozers
qs.e: Vegetative canopy intercepts rain impact, while tree root systems anchor topsoil and increase infiltration.

qs.q: The Ajaokuta steel complex in Kogi State was established near Itakpe iron ore deposits and Enugu coal deposits to produce
o: Refined petroleum gasoline and diesel fuel
Industrial steel billets, rods, and heavy structural sections
qs.e: Ajaokuta was planned as an integrated steel plant to supply raw steel products for Nigerian industrialization.

qs.q: Shifting cultivation in tropical rainforests is sustainable only when human population density is extremely low and fallow periods are
o: Reduced to zero through continuous annual cropping
Interrupted by severe burning every three months
Long enough for forest vegetation and soil fertility to recover fully
Flooded continuously with industrial chemical effluents
qs.e: Sufficiently long fallow periods (10-20 years) allow natural vegetation regeneration and soil nutrient recovery.

qs.q: Spheroidal weathering of granite boulders in humid tropical environments is produced by chemical hydration and
o: Glacial ice scratching on boulder tops
Concentric spalling of outer weathered rock shells
Wind deflation carving deep sand flutes
qs.e: Water penetrating granite joints causes outer layers to swell, hydrate, and peel off in concentric shells.

qs.q: The sector model of urban land use developed by Homer Hoyt modified Burgess model by emphasizing the role of
o: Concentric circular zones expanding equally in all directions
Subterranean sewer networks limiting building heights
Transportation corridors in directing urban land use growth
High-altitude mountain barriers blocking industrial expansion
qs.e: Hoyt showed that urban growth follows transport arteries outward in wedge-shaped sectors.

qs.q: In desert coastal landforms, sabkhas are supratidal mudflats characterized by intense evaporation and heavy deposition of
o: Evaporite salt crystals including halite and gypsum
qs.e: Sabkhas are arid coastal salt flats where intense evaporation precipitates halite, gypsum, and anhydrite.

qs.q: A customs union differs from a free trade area because member states adopt a common
o: National system of municipal property taxation
External tariff policy applied to non-member countries
qs.e: Customs unions eliminate internal tariffs among members and enforce a unified external tariff on imports from outside.

qs.q: A centripetal drainage pattern occurs when streams flow inward from surrounding high terrain toward a central
o: Inland depression, lake, or closed basin
qs.e: Centripetal drainage flows inward from surrounding highlands into a central sink or inland lake (e.g., Lake Chad).

qs.q: On a topographic map, a re-entrant is identified by contour lines forming V-shapes that point toward
o: Lower elevation ground along a spur ridge
The exact midpoint of a flat lake surface
An isolated coastal sand dune crest
Higher elevation ground along a valley or ravine
qs.e: Contour V-shapes pointing uphill indicate a valley or re-entrant stream channel.

qs.q: Brain drain in population geography describes the international emigration of highly skilled and educated citizens from
o: Metropolitan capital cities into remote rural hamlets
Industrial manufacturing zones into coastal fishing ports
Sub-tropical desert oases into polar tundra regions
Developing nations into developed nations seeking better opportunities
qs.e: Brain drain refers to loss of educated professionals (doctors, engineers) emigrating to wealthier countries.

qs.q: The Mambilla Plateau in Taraba State, Nigeria, is uniquely suited for tea production and cattle ranching because of its
o: Hot humid coastal mangrove swamp habitat
High elevation, cool temperate climate, and tsetse-free environment
qs.e: High altitude (>1,500 m) gives Mambilla a cool climate, making it tsetse-fly free and ideal for cattle and tea.

qs.q: The South-West Monsoon winds in West Africa bring heavy rainfall when they blow across warm Atlantic waters as humid
qs.e: Tropical Maritime air originates over the Atlantic Ocean, absorbing moisture that yields monsoon rainfall.

qs.q: In map scale geometry, if a map of scale 1:25,000 is reduced to one-fourth (1/4) of its original linear dimensions, its new scale is
qs.e: Reducing linear scale by 1/4 means 1 cm on new map represents 4 * 25,000 = 100,000 cm ground distance.

qs.q: Which major sedimentary rock formation in Nigeria contains extensive bituminous coal seams mined for industrial energy?
o: Mamu and Nsukka formations in the Enugu basin
qs.e: Enugu coal deposits occur within Cretaceous sedimentary rock layers of the Mamu and Nsukka formations.

qs.q: Chemical weathering by carbonation in karst regions dissolves limestone rock along joint planes, creating deep vertical shafts called
qs.e: Swallow holes (sinkholes) form where acidic rainwater dissolves limestone along joint intersections.

qs.q: In coastal geomorphology, marine erosion cuts notch lines at cliff bases, causing cliff collapse and retreat that leaves behind a flat
qs.e: Cliff retreat under wave attack leaves a gently sloping rock bench known as a wave-cut platform at low tide.

qs.q: According to Demographic Transition Theory, Stage 4 is characterized by low birth rates, low death rates, and a population that is
o: Expanding at an explosive exponential rate
Declining rapidly due to catastrophic plagues
Migrating entirely into rural farm hamlets
qs.e: Stage 4 features low birth and death rates, stabilizing total population size in urbanized industrial societies.

qs.q: The Chad Basin in North-Eastern Nigeria is a major structural basin of inland drainage filled with sediments of which era?
qs.e: The Chad Basin is an epeirogenic inland drainage basin filled with Tertiary and Quaternary continental sediments.

qs.q: The Coriolis force caused by Earth rotation deflects ocean currents and prevailing winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the
qs.e: Coriolis force deflects moving objects right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere.

qs.q: Soil texture consisting of equal balanced proportions of sand, silt, and clay particle size fractions is termed
qs.e: Loam is an ideal agricultural soil combining sand, silt, and clay for optimal drainage and fertility.

qs.q: The geographical process where an increasing percentage of a country's total population lives in cities and towns is
qs.e: Urbanisation describes the growth in proportion of people living in urban areas relative to rural areas.

qs.q: The boundary line where two contrasting air masses meet in the atmosphere is defined as a weather
qs.e: A weather front is a transition zone between two air masses of differing temperature and moisture.

qs.q: The cultivation of cash crops on large commercial estates using modern scientific management is
qs.e: Plantations are large commercial estates devoted to single cash crop cultivation for export.

qs.q: Which mode of transport offers direct high-speed international passenger and light freight transport across continents?
qs.e: Air transport provides unmatched speed for intercontinental travel and high-value cargo transport.

qs.q: The mechanical wearing away and removal of soil and rock material by natural agents of wind, water, and ice is
qs.e: Erosion is the active detachment and transportation of surface soil and rock material by fluid agents.

qs.q: Commercial trade conducted entirely within the domestic national territorial boundaries of a country is called
qs.e: Internal (domestic) trade occurs within a single country between local buyers and sellers.

qs.q: Igneous rocks formed when molten magma cools and solidifies deep beneath the Earth surface are classified as
qs.e: Plutonic rocks (e.g. granite) cool slowly deep underground, developing coarse crystalline textures.

qs.q: Exfoliation in arid desert regions causes outer rock layers to peel off because rocks are poor conductors of
o: Heat, causing unequal expansion between surface and interior layers
Electricity, causing electrostatic shattering during dust storms
Sound, causing acoustic vibration fractures during high winds
Water, preventing absorption of subterranean groundwater
qs.e: Rocks conduct heat poorly, so outer layers heat and expand while inner rock stays cool, leading to fracturing.

qs.q: Slum areas in rapidly expanding developing cities are characterized primarily by
o: Inadequate housing, overcrowding, and lack of basic sanitation
Excessive park green spaces and low population density
High per capita income and luxurious high-rise apartments
Complete absence of any human population or economic activity
qs.e: Slums develop when rapid urban growth outpaces infrastructure, leading to poor sanitation and housing.

qs.q: Gully erosion severely impairs agricultural land development by dissecting fields into deep
o: Steep-sided ravines that impede farm machinery operation
Smooth shallow sand dunes suitable for wheat cropping
Waterlogged rice paddies fed by permanent streams
Flat alluvial terraces ideal for motorized ploughing
qs.e: Gullies carve deep channels that destroy topsoil and prevent the use of farm equipment.

qs.q: A trade quota is a government regulation that imposes a strict numerical limit on the
o: Quantity of a specific good imported during a given time period
Monetary value of local currency notes printed by the central bank
Number of foreign tourists visiting national game reserves
Volume of agricultural crops produced by domestic farmers
qs.e: Import quotas cap the physical volume of specific foreign merchandise entering a country.

qs.q: Road transport is preferred over rail transport for short distance journeys because of its greater
o: Fuel efficiency per ton-kilometre for bulk mineral freight
Flexibility and direct door-to-door delivery capability
Immunity to urban traffic congestion during peak hours
Lower construction cost for heavy multi-lane asphalt expressways
qs.e: Motor vehicles travel on any road network, providing direct door-to-door freight and passenger service.

qs.q: The trellis drainage pattern develops in regions where rivers flow along soft rock valleys joined at right angles across
o: Flat horizontal granite batholiths on desert plains
Hard rock ridges in folded mountain structures
Isolated volcanic cones radiating from a central peak
Karst limestone sinkholes collapsing into underground caves
qs.e: Trellis drainage features parallel main streams connected at right angles by short tributaries in folded strata.

qs.q: When local time at Greenwich Meridian (0 degrees) is 6:00 a.m., what is the local time at longitude 75 degrees East?
qs.e: 75 degrees East is 5 hours ahead of GMT (75 / 15 = 5 hrs). 6:00 a.m. plus 5 hours is 11:00 a.m.

qs.q: A map distance of 4 cm represents a ground distance of 20 km. What is the Representative Fraction (RF) scale?
On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, a road distance measuring 12 cm on the map corresponds to a ground distance of
qs.e: At 1:50,000 scale, 1 cm = 0.5 km. 12 cm map distance * 0.5 km/cm = 6 km ground distance.

qs.q: Organically formed sedimentary rocks formed from the accumulated skeletal shells of microscopic marine organisms include
qs.e: Chalk and fossiliferous limestone form from accumulated calcium carbonate shells of marine organisms.

qs.q: The fertility rate of a population measures the average number of live children born to a woman during her
o: Total lifespan from birth to natural death
Period of formal employment in the civil service
qs.e: Total fertility rate estimates average births per woman over her childbearing years (15-49).

qs.q: Chemical weathering through carbonation attacks limestone structures because rainwater contains dissolved
qs.e: Rainwater absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide to form weak carbonic acid, dissolving limestone.

qs.q: The rank-size rule in urban geography predicts that the nth largest city in a country will have a population equal to
o: Double the population of the second largest city
One-nth of the population of the largest city
The exact sum of all smaller rural village populations
One-half of the national total gross domestic product
qs.e: Rank-size rule states that the nth city's population equals 1/n times the largest city's population.

qs.q: Mass wasting involving the rapid downslope movement of water-saturated soil and rock debris along valleys is a
qs.e: Mudflows occur when heavy rain saturates loose soil and regolith, causing rapid flow down valleys.

qs.q: An embargo in foreign trade policy represents a complete government prohibition on
o: Commerce or trade with a specific foreign nation
Registration of motorized road freight vehicles
qs.e: An embargo is an official ban on trade or commercial activity with a particular country.

qs.q: A dendritic drainage pattern typically develops on land surfaces underlain by rocks that exhibit
o: Alternating steep bands of hard granite and soft shale
Uniform resistance to river erosion in all directions
Intersecting sets of master fault fractures at right angles
Radial volcanic slopes ascending to a central peak
qs.e: Dendritic drainage forms tree-like branching networks on rocks of uniform resistance.

qs.q: A slope rises from 150 m to 450 m elevation over a map distance of 6 cm on a scale of 1:50,000. Calculate the gradient.
In topographic map reading, contour lines that cross a river valley form V-shapes that point toward the
o: Exact center of the nearest coastal ocean bay
Upstream direction or source of the river
Summit of the highest adjacent mountain peak
qs.e: Contour lines crossing a valley bend into V-shapes pointing upstream toward higher elevation.

qs.q: Population distribution across West Africa is influenced heavily by rainfall, resulting in highest rural population densities in
o: Bare rocky summits of high volcanic peaks
Moist southern forest and Guinea savanna zones
qs.e: Higher rainfall and agricultural productivity support denser populations in southern forest and savanna zones.

qs.q: Groundnut pyramids were historically famous commercial agricultural landmarks in which Northern Nigerian city?
qs.e: Kano was famous for massive stacked bags of harvested groundnuts (groundnut pyramids) awaiting rail export.

qs.q: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) marks the meeting surface between the North-East Trade winds and the
qs.e: The ITCZ is the low-pressure belt where dry North-East Trades meet moist South-West Monsoons.

qs.q: A climate graph showing high uniform monthly temperatures around 26°C with two distinct rainfall peaks in May and October illustrates an
o: Hot desert climate with winter snow
Equatorial climate with double rainfall maxima
qs.e: Equatorial stations near the equator exhibit two annual rainfall peaks following the overhead sun passes.

qs.q: Frost shattering is a physical weathering process that breaks rocks apart when water trapped in rock pores
o: Boils and evaporates into high-pressure steam
Dissolves silica crystals into liquid solution
Freezes and expands by about nine percent in volume
Combines chemically with iron to form rust
qs.e: Water expands by approximately 9% upon freezing, exerting immense pressure that shatters rock joints.

qs.q: Shelterbelts and windbreaks are planted across agricultural fields in semi-arid regions primarily to prevent
o: Gully formation caused by torrential river floods
Subterranean cavern collapse in limestone rocks
Wind erosion and soil moisture desiccation
Volcanic ash accumulation on crop leaves
qs.e: Rows of trees planted perpendicular to wind direction reduce wind speed and protect topsoil from wind erosion.

qs.q: The Kainji and Jebba hydro-electric power stations are constructed along which major Nigerian river?
qs.e: Kainji and Jebba dams are major hydroelectric power projects located on the River Niger.

qs.q: Nomadic pastoralists move their herds seasonally to avoid dry-season pasture shortages and tsetse fly infestation in a practice called
qs.e: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of pastoralists and livestock between highland and lowland pastures.

qs.q: Hydrolysis of feldspar in granite rocks chemically converts potassium aluminum silicate into kaolinite clay, releasing soluble
o: Metallic gold veins into river gravels
Solid basalt blocks onto land surfaces
Silica and potassium compounds into soil water
qs.e: Hydrolysis breaks down orthoclase feldspar, yielding kaolinite clay and releasing soluble silica and potassium.

qs.q: In urban geography, edge cities are major suburban commercial and employment nodes that develop near
o: High-altitude mountain summits far from highways
Outer freeway intersections and orbital ring roads
Inland mangrove swamps near national borders
qs.e: Edge cities emerge as self-contained suburban hubs near outer highway junctions.

qs.q: In arid geomorphology, zeugens are ridge-and-furrow landforms produced by wind abrasion where horizontal rock strata consist of
o: Vertical joints in granite batholiths on mountain tops
Soluble gypsum beds dissolving in underground caves
Alternating layers of hard and soft rock capped by a resistant top layer
Loose sand dunes migrating across coastal lagoons
qs.e: Zeugens form where wind cuts through joints in a resistant cap rock into softer underlying rock layers.

qs.q: The balance of trade measures the difference in monetary value between a nation's total
o: Government tax revenue and annual expenditure
Foreign loan repayments and domestic savings
Agricultural crop production and industrial output
qs.e: Balance of trade tracks the net financial value of exported minus imported tangible physical goods.

qs.q: A braided river channel forms when a stream carries an excessive load of coarse bed material relative to its discharge, causing
o: Rapid vertical gorge cutting into granite basement rocks
Dissolution of soluble limestone beds along fault joints
Formation of deep circular plunge pools below waterfalls
Deposition of mid-channel sand and gravel bars that split flow
qs.e: Braided channels develop when heavy sediment loads cause mid-channel bars that divide stream flow into multiple channels.

qs.q: On a topographic map, a pass or col along a mountain ridge is recognized by contour lines that form
o: Concentric closed circles with inward-pointing tick marks
Vertical parallel lines merging into a single cliff boundary
Linear horizontal vectors pointing toward coastal lagoons
Two opposing sets of index contours curving away from a central low point
qs.e: A col is shown by hour-glass shaped contour patterns between two opposing higher hill summits.

qs.q: Emigration from developing West African nations affects home economies by reducing local labor force while increasing
o: Domestic demand for basic food staple crops
Congestion in metropolitan primary school classrooms
Municipal expenditure on public urban sanitation
Foreign currency remittances sent back by emigrants
qs.e: Emigrants send home substantial financial remittances that support family incomes and foreign exchange reserves.

qs.q: The Niger Delta region in Nigeria experiences severe ecological degradation from oil exploration, characterized by
o: Radioactive nuclear waste dumping in desert oases
Severe frost shattering on high mountain peaks
Widespread sand dune movement encroaching on farmland
Petroleum spills, gas flaring, and destruction of mangrove ecosystems
qs.e: Crude oil extraction in the Niger Delta has caused widespread oil spills, gas flaring, and mangrove damage.

qs.q: Tropical Continental (cT) air mass originating over the Sahara Desert brings dry, dusty harmattan conditions to West Africa during
qs.e: In winter, the Saharan air mass moves south, blowing dry dusty harmattan winds across West Africa.

qs.q: In cartography, an equal-area map projection preserves correct relative sizes of landmasses while distorting their
qs.e: Equal-area projections maintain true area proportions, but distort local shapes and angles.

qs.q: Which major limestone formation in Anambra and Cross River states provides raw materials for cement manufacturing in South-Eastern Nigeria?
qs.e: Nkalagu limestone beds supply raw calcium carbonate for cement plants in South-Eastern Nigeria.

qs.q: Hydrolysis is the most potent chemical weathering process in tropical regions because high water temperatures accelerate the reaction of
o: Nitrogen gas with quartz crystal lattices
Carbonate ions with basaltic volcanic glass
Sulfur dioxide with organic peat deposits
Hydrogen ions with mineral silicate structures
qs.e: Warm water increases H+ ion activity, rapidly breaking down silicate minerals in igneous and metamorphic rocks.

qs.q: In coastal geomorphology, a sea arch collapses when wave erosion undermines its roof, leaving an isolated standing rock pillar called a
qs.e: Continuous wave erosion causes sea arch roofs to collapse, leaving an isolated vertical rock column known as a stack.

qs.q: According to the Demographic Transition Model, Stage 5 represents a modern demographic phase where birth rates fall below death rates, causing
o: Explosive population expansion exceeding food supply
Massive rural-to-urban drift into agricultural hamlets
Sudden surge in infant mortality from infectious plagues
Natural population decline and aging demographic structure
qs.e: Stage 5 features sub-replacement fertility leading to population decline and an aging population pyramid.

qs.q: The Sokoto Basin in North-Western Nigeria is a major sedimentary basin consisting of marine and continental strata of which geological age?
qs.e: The Sokoto Basin (southeastern margin of the Iullemmeden Basin) contains Cretaceous and Tertiary sedimentary strata.

qs.q: The revolution of the Earth on its tilted axis (23.5 degrees) relative to its orbital plane causes the seasonal migration of the overhead sun between the
o: Prime Meridian and International Date Line
Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
qs.e: Earth's axial tilt causes the overhead midday sun to shift annually between 23.5°N (Cancer) and 23.5°S (Capricorn).

qs.q: A scale of 2 cm representing 1 km expressed as a Representative Fraction (R.F.) is
qs.e: Converting 1 km to centimeters gives 100,000 cm. Thus 2 cm : 100,000 cm simplifies to 1:50,000.

qs.q: A scale of 4 cm representing 1 km expressed as a Representative Fraction (R.F.) is equal to
qs.e: 1 km equals 100,000 cm. So 4 cm : 100,000 cm simplifies to 1:25,000.

qs.q: Which type of scale is expressed as a statement such as 'One centimetre represents two kilometres'?
qs.e: A statement scale describes the relationship between map distance and ground distance in words.

qs.q: A map scale expressed as 1:100,000 means that 1 cm on the map represents what distance on the ground?
qs.e: 100,000 cm divided by 100,000 cm/km equals 1 km.

qs.q: A statement scale of 1 cm to 5 km corresponds to an R.F. of
qs.e: 5 km equals 500,000 cm, so 1 cm to 500,000 cm is 1:500,000.

qs.q: Contour lines that are spaced very close together on a topographical map represent a
qs.e: Close contour lines indicate a rapid change in elevation over a short horizontal distance, representing steep terrain.

qs.q: Contour lines that are widely spaced apart on a map indicate a
qs.e: Widely spaced contour lines indicate that elevation changes slowly over ground distance, representing gentle or flat terrain.

qs.q: On a topographical map, V-shaped contour lines pointing towards higher elevation indicate a
qs.e: Contours forming a V-shape pointing upstream (towards higher numbers) represent a river valley.

qs.q: What feature is indicated by V-shaped contour lines pointing towards lower elevation?
qs.e: Contours forming a V-shape pointing downhill (towards lower contour values) represent a ridge or spur.

qs.q: Concentric closed contour lines with values increasing towards the centre represent a
qs.e: Closed concentric circles with increasing contour values inside show a hill or mountain peak.

qs.q: Gradient in geography is defined as the ratio of
qs.e: Gradient measures slope steepness as Vertical Interval (V.I.) divided by Horizontal Distance (H.D.).

qs.q: Which of the following gradient expressions represents the steepest slope?
qs.e: A smaller ratio denominator (e.g. 1 in 2 vs 1 in 50) represents a steeper incline.

qs.q: Which of the following gradient expressions represents the gentlest slope?
qs.e: The larger the second number in a 1-in-N gradient, the gentler the slope.

qs.q: To calculate gradient correctly, Vertical Interval and Horizontal Distance must both be expressed in the
qs.e: Both V.I. and H.D. must be converted to identical units (e.g. meters) before computing the fraction.

qs.q: On a standard climate graph, monthly mean temperatures are usually plotted using a
qs.e: Temperature data on climate graphs are represented by a continuous line graph, typically drawn in red.

qs.q: Monthly rainfall figures on a standard climate graph are depicted using
qs.e: Precipitation (rainfall) values are represented as vertical bar columns (histograms), usually shaded blue.

qs.q: The annual range of temperature is calculated from climate graph data by finding the difference between the
o: Hottest month and coldest month mean temperatures
Total annual rainfall and mean temperature
Maximum daily temperature and minimum daily temperature
qs.e: Annual temperature range equals the mean temperature of the warmest month minus the mean temperature of the coolest month.

qs.q: A climate graph showing high uniform temperatures (around 27°C) all year with a very small annual range (<3°C) represents an
qs.e: Equatorial regions experience small seasonal variations in temperature, remaining near 26-28°C throughout the year.

qs.q: Population density of a country or region is defined as the number of people per unit of
qs.e: Population density is calculated by dividing total population by total land area in square kilometers.

qs.q: The difference between Crude Birth Rate and Crude Death Rate in a population (excluding migration) is called the
qs.e: Natural increase rate is the excess of births over deaths in a population per thousand people.

qs.q: The rapid movement of people from rural villages to cities and towns is referred to as
qs.e: Rural-urban migration describes the flow of population from rural agricultural areas to urban centres.

qs.q: Factors that attract migrants to a new destination, such as job opportunities and better education, are called
qs.e: Pull factors are positive attributes of a destination that draw people to move there.

qs.q: The confluence of the River Niger and River Benue in Nigeria occurs at
qs.e: Lokoja in Kogi State is famous as the confluence town where the River Niger and River Benue merge.

qs.q: The major coal mining center in Nigeria is located at
qs.e: Enugu in South-Eastern Nigeria is historically known as the Coal City due to sub-bituminous coal mining.

qs.q: Tin and columbite are extensively mined on the highland of
qs.e: The Jos Plateau in Plateau State is Nigeria's chief mining region for tin ore (cassiterite) and columbite.

qs.q: Crude petroleum and natural gas reserves in Nigeria are predominantly concentrated in the
qs.e: Nigeria's vast oil and gas deposits lie in the sedimentary basin of the Niger Delta and offshore Gulf of Guinea.

qs.q: Which vegetation belt spans across the northernmost border of Nigeria?
qs.e: The Sahel Savanna occupies the extreme northern fringe of Nigeria (Borno, Yobe, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto).

qs.q: Which mode of transport is most suitable and cost-effective for carrying heavy, bulky, low-value commodities over long land distances?
qs.e: Railways excel at transporting bulky goods like coal, cement, and minerals over long distances at low unit cost.

qs.q: Which mode of transport provides direct door-to-door delivery service for passengers and goods?
qs.e: Road vehicles offer high flexibility and door-to-door reach without requiring cargo transfer terminals.

qs.q: Which mode of transport is the fastest but also the most expensive per ton-kilometre?
qs.e: Air transport offers high speed for urgent or perishable goods but incurs high operational costs.

qs.q: Which mode of transport is ideal for continuous movement of crude oil, refined petroleum products, and natural gas?
qs.e: Pipelines provide uninterrupted, automated flow of liquids and gases over vast distances.

qs.q: Trade between different nations across international borders is termed
qs.e: International trade involves buying and selling goods and services across sovereign country borders.

qs.q: Goods and services purchased from foreign countries and brought into a country are called
qs.e: Imports are foreign-produced commodities bought into a country.

qs.q: Goods and services produced domestically and sold to foreign nations are called
qs.e: Exports are domestically produced goods sold to buyers in other countries.

qs.q: Visible trade refers to international trade in
o: Tangible physical goods (e.g. crude oil, machinery, cocoa)
qs.e: Visible trade involves physical merchandise that can be touched and inspected at customs.

qs.q: Industries that convert raw agricultural or mineral materials into semi-finished or finished products are classified as
qs.e: Secondary activities involve manufacturing and industrial processing of primary raw materials.

qs.q: An industry whose location is strongly tied to the source of raw materials because the raw materials are heavy, bulky, or weight-losing is called a
qs.e: Weight-losing industries (e.g. cement, palm oil milling, iron smelting) locate near raw material deposits to reduce transport costs.

qs.q: Mineral resources that do not regenerate on a human timescale once extracted, such as petroleum and coal, are termed
qs.e: Fossil fuels and mineral ores are finite non-renewable resources formed over millions of years.

qs.q: The mineral ore from which aluminum metal is commercially extracted is
qs.e: Bauxite is the primary ore processed into alumina and smelted into aluminum.

qs.q: A settlement pattern where buildings are arranged tightly around a central feature like a church, market, or crossroads is called a
qs.e: Nucleated settlements feature clustered dwellings surrounding a central focal point.

qs.q: A settlement pattern where houses are spread far apart over farm land without a clear center is called a
qs.e: Dispersed settlements consist of isolated farmsteads separated by large fields.

qs.q: Dwellings built in a continuous single line along a main road, river bank, or railway line form a
qs.e: Linear settlements extend ribbon-like along linear transport features.

qs.q: Urbanisation is defined as the process by which an increasing proportion of a country's total population comes to live in
qs.e: Urbanisation represents demographic growth in urban centers relative to rural areas.

qs.q: Earth completes one full rotation on its axis through 360 degrees in approximately
qs.e: Earth rotates 360° on its axis every 24 hours, giving an angular speed of 15° per hour.

qs.q: Day and night on Earth are caused primarily by the
o: Rotation of Earth on its axis from West to East
Revolution of Earth around the Sun
Movement of the Moon around Earth
qs.e: Earth's rotation causes different parts of the globe to face or turn away from the Sun, creating day and night.

qs.q: The atmospheric layer closest to the Earth's surface where all weather phenomena (clouds, rain, wind) occur is the
qs.e: The troposphere contains most of the atmosphere's mass and water vapor, driving weather.

qs.q: The normal environmental lapse rate of temperature in the troposphere is approximately a decrease of
qs.e: Standard lapse rate causes air temperature to drop by ~6.5°C per 1,000 m increase in altitude.

qs.q: Ocean currents that flow from tropical equatorial regions towards higher latitudes are classified as
qs.e: Warm currents carry warm equatorial water northward or southward towards polar regions.

qs.q: Ocean currents that flow from high polar or temperate latitudes towards the equator are called
qs.e: Cold currents transport cold polar waters towards the equator.

qs.q: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava are classified as
qs.e: Igneous rocks form directly from cooled molten rock (magma underground or lava on surface).

qs.q: Rocks formed by the accumulation, compaction, and cementation of mineral sediments or organic matter are
qs.e: Sedimentary rocks form through deposition and lithification of weathered sediments or organic remains.

qs.q: A vertical cross-section through the soil showing its individual layers from the surface down to bedrock is called a
qs.e: A soil profile displays all distinct horizontal layers (horizons) down to unweathered bedrock.

qs.q: Decayed organic matter derived from decomposed plant leaves and animal remains in topsoil is called
qs.e: Humus is dark organic material that enriches topsoil fertility and water retention.

qs.q: Denudation is the general term encompassing all natural processes that wear down and lower the Earth's surface, including
o: Weathering, erosion, transportation, and mass wasting
qs.e: Denudation combines weathering, erosion, mass movement, and transport that strip surface rocks.

qs.q: The disintegration or decay of rocks in situ (in their original place) without transportation is called
qs.e: Weathering is the static breakdown of rocks in place without agent transport.

qs.q: Physical (mechanical) weathering involves the breakdown of rocks into smaller fragments without any change in their
qs.e: Physical weathering fractures rock mechanically without altering its mineral chemistry.

qs.q: Chemical weathering involves the alteration and decomposition of rock minerals through
o: Chemical reactions with water, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and organic acids
qs.e: Chemical weathering alters original minerals into new chemical compounds (e.g. clay minerals).

qs.q: The process where river water or wind hurls sand and pebbles against rock surfaces, wearing them down like sandpaper, is called
qs.e: Abrasion is mechanical scraping of rock surfaces by sediment carried by wind, water, or ice.

qs.q: The process where rock particles and pebbles carried by a river or waves collide against each other and break into smaller, rounder fragments is
qs.e: Attrition involves sediment-on-sediment collisions that smooth and reduce particle sizes.

qs.q: The sheer force of moving water slamming into air trapped in river banks or cliff cracks, forcing them to fracture, is called
qs.e: Hydraulic action uses water force and air compression in fractures to dislodge rock.

qs.q: The chemical dissolving of soluble rocks (such as limestone) by river or sea water is termed
qs.e: Corrosion is the chemical solvent action of water dissolving soluble rock minerals.

qs.q: An agricultural system where crops are grown primarily to feed the farmer's family with little or no surplus for sale is
qs.e: Subsistence farming produces food consumed directly by the farm household.

qs.q: Large-scale agricultural estates specializing in the monoculture of a single cash crop for export are known as
qs.e: Plantations are large commercial estates growing single cash crops (e.g. rubber, tea, oil palm).

qs.q: Which of the following map scales represents the largest scale?
qs.e: The smaller the denominator in a Representative Fraction, the larger the scale and the more detail shown.

qs.q: Which of the following scale ratios represents the smallest scale map?
qs.e: A larger denominator indicates a smaller scale map covering a larger area with less detail.

qs.q: If a distance between two settlements on a 1:50,000 map measures 8 cm, what is the actual ground distance?
qs.e: Actual distance = 8 cm * 50,000 = 400,000 cm = 4 km.

qs.q: On a map with a scale of 1:25,000, a road segment measures 12 cm. What is the real-world length of the road?
qs.e: Actual distance = 12 cm * 25,000 = 300,000 cm = 3 km.

qs.q: If a map of scale 1:50,000 is enlarged to twice its original linear scale, the new scale becomes
qs.e: Enlarging a map by a factor of 2 halves the scale denominator, resulting in 1:25,000.

qs.q: If a topographical sheet at a scale of 1:20,000 is reduced by half, what will be its new scale?
qs.e: Reducing a map scale by half doubles the denominator: 20,000 * 2 = 40,000, giving 1:40,000.

qs.q: A feature measuring 6 cm on a 1:100,000 map represents a ground distance of
To convert a linear scale of 1 cm representing 2.5 km to R.F., the fraction is written as
The difference in elevation between two successive contour lines on a map is known as the
qs.e: Vertical Interval (V.I.) is the constant elevation difference between adjacent contour lines.

qs.q: A point on a map marked with a dot and a specific height value, such as .245, is called a
qs.e: A spot height shows the precise elevation of a specific ground point on a topographical map.

qs.q: A low area or pass situated between two hill peaks along a ridge is referred to as a
qs.e: A col or saddle is a dip or pass along a mountain ridge situated between two higher summits.

qs.q: On a topographical sheet, a surveyed point marked by a small triangle with a height value is a
qs.e: A trigonometrical station (triangulation pillar) is indicated on maps by a triangle symbol with height.

qs.q: A steep slope on one side of a ridge and a gentle slope on the opposite side forms an asymmetrical landform called an
qs.e: An escarpment features a steep scarp slope on one side and a gentle dip slope on the other.

qs.q: What drainage pattern develops when streams flow outward in all directions from a central elevated dome or hill?
qs.e: Radial drainage forms when rivers radiate outward from a central high peak or volcanic dome.

qs.q: What drainage pattern resembles the branches of a tree and develops on uniform rock strata?
qs.e: Dendritic drainage has a tree-like branching network forming on homogeneous rock types.

qs.q: A drainage pattern in which streams flow inward towards a central depression or lake basin is called
qs.e: Centripetal drainage occurs when streams converge into a central basin or depression like Lake Chad.

qs.q: A gradient of 1 in 1 means that for every 1 metre of vertical rise, the horizontal distance is
qs.e: A 1 in 1 gradient represents a 45-degree slope where vertical rise equals horizontal distance.

qs.q: If a road rises vertically by 50 metres over a horizontal distance of 500 metres, its gradient is
qs.e: Gradient = 50 m / 500 m = 1 / 10 or 1 in 10.

qs.q: If the Vertical Interval between two points is zero, the gradient between them is
qs.e: Zero vertical change over any horizontal distance results in a gradient of zero, indicating flat ground.

qs.q: Point A has an elevation of 200 m and Point B is at 400 m. If the horizontal ground distance between them is 2,000 m, the gradient is
Contour height at X is 150 m and at Y is 450 m. If the ground distance between X and Y is 6,000 m, what is the gradient?
Two points on a 1:50,000 map are 4 cm apart. Point P is at 100 m elevation and Point Q is at 300 m. The gradient between P and Q is
A climate graph showing high rainfall in summer months (June-September) and almost zero rainfall in winter months is typical of a
qs.e: Tropical Savanna (Continental) climates feature distinct wet summer seasons and dry winter seasons.

qs.q: A climate graph with dry hot summers and cool wet winters is characteristic of which climate type?
qs.e: Mediterranean climates (Cs) are uniquely characterized by dry summer months and rainfall concentrated in winter.

qs.q: If a station has monthly mean temperatures of 25°C in Jan, 27°C in April, 30°C in July, and 24°C in Dec, what is its annual temperature range?
qs.e: Warmest month (July = 30°C) minus coolest month (Dec = 24°C) gives 30 - 24 = 6°C.

qs.q: A climate graph displaying two distinct rainfall peaks (double rainfall maxima) in May/June and September/October represents an
qs.e: Southern West Africa (Equatorial belt) receives double rainfall maxima corresponding to the passage of the ITCZ overhead twice a year.

qs.q: If the monthly rainfall totals for a station add up to 2,450 mm over twelve months, the climate is best classified as
qs.e: Annual precipitation exceeding 2,000 mm is indicative of a humid tropical or rainforest climate.

qs.q: A station records monthly mean temperatures ranging between 32°C in July and 14°C in January. Its annual temperature range is
qs.e: 32°C - 14°C = 18°C annual temperature range.

qs.q: Adverse conditions in a home region that compel people to leave, such as famine, drought, or conflict, are called
qs.e: Push factors are negative circumstances in a place of origin that force individuals to migrate.

qs.q: The average number of years a newborn baby is expected to live under current mortality conditions is known as
qs.e: Life expectancy at birth measures the statistical average lifespan of a population.

qs.q: A population pyramid with a broad base tapering rapidly towards the top indicates a population with a high proportion of
o: Elderly people and low birth rate
Young children and high birth rate
qs.e: A wide pyramid base signifies high crude birth rates and a young age structure.

qs.q: If a state has a total population of 15,000,000 and a land area of 50,000 km², what is its population density?
qs.e: Population density = 15,000,000 / 50,000 = 300 persons per sq km.

qs.q: A country has 8,000,000 people living in a total land area of 160,000 km². What is its population density?
qs.e: Population density = 8,000,000 / 160,000 = 50 persons per sq km.

qs.q: Which region of Nigeria has the highest population density?
qs.e: South-Eastern Nigeria (Anambra, Imo) has population densities exceeding 700 persons/km² due to agricultural and commercial settlement.

qs.q: Which cash crop was historically famous in Northern Nigeria for being piled into giant groundnut pyramids?
qs.e: Kano in Northern Nigeria was renowned for groundnut pyramids during the cash-crop boom.

qs.q: The primary cocoa-producing region of Nigeria is situated in the
qs.e: South-Western Nigeria accounts for over 70% of Nigeria's cocoa production.

qs.q: The largest hydroelectric power station in Nigeria is located at
qs.e: Kainji Dam in Niger State on the River Niger is Nigeria's pioneer major hydroelectric scheme.

qs.q: The mangrove swamp forest zone in Nigeria is located along the
qs.e: Mangrove vegetation thrives in brackish water coastal swamps and tidal estuaries across the Niger Delta.

qs.q: Limestone deposits used for cement production at Ewekoro and Sagamu are located in which state?
qs.e: Ogun State hosts major limestone quarries and cement manufacturing plants at Ewekoro and Sagamu.

qs.q: Which region of Nigeria is the main producer of commercial oil palm and palm kernel?
qs.e: The rainforest and palm belt of Eastern and Southern Nigeria (Imo, Abia, Edo, Cross River) leads oil palm production.

qs.q: The Ajaokuta steel complex was established in Kogi State primarily due to proximity to deposits of
qs.e: Itakpe Hill in Kogi State holds massive high-grade iron ore deposits supplied to Ajaokuta.

qs.q: The Mambilla Plateau, famous for tea plantations and cool temperate climate, is located in which state?
qs.e: The Mambilla Plateau is located in Taraba State in North-Eastern Nigeria.

qs.q: Which major river enters Nigeria from the west near Kebbi State, flows south, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean?
qs.e: River Niger enters Nigeria from Benin/Niger border, flows through Kainji/Jebba/Lokoja, and forms the Niger Delta.

qs.q: River Benue originates from the highlands of
qs.e: River Benue rises in the Adamawa Highlands of northern Cameroon before flowing west into Nigeria.

qs.q: The main source of the River Niger is located in the highlands of
qs.e: River Niger rises in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea near the Sierra Leone border.

qs.q: Which physical relief feature covers most of Northern Nigeria, forming an undulating plain at 300 to 600 metres elevation?
qs.e: The High Plains of Hausaland cover extensive areas of Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, and Zamfara states.

qs.q: The cheapest mode of transport for international trade involving bulky freight across continents is
qs.e: Maritime shipping carries massive cargo volumes across oceans at the lowest per-ton cost.

qs.q: Nigeria's Western Railway line connects the coastal port of Lagos to which major northern city?
qs.e: The Western line runs from Lagos through Ibadan, Ilorin, Jebba, Minna, and Kaduna to Kano.

qs.q: Nigeria's Eastern Railway line runs from the port of Port Harcourt northwards to
qs.e: The Eastern line connects Port Harcourt through Enugu, Makurdi, and Jos to Maiduguri in Borno State.

qs.q: Which major ocean port complex handles the largest share of Nigeria's international container sea trade?
o: Lagos Port Complex (Apapa and Tin Can Island)
qs.e: Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos handle over 70% of Nigeria's sea imports and container traffic.

qs.q: A major disadvantage of water transport on inland rivers in tropical Africa is
o: High fuel consumption compared to trucks
Seasonal fluctuations in water volume and presence of rapids/waterfalls
qs.e: African rivers face navigational bottlenecks from dry-season low water levels, rapids, and waterfalls.

qs.q: Containerisation in modern ocean shipping has greatly improved port efficiency by
o: Increasing the manual labor required at docks
Standardizing cargo handling, reducing turnaround time, and minimizing theft
qs.e: Containerisation uses standardized steel boxes that allow rapid automated loading and intermodal transfers.

qs.q: Invisible trade refers to international exchange involving
o: Services (e.g. tourism, banking, freight insurance, education)
qs.e: Invisible trade consists of non-physical service transactions.

qs.q: The regional economic bloc formed by West African states to promote intra-regional trade is known as
qs.e: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) fosters economic integration in West Africa.

qs.q: The financial statement recording all monetary transactions between a country's residents and the rest of the world over a year is the
qs.e: Balance of Payments tracks all visible, invisible, and capital account inflows and outflows.

qs.q: Balance of Trade is defined specifically as the difference between the total value of a nation's
o: Total national income and tax revenue
qs.e: Balance of Trade measures visible physical commodity exports minus visible imports.

qs.q: A favorable Balance of Trade occurs when a country's
o: Value of visible imports exceeds visible exports
Government expenditures equal total tax collection
Foreign debt exceeds gross domestic product
Value of visible exports exceeds the value of visible imports
qs.e: A trade surplus (favorable trade balance) happens when export earnings exceed import expenditures.

qs.q: A tax or customs duty levied by a government on imported foreign goods to protect domestic industries is a
qs.e: Tariffs are import taxes designed to raise revenue and make foreign goods more expensive.

qs.q: Industries that can locate anywhere without being constrained by raw material or market proximity, such as electronics assembly or software development, are termed
qs.e: Footloose industries have light inputs/outputs and rely on electricity and communications, giving location flexibility.

qs.q: Cement manufacturing plants at Ewekoro, Gboko, and Nkalagu in Nigeria are located directly adjacent to quarries of
qs.e: Limestone is heavy and weight-losing during calcination, pulling cement factories to limestone quarry sites.

qs.q: Weight-gaining industries, such as soft drink bottling and bakery production, locate near
qs.e: Adding water or weight during processing makes finished goods heavier/bulkier, pulling plants near urban markets.

qs.q: Hematite and magnetite are the chief mineral ores extracted for the production of
qs.e: Hematite (Fe2O3) and magnetite (Fe3O4) are major iron ores smelted in blast furnaces.

qs.q: Which non-metallic mineral resource is the main raw material used in glass manufacturing?
qs.e: Silica sand provides silicon dioxide, melted at high temperatures to produce glass.

qs.q: Cassiterite is the principal ore mined for the recovery of which metal?
qs.e: Cassiterite (SnO2) is the primary mineral ore of tin, mined on the Jos Plateau.

qs.q: A large continuous urban area formed by the merging together of several expanding towns and cities is called a
qs.e: Conurbations (e.g. Randstad, Ruhr valley) form when growing cities merge together.

qs.q: The single dominant city in a country that is disproportionately larger than any other city in population and economic influence is a
qs.e: A primate city (e.g. Lagos in historical context) is at least twice as large as the second-ranked city.

qs.q: A 'wet-point' settlement is situated specifically at a location chosen for access to a reliable supply of
o: Fresh drinking water in a dry region
qs.e: Wet-point settlements locate near springs, oases, or rivers in dry environments.

qs.q: A 'dry-point' settlement is established on elevated land primarily to avoid
qs.e: Dry-point settlements occupy mounds or ridges above flood-prone floodplains or marshes.

qs.q: In urban land use models, the Central Business District (CBD) is characterized by
o: Low land prices and extensive single-story farms
High land values, tall commercial skyscrapers, and high pedestrian density
qs.e: The CBD sits at the urban core with peak land values and commercial office towers.

qs.q: The Burgess Concentric Zone Model depicts urban growth extending outward from the CBD in a series of
qs.e: Burgess proposed five concentric rings extending from CBD to commuter zone.

qs.q: The Earth revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit once every
qs.e: Earth's revolution around the Sun takes 365.25 days, giving rise to the leap year every four years.

qs.q: Earth's rotation from West to East means that places located further to the East experience solar time that is
o: Behind places further to the West
Identical to places on the Equator
Ahead of places further to the West
qs.e: Because Earth rotates West to East, Eastern longitudes see sunrise earlier and gain time (+1 hour per 15° East).

qs.q: If it is 12:00 noon Greenwich Mean Time (0° longitude), what is the local solar time at Town X located at 45°E?
qs.e: Time difference = 45° / 15° per hour = 3 hours. Since Town X is East, time is 12:00 + 3 hours = 3:00 PM.

qs.q: Lines drawn on a weather map connecting places having equal atmospheric pressure are called
qs.e: Isobars connect points of equal atmospheric pressure.

qs.q: Lines connecting places of equal rainfall on a geographical weather map are known as
qs.e: Isohyets are lines joining places receiving equal precipitation.

qs.q: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a low-pressure belt near the Equator where which wind systems converge?
o: North-East Trade winds and South-East Trade winds
qs.e: The ITCZ forms where trade winds from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres meet.

qs.q: The primary driving force that initiates surface ocean current circulation across major ocean basins is the
o: Volcanic eruptions on the ocean floor
Prevailing planetary wind systems (e.g. Trade winds, Westerlies)
qs.e: Planetary winds drag surface ocean waters continuously along prevailing wind directions.

qs.q: Which cold ocean current washing the north-western coast of Africa contributes to the aridity of the Sahara Desert?
qs.e: The cold Canary Current desaturates air along West Africa's northern coast, reinforcing Sahara coastal aridity.

qs.q: The cold Benguela Current flows along the south-western coast of Africa and intensifies hyper-arid conditions in the
qs.e: The cold Benguela Current creates stable air and coastal fogs, forming the coastal Namib Desert.

qs.q: Pre-existing rocks that have undergone structural or mineralogical alteration under extreme heat and pressure are called
qs.e: Metamorphism alters rock texture and mineralogy without complete melting.

qs.q: Granite is a coarse-grained crystalline rock classified as a plutonic
qs.e: Granite forms from slow cooling of magma deep below Earth's surface.

qs.q: Basalt is a fine-grained, dark-colored rock formed by rapid cooling of lava on Earth's surface, making it an
qs.e: Basalt forms from rapid lava cooling at the surface during volcanic eruptions.

qs.q: The dense multi-layered forest with tall hardwood trees, buttress roots, and climbing lianas in humid tropical lowlands is the
qs.e: Tropical rainforests feature canopy layers, lianas, epiphytes, and broadleaf hardwoods.

qs.q: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportions of which three particle sizes?
qs.e: Soil texture measures proportions of coarse sand (0.05-2mm), medium silt (0.002-0.05mm), and fine clay (<0.002mm).

qs.q: Leaching in tropical soils refers to the process where heavy rainfall
o: Deposits fresh fertile silt on floodplains
Evaporates topsoil water to leave salt crusts
Washes soluble plant nutrients and mineral bases downward out of the topsoil
qs.e: Leaching dissolves and washes soluble minerals down from Horizon A into Horizon B.

qs.q: The peeling off of outer rock layers in curved concentric sheets due to repeated thermal expansion and contraction in deserts is
qs.e: Diurnal heating and cooling cause outer rock layers to expand and peel away like onion skins.

qs.q: Frost shattering (freeze-thaw action) is a physical weathering process prevalent in high mountains and cold climates where water
o: Freezes in rock crevices, expands by 9%, and wedges the rock apart
Combines with iron to produce rust
qs.e: Water expanding by 9% upon freezing exerts high pressure inside rock fractures, shattering them.

qs.q: Chemical weathering process where atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in rainwater to form weak carbonic acid that attacks limestone is called
qs.e: Rainwater plus CO2 forms carbonic acid, which converts insoluble calcium carbonate into soluble calcium bicarbonate.

qs.q: The rusting and crumbling of iron-rich rocks when exposed to moist air is caused by the chemical weathering process of
qs.e: Oxidation occurs when oxygen reacts with ferrous iron minerals to form ferric iron oxides (rust).

qs.q: A mass wasting process involving the slow, imperceptible downhill movement of soil and regolith under gravity is called
qs.e: Soil creep is a slow, continuous gravity-driven downslope creep of surface soil.

qs.q: Rapid downslope collapse of a large mass of rock and soil along a slippery failure plane on a steep mountain slope is a
qs.e: Landslides involve rapid mass movement of rock and soil downslope along a distinct failure plane.

qs.q: A steep-sided, narrow river valley with a steep gradient in a river's upper course is described as a
qs.e: Upper course rivers erode vertically downwards, producing narrow V-shaped cross-profiles.

qs.q: A crescent-shaped lake formed when a river meander neck is cut through during a flood is an
qs.e: Oxbow lakes form when floods cut across meander necks, abandoning the old river loop.

qs.q: A fan-shaped or triangular deposit of sediment formed at the mouth of a river where it enters a quiet sea or lake is a
qs.e: Deltas accumulate when river velocity drops upon entering standing sea or lake water.

qs.q: Raised natural embankments built up along the banks of a river course by repeated flood sediment deposition are called
qs.e: Levees form when floodwaters overflow banks and drop coarse sediment along channel margins.

qs.q: Mushroom rocks (rock pedestals) in arid deserts are formed primarily by wind abrasion concentrated near the ground because
o: Upper rock layers are dissolved by rain
Wind-blown sand grains are heavy and carried mostly within 1 metre above the ground surface
Camels rub against the rock base
qs.e: Saltating sand grains travel close to the ground, eroding the base of rock outcrops faster than the top.

qs.q: Deep, narrow steep-sided rock troughs carved in desert landscapes by wind abrasion acting on alternating parallel bands of hard and soft rock arranged horizontally are
qs.e: Zeugens feature ridge-and-furrow landscape carved into horizontal hard/soft rock layers.

qs.q: Farming that combines crop cultivation and livestock rearing on the same farm is called
qs.e: Mixed farming integrates crop production with animal husbandry on a single agricultural unit.

qs.q: The seasonal movement of pastoral herders and their livestock between summer mountain pastures and winter lowland valleys is
qs.e: Transhumance is seasonal livestock migration between high and low pastures.

qs.q: Shifting cultivation (bush fallowing) maintains soil fertility over time by
o: Constructing concrete terraces on steep slopes
Abandoning cultivated plots to natural bush fallow for several years to regenerate soil nutrients
qs.e: Bush fallowing relies on natural vegetation regrowth during fallow periods to restore organic matter and nutrients.

qs.q: On a 1:50,000 topographical map, a straight railway line measures 14 cm. The distance in kilometres is
If two hills are 10 km apart in reality, how far apart will they be on a map scaled at 1:250,000?
A statement scale of 5 cm to 1 km converts to an R.F. of
On a 1:50,000 map, a stream length measures 16 cm. What is its length on ground?
If a map scale is 1:25,000, what map distance represents a real-world distance of 5 km?
What is the R.F. of a map on which 10 cm represents 1 km?
qs.e: 1 km = 100,000 cm. 10 cm : 100,000 cm simplifies to 1:10,000.

qs.q: A lake covers an area of 5 cm² on a map scaled 1:50,000. If the map is enlarged 3 times, what is the new map area?
qs.e: Enlarging linear dimensions by 3 increases area by 3² = 9. Thus 5 cm² * 9 = 45 cm².

qs.q: A rectangular farm measures 4 cm by 5 cm on a map of scale 1:50,000. What is the actual area in square kilometres?
qs.e: Map area = 20 cm². At 1:50,000, 1 cm = 0.5 km, so 1 cm² = 0.25 km². 20 * 0.25 = 5 km².

qs.q: If a forest reserve has an area of 16 cm² on a 1:100,000 map, what is its actual ground area in square kilometres?
qs.e: At 1:100,000, 1 cm represents 1 km, so 1 cm² represents 1 km². Thus 16 cm² = 16 km².

qs.q: A map with scale 1:50,000 is reduced by half in linear dimensions. A parcel of land originally 12 cm² will now cover
qs.e: Reducing linear scale by half reduces area to (1/2)² = 1/4. So 12 / 4 = 3 cm².

qs.q: If a map of scale 1:100,000 is enlarged 4 times linearly, its new scale becomes
qs.e: Enlarging 4 times reduces the denominator fourfold: 100,000 / 4 = 25,000, giving 1:25,000.

qs.q: On a map of scale 1:50,000, a square field has an area of 4 cm². What is the side of this field on the ground in kilometres?
qs.e: Map side = sqrt(4 cm²) = 2 cm. At 1:50,000, 2 cm = 2 * 0.5 km = 1 km.

qs.q: If the forward bearing of point B from point A is 045°, what is the back bearing of point A from point B?
qs.e: Back bearing = Forward bearing + 180° (since 045° < 180°). 45° + 180° = 225°.

qs.q: The forward bearing of a village from a mountain top is 240°. What is the back bearing from the village to the mountain top?
qs.e: Back bearing = Forward bearing - 180° (since 240° > 180°). 240° - 180° = 060°.

qs.q: Concentric closed contours with hachures pointing inward indicate a
qs.e: Hachured closed contours indicate a bowl-shaped depression or sinkhole where elevation decreases inward.

qs.q: If the true bearing of a town is 135°, what is its compass direction?
qs.e: 135° corresponds exactly to South-East on a 16-point cardinal compass.

qs.q: A permanent mark carved into a wall or rock by surveyors to record elevation above sea level is a
qs.e: A benchmark (marked BM on maps) is a permanent reference mark showing precise elevation.

qs.q: What type of slope is represented on a map where contours are close at the top and widely spaced at the bottom?
qs.e: A concave slope is steep near the summit (close contours) and gentle near the base (widely spaced contours).

qs.q: A convex slope is depicted on a contour map by lines that are
o: Closely spaced near the top and widely spaced near the bottom
Widely spaced near the top and closely spaced near the bottom
Evenly spaced throughout the entire slope
Merging together into a single line at the summit
qs.e: A convex slope starts gentle at the top (widely spaced contours) and becomes steeper towards the base (closely spaced contours).

qs.q: If two points on a map are mutually visible without any intervening landform blocking the line of sight, they are said to be
qs.e: Intervisibility means two points on a map have an unobstructed line of sight between them.

qs.q: What drainage pattern forms in folded mountain regions where main rivers run parallel and tributaries join at right angles?
qs.e: Trellis drainage develops in alternate hard and soft rock belts where tributaries join main streams at 90°.

qs.q: The forward bearing from point X to point Y is 310°. The back bearing from Y to X is
qs.e: Back bearing = 310° - 180° = 130°.

qs.q: The angular difference between True North and Magnetic North shown on a topographical map margin is called
qs.e: Magnetic declination (or variation) is the angle between True North and Magnetic North.

qs.q: On a topographical map, a linear arrangement of nucleated settlements along a highway is described as a
