qs.e: Linear settlement patterns develop along transport lines like roads, railways, or rivers.

qs.q: A hill summit is at 600 m and its base is at 100 m. The distance on a 1:50,000 map from base to summit is 5 cm. What is the gradient?
Elevation at point M is 250 m and at point N is 500 m. The map distance on a 1:50,000 map is 10 cm. Calculate the gradient.
A road ascends from 300 m to 400 m elevation over a map distance of 8 cm on a 1:50,000 map. What is the gradient?
Point K is at 120 m and Point L is at 420 m elevation. Map distance on a 1:50,000 map is 3 cm. Calculate the gradient.
What is the gradient between two contours of 50 m and 300 m separated by 5 cm on a 1:100,000 map?
A slope rises 150 m over a map distance of 6 cm on a 1:50,000 map. Express the gradient as a simple ratio.
Calculate the gradient between 400 m and 900 m contours separated by 4 cm on a 1:25,000 map.
Point C is at 100 m and Point D is at 200 m elevation. Map distance on a 1:25,000 map is 10 cm. Find the gradient.
A mountain trail goes from 300 m to 600 m elevation over 12 cm on a 1:50,000 map. What is the gradient?
If a slope has a gradient of 1 in 10 and the horizontal distance is 5 km, what is the vertical rise?
qs.e: Vertical rise = H.D. / 10 = 5,000 m / 10 = 500 m.

qs.q: A railway line has a maximum allowable gradient of 1 in 50. To climb a vertical height of 200 m, what minimum horizontal distance is needed?
qs.e: Horizontal distance = 200 m * 50 = 10,000 m = 10 km.

qs.q: A road climbs from an elevation of 50 m to 250 m over a map distance of 8 cm on a 1:25,000 map. What is the gradient?
A climate graph showing less than 250 mm of total annual rainfall and high daytime temperatures represents a
qs.e: Arid desert climates receive less than 250 mm of annual rainfall with high diurnal temperatures.

qs.q: On a climate graph for Kano, Northern Nigeria, peak rainfall occurs in which month?
qs.e: In northern Nigeria (Sudan savanna), the maritime monsoon winds reach their northernmost extent in August, causing peak rainfall.

qs.q: On a climate graph for Warri in the Niger Delta, rainfall occurs during how many months of the year?
qs.e: Coastal stations in the Niger Delta like Warri experience rainfall throughout all 12 months due to onshore maritime winds.

qs.q: If a climate graph shows monthly temperatures of 26°C, 27°C, 28°C, 28°C, 27°C, 26°C, 25°C, 25°C, 26°C, 27°C, 27°C, 26°C, the mean annual temperature is
qs.e: Sum of monthly temperatures = 318°C. 318 / 12 = 26.5°C.

qs.q: A climate graph featuring warm moist summers and cold dry winters in Eastern China represents a
o: Warm Temperate Eastern Margin (China type) climate
qs.e: The China type climate experiences warm wet summers driven by monsoons and cold dry winters driven by continental anticyclones.

qs.q: On a climate graph, a dip in rainfall during August in Southern Nigeria between two rain peaks is called the
qs.e: The August Break is a temporary decline in rainfall occurring in Southern Nigeria during August when the ITCZ moves furthest north.

qs.q: A climate graph for Jos shows significantly lower mean annual temperatures than surrounding lowland stations like Bauchi due to
qs.e: Jos sits at an elevation of over 1,200 m on the Jos Plateau, lowering temperatures by approximately 6.5°C per 1,000 m ascent.

qs.q: If a climate graph shows a single rainfall peak in July-August and an annual rainfall of 850 mm, the vegetation zone is most likely
qs.e: Annual rainfall of 600-1000 mm with a single summer peak is characteristic of the Sudan Savanna belt.

qs.q: A station at 55°N latitude records monthly temperatures of -15°C in Jan and 18°C in July. What is its annual temperature range?
Which climate graph feature best distinguishes a Northern Hemisphere Savanna from a Southern Hemisphere Savanna?
o: The months in which the high-rainfall summer peak occurs
qs.e: Northern Hemisphere savannas experience rain peaks in June-August, whereas Southern Hemisphere savannas experience rain peaks in December-February.

qs.q: A climate graph displaying mild temperatures year-round (10°C to 17°C) and evenly distributed rainfall in all months represents a
o: Cool Temperate Western Margin (British type) climate
qs.e: The British type climate receives rain year-round from prevailing westerly winds and warm ocean currents.

qs.q: If a country records a Crude Birth Rate of 42 per 1,000 and a Crude Death Rate of 14 per 1,000, what is its rate of natural increase?
qs.e: Rate of natural increase = 42 - 14 = 28 per 1,000 or 2.8%.

qs.q: The ratio of the economically inactive population (aged 0-14 and 65+) to the working-age population (aged 15-64) is called the
qs.e: The dependency ratio measures the burden on the productive working population.

qs.q: A country with a population of 25,000,000 covers an area of 100,000 km². Calculate its density.
qs.e: Density = 25,000,000 / 100,000 = 250 persons/km².

qs.q: Demographic Transition Model Stage 2 is characterized by
o: Low birth rate and low death rate
High birth rate and rapidly falling death rate
High birth rate and high death rate
Falling birth rate and rising death rate
qs.e: Stage 2 experiences high birth rates alongside rapidly declining mortality due to medical and sanitary improvements.

qs.q: Which of the following is a major push factor driving emigration from rural agricultural zones in West Africa?
o: Soil degradation and lack of farm land
qs.e: Soil depletion, farm fragmentation, and drought act as strong rural push factors.

qs.q: Sex ratio in population studies is defined as the number of
qs.e: Sex ratio measures the number of males per 100 females in a given population.

qs.q: If a population has 40% children (0-14), 5% elderly (65+), and 55% working adults (15-64), what is the dependency ratio?
Optimum population is defined as the population size that
o: Exceeds the food production capacity of a nation
Maximizes per capita income given available resources and technology
Is lower than the available natural resources can support
Has zero birth rate and zero death rate
qs.e: Optimum population achieves the highest standard of living given current resources and technology.

qs.q: Underpopulation exists when a country has
o: More people than its food supply can support
Fewer people than needed to fully utilize its natural resources efficiently
qs.e: Underpopulation occurs when expanding population would increase per capita income by fully exploiting resources.

qs.q: Overpopulation occurs when a region's population size
o: Grows at a rate of 1% per annum
Is less than its land area in square kilometres
Exceeds the carrying capacity of its resources and technology, lowering living standards
qs.e: Overpopulation happens when population exceeds resource capacity, leading to reduced standard of living.

qs.q: According to Malthusian population theory, human population grows geometrically while food production increases
qs.e: Malthus postulated that population grows geometrically (1, 2, 4, 8) while food supply grows arithmetically (1, 2, 3, 4).

qs.q: A country with 12,000,000 population and land area 40,000 km² experiences a population increase of 20%. What is its new density?
qs.e: Original pop = 12M. New pop = 12M * 1.2 = 14.4M. New density = 14.4M / 40,000 = 360 persons/km².

qs.q: The Obudu Cattle Ranch and Resort, situated on a high plateau in Cross River State, is part of the
qs.e: Obudu is located on the Sankwala Mountains (Oban Hills extension) in Cross River State.

qs.q: Which of the following is a inland drainage basin in Nigeria where rivers do not flow into the ocean?
qs.e: The Chad Basin in north-eastern Nigeria is an endorheic basin draining into Lake Chad.

qs.q: Rubber plantations in Nigeria are heavily concentrated in which state?
qs.e: Edo State (around Benin City) and Delta State are Nigeria's chief natural rubber producers.

qs.q: Which agricultural project in Northern Nigeria utilizes water from the Tiga Dam for irrigation?
qs.e: The Kano River Project relies on water impounded by Tiga Dam on the Kano River.

qs.q: Bakolori Dam in Zamfara State was constructed primarily to irrigate crops along the valley of River
qs.e: Bakolori Dam on the Rima River provides dry-season irrigation for crops in Zamfara and Sokoto.

qs.q: Which major petroleum refinery in Nigeria is located in Kaduna State to supply northern markets?
qs.e: Kaduna Refinery was constructed inland to serve fuel demands across Northern Nigeria.

qs.q: Lead and zinc mineral deposits in Nigeria are mined in the vicinity of
qs.e: Abakaliki in Ebonyi State is well known for lead and zinc mineralization.

qs.q: The Udi-Nsukka escarpment in Enugu State is characterized by severe soil erosion forming deep landscape features called
qs.e: The Udi escarpment suffers from catastrophic gully erosion due to friable sandy soils and heavy rainfall.

qs.q: Salt production from natural brine springs in Nigeria is traditionally practiced at Keana in Nasarawa State and
qs.e: Uburu (Ebonyi) and Keana (Nasarawa) are traditional salt-brine processing centers.

qs.q: Which soil type dominates the semi-arid savanna of Northern Nigeria, formed under low rainfall conditions?
qs.e: Light reddish-brown pedocal soils with low organic content dominate the northern savanna.

qs.q: The fertile seasonally flooded river valley soils in Northern Nigeria used for dry-season cropping are called
qs.e: Fadama soils are rich alluvial soils in floodplain depressions used for irrigation farming.

qs.q: Which major mountain range forms the eastern natural border between Nigeria and Cameroon?
qs.e: The eastern boundary of Nigeria features mountain chains including Gotel, Mandara, and Shebshi.

qs.q: The Jebba Hydroelectric Power station is constructed on which river?
qs.e: Jebba Dam is located downstream of Kainji on the main channel of the River Niger.

qs.q: Shiroro Hydroelectric Power Dam is situated on which major tributary of the River Niger?
qs.e: Shiroro Dam in Niger State generates hydroelectricity from the Kaduna River.

qs.q: Which Nigerian port city is located on the Bonny River estuary in the Niger Delta?
qs.e: Port Harcourt is situated along the Bonny River, serving as a major oil export port.

qs.q: The main advantage of pipeline transport over road tanker trucks for petroleum distribution is that pipelines
o: Can carry solid goods alongside liquids
Are unaffected by surface traffic congestion and operate continuously with low maintenance
Are flexible in changing routes daily
qs.e: Pipelines operate 24/7 without weather or traffic delays once laid underground.

qs.q: Inland water transport on the River Niger is navigable for heavy barges up to Lokoja primarily during which season?
qs.e: Monsoon rains swell river depth during July-October, enabling barge navigation up to Lokoja and Baro.

qs.q: Which deep-water port commissioned in Lagos State was designed to accommodate ultra-large modern container vessels?
qs.e: Lekki Deep Sea Port is Nigeria's modern deep-water port capable of handling post-Panamax ships.

qs.q: Trans-African Highway routes crossing Nigeria include the Trans-Sahara Highway connecting Lagos to
qs.e: The Trans-Sahara Highway route links Lagos (Nigeria) to Algiers (Algeria) across the Sahara Desert.

qs.q: Which inland river port on the River Niger in Kwara State was historically developed as a rail-river transfer terminus?
qs.e: Baro was developed as a railhead terminal where northern agricultural produce met River Niger steamships.

qs.q: A major limitation of road transport in developing nations is
o: Inability to access remote rural villages
High maintenance costs, quick road deterioration, and traffic congestion
qs.e: Road networks suffer from pot-holes, heavy traffic, and high maintenance demands under heavy axle loads.

qs.q: Which sea port in Rivers State specializes heavily in oil and gas cargo handling and offshore support operations?
qs.e: Onne Oil and Gas Free Zone Port is a dedicated hub for offshore oilfield supplies and gas exports.

qs.q: The term 'Intermodal Transport' refers to the movement of cargo using
o: Multiple modes of transport (e.g. road, rail, sea) without handling the cargo itself when changing modes
A single wooden cart across river bridges
qs.e: Intermodal transport uses standardized containers transferred seamlessly across ships, trains, and trucks.

qs.q: Which inland container depot (dry port) was established in Northern Nigeria to clear customs inland?
qs.e: Kaduna Inland Dry Port allows importers in Northern Nigeria to clear containerized goods locally.

qs.q: The standard gauge railway line constructed in Nigeria between Abuja and Kaduna was designed primarily to
o: Transport heavy coal from Enugu to Kano
Provide fast, safe passenger transit and reduce highway congestion on the express corridor
qs.e: The Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge rail line provides high-speed commuter and passenger service.

qs.q: Heavy siltation at river mouths and estuaries along the Bight of Benin poses a major challenge to shipping by
o: Reducing water draft and requiring continuous expensive dredging
qs.e: Silt accumulation lowers water depth in access channels, forcing ports like Calabar to dredge frequently.

qs.q: What is the term for roads that connect rural farming villages to major arterial highways?
qs.e: Feeder roads link agricultural hinterlands to main arterial trunk roads.

qs.q: Trunk A highways in Nigeria are constructed and maintained by the
qs.e: Trunk A highways form the national arterial road network funded and managed by the Federal Government.

qs.q: A physical limit placed by a government on the total quantity of a specific good that may be imported during a given period is an import
qs.e: An import quota restricts the physical volume of imported goods allowed entry.

qs.q: Nigeria's principal export commodity driving the bulk of its foreign exchange earnings is
o: Crude petroleum and liquefied natural gas
qs.e: Crude oil and gas account for over 85% of Nigeria's foreign export revenue.

qs.q: The practice of exporting goods to a foreign country at a price lower than their domestic cost of production is called
qs.e: Dumping involves selling goods abroad below cost to undercut foreign competitors.

qs.q: Entrepôt trade refers to a commercial activity where a port city
o: Bans all foreign merchant ships from entering
Imports goods from one nation solely to re-export them to other nations without transformation
qs.e: Entrepôt ports act as intermediate distribution hubs re-exporting imported goods.

qs.q: A complete government ban on trade or commercial interaction with a specific foreign nation is known as an
qs.e: An embargo is a legal prohibition on commerce with a designated nation.

qs.q: Which of the following constitutes a major item of invisible export for a country receiving foreign travelers?
qs.e: Expenditures by foreign tourists generate foreign exchange through invisible exports.

qs.q: Terms of Trade measure the ratio of a country's
o: Export price index to its Import price index
Total population to total gross domestic product
qs.e: Terms of Trade = (Index of Export Prices / Index of Import Prices) * 100.

qs.q: A nation experiences a deterioration in its Terms of Trade when
o: Export prices rise faster than import prices
Import prices rise faster than export prices
The nation eliminates all import tariffs
qs.e: When import prices escalate relative to export prices, a nation must export more volume to buy the same imports.

qs.q: Which agreement established the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to create a single liberalized market across Africa?
qs.e: AfCFTA aims to eliminate tariffs on 90% of goods traded across African member states.

qs.q: Counter-trade is an international trade arrangement that involves
o: Imposing 100% tariffs on foreign luxury items
Direct exchange of goods and services for other goods rather than hard currency payment
qs.e: Counter-trade operates like international barter (e.g. trading crude oil directly for infrastructure construction).

qs.q: The clustering of related industrial plants in a specific metropolitan region to share infrastructure and skilled labor is called
qs.e: Agglomeration economies occur when factories cluster together to share utilities, suppliers, and labor pools.

qs.q: Heavy manufacturing industries like iron and steel plants require large inputs of
o: Heavy raw materials, reliable power, abundant water, and capital
qs.e: Steel manufacturing demands massive bulk inputs of iron ore, coking coal/gas, flux, and water.

qs.q: Which industrial zone in Nigeria is the largest concentration of manufacturing plants, accounting for over 50% of national industrial output?
qs.e: The Lagos-Otta-Ibadan corridor dominates Nigerian manufacturing due to port access, large consumer markets, and power infrastructure.

qs.q: Alfred Weber's Least Cost Theory of industrial location posits that an industry's location is primarily determined by minimizing
o: Transportation costs for raw materials and finished products
qs.e: Weber's theory emphasizes minimizing transport costs relative to raw material weight-loss or weight-gain.

qs.q: Associated natural gas in petroleum reservoirs is often flared in oilfields, causing severe environmental
o: Air pollution, acid rain, and greenhouse gas emissions
qs.e: Gas flaring releases thermal radiation, carbon emissions, sulfur oxides, and toxic soot into local ecosystems.

qs.q: Which metamorphic mineral is widely utilized as heat insulation and fireproofing material, though restricted due to health risks?
qs.e: Asbestos fibers resist high heat and fire, though inhalation causes lung disease (asbestosis).

qs.q: Open-cast mining (strip mining) is commonly employed when mineral deposits are situated
o: Deep underground beneath 2,000 metres of rock
Near the earth's surface beneath thin overburden
qs.e: Open-cast mining excavates surface layers to extract shallow mineral beds efficiently.

qs.q: Deep shaft mining is required for extracting mineral seams located
o: Exclusively in shallow river sand beds
At great depths underground beneath thick rock strata
qs.e: Shaft mining constructs vertical shafts and underground tunnels to reach deep mineral veins.

qs.q: The Hoyt Sector Model of urban land use suggests that functional zones expand outward from the CBD in
o: Wedge-shaped sectors along major transport corridors
qs.e: Hoyt emphasized sector growth along rail corridors and highways.

qs.q: Harris and Ullman's Multiple Nuclei Model states that a large city develops around
o: Several independent focal nodes rather than a single CBD
qs.e: Multiple nuclei models acknowledge specialized nodes (e.g. airports, industrial parks, ports).

qs.q: Suburbanisation refers to the outward movement of population and commercial businesses from inner city cores to the
o: Urban fringes and suburban outer zones
qs.e: Suburbanisation expands suburban residential residential areas surrounding city cores.

qs.q: Shanty towns, favelas, or informal settlements on urban fringes are characterized by
o: Paved roads with underground utility lines
Self-built makeshift housing, high population density, and lack of basic municipal services
qs.e: Informal settlements arise from rapid urbanisation outpacing municipal housing and infrastructure.

qs.q: In settlement geography, the term 'Site' refers to the
o: Exact physical land characteristics on which a settlement is built (e.g. hill top, river bend)
Location of a settlement relative to surrounding regions and transport routes
Total economic trade output of a city
National capital status of a city
qs.e: Site describes local physical features (relief, soil, water) of the ground occupied.

qs.q: The term 'Situation' of a settlement describes its location relative to
o: The depth of its domestic water well
Surrounding physical features, trade routes, regions, and other settlements
The slope angle of its central building
qs.e: Situation places a settlement in its broader regional accessibility context.

qs.q: Walter Christaller's Central Place Theory uses which geometric shape to represent idealized market service areas without gaps or overlaps?
qs.e: Hexagonal service areas cover space completely without the overlaps or gaps created by circles.

qs.q: In Central Place Theory, the 'Threshold Population' is the
o: Maximum distance a consumer is willing to travel to purchase a good
Total land area covered by a city
Highest elevation where houses can be built
Minimum number of consumers required to support a specific business or service profitably
qs.e: Threshold population is the minimum market size needed to sustain a commercial function.

qs.q: In Central Place Theory, the 'Range' of a good or service is defined as the
o: Maximum distance consumers are willing to travel to purchase that good or service
Minimum population needed to open a shop
Total profit earned by a store per year
Number of employees working in a store
qs.e: Range is the maximum spatial distance customers will travel for a specific service.

qs.q: High-order central places (e.g. regional capitals) provide high-order goods and services characterized by
o: Small threshold populations and tiny ranges (e.g. bread, matches)
Large threshold populations and wide spatial ranges (e.g. universities, specialized hospitals)
qs.e: High-order services require large population catchments and serve wide geographical areas.

qs.q: If local time at Greenwich (0°) is 12:00 noon, what is the local time at a city on longitude 60°W?
qs.e: Time difference = 60° / 15° per hour = 4 hours. Since it is West, time is 12:00 - 4 hours = 8:00 AM.

qs.q: On which two dates of the year are day and night of equal length (12 hours each) all over the Earth (Equinoxes)?
qs.e: On the spring (March 21) and autumnal (September 23) equinoxes, the Sun is directly overhead at the Equator.

qs.q: The Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs on June 21 when the Sun's vertical rays are overhead at the
qs.e: On June 21, the Sun is vertically overhead at the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N), producing the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere.

qs.q: If the local time at Town A (30°W) is 9:00 AM, what is the local time at Town B (60°E)?
qs.e: Longitude difference = 30° + 60° = 90°. Time difference = 90° / 15° = 6 hours ahead. 9:00 AM + 6 hours = 3:00 PM.

qs.q: The deflection of prevailing winds and ocean currents to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere is caused by the
o: Revolution of Earth around the Sun
Coriolis effect resulting from Earth's rotation
qs.e: Earth's rotation generates the Coriolis force, deflecting moving air and water currents.

qs.q: Land and sea breezes along coastal zones are caused by differences in the
o: Earth's rotation speed at different latitudes
Gravitational pull of the Moon on oceans
Specific heat capacities and heating rates of land and water bodies
qs.e: Land heats up and cools down much faster than water, driving diurnal pressure differences and breezes.

qs.q: The dry, dusty trade wind that blows from the Sahara Desert across West Africa between November and March is the
qs.e: The Harmattan is a dry North-East Trade wind laden with Saharan dust.

qs.q: Orographic (relief) rainfall occurs when moisture-laden winds are forced to rise over a
o: Mountain barrier or highland relief feature
qs.e: Highland barriers force moist air upward, cooling it adiabatically to form relief rain.

qs.q: Convectional rainfall is characteristic of equatorial regions and typically occurs during the
o: Cool early morning hours before sunrise
Hot afternoon following strong morning solar heating and rapid air updrafts
qs.e: Intense morning insolation creates strong thermal convection currents leading to afternoon thunderstorms.

qs.q: The Gulf Stream is a major warm ocean current that flows northward along the eastern coast of
qs.e: The Gulf Stream originates in the Gulf of Mexico and flows up the US East Coast towards Western Europe.

qs.q: Which warm ocean current keeps ports in North-Western Europe (e.g. Hammerfest in Norway) ice-free throughout the winter?
qs.e: The North Atlantic Drift (extension of Gulf Stream) warms Western European coastal waters.

qs.q: The meeting zone of the warm Gulf Stream and the cold Labrador Current off Newfoundland creates ideal conditions for rich
o: Fishing grounds (Grand Banks) and frequent dense sea fog
qs.e: Cold and warm current mixing promotes plankton blooms (rich fishing grounds) and heavy sea fog.

qs.q: Cold ocean currents flowing along tropical western continental coasts produce coastal deserts because the cold water
o: Evaporates instantly to form violent rainstorms
Cools the overlying air, creating stable atmospheric conditions that suppress convection and rainfall
qs.e: Cold water cools lower air, creating temperature inversions that inhibit upward convection and precipitation.

qs.q: Sandstone is a mechanically formed sedimentary rock composed mainly of consolidated grains of
qs.e: Sandstone consists predominantly of cemented quartz sand grains.

qs.q: Limestone is an organically or chemically formed sedimentary rock composed primarily of
qs.e: Limestone consists of calcite (CaCO3) derived from marine shell remains or chemical precipitation.

qs.q: Under intense heat and pressure, limestone metamorphoses into
qs.e: Metamorphism of limestone recrystallizes calcite grains to produce marble.

qs.q: Metamorphism of shale or clay under regional heat and pressure produces
qs.e: Shale subjected to regional pressure transforms into slate.

qs.q: Laterite (latosol) soils formed under high tropical temperatures and heavy rainfall are rich in iron and aluminum oxides but deficient in
qs.e: Intense leaching removes silica and soluble bases, leaving reddish iron/aluminum laterite residue.

qs.q: Trees in the Tropical Savanna, such as the Baobab and Acacia, adapt to seasonal drought through xerophytic features including
o: Thick corky bark, deep taproots, water-storing trunks, and small or thorny leaves
Broad thin leaves that shed constantly in rain
qs.e: Savanna plants adapt to dry seasons with water storage, thick bark, and reduced leaf transpiration.

qs.q: Coniferous boreal forests (Taiga) of cold northern latitudes feature evergreen trees with needle-like leaves adapted to prevent
o: Excessive moisture loss during freezing winters
qs.e: Waxy needle leaves minimize transpiration during long freezing winters when soil water is ice-bound.

qs.q: Soil erosion caused by thin sheets of running water removing a uniform layer of topsoil over a wide area is called
qs.e: Sheet erosion strips a uniform surface layer of fertile topsoil across exposed fields.

qs.q: Accumulations of angular rock fragments that collect at the base of steep cliffs as a result of frost shattering are called
qs.e: Talus (scree) cones accumulate at cliff bases from frost-shattered rock fragments.

qs.q: Solifluction is a mass wasting process common in periglacial regions where water-saturated soil slides over an impermeable layer of
qs.e: Summer thawing melts surface topsoil, which slides over the impermeable frozen subsoil (permafrost).

qs.q: Biological weathering involves rock breakdown caused by living organisms, such as
o: Tree roots growing into rock joints and wedging them open
qs.e: Plant roots exert physical force inside rock crevices, wedging them apart.

qs.q: Chemical weathering where feldspar minerals in granite react with water to form clay minerals (kaolin) is called
qs.e: Hydrolysis involves chemical reaction between hydrogen ions in water and feldspar minerals, yielding kaolin clay.

qs.q: Biological chemical weathering occurs when lichens and mosses growing on bare rock surfaces release
o: Organic acids that slowly dissolve rock minerals
qs.e: Lichens produce chelating organic acids that break down rock minerals to extract nutrients.

qs.q: Block disintegration is a physical weathering process in deserts where rocks with distinct joint networks break apart into
o: Large rectangular blocks due to repeated thermal expansion and contraction along joint planes
qs.e: Thermal expansion and contraction along intersecting joint lines causes rocks to split into large blocks.

qs.q: Granite landforms featuring rounded, dome-like rock outcrops formed by deep subsurface chemical weathering followed by stripping of regolith are called
qs.e: Bornhardts (domed inselbergs) form by deep subsurface chemical weathering (etchplanation) followed by stripping.

qs.q: Deep weathering beneath the surface in warm, humid tropical regions where rocks are altered to depths of 30-100 metres is termed
qs.e: Abundant water and high temperatures cause deep chemical weathering (etchplanation) under tropical rain forests.

qs.q: Hydration is a chemical weathering process where mineral grains absorb water into their crystal structure, causing them to
o: Contract and shrink into tight crystals
Expand in volume and exert stress on surrounding minerals
qs.e: Absorbing water expands mineral volume (e.g. anhydrite expanding into gypsum), causing rock disintegration.

qs.q: Which factor accelerates chemical weathering rates most dramatically?
o: High temperatures combined with abundant rainfall and humidity
Freezing temperatures and dry polar winds
Zero soil moisture and desert sand storms
qs.e: Chemical reaction rates double with every 10°C temperature rise, making warm humid tropics prime weathering zones.

qs.q: Stream-lined, sharp-crested rock ridges oriented parallel to the prevailing wind in deserts, carved from vertical bands of hard and soft rock, are called
qs.e: Yardangs form when wind abrasion carves vertical belts of soft rock, leaving standing hard rock ridges.

qs.q: A crescent-shaped sand dune in deserts with its horns or tips pointing downwind in the direction of prevailing wind movement is a
qs.e: Barchans are crescent dunes whose horns point downwind in unidirectional wind regimes.

qs.q: Elongated, steep-sided U-shaped valleys with flat floors carved by alpine valley glaciers are known as
qs.e: Glacial ice plucks and abrades V-shaped river valleys into steep-sided, flat-bottomed U-shaped troughs.

qs.q: Armchair-shaped steep-walled hollows carved into mountain sides by glacial erosion at the head of an alpine valley are called
qs.e: Corries (cirques) are steep-walled bowl-shaped depressions formed by glacial plucking and freeze-thaw.

qs.q: A narrow, knife-edge rock ridge formed between two adjacent eroding glacial cirques is an
qs.e: Arêtes are sharp rock ridges separating two adjacent back-to-back corries.

qs.q: A steep, horn-shaped mountain peak formed when three or more glacial cirques erode backward into a single mountain summit is a
qs.e: Pyramidal peaks (e.g. Matterhorn) form where three or more corries cut back into a single peak.

qs.q: Coastal erosion feature formed when waves erode a hollow through a headland from both sides, creating an arch, which eventually collapses to leave an isolated pillar called a
qs.e: Collapse of a coastal arch roof leaves an isolated standing rock pillar known as a stack.

qs.q: A narrow ridge of sand or shingle connected to the mainland at one end and extending out into open sea across a bay mouth is a
qs.e: Spits form by longshore drift depositing sand across bay indentations.

qs.q: A spit or sandbar that extends all the way across a coastal bay to connect two headlands, trapping a lagoon behind it, is a
qs.e: A bay bar completely seals off a bay mouth, creating an isolated coastal lagoon behind it.

qs.q: A ridge of sand or gravel that connects an offshore island directly to the mainland coastline is called a
qs.e: Tombolos are depositional features connecting an island to the mainland (e.g. Chesil Beach).

qs.q: In Karst limestone landscapes, icicle-like calcium carbonate deposits hanging down from the ceiling of an underground cave are called
qs.e: Stalactites hang from cave ceilings ('hold tight to the ceiling').

qs.q: In Karst caves, calcium carbonate deposits growing upward from the floor formed by dripping mineralized water are
qs.e: Stalagmites grow upward from cave floors ('might reach the top').

qs.q: Which cash crop thrives best in deep, well-drained loamy soils under high temperatures (24-30°C) and heavy rainfall (1,500-2,000 mm) with shade trees in South-Western Nigeria?
qs.e: Cocoa requires warm, humid rainforest conditions with high rainfall and protective forest canopy shade.

qs.q: Terrace farming is an agricultural soil conservation technique practiced on steep mountain slopes to
o: Reduce surface runoff speed, prevent soil erosion, and retain soil moisture
qs.e: Terraces create flat step-like steps on hillsides, slowing surface runoff and trapping topsoil.

qs.q: Market gardening (truck farming) is characterized by intensive cultivation of vegetables, fruits, and flowers close to
qs.e: Truck farming locates near urban markets to deliver perishable produce quickly.

qs.q: Nomadic pastoralism in the semi-arid Sahel region of West Africa is an adaptation to
o: Low, erratic rainfall and sparse seasonal pasture availability
qs.e: Nomads move livestock continuously to follow unpredictable seasonal rainfall and grass growth.

qs.q: Crop rotation preserves soil fertility by
o: Planting cocoa trees exclusively for fifty years
Alternating different crops (e.g. nitrogen-fixing legumes and cereals) sequentially on the same field
Leaving fields flooded with salt water
qs.e: Alternating crops with legumes restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.

qs.q: Which major agricultural cash crop in Northern Nigeria requires sandy-loam soils and a distinct dry season for harvesting and drying?
qs.e: Groundnuts favor light sandy soils in dry savanna belts that allow easy pod harvesting.

qs.q: Green revolution refers to the rapid increase in agricultural crop yields achieved through the adoption of
o: Shifting cultivation and wooden hand hoes
High-yielding seed varieties (HYVs), chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and controlled irrigation
qs.e: Green Revolution technology combines HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation to boost cereal yields.

qs.q: Hydroponics is an intensive modern farming method that involves growing crops
o: In nutrient-rich water solutions without using natural soil
qs.e: Hydroponics cultivates plants in liquid nutrient solutions without soil media.

qs.q: If a scale of 2 cm to 5 km is enlarged 5 times linearly, the new statement scale is
qs.e: Original: 1 cm to 2.5 km. Enlarged 5 times: 1 cm to 0.5 km, which is 2 cm to 1 km.

qs.q: A map drawn to scale 1:250,000 is reduced to one-fifth of its linear size. What is the R.F. of the new map?
qs.e: Reducing by 1/5 multiplies denominator by 5: 250,000 * 5 = 1,250,000.

qs.q: An island measures 10 cm² on a 1:25,000 map. What is the area of the island in square kilometres?
A road of ground length 15 km is represented by 6 cm on a map. What is the Representative Fraction of the map?
A plantation covers an irregular area of 24 cm² on a map scaled 1:50,000. If the map is reduced to one-third of its original size, what is the new map area?
qs.e: Area reduction factor is (1/3)² = 1/9. 24 / 9 = 2.67 cm².

qs.q: A catchment basin measures 36 cm² on a 1:50,000 map. Express its ground area in hectares (1 km² = 100 hectares).
qs.e: 1 cm² at 1:50,000 = 0.25 km². Ground area = 36 * 0.25 = 9 km². 9 km² * 100 = 900 hectares.

qs.q: A map user measures a distance of 18.5 cm between two coastal settlements on a map of scale 1:50,000. The ground distance is
Which technique is used to construct a cross-section profile of terrain from a topographical contour map?
qs.e: Transect profiling plots contour elevation points along a straight base line onto graph paper to show terrain relief.

qs.q: A landform showing closely packed contours that merge together at one point indicates the presence of a
qs.e: When contours touch or merge together on a map, it indicates a vertical cliff or precipice.

qs.q: In a 6-figure grid reference 452816, the digits '45' represent the
qs.e: The first three digits (452) give the Easting position, where '45' is the main Easting line.

qs.q: In a 6-figure grid reference 348921, the digits '92' represent the main
qs.e: The second group of three digits (921) gives the Northing position, where '92' is the main Northing line.

qs.q: An observer at point A (elevation 400 m) looks towards point B (elevation 200 m). If an intervening ridge reaches 450 m, the two points are
qs.e: The intervening ridge at 450 m is higher than both points, blocking line of sight and preventing intervisibility.

qs.q: On a 1:50,000 map, a river drops from 350 m to 150 m elevation over a map distance of 8 cm. What is the gradient of the river bed?
If Magnetic North is 5° West of True North and the magnetic bearing of a church is 085°, what is its true bearing?
qs.e: True bearing = Magnetic bearing - West declination = 085° - 5° = 080°.

qs.q: Two settlements are separated by 10 cm on a 1:100,000 map. Settlement X is at 100 m and Settlement Y is at 300 m. What is the gradient?
A cliff face drops 300 m vertically over a horizontal distance of 150 m. Express its gradient.
qs.e: Gradient = 300 m / 150 m = 2 / 1 (a vertical rise of 2 m per 1 m horizontal distance).

qs.q: A hill slope has a gradient of 1 in 25. Express this gradient as a percentage.
qs.e: Percentage gradient = (1 / 25) * 100 = 4%.

qs.q: A slope gradient of 1 in 20 converted to percentage gradient is equal to
qs.e: Percentage gradient = (1 / 20) * 100 = 5%.

qs.q: A slope gradient of 1 in 5 expressed as a percentage is
qs.e: Percentage gradient = (1 / 5) * 100 = 20%.

qs.q: If a highway gradient is 10%, what is its equivalent expression in 1 in N format?
qs.e: 10% = 10/100 = 1/10, which corresponds to 1 in 10.

qs.q: A pipeline route rises 150 m over a map distance of 15 cm on a 1:50,000 map. Calculate the gradient.
A road gradient of 2.5% corresponds to a ratio gradient of
If a station has an annual temperature range of 1°C and total rainfall of 3,100 mm, it is located near the
qs.e: Minimal temperature range with extremely heavy annual rainfall is characteristic of equatorial lowlands.

qs.q: In interpreting a climate graph, a thermal anomaly where high temperatures occur just before the onset of rains in April/May is typical of
qs.e: Tropical monsoon regions reach peak temperatures right before summer monsoon rains bring cloud cover and cooling.

qs.q: If a climate graph shows monthly rainfall totals of [10, 15, 40, 80, 150, 220, 280, 310, 240, 110, 20, 5] mm, the total annual rainfall is
What type of climate graph is characterized by monthly temperatures remaining below 0°C for eight months of the year?
qs.e: Tundra and polar climates have long freezing winters where monthly temperatures stay below 0°C for most of the year.

qs.q: A station records temperatures of 28°C (Jan), 31°C (Mar), 35°C (May), 27°C (Aug), 29°C (Oct), 27°C (Dec). Why is August cooler than May?
o: Sun is overhead at the Antarctic Circle in August
Cold ocean currents move inland in August
Harmattan winds blow strongly in August
Heavy cloud cover and rainfall during the peak monsoon period reduce surface solar radiation
qs.e: Dense monsoon cloud cover and rain evaporation in August lower ground temperatures compared to dry pre-monsoon May.

qs.q: Station X (elevation 50 m) and Station Y (elevation 1,550 m) are at the same latitude. If Station X has a mean annual temp of 27°C, estimate Station Y temp using standard lapse rate (6.5°C per 1,000 m).
qs.e: Elevation difference = 1,500 m. Temp drop = 1.5 * 6.5 = 9.75°C. Station Y temp = 27 - 9.75 = 17.25°C.

qs.q: Which state in Nigeria has the lowest average population density due to vast savanna expanses and historical factors?
qs.e: Niger State is Nigeria's largest state by land mass but has a very low population density.

qs.q: Brain drain refers to the international migration of
o: Highly skilled professionals and educated individuals seeking better opportunities abroad
qs.e: Brain drain is the outflow of doctors, engineers, teachers, and specialists from developing to developed countries.

qs.q: A population pyramid with a narrow base and broad top/middle sections is typical of a country in Demographic Transition Stage
o: Stage 4 (Low birth rate, low death rate, aging population)
qs.e: Stage 4 pyramids (e.g. in Western Europe) feature narrow bases (low birth rates) and broad upper sections (aging population).

qs.q: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is expressed as the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per
o: 1,000 live births in a given year
qs.e: IMR measures infant deaths under age 1 per 1,000 live births annually.

qs.q: Total Fertility Rate (TFR) measures the average number of children
o: A woman would bear during her childbearing years (ages 15-49)
Surviving past five years of age
qs.e: TFR represents the average number of children born per woman across her reproductive lifetime.

qs.q: Which of the following describes physiological population density?
o: Total population divided by total geographic land area
Urban population divided by total land area
Total population divided by arable (cultivable) land area
Rural population divided by forest area
qs.e: Physiological density measures population pressure specifically on arable agricultural land.

qs.q: Agricultural density is defined as the number of
o: Total people per unit of total land
Farmers per unit of arable land
qs.e: Agricultural density divides the total rural farmer population by the total area of arable land.

qs.q: If a country's population grows at a constant annual rate of 3.5%, using the Rule of 70, how many years will it take for the population to double?
qs.e: Doubling time = 70 / annual growth rate (%) = 70 / 3.5 = 20 years.

qs.q: A country with 45,000,000 people and 900,000 km² land area has 15% arable land. What is its physiological population density?
qs.e: Total land = 900,000 km². Arable land = 15% of 900,000 = 135,000 km². Physiological density = 45,000,000 / 135,000 = 333.3 persons/km².

qs.q: If CBR is 38/1000, CDR is 10/1000, Immigration rate is 5/1000, and Emigration rate is 3/1000, what is the total population growth rate?
qs.e: Growth rate = (CBR - CDR) + (Immigration - Emigration) = (38 - 10) + (5 - 3) = 28 + 2 = 30 per 1,000 (3.0%).

qs.q: In Nigeria, marble deposits are quarried for industrial processing at Lokoja, Ibeto, and
qs.e: Jakura near Lokoja in Kogi State hosts major industrial marble quarries.

qs.q: The Hadejia-Nguru wetlands in North-Eastern Nigeria are ecologically important as a sanctuary for
qs.e: Hadejia-Nguru wetlands (Ramsar site) provide critical wintering habitat for palaearctic migratory birds.

qs.q: Which cash crop was introduced heavily into the Middle Belt of Nigeria around Niger and Benue states?
qs.e: Beniseed and soybeans are major cash crops produced in the Middle Belt (Nasarawa, Benue, Niger).

qs.q: Bitumen deposits in Nigeria occur in a continuous belt stretching across which states?
qs.e: Vast tar sand (bitumen) belt runs through Ondo, Ogun, Lagos, and Edo states.

qs.q: Which plateau in Northern Nigeria separates the headwaters of rivers flowing into Lake Chad from those flowing into the River Niger?
qs.e: The Jos Plateau forms Nigeria's primary hydrological apex, dividing drainage between River Niger/Benue and Lake Chad.

qs.q: The Biu Plateau in Borno State is geographically distinct from the Jos Plateau because it was formed by
qs.e: Biu Plateau is a volcanic plateau composed of young basaltic lava flows and cinder cones.

qs.q: In Nigeria, sugarcane cultivation for industrial refining at Bacita is favored by alluvial soils along the valley of River
qs.e: Bacita sugarcane plantation in Kwara State benefits from fertile alluvial floodplains along the Niger valley.

qs.q: Why is cattle rearing in Southern Nigeria restricted compared to the Northern savanna belt?
o: High humidity and tsetse fly infestation carrying trypanosomiasis
qs.e: Humid forest conditions harbor tsetse flies, which transmit nagana to non-resistant cattle breeds.

qs.q: Which mode of transport is most vulnerable to weather disruptions such as thick fog, Harmattan haze, and thunderstorms?
qs.e: Poor visibility from Harmattan dust haze or severe storms frequently grounds air traffic.

qs.q: The railway line from Lagos through Ibadan to Kano was built during the colonial era primarily to
o: Evacuate cash crops (groundnut, cotton, cocoa) to seaports for export
Promote tourism across savanna game reserves
qs.e: Colonial railways were built as extraction corridors from interior crop/mineral belts to coastal export ports.

qs.q: Which factor explains why air transport carries a very small fraction of total freight volume despite covering long distances quickly?
o: Lack of international airports in Africa
High freight tariffs per unit weight and strict payload limits
Slow loading speeds at air terminals
qs.e: High cost per kilogram restricts air freight to light, high-value, or time-sensitive items like medical supplies.

qs.q: The dredging of the Lower River Niger from Lokoja to Onitsha and Baro aims to achieve a minimum draft of
o: 2.5 to 3.0 metres for year-round barge navigation
qs.e: Dredging ensures a 2.5-3m channel depth so river barges can transport bulk cargo year-round.

qs.q: Which transportation metric measures the amount of freight transported multiplied by the distance traveled?
qs.e: Ton-kilometres (or ton-miles) measure freight transport performance.

qs.q: Coastal shipping between domestic sea ports within the same country is known as
qs.e: Cabotage refers to coastal maritime transport and trade conducted between ports of the same nation.

qs.q: A transport network metric that compares the actual number of links in a network to the maximum possible links between nodes is called
qs.e: The Gamma index measures transport network connectivity by comparing actual links to potential links.

qs.q: Which physical geographical constraint heavily raised the construction cost of the Eastern Railway across Benue State?
o: Cutting through volcanic lava pipes on Biu Plateau
Tunneling through granite rocks in Sokoto
Bridging wide floodplains and the River Benue at Makurdi
qs.e: Building the massive rail-road bridge across the wide Benue River at Makurdi required major engineering.

qs.q: Why is intra-regional trade among West African ECOWAS nations historically low (below 15% of total trade)?
o: ECOWAS countries share a single currency
Highways between member states do not exist
Customs duties are 0% across all borders
Member states produce similar primary agricultural/mineral commodities and lack industrial complementarity
qs.e: West African economies mostly export raw commodities to Europe/Asia rather than complementary manufactured goods to neighbors.

qs.q: A Free Trade Zone (FTZ) or Export Processing Zone (EPZ) is a designated area where businesses enjoy
o: Exemption from customs duties, tax holidays, and streamlined regulatory procedures
Free electricity provided by government permanently
Mandatory state ownership of company shares
qs.e: FTZs attract export-oriented manufacturing by offering tax incentives and duty-free import of raw materials.

qs.q: Trade protectionism is economic policy intended to protect domestic industries by
o: Eliminating all import duties on foreign manufactured goods
Imposing tariffs, quotas, and non-tariff barriers on foreign imports
Encouraging foreign firms to dump cheap goods
qs.e: Protectionism uses trade barriers to shield domestic producers from foreign competition.

qs.q: If a country's Export Price Index is 120 and its Import Price Index is 150, what is its Terms of Trade index?
qs.e: Terms of Trade = (Export Index / Import Index) * 100 = (120 / 150) * 100 = 80.0.

qs.q: The theory of Comparative Advantage formulated by David Ricardo states that a country should specialize in producing goods that it can produce at a lower
o: Absolute wage rate in local currency
Opportunity cost relative to other nations
qs.e: Comparative advantage focuses on relative opportunity cost efficiency between trading nations.

qs.q: If an oil-exporting nation experiences a 40% drop in crude oil prices while import prices for food and machinery rise by 10%, its Terms of Trade index changes by
qs.e: New Export Index = 60; New Import Index = 110. New TOT = (60 / 110) * 100 = 54.5.

qs.q: Which non-tariff trade barrier involves complex administrative procedures, stringent health standards, and delays at customs designed to hinder imports?
o: Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) and sanitary regulations
qs.e: Non-tariff barriers use technical, safety, and bureaucratic procedures to restrict foreign imports subtly.

qs.q: In Weber's industrial location model, a Material Index (MI) greater than 1.0 indicates that the industry is
o: Weight-gaining and should locate near markets
Weight-losing and should locate near raw material sources
qs.e: MI = Weight of localized raw materials / Weight of finished product. MI > 1 means weight loss during production, pulling location to raw materials.

qs.q: High-tech manufacturing corridors (like Silicon Valley or M4 Corridor) that rely on university research labs and venture capital are examples of
qs.e: Technopoles are science and technology parks integrating research institutes and high-tech firms.

qs.q: Industrial inertia occurs when a manufacturing plant
o: Remains in its original location even after the original geographical advantages have disappeared
Moves to a new location every three years
qs.e: Inertia happens because fixed capital investment and established supply chains keep factories in place despite lost initial advantages.

qs.q: A brewery uses 2 tons of local water (ubiquitous) and 1 ton of imported barley/hops (localized) to produce 3 tons of beer. Under Weber's model, where should the brewery locate?
qs.e: Because water is available everywhere (ubiquitous) and finished beer is heavy and bulky to transport, the brewery locates at the market.

qs.q: Columbite, mined alongside tin on the Jos Plateau, is an important mineral used in the manufacture of
o: Heat-resistant steel alloys for jet engines and space rockets
qs.e: Niobium from columbite provides high thermal resistance in specialized aerospace steel alloys.

qs.q: Environmental degradation caused by un-reclaimed mining pits on the Jos Plateau includes
o: Landscape scarification, water-logged abandoned pits, and loss of arable farm land
qs.e: Tin mining left extensive unreclaimed open pits across the Jos Plateau landscape.

qs.q: Geothermal energy is a renewable energy resource derived from heat stored in
o: Earth's subterranean magma and hot rock formations
qs.e: Geothermal energy taps natural steam and hot water in volcanic or tectonic zones.

qs.q: Resource curse (Dutch Disease) in mineral-rich developing economies refers to the economic phenomenon where
o: Mineral deposits vanish overnight due to chemical weathering
A boom in natural resource exports inflates the currency exchange rate, making agricultural and manufacturing sectors uncompetitive
Excessive coal mining causes severe regional earthquakes
Foreign mining firms ban local workers
qs.e: Dutch disease occurs when resource export booms appreciate real exchange rates, harming other export sectors.

qs.q: Low-order central places (e.g. small rural villages) provide low-order goods characterized by
o: Large ranges and huge threshold catchments
Small threshold populations and short ranges purchased frequently (e.g. salt, soap)
qs.e: Low-order convenience goods are bought frequently with minimal travel distance.

qs.q: Counter-urbanisation is a demographic trend in developed countries where people move from
o: Rural villages into high-density city centers
Major urban cities into rural areas and small towns
qs.e: Counter-urbanisation involves population decentralization from major cities into rural areas.

qs.q: The Rank-Size Rule for urban settlements states that the nth largest city in a country will have a population equal to
o: 1/n times the population of the largest city
n times the population of the smallest city
The square root of the total national population
qs.e: Rank-Size Rule (Zipf's Law) predicts P_n = P_1 / n.

qs.q: Gentrification in inner-city urban neighborhoods involves the process where
o: Urban land is converted into corn fields
Deteriorating urban housing is renovated by wealthier residents, raising property values and displacing lower-income tenants
Highways are demolished to build canals
qs.e: Gentrification reinvests private capital into historic inner-city housing, altering demographics.

qs.q: If the largest city in a nation following the Rank-Size Rule has 8,000,000 inhabitants, what is the expected population of the 4th ranked city?
Urban heat island effect causes metropolitan centers to maintain higher surface temperatures than rural surroundings due to
o: Higher atmospheric pressure over rural fields
Geothermal lava flows under city streets
High absorption of solar heat by asphalt and concrete, reduced vegetation evapotranspiration, and waste heat emissions
qs.e: Urban building materials and artificial heat emissions trap thermal energy in urban centers.

qs.q: The International Date Line (IDL) located near 180° longitude deviates from a straight line across the Pacific Ocean to avoid
o: Dividing island groups and national territories into two different calendar dates
High volcanic activity in the Ring of Fire
qs.e: The IDL bends around landmasses so island nations maintain a uniform calendar date.

qs.q: When crossing the International Date Line from West to East (e.g. from Asia to North America), a traveler must
o: Subtract one day (repeat a calendar date)
Set the watch back by 1 hour
qs.e: Crossing from West to East across 180° gains 24 hours, requiring the traveler to repeat a calendar day.

qs.q: If a football match starts in London (0° longitude) at 4:00 PM GMT, at what local time can viewers in Tokyo (135°E) watch the live broadcast?
qs.e: Time difference = 135° / 15° = 9 hours ahead. 4:00 PM + 9 hours = 1:00 AM the following day.

qs.q: The rain-shadow area on the leeward side of a mountain range receives low rainfall because the descending air
o: Gains massive water vapor from clouds
Warms adiabatically, absorbs moisture, and decreases in relative humidity
qs.e: Air descending the leeward slope warms adiabatically, suppressing cloud formation and creating dry conditions.

qs.q: An inversion of temperature occurs when air temperature
o: Increases with altitude instead of decreasing
Decreases at double the standard lapse rate
qs.e: Temperature inversion traps a layer of warm air above cooler air near the ground.

qs.q: In the Koppen climate classification, the letter code 'Af' denotes a
o: Tropical Savanna climate with dry winters
Tropical Rainforest climate with high rainfall in all months
qs.e: In Koppen's system, 'A' stands for tropical humid and 'f' indicates fully humid with no dry season.

qs.q: The Fohn or Chinook wind is a warm, dry wind that descends on the leeward side of mountain ranges due to
o: Adiabatic heating of dry descending air at the Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (10°C per 1,000 m)
qs.e: Descending air warms at the dry adiabatic rate (~10°C/1000m), making the wind warm and dry.

qs.q: Which cold ocean current washes the western coast of South America, producing the extremely dry Atacama Desert?
qs.e: The cold Peru (Humboldt) Current drives extreme coastal aridity in Chile and Peru.

qs.q: The Kuroshio Current in the North Pacific Ocean is a warm current analogous in position and behavior to the Atlantic's
qs.e: Kuroshio is the western boundary warm current of the North Pacific, equivalent to the Atlantic Gulf Stream.

qs.q: Deep ocean water upwelling occurs along certain coasts when prevailing offshore winds drag surface water away, bringing up
o: Nutrient-rich cold water that supports dense marine food webs
qs.e: Upwelling brings cold, nutrient-laden bottom waters to the surface, boosting plankton and fish populations.

qs.q: The atmospheric-oceanic phenomenon where the trade winds weaken and cold upwelling off Peru ceases, causing collapse of fisheries, is called
qs.e: El Nino suppresses cold upwelling off Peru, devastating plankton and anchovy fisheries.

qs.q: Quartzite is a hard metamorphic rock formed from the metamorphism of
qs.e: Quartz sandstone recrystallizes under high temperature and pressure to form quartzite.

qs.q: Gneiss is a high-grade foliated metamorphic rock characterized by distinct light and dark mineral bands, formed from
qs.e: Granite subjected to extreme regional metamorphism develops banded mineral texture (gneiss).

qs.q: Fossils are almost exclusively preserved and found within which major rock class?
qs.e: Sedimentary deposition preserves organic remains; igneous heat and metamorphic pressure destroy fossils.

qs.q: Coal is an organically formed sedimentary rock formed over millions of years from the compaction and carbonization of ancient
o: Dense swamp vegetation and plant matter
qs.e: Coal originates from compressed, anaerobic decay of ancient forest and swamp vegetation.

qs.q: Gully erosion differs from rill erosion because gullies form
o: Tiny rivulets easily erased by harrowing
Deep, wide channels that cannot be smoothed out by normal farm plowing
qs.e: Gullies are large, permanent erosional chasms cut by concentrated surface runoff.

qs.q: Plants adapted to survive in dry desert environments with minimal rainfall are called
qs.e: Xerophytes possess specialized structures (succulence, thorns, deep roots) for arid conditions.

qs.q: Mangrove vegetation in tropical estuaries possesses specialized breathing roots that stick out above oxygen-poor mud, called
qs.e: Pneumatophores emerge above water level to absorb atmospheric oxygen in anaerobic tidal mud.

qs.q: A Soil Catena refers to a sequence of different soil profiles occurring along a slope gradient due to differences in
o: Relief, drainage, and water movement from hilltop to valley bottom
qs.e: Catenas show soil variation down a slope driven by relief and hydrological drainage.

qs.q: Corestones are rounded boulders of unweathered bedrock left behind in a soil matrix when surrounding rock undergoes
o: Deep subsurface spheroidal weathering along joint sets
qs.e: Spheroidal weathering attacks rectangular rock blocks along joints, rounding corners to leave solid corestones.

qs.q: A mudflow differs from a landslide because a mudflow consists of
o: A highly fluid, saturated mass of fine-grained soil and water moving rapidly down river channels
Dry angular rock blocks sliding down cliffs
Slow movement of topsoil over permafrost
qs.e: Mudflows are fluid slurry mixtures of water and fine sediment traveling rapidly along valleys.

qs.q: Which weathering process is primarily responsible for the formation of sinkholes and caverns in Karst limestone regions?
qs.e: Carbonic acid in groundwater dissolves calcium carbonate along joints, creating underground caverns and sinkholes.

qs.q: The angle of repose is the maximum slope angle at which loose weathered material remains stable without
o: Slumping or sliding downslope under gravity
qs.e: Angle of repose is the threshold slope angle for loose granular materials before mass movement occurs.

qs.q: Spheroidal weathering occurs underground when water penetrates jointed rock blocks, attacking them from all sides and rounding off the sharp edges because
o: Underground earthworms rub rock corners smooth
Subterranean rivers carry sand blasting tools
Corners and edges have greater surface area exposed to chemical weathering than flat faces
qs.e: Rock corners expose three faces to chemical attack, weathering faster than flat faces and yielding rounded corestones.

qs.q: The formation of tors on granite landscapes (such as in South-West England or Jos Plateau) is explained by two-stage weathering involving
o: Deep subsurface chemical weathering along joints followed by surface stripping of loose regolith by erosion
Volcanic ash explosions followed by glacial gouging
Wind abrasion followed by marine submergence
Frost shattering followed by coral reef growth
qs.e: Tors form when subsurface chemical weathering rots jointed granite, followed by erosional stripping of saprolite.

qs.q: Salt crystallization (haloclasty) is a physical weathering process common in coastal and arid regions where saline water evaporates in rock pores, causing
o: Growing salt crystals to exert internal pressure that disintegrates the rock surface
qs.e: Evaporating salt water leaves growing salt crystals that force pore walls apart, causing honeycomb weathering.

qs.q: Etchplain formation theory states that tropical inselbergs emerge when
o: Glaciers carve steep U-shaped troughs through flat coastal plains
Wind dunes solidify into sandstone towers
A change in climate or tectonic uplift leads to stripping of deeply weathered saprolite, exposing resistant unweathered bedrock domes
Volcanic lava flows cool inside ocean basins
qs.e: Etchplanation produces inselbergs when stripping removes rotted rock (saprolite) to expose underlying resistant rock.

qs.q: River capture (stream piracy) occurs when an actively eroding river cuts back by headward erosion through a watershed and
o: Flows backward into an ocean trench
Deposits all its sediment load in a desert playa
Intercepts and diverts the headwaters of a neighboring weaker stream
qs.e: Headward erosion allows a powerful stream to breach a divide and capture an adjacent river's upper flow.

qs.q: The point along a captured river course where its flow was diverted into the capturing river, marked by a sharp bend, is the
qs.e: Elbow of capture is the right-angled bend where the intercepted stream diverts into the pirate stream.

qs.q: An abandoned dry valley left downstream of an elbow of capture where river flow was intercepted is called a
qs.e: Wind gaps are dry mountain passes representing former river valleys whose water was diverted by capture.

qs.q: River rejuvenation occurs when a change in base level (e.g. tectonic uplift or sea level drop) causes a river to
o: Deposit its entire sediment load and dry up
Flow backward towards its source mountain
Renew vertical downcutting and erode deeply into its former floodplain
qs.e: Rejuvenation restores erosional energy, causing the river to cut down into its bed and form terraces.

qs.q: A sharp break in a river's longitudinal profile representing the junction between its old grading and a new rejuvenated profile is a
qs.e: Knick points (often marked by waterfalls or rapids) mark the upstream migration of rejuvenation.

qs.q: Deeply incised meanders with steep valley walls carved when a meandering river undergoes rapid rejuvenation are termed
qs.e: Incised meanders form when rejuvenation forces a meandering river to erode vertically into bedrock.

qs.q: Longshore drift refers to the zig-zag movement of sand and shingle along a beach driven by
o: Tidal waves pulling sand straight into deep water
Swash approaching at an angle with prevailing winds and backwash returning perpendicular under gravity
qs.e: Angled swash pushes sediment up the beach at an angle; backwash pulls it straight down the slope.

qs.q: Smooth, asymmetric bedrock hills carved by glaciers, featuring a smooth abraded stoss side and a steep plucked lee side, are called
qs.e: Roches moutonnées show smooth ice-scoured stoss slopes and steep plucked lee slopes.

qs.q: Elongated, teardrop-shaped hills of glacial till streamlined by ice flow, with the blunt end facing up-glacier, are
qs.e: Drumlins are streamlined depositional mounds of till formed under moving ice sheets.

qs.q: Winding, narrow ridges of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing inside sub-glacial tunnels are
qs.e: Eskers represent fossilized sub-glacial stream beds composed of sorted glaciofluvial gravels.

qs.q: A funnel-shaped, drowned river valley at a coastline formed by rising sea levels or land subsidence is an
qs.e: Estuaries (rias) form when sea level rise submerges lower river valleys.

qs.q: A steep-sided, deep glacial trough submerged by rising sea levels along mountainous coastlines is a
qs.e: Fiords are glaciated U-shaped mountain valleys inundated by post-glacial sea level rise.

qs.q: Which environmental factor is the primary limit to crop production in the Sahelian agricultural zone of West Africa?
o: Low, highly variable annual rainfall and frequent droughts
qs.e: Moisture deficiency and short rainy seasons severely restrict crop choices in the Sahel.

qs.q: Commercial grain farming (e.g. wheat growing on the North American Prairies) is characterized by
o: Extensive land area, heavy mechanization, low labor input per hectare, and high output per worker
Tiny hand-weeded plots and high labor per hectare
qs.e: Extensive grain farming uses massive farm machinery over vast acreage with minimal human labor per hectare.

qs.q: Intensive wet rice cultivation in South-East Asia differs from commercial grain farming because wet rice farming relies on
o: Huge combine harvesters on 5,000 hectare dry fields
High human manual labor input per unit area, small farm plots, and flooded paddy fields
qs.e: Paddy rice farming uses intensive family labor for transplanting, weeding, and harvesting small terraced fields.

qs.q: Von Thunen's Regional Model of Agricultural Land Use posits that crop zones surround a central market city in concentric rings based on
o: Transportation costs and land rent (locational rent) of different farm products
qs.e: Von Thunen showed that perishable or bulky goods locate near central markets to minimize freight costs.

qs.q: In Von Thunen's land use model, which agricultural activity occupies the innermost ring directly surrounding the central market town?
o: Dairying and intensive market gardening (perishable goods)
qs.e: Perishable milk and fresh vegetables command the highest locational rent and sit closest to the market.

qs.q: If a map scaled 1:100,000 is copied such that 1 cm² on the original becomes 16 cm² on the copy, what is the linear scale of the copy?
qs.e: Area enlarged 16 times means linear scale enlarged sqrt(16) = 4 times. Denominator: 100,000 / 4 = 25,000.

qs.q: A map with scale 1:X is enlarged by a linear factor of 2.5, resulting in a new scale of 1:20,000. What was the original scale 1:X?
qs.e: Enlarging by 2.5 divides the denominator by 2.5. Thus X / 2.5 = 20,000 => X = 50,000.

qs.q: On a map of scale 1:50,000, a triangular reservoir has base 6 cm and height 4 cm. What is its actual area in hectares?
qs.e: Triangle map area = 0.5 * 6 * 4 = 12 cm². At 1:50,000, 1 cm² = 0.25 km² = 25 hectares. 12 * 25 = 300 hectares.

qs.q: A drainage pattern exhibiting stream capture, wind gaps, and incised meanders is characteristic of a landscape that has undergone
qs.e: Rejuvenation revives river erosional energy, leading to incised meanders, stream capture, and knick points.

qs.q: Point A is at grid reference 120400 (elevation 500 m) and Point B is at 160400 (elevation 100 m) on a 1:50,000 map. If grid squares are 1 km by 1 km, what is the gradient between A and B?
qs.e: Easting distance = 16 - 12 = 4 grid units = 4 km = 4000 m (HD). VI = 500 - 100 = 400 m. Gradient = 400 / 4000 = 1 in 10.

qs.q: An observer at Point P (elevation 100 m) attempts to view Point Q (elevation 300 m) 6 km away across a uniform convex slope. The line of sight will be
o: Clear because Q is higher than P
Obstructed by the bulging curvature of the convex slope
Unobstructed due to constant slope angle
Blocked only if vegetation exceeds 100 m
qs.e: On a convex slope, the land bulges upward along the middle section, obstructing sight between lower and upper points.

qs.q: A mountain path rises from 200 m to 800 m elevation. If the gradient is 1 in 8, what map distance in cm represents this path on a 1:50,000 map?
If a river falls 40 m over a course length of 10 km, what is its average gradient in metres per kilometre?
qs.e: Gradient per km = 40 m / 10 km = 4 m/km.

qs.q: Two points A (150 m) and B (650 m) are separated by 5 cm on a map. If the gradient between them is 1 in 10, what is the scale denominator of the map?
A civil engineer designing a mountain highway requires that the slope not exceed a gradient of 1 in 20 (5%). If the elevation gain is 350 m, what is the minimum real-world road distance required?
qs.e: Minimum H.D. = 350 m * 20 = 7,000 m = 7 km.

qs.q: On a 1:50,000 topographical map, the distance between contour line 100 m and contour line 500 m is 4 cm along Route A and 8 cm along Route B. The ratio of the gradient along Route A to Route B is
qs.e: V.I. is 400 m for both. Route A H.D. = 2000 m (grad 1/5). Route B H.D. = 4000 m (grad 1/10). Ratio (1/5) : (1/10) = 2:1.

qs.q: Comparing two climate graphs, Station A has an annual temp range of 3°C while Station B has an annual temp range of 28°C. This indicates that
o: Station A is desert while Station B is ocean island
Station A is polar while Station B is tropical
Station A has higher elevation than Station B
Station A is maritime/equatorial while Station B is continental/high-latitude
qs.e: Small temperature ranges signify maritime or equatorial locations, whereas large ranges indicate high-latitude continental landmasses.

qs.q: Station Z records monthly temperatures [20, 22, 25, 28, 26, 23, 21, 21, 23, 25, 24, 21]°C and rainfall concentrated in Dec-Feb. In which hemisphere and climate zone is Station Z located?
qs.e: Rainfall during Dec-Feb (Southern Hemisphere winter/rainy period) with mild summer temperatures indicates a Southern Hemisphere Mediterranean climate.

qs.q: A climatologist analyzes a graph with annual temp of 26°C, annual temp range of 2°C, total annual rainfall of 2,200 mm, and a brief 1-month rainfall drop to 45 mm. Under Köppen classification, this is
qs.e: Köppen classifies high-rainfall tropical climates with a short dry season where rainfall drops slightly below 60 mm as Tropical Monsoon (Am).

qs.q: In a population of 10,000,000, there are 3,500,000 children (0-14) and 500,000 elderly (65+). Calculate the working-age population and dependency ratio.
qs.e: Working pop = 10M - (3.5M + 0.5M) = 6M. Dependency ratio = 4M / 6M * 100 = 66.7%.

qs.q: A region of 200,000 km² has 60,000 km² of arable land. Its rural farming population is 3,000,000 and total population is 12,000,000. Calculate its arithmetic density and agricultural density.
o: Arithmetic = 60 persons/km²; Agricultural = 50 farmers/km² of arable land
qs.e: Arithmetic density = 12M / 200k = 60 persons/km². Agricultural density = 3M farmers / 60k arable km² = 50 farmers/km².

qs.q: If a nation's population pyramid exhibits a pronounced constriction between ages 20 and 34 for males only, the primary demographic driver is
o: Selective male out-migration or war casualties
Rapid drop in crude birth rate 20 years ago
qs.e: A gender-specific indentation in young adult age cohorts indicates male emigration for work or war mortality.

qs.q: The Gongola River is a major tributary that joins the River Benue at
qs.e: River Gongola flows south through Bauchi and Gombe before merging with River Benue at Numan.

qs.q: Highland temperate vegetation featuring eucalyptus trees and short mountain grasses is found in Nigeria on the
qs.e: Cool climate at high elevations on Mambilla and Jos plateaux supports temperate grasses and planted eucalyptus.

qs.q: The Sokoto Basin in North-Western Nigeria is composed geologically of marine and continental sedimentary rocks of which era?
qs.e: Sokoto Basin forms part of the Iullemmeden Basin consisting of Cretaceous and Tertiary sediments overlying basement rock.

qs.q: Which factor accounts for the existence of an isolated dry pocket (drought corridor) along the coastal belt near Accra and parts of South-Western Togo/Benin?
o: Coastal orientation parallel to moisture-bearing winds and upwelling of cold Benguela waters
qs.e: The Dahomey Gap occurs because SW monsoon winds blow parallel to the coastline and cold water upwelling reduces cloud formation.

qs.q: The Cross River estuary and adjacent coastal mangrove zone differ from the western Niger Delta primarily by receiving higher annual rainfall exceeding
qs.e: South-Eastern coastal Nigeria (around Debundscha and Calabar) receives over 4,000 mm of annual rainfall.

qs.q: The concept of 'Break-of-Bulk point' in transport geography refers to a location where
o: A railway line reaches a dead end in a desert
Heavy trucks break down due to overload
Cargo must be transferred from one mode of transport to another
Goods are manufactured from raw iron
qs.e: Break-of-bulk points (e.g. seaports) occur where freight changes transport mode, attracting processing industries.

qs.q: In transport geography, the 'Detour Index' evaluates network efficiency by calculating the ratio of
o: Total fuel consumed to total distance
Actual route distance to direct straight-line distance between two points
qs.e: Detour index compares actual travel distance along a winding road to the shortest straight-line distance.

qs.q: An industrial analyst evaluates transport costs: Terminal handling cost = $50 fixed; Long-distance hauling cost = $0.10/km by rail vs $0.30/km by road. At what distance does rail become cheaper than road?
The economic principle explaining why transport cost per unit distance decreases as total distance increases is known as the
qs.e: The tapering principle reflects fixed terminal costs being spread over longer distances, lowering per-km rates.

qs.q: A Customs Union differs from a Free Trade Area because member states of a Customs Union must also adopt a
o: Common External Tariff (CET) against non-member nations
qs.e: A Customs Union establishes a uniform tariff wall (CET) applied by all member countries against external imports.

qs.q: Country A can produce 10 tons of wheat or 5 cars per worker. Country B can produce 6 tons of wheat or 2 cars per worker. Which statement is correct?
o: Country A has comparative advantage in wheat, Country B in cars
Country B has absolute advantage in both wheat and cars
Neither country can benefit from trade
Country A has comparative advantage in cars, while Country B has comparative advantage in wheat
qs.e: Country A opportunity cost of 1 car = 2 wheat. Country B opportunity cost of 1 car = 3 wheat. Country A produces cars cheaper (2 < 3), Country B produces wheat cheaper (1/3 < 1/2 car).

qs.q: The 'Marshall-Lerner Condition' in international economics states that a currency devaluation will improve a nation's trade balance only if the sum of price elasticities of demand for exports and imports is
qs.e: The Marshall-Lerner condition specifies that export and import demand elasticities combined must exceed unity for devaluation to cure a trade deficit.

qs.q: Deindustrialization in older industrial regions (e.g. the Rust Belt) is characterized by
o: Rapid increase in heavy steel production
Decline in manufacturing employment and shifting of production to low-cost offshore regions
Migration of urban workers to traditional farms
Complete elimination of service sector jobs
qs.e: Deindustrialization reflects structural economic transition from heavy manufacturing to service economies.

qs.q: Under Weber's location model, an industry uses two localized raw materials: M1 (weight 4 tons) and M2 (weight 2 tons) to produce 3 tons of finished product P. The Material Index is
o: 2.0 (Weight-losing, pulled towards raw material location triangle)
qs.e: MI = Total localized raw materials weight / Finished product weight = (4 + 2) / 3 = 6 / 3 = 2.0.

qs.q: Which technique is employed in alluvial mining to separate dense gold or tin grains from lighter river gravels using running water?
qs.e: Placer mining utilizes water washing to settle heavy mineral grains out of lighter gravels.

qs.q: The Hubbert Peak Theory models the production curve of finite non-renewable resources (like crude oil) as following a
o: Symmetrical bell-shaped curve where extraction reaches a maximum peak before irreversible decline
Linear line continuously rising to infinity
Horizontal straight line at constant volume
qs.e: Hubbert's peak predicts that resource extraction follows a bell-shaped curve peaking when half the reserve is depleted.

qs.q: A megalopolis is defined as an extensive urban region formed by the merging of
o: Multiple adjacent metropolitan conurbations stretching across hundreds of kilometres
qs.e: Megalopolis (e.g. BosWash corridor in USA) connects multiple metropolitan areas into a massive urban chain.

qs.q: Which urban land use zone typically experiences the highest land values and steepest bid-rent competition?
o: Peak Land Value Intersection (PLVI) within the CBD
qs.e: PLVI represents the accessible intersection in the CBD with maximum land rent.

qs.q: William Alonso's Bid-Rent Theory explains that land use patterns radiate outward from the CBD because different activities have varying willingness to pay land rent based on
qs.e: Bid-rent theory shows commercial activities outbid residential and agricultural uses for high-accessibility central land.

qs.q: If a nation exhibits a Primate City distribution where the largest city has 12,000,000 people and the second largest has only 1,500,000, this indicates severe
o: Spatial imbalance in national urban development and economic centralization
qs.e: Extreme primacy reflects hyper-concentration of economic capital and political power in a single urban core.

qs.q: At 12:00 noon local time at Longitude 15°E, a solar observation radio signal is transmitted to a ship where local time is 8:30 AM. What is the ship's longitude?
qs.e: Time difference = 12:00 - 8:30 = 3.5 hours = 210 minutes. Longitude diff = 210 / 4 min per deg = 52.5°. Ship is West of 15°E: 15° - 52.5° = 37.5°W.

qs.q: An airplane departs City P (45°W) at 10:00 AM local time on a 10-hour flight to City Q (75°E). What is the local time in City Q when the flight arrives?
qs.e: Longitude diff = 45° + 75° = 120° = 8 hours ahead. Departure time in City Q time = 10:00 AM + 8 hrs = 6:00 PM. Arrival time = 6:00 PM + 10 hrs flight = 4:00 AM next day.

qs.q: El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) involves the anomalous warming of surface ocean waters in the
o: Central and Eastern Tropical Pacific Ocean, disrupting global weather patterns
qs.e: El Nino warms Eastern Pacific waters, causing droughts in Australia/Indonesia and heavy floods in South America.

qs.q: If saturated air at 20°C rises over a 3,000 m mountain, cooling at the Saturated Adiabatic Lapse Rate (5°C/1000m), and then descends the leeward side to sea level at the Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (10°C/1000m), its final temperature is
qs.e: Ascent: Temp drops 3 * 5 = 15°C to 5°C at peak (3000m). Descent: Temp rises 3 * 10 = 30°C. Final temp = 5 + 30 = 35°C.

qs.q: The thermohaline circulation (Global Conveyor Belt) in deep oceans is driven primarily by differences in water
o: Temperature (thermal) and salinity (haline), which alter water density
qs.e: Cold, highly saline water sinks in polar regions, driving global deep-water density circulation.

qs.q: In the North Atlantic ocean gyre, oceanic circulation moves in a clockwise direction primarily due to the combined action of
o: Counter-clockwise Coriolis force and Polar Easterlies
Trade winds, Westerlies, and clockwise Coriolis deflection in the Northern Hemisphere
qs.e: Subtropical gyres rotate clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere due to Coriolis deflection of wind-driven currents.

qs.q: Rock salt (halite) and gypsum are classified as chemically formed sedimentary rocks called
qs.e: Evaporites precipitate when mineral-rich water evaporates in arid saline lakes or shallow seas.
