qs.e: Seed rate determines the total weight of seed needed per unit area based on plant density and seed mass.

qs.q: What operation involves removing tree branches at a specific height above livestock reach to produce fodder sprouts?
qs.e: Pollarding cuts upper tree branches above ground level to produce new shoots out of reach of grazing animals.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of parboiling paddy rice prior to milling?
o: Gelatinizes starch, improves nutritional value, and reduces grain breakage during milling
Destroys all protein molecules in grain
Turns white rice into red bean paste
qs.e: Parboiling (soaking, steaming, drying) drives bran nutrients into the endosperm and hardens grains, reducing breakage.

qs.q: What field practice involves planting arable crops between hedgerows of leguminous trees that are periodically pruned?
qs.e: Alley cropping integrates food crops grown in alleys formed by fast-growing leguminous trees (e.g., Leucaena).

qs.q: What term describes planting a second crop into an established primary crop before the primary crop is harvested?
qs.e: Relay cropping sows a successor crop into a standing crop prior to harvesting the main crop.

qs.q: Which cultural practice involves harvesting a second crop from basal shoots left after cutting main plant stalks, as in sugarcane or sorghum?
qs.e: Ratooning allows stubble shoots left in the ground after harvest to grow and yield a subsequent crop.

qs.q: What term refers to the practice of growing crops in nutrient-enriched water solutions without soil?
qs.e: Hydroponics is the soil-less cultivation of plants in aqueous liquid nutrient solutions.

qs.q: Which field operation levels the soil surface and compacts loose topsoil after sowing fine seeds?
qs.e: Rolling uses heavy rollers to press loose soil around seeds, improving seed-to-soil contact for moisture uptake.

qs.q: What post-harvest storage technique uses airtight containers to suffocate insect pests through carbon dioxide accumulation?
qs.e: Hermetic storage seals grain in gastight bags/silos; insect respiration depletes oxygen and elevates CO2, killing pests.

qs.q: Which insect pest possesses piercing and sucking mouthparts that extract sap from cocoa pods and young shoots?
qs.e: Sahlbergella singularis (cocoa capsid/mirid) uses piercing-sucking mouthparts to feed on cocoa shoots and pods.

qs.q: Which larva bores into stems of growing maize plants, causing dead-heart symptoms and stem breakage?
qs.e: Busseola fusca (maize stem borer) caterpillars tunnel inside stalks, destroying growing points.

qs.q: Which insect pest feeds on cotton bolls, causing lint staining and premature boll dropping?
qs.e: Dysdercus superstitiosus (cotton stainer) punctures bolls and introduces Nematospora fungi that stain lint red/yellow.

qs.q: Which insect vector transmits groundnut rosette virus during sap feeding on peanut leaves?
qs.e: Aphis craccivora (groundnut aphid) is the primary vector transmitting rosette virus complex in groundnuts.

qs.q: What insect order includes beetles and weevils characterized by hardened forewings known as elytra?
qs.e: Coleoptera (beetles and weevils) have modified rigid front wings called elytra that protect delicate hind wings.

qs.q: Which insect pest attacks tomato fruits by boring holes and feeding on internal pulp?
qs.e: Helicoverpa armigera (tomato fruit borer) caterpillars tunnel into developing tomato fruits, causing rot.

qs.q: Which insect pest causes web-like nests and defoliation on citrus tree leaves?
qs.e: Papilio demodocus (citrus butterfly) caterpillars feed aggressively on young citrus foliage.

qs.q: What gaseous pesticide group is applied in enclosed airtight structures to eliminate grain store pests?
qs.e: Fumigants (e.g. aluminium phosphide generating phosphine gas) diffuse as toxic gas through enclosed grain masses.

qs.q: Which insect species lays eggs in ripening fruit pulp, causing maggots to destroy mangoes and citrus?
qs.e: Bactrocera dorsalis (oriental fruit fly) deposits eggs under fruit skin, where larvae feed on pulp.

qs.q: Which physical pest control method uses solar radiation under plastic sheets to sterilize soil of pests and weed seeds?
qs.e: Soil solarization covers moist soil with transparent polyethylene film during hot weather to trap heat and kill soil-borne pests.

qs.q: Which insect pest sucks sap from cowpea flowers and pods, causing flower abortion and pod shriveling?
qs.e: Maruca vitrata (legume pod borer) caterpillars feed on cowpea flowers, buds, and pods.

qs.q: What mouthpart modification allows aphids to pierce plant epidermal cells and extract phloem sap?
qs.e: Hemipteran insects (aphids) have needle-like stylets adapted for piercing plant tissues and sucking phloem sap.

qs.q: Which insect species is a major pest of stored flour and processed cereal products?
qs.e: Tribolium castaneum (red flour beetle) infests milled flour, bran, and processed grain products.

qs.q: What natural biopesticide derived from a soil bacterium is widely used to control lepidopteran caterpillars?
qs.e: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) produces endotoxin proteins that disrupt caterpillar gut membranes.

qs.q: Which fungal pathogen causes blast disease in rice, producing diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and neck rot on panicles?
qs.e: Pyricularia oryzae (Magnaporthe oryzae) causes rice blast, forming spindle-shaped brown leaf spots.

qs.q: Which bacterial pathogen causes bacterial wilt in tomatoes and potatoes, leading to rapid drooping of green leaves?
qs.e: Ralstonia solanacearum invades root vascular bundles, blocking water transport and causing sudden green wilting.

qs.q: Which fungal disease causes leaf spot (tikka disease) on groundnut foliage in West Africa?
qs.e: Cercospora arachidicola (and Cercosporidium personatum) cause brown circular leaf spots on groundnut leaves.

qs.q: Which fungal pathogen causes late blight in Irish potatoes and tomatoes, resulting in rapid foliar necrosis?
qs.e: Phytophthora infestans causes destructive late blight, forming dark water-soaked leaf lesions under cool wet conditions.

qs.q: Which fungal pathogen causes stem rot and vascular wilt in cowpeas and vegetable crops?
qs.e: Fusarium oxysporum is a soil-borne vascular wilt fungus causing browning of xylem vessels and plant wilting.

qs.q: Which fungal disease produces large black galls filled with powdery dark spores on maize ears and tassels?
qs.e: Ustilago maydis (maize smut) forms tumor-like galls on aerial corn tissues filled with dark teliospores.

qs.q: Which bacterial disease of cassava causes angular water-soaked leaf spots, gum exudation on stems, and dieback?
qs.e: Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis causes cassava bacterial blight (CBB), characterized by angular leaf spots and stem gumming.

qs.q: Which fungal pathogen produces toxic aflatoxins in stored groundnuts and maize under humid conditions?
qs.e: Aspergillus flavus synthesizes carcinogenic aflatoxins in improperly dried seeds stored above 13% moisture.

qs.q: Which pathogen causes damping-off disease in young nursery seedlings, causing stems to collapse at soil level?
qs.e: Pythium species attack succulent seedling stems near the soil surface, causing rotting and collapse.

qs.q: Which fungal disease causes leaf spots with concentric dark rings on tomato leaves, known as early blight?
qs.e: Alternaria solani causes early blight, forming target-like spots with concentric rings on foliage.

qs.q: What term refers to an plant disease that is constantly present in a specific agricultural region year after year?
qs.e: An endemic disease occurs regularly at predictable levels within a given geographical location.

qs.q: Which disease of banana and plantain causes yellowing and wilt of leaves due to vascular fungal blockage?
qs.e: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense causes Panama disease, blocking vascular bundles and causing leaf wilt.

qs.q: What environmental condition favors the rapid spread of downy mildew fungi on leafy vegetables?
o: Arid desert heat and total absence of dew
High humidity, cool temperatures, and free leaf moisture
High soil salinity and deep tillage
Direct sunlight and zero soil moisture
qs.e: Downy mildew sporangia require free water droplets on leaf surfaces and cool, humid air for germination and infection.

qs.q: Which aerial hemiparasitic weed grows on branches of cocoa and citrus trees, absorbing sap through haustoria?
qs.e: Loranthus (mistletoe) attaches to tree branches via haustoria to extract water and mineral nutrients.

qs.q: Which selective herbicide is applied to control broadleaf weeds in monocotyledonous cereal crop fields?
qs.e: 2,4-D is a selective synthetic auxin herbicide that targets dicotyledonous broadleaf weeds without harming monocot crops.

qs.q: What seed dispersal mechanism facilitates the widespread distribution of Tridax procumbens achenes by wind?
o: Feathery pappus structure acting as a parachute
Sticky barbs adhering to animal fur
Buoyant fibrous husk floating on water
qs.e: Tridax procumbens seeds carry a modified calyx (pappus) of feathery bristles that float in air currents.

qs.q: Which non-selective contact herbicide destroys green plant tissue rapidly upon exposure but does not translocate to roots?
qs.e: Paraquat is a fast-acting contact herbicide that disrupts cell membranes in light but does not translocate to subterranean roots.

qs.q: What anatomical feature of Cyperus rotundus distinguishes sedges from true grass weeds?
o: Hollow cylindrical stems with swollen nodes
Parallel leaf venation with fibrous roots
Solid triangular stems without prominent nodes
qs.e: Sedges (Cyperaceae) have solid, triangular stems in cross-section and 3-ranked leaves without swollen nodes.

qs.q: Which selective pre-emergence herbicide is widely sprayed in maize fields to control annual grass and broadleaf weeds?
qs.e: Atrazine is a selective triazine herbicide safely used in maize and sorghum fields to inhibit photosynthesis in germinating weeds.

qs.q: What is the primary mode of weed dispersal for seeds possessing hooked spines or sticky glandular hairs?
o: Epizoochory or transport on animal fur and clothing
qs.e: Hooks, barbs, and sticky resins enable weed seeds (e.g. Boerhavia, Desmodium) to cling to animal fur or clothing.

qs.q: Which parasitic weed lacks chlorophyll completely and appears as yellow thread-like vines wrapping around crop stems?
qs.e: Cuscuta (dodder) is a total stem holoparasite with leafless yellow stems that penetrate host tissues with haustoria.

qs.q: Which weed species is an invasive sprawling herb with bright red or yellow bracts, commonly called wild poinsettia?
qs.e: Euphorbia heterophylla (wild poinsettia/milkweed) is a troublesome weed in leguminous and cereal fields.

qs.q: What phenomenon occurs when one weed species releases biochemical chemicals that inhibit the germination of neighboring crop plants?
qs.e: Allelopathy is the suppression of neighboring plants through biochemical exudates released into soil.

qs.q: Which soil particle size range corresponds to silt according to the USDA particle size classification system?
qs.e: According to USDA classification, sand ranges from 0.05 to 2.0 mm, silt from 0.002 to 0.05 mm, and clay is smaller than 0.002 mm.

qs.q: Which type of soil structure is characterized by thin, horizontal plates overlapping each other and commonly impairs root penetration?
qs.e: Platy soil structure consists of thin horizontal plates that restrict downward root growth and water percolation.

qs.q: What effect does adding organic manure have on the cation exchange capacity (CEC) of sandy soils?
o: Has no effect on the CEC
qs.e: Organic matter possesses a high negative charge density, which greatly enhances the cation exchange capacity of sandy soils.

qs.q: Which type of soil water is held tightly around soil particles by adhesive forces and is unavailable to plant roots?
qs.e: Hygroscopic water forms a thin film held tightly by molecular forces (tension > 31 atm) and cannot be absorbed by plants.

qs.q: What term describes the ease with which air and water move through a soil profile?
qs.e: Permeability measures the rate at which fluids (water and air) pass through interconnected soil pores.

qs.q: What is the effect of excessive soil tillage on aggregate stability and soil structural collapse?
o: Destroys soil aggregates and promotes surface crusting
qs.e: Frequent intense cultivation pulverizes soil aggregates, accelerates organic matter oxidation, and encourages surface crusting.

qs.q: What instrument is used in field soil surveys to estimate soil colour using hue, value, and chroma coordinates?
qs.e: The Munsell soil colour chart provides standard colour chips categorized by hue, value (lightness), and chroma (purity).

qs.q: What is the principal cause of soil salinization in arid and semi-arid irrigated agricultural lands?
o: Excessive application of organic farmyard manure
Deep root extraction by leguminous trees
Evaporation of irrigation water leaving dissolved salts at the surface
qs.e: In dry areas, high evaporation rates draw soil water upward, depositing dissolved salts in the surface layer.

qs.q: Which microbial process converts nitrogenous organic residues into ammonium compounds in the soil?
qs.e: Ammonification is the biological breakdown of complex organic nitrogen compounds (proteins, amino acids) into ammonia/ammonium.

qs.q: Which term describes the resistance of soil to deformation or rupture under applied mechanical pressure?
qs.e: Soil consistency describes physical attributes such as stickiness, plasticity, and firmness at different moisture levels.

qs.q: Which gas accounts for the highest volume percentage in well-aerated surface soil air under normal conditions?
qs.e: Soil air contains about 78% nitrogen, similar to atmospheric air, while oxygen is slightly lower and carbon dioxide higher.

qs.q: How many kilograms of Nitrogen are contained in a 50 kg bag of Urea fertilizer containing 46 percent N?
qs.e: Amount of Nitrogen = 50 kg * 0.46 = 23.0 kg.

qs.q: Which soil bacterium oxidizes ammonium ions into nitrite ions during the first step of biological nitrification?
qs.e: Nitrosomonas bacteria oxidize ammonium (NH4+) to nitrite (NO2-), which is subsequently oxidized to nitrate by Nitrobacter.

qs.q: Which nutrient deficiency causes 'blossom end rot' in tomatoes due to poor cell wall integrity?
qs.e: Calcium is structural in cell walls (calcium pectate); its lack causes tissue collapse at the blossom end of fruits.

qs.q: Which term describes the loss of soil nitrogen to the atmosphere as nitrogen gas under anaerobic, waterlogged conditions?
qs.e: Denitrification is the anaerobic conversion of soil nitrate (NO3-) into gaseous dinitrogen (N2) by facultative bacteria.

qs.q: What visual symptom is characteristic of iron deficiency in young developing crop leaves?
o: General yellowing of lower mature leaves
Interveinal chlorosis on young upper leaves
qs.e: Iron is immobile in plants; deficiency appears as distinct interveinal chlorosis on the youngest developing upper leaves.

qs.q: What effect does persistent application of ammonium sulphate fertilizer have on soil chemical properties over time?
qs.e: Ammonium sulphate leaves an acidic residue in soil as ammonium is nitrified, lowering soil pH over time.

qs.q: Which secondary plant nutrient is an essential constituent of sulphur-containing amino acids such as methionine and cysteine?
qs.e: Sulphur is required for the synthesis of key amino acids (methionine, cysteine) essential for protein formation.

qs.q: Which free-living soil bacterium fixes atmospheric nitrogen independently without forming root nodules?
qs.e: Azotobacter and Clostridium are free-living (non-symbiotic) nitrogen-fixing bacteria in agricultural soils.

qs.q: How many total kilograms of plant nutrients (N + P2O5 + K2O) are present in a 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 fertilizer?
qs.e: Total nutrient percentage = 15 + 15 + 15 = 45%. Weight of nutrients = 50 kg * 0.45 = 22.5 kg.

qs.q: What is the main advantage of foliar application of micro-nutrients compared to soil application?
o: Rapid uptake and bypasses soil nutrient fixation
Slower uptake with long residual effect
qs.e: Foliar spraying allows plants to absorb micro-nutrients directly through leaf stomata, avoiding soil fixation issues.

qs.q: Which nitrogenous fertilizer contains nitrogen in both ammonium and nitrate forms?
qs.e: Calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN) provides 27% N, half as ammonium (NH4+) and half as nitrate (NO3-).

qs.q: What process describes the conversion of soil organic nitrogen into inorganic mineral forms available to plants?
qs.e: Mineralization is the microbial conversion of organic nitrogen into inorganic ammonium and nitrate ions.

qs.q: Which organic manure type is derived from dried, pulverized bird droppings accumulated in arid regions?
qs.e: Guano consists of the accumulated excrement of seabirds or bats, rich in nitrogen and phosphate.

qs.q: What term refers to the maximum amount of a plant nutrient that soil can adsorb and exchange under specified conditions?
qs.e: Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) measures the total capacity of soil to hold exchangeable cations (Ca2+, Mg2+, K+, Na+, H+).

qs.q: Which instrument is directly used in the field to measure soil moisture tension or matric potential?
qs.e: A tensiometer measures soil matric suction (tension), indicating how tightly water is held by soil particles.

qs.q: What is the main operational disadvantage of overhead sprinkler irrigation in windy tropical regions?
o: Severe root rot due to localized wetting
High evaporation losses and uneven water distribution
High labor cost compared to manual watering
qs.e: Strong winds distort sprinkler spray patterns, causing non-uniform application and high evaporation losses.

qs.q: Which subsurface drainage system utilizes perforated plastic pipes buried below the soil surface to collect excess water?
qs.e: Subsurface tile drainage uses buried perforated pipes to carry excess gravitational water away from crop root zones.

qs.q: If a soil sample at field capacity holds 30 percent water by weight and its permanent wilting point is 12 percent, what is its available water capacity?
qs.e: Available Water Capacity = Field Capacity - Permanent Wilting Point = 30% - 12% = 18%.

qs.q: Which soil texture generally exhibits the highest total available water holding capacity for plant uptake?
qs.e: Silt loam soils have a balanced pore size distribution, providing the highest volume of available capillary water.

qs.q: Which soil physical condition severely restricts root water uptake even when soil moisture content is high?
qs.e: Soil compaction destroys macro-pores, restricting root growth and reducing oxygen availability needed for active water uptake.

qs.q: Which surface drainage layout uses parallel ditches to remove surface water from flat farmlands?
qs.e: A parallel ditch drainage system consists of equally spaced shallow ditches dug across flat fields to collect surface runoff.

qs.q: Which type of irrigation structure controls water flow into field furrows from an open canal?
qs.e: Siphon tubes transfer water over irrigation canal banks into individual crop furrows uniformly.

qs.q: Which parameter describes the ratio of yield produced per unit volume of water consumed by a crop?
qs.e: Water Use Efficiency (WUE) is expressed as crop yield produced per unit of water evapotranspired or applied.

qs.q: Which part of a tractor disc plough absorbs lateral side draft forces and stabilizes straight forward movement?
o: Rear furrow wheel or land wheel
qs.e: The rear furrow wheel presses against the furrow wall, counteracting side draft forces.

qs.q: Which nozzle type on a knapsack sprayer produces a flat fan-shaped spray pattern recommended for herbicide application?
qs.e: Flat fan nozzles deliver uniform rectangular spray swaths ideal for soil and foliage herbicide applications.

qs.q: Which nozzle type produces a fine circular mist pattern ideal for applying insecticides and fungicides to crop foliage?
qs.e: Hollow cone nozzles produce fine droplets with high penetration suitable for canopy insecticide coverage.

qs.q: What is the primary function of the tractor differential lock mechanism when operating on slippery mud?
o: Locks both rear drive wheels together so they rotate at equal speed
Increases PTO rotational speed by 200 percent
Shuts off engine fuel supply automatically
qs.e: Differential locks force both drive wheels to rotate together, preventing single-wheel spinning in soft mud.

qs.q: Which component in liquid-cooled tractor engines regulates coolant flow based on engine operating temperature?
qs.e: The thermostat opens at designated temperatures (~80-85 °C) to allow coolant flow into the radiator.

qs.q: Which primary tillage implement uses heavy curved tines with reversible shovel points to shatter hard soil without inversion?
qs.e: Chisel ploughs loosen soil deeply (25-30 cm) using curved shanks without turning over topsoil.

qs.q: What component in a diesel fuel system purges trapped air bubbles from fuel lines?
qs.e: Priming pumps and bleed screws allow operators to vent trapped air from diesel fuel circuits ('bleeding the system').

qs.q: Which machine is used to chop green forage crops into uniform short pieces for silage production?
qs.e: Forage harvesters cut standing forage and chop green stems into short lengths for silo packing.

qs.q: What total field area in square metres is covered by a rectangular farmland plot measuring 250 metres in length and 120 metres in width?
qs.e: Area = Length * Width = 250 m * 120 m = 30,000 m². In hectares = 30,000 / 10,000 = 3.0 ha.

qs.q: What calculation determines the area of a triangular farmland plot with a base of 150 metres and a perpendicular height of 80 metres?
qs.e: Triangle Area = 0.5 * Base * Height = 0.5 * 150 m * 80 m = 6,000 m² = 0.6 ha.

qs.q: What surveying technique divides a irregular farm field into a network of connected triangles to compute total land area?
qs.e: Triangulation divides irregular land areas into triangles whose side lengths and angles are measured to compute area.

qs.q: What term defines a permanent fixed benchmark point of known elevation above sea level used as a height reference?
qs.e: A benchmark (BM) is a permanent marked point of known height above sea level used in leveling.

qs.q: Which survey line connects opposite corners of a survey framework to verify measurement accuracy?
qs.e: Check lines (proof lines) run across triangles to verify chain survey plotting accuracy.

qs.q: Which survey method measures both horizontal angles and vertical distances using a transit theodolite?
qs.e: Theodolites measure precise horizontal and vertical angles for high-precision land surveying.

qs.q: What angle convention expresses bearings measured clockwise from magnetic North between 0 and 360 degrees?
qs.e: Whole Circle Bearings (WCB) measure angles continuously clockwise from North from 0° to 360°.

qs.q: What survey line joins framework stations on opposite sides of a survey loop to fix intermediate detail features?
qs.e: Tie lines connect main framework lines to locate nearby landscape details and check survey accuracy.

qs.q: What surveying error occurs when a measuring chain sags below horizontal alignment under its own weight?
qs.e: Sag error causes chains to form catenary curves, making recorded distance longer than true horizontal distance.

qs.q: Which survey instrument consists of a drawing board mounted on a tripod used for direct field plotting?
qs.e: Plane table surveying plots field sightlines directly onto map paper mounted on a portable board.

qs.q: Which hand-held instrument measures vertical slope angles and ground incline percentages in the field?
qs.e: Clinometers measure slope gradient angles and vertical inclination.

qs.q: What survey type fixes legal land boundaries and property ownership corners for land titling?
qs.e: Cadastral surveys establish legal property boundaries and corner monuments for ownership deeds.

qs.q: If a survey map scale is 1:10,000, what actual field distance in metres is represented by a 5 cm line on the map?
qs.e: Field distance = 5 cm * 10,000 = 50,000 cm = 500 m.

qs.q: What relationship exists between the Fore Bearing (FB) and Back Bearing (BB) of a survey line in degrees?
qs.e: Back Bearing differs from Fore Bearing by exactly 180° (BB = FB + 180° if FB < 180°, or FB - 180° if FB > 180°).

qs.q: What term describes synthetic plant growth regulators applied to prevent lodging in dense cereal crops?
qs.e: Plant growth retardants (e.g., chlormequat) shorten internodes, stiffening cereal stems against wind lodging.

qs.q: Which chemical substance added to pesticide tank mixtures reduces surface tension of spray droplets on waxy leaves?
qs.e: Surfactants lower liquid surface tension, expanding droplet spreading and adhesion on waxy leaf cuticles.

qs.q: Which chemical insecticide group acts by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase enzyme activity in insect nervous systems?
qs.e: Organophosphates (e.g. malathion) and carbamates (e.g. carbaryl) inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing fatal nervous spasms.

qs.q: Which copper-based inorganic fungicide is prepared by mixing copper sulphate and hydrated lime in water?
qs.e: Bordeaux mixture is a classic protective fungicide made from copper sulphate (CuSO4) and slaked lime (Ca(OH)2).

qs.q: Which chemical substance causes plants to shed leaves prematurely before mechanical harvesting, as in cotton?
qs.e: Defoliants cause rapid leaf abscission, facilitating mechanical cotton picking.

qs.q: Which chemical agent speeds up drying of green plant foliage before crop harvesting?
qs.e: Desiccants dry out green foliage rapidly to facilitate mechanical harvesting.

qs.q: What parameter measures acute mammalian toxicity of an agrochemical, defined as the dose required to kill 50 percent of test animals?
qs.e: LD50 (Lethal Dose 50%) expresses toxicity in mg chemical per kg body weight; lower LD50 values indicate higher toxicity.

qs.q: Which chemical insecticide is widely used as a grain protectant dust applied directly to stored cereal seeds?
qs.e: Pirimiphos-methyl (Actellic) is an organophosphate insecticide safe for grain store pest control.

qs.q: What condition occurs in fish ponds when excessive algal blooms die off, causing severe oxygen depletion?
qs.e: Decaying algal masses consume dissolved oxygen through bacterial decomposition, causing nocturnal fish asphyxiation.

qs.q: What instrument measures dissolved oxygen levels directly in fish pond water?
o: Dissolved oxygen meter or Winkler titration kit
qs.e: DO meters use polarographic sensors to measure dissolved oxygen concentration in mg/L (ppm).

qs.q: What is the recommended Secchi disc transparency reading for a well-managed green fish pond?
qs.e: A transparency reading of 30-40 cm indicates optimal phytoplankton density for fish culture.

qs.q: What artificial hormone injection technique induces ripe female catfish broodstock to ovulate eggs in hatcheries?
o: Hypophysation using pituitary extract or synthetic gonadotropin
qs.e: Hypophysation injects pituitary extracts or GnRH analogs (e.g., Ovaprim) to trigger final oocyte maturation.

qs.q: What modern aquaculture system recycles pond water through mechanical and biological filters to remove toxic ammonia?
qs.e: RAS filters and purifies culture water through biofilters, enabling high-density fish production with minimal water replacement.

qs.q: Which toxic nitrogenous waste compound accumulates in fish ponds from fish excretion and uneaten feed decomposition?
qs.e: Un-ionized ammonia (NH3) excreted across fish gills is highly toxic to fish even at low concentrations (>0.05 mg/L).

qs.q: Which fish species is a large indigenous African catfish with four pairs of barbels, botanically Heterobranchus longifilis?
qs.e: Heterobranchus longifilis is a fast-growing clariid catfish with a distinct adipose fin.

qs.q: What phenomenon causes wild tilapia ponds to become overcrowded with stunted small fish?
o: Precocious breeding and rapid uncontrolled reproduction
qs.e: Tilapia reach sexual maturity at early age (3-4 months), breeding rapidly and overpopulating ponds.

qs.q: What equipment measures water salinity in brackish water aquaculture ponds?
qs.e: Optical refractometers measure light refraction through water drops to determine salinity in parts per thousand (ppt).

qs.q: Which timber tree species produces lightweight white timber botanically named Triplochiton scleroxylon?
qs.e: Triplochiton scleroxylon is Obeche, producing soft, cream-colored timber used for plywood and carving.

qs.q: Which non-timber forest product is extracted from tree bark and used in leather tanning industries?
qs.e: Tannins are polyphenolic plant exudates extracted from bark (e.g. mangrove, acacia) used to tan hides into leather.

qs.q: What instrument measures standing tree height using geometric triangulation principles?
qs.e: Hypsometers (e.g. Haga altimeter, Suunto clinometer) measure standing tree height optically.

qs.q: What tool measures standing tree trunk diameter at breast height (1.3 metres above ground)?
qs.e: Diameter tapes (pi tapes) read tree diameter at breast height (DBH) directly when wrapped around trunks.

qs.q: What term defines the study of tree species identification and taxonomy?
qs.e: Dendrology is the botanical study of woody plants and tree species classification.

qs.q: Which timber tree species yields extremely dense, heavy black wood botanically named Diospyros mespiliformis?
qs.e: Diospyros mespiliformis (African ebony) produces dense black heartwood used for carving and piano keys.

qs.q: What special nursery bed uses bottom heat and high humidity frames to root difficult leafy softwood cuttings?
qs.e: Mist propagation units spray intermittent water mist to maintain 100% relative humidity, keeping leaf cuttings turgid while rooting.

qs.q: Which technique prunes ornamental hedges into precise geometric or animal topiary shapes?
qs.e: Topiary is the horticultural practice of clipping shrubs into defined ornamental geometric shapes.

qs.q: What Japanese horticultural art form stunts potted trees to grow dwarf miniatures mimicking ancient forest trees?
qs.e: Bonsai is the art of growing containerized trees through root pruning and branch wiring.

qs.q: Which leafy vegetable species is known as soko or cockscomb and belongs to the family Amaranthaceae?
qs.e: Celosia argentea (soko) is a popular green vegetable with colorful inflorescences.

qs.q: Which horticultural practice involves growing turf grass on specialized farms, harvesting root-mats as sod rolls, and laying them on lawns?
qs.e: Sodding lays pre-grown mature grass sheets (sod) for instant lawn establishment.

qs.q: Which post-harvest treatment removes field heat rapidly from freshly harvested leafy vegetables using chilled water or forced air?
qs.e: Pre-cooling rapidly lowers harvested produce temperatures to slow respiration and extend shelf life.

qs.q: What term describes the complete desertion of a beehive by an entire colony due to severe disturbance or starvation?
qs.e: Absconding is the total abandonment of a hive by all bees in response to pests, heat, or food lack.

qs.q: Which bacterial gene inserted into insect-resistant Bt cowpea and cotton produces crystalline proteins toxic to pod borers?
qs.e: Bt crops express Cry endotoxin proteins derived from Bacillus thuringiensis, killing lepidopteran pests.

qs.q: What term describes the capability of an isolated plant cell to divide and regenerate into a complete whole plant in tissue culture?
qs.e: Cellular totipotency is the innate capacity of a plant cell to differentiate and regenerate an entire plant.

qs.q: Which soil bacterium species serves as a natural vector for transferring foreign genes into dicotyledonous plant genomes?
qs.e: Agrobacterium tumefaciens transfers its Ti-plasmid T-DNA into plant genomes, widely used in genetic transformation.

qs.q: What technique amplifies targeted DNA segments rapidly in vitro using thermal cycling and Taq polymerase?
qs.e: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) exponentially multiplies specific DNA sequences using thermal cycles.

qs.q: Which enzyme cuts double-stranded DNA molecules at specific nucleotide recognition sequences?
qs.e: Restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) cut DNA at specific palindromic recognition sequences.

qs.q: What term describes unorganized, proliferating masses of undifferentiated parenchymatous cells in plant tissue culture?
qs.e: Callus is an unorganized mass of dividing, undifferentiated cells produced on auxin/cytokinin culture media.

qs.q: A tractor purchased for ₦6,000,000 has an estimated useful lifespan of 10 years and a salvage value of ₦1,000,000. Using straight-line depreciation, what is its annual depreciation charge?
qs.e: Annual Depreciation = (Initial Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = (6,000,000 - 1,000,000) / 10 = ₦500,000/year.

qs.q: Why is the price elasticity of demand for essential staple food crops like cassava and rice generally price inelastic?
o: Staple crops are luxury goods consumed by high earners
Staple food crops are basic necessities with few close substitutes
Staple crops can be stored indefinitely without loss
Staple crops receive heavy government subsidies
qs.e: Essential food staples have inelastic demand because consumers must buy basic calories regardless of price changes.

qs.q: What term defines a market situation where a single buyer dominates the purchase of an agricultural commodity from many small farmers?
qs.e: A monopsony is a market structure with only one buyer for a product or service.

qs.q: Which farm budgeting tool plans minor adjustments to an existing farm operation, such as replacing 2 hectares of maize with cowpeas?
qs.e: Partial budgeting evaluates financial impacts of small changes in farm operations by comparing added costs/lost revenue vs added revenue/saved costs.

qs.q: At what profit-maximizing point should a farm manager expand production output in competitive markets?
o: Where Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost
Where Total Revenue equals Total Variable Cost
Where Fixed Cost equals Variable Cost
qs.e: Profit maximization occurs at the output level where Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost (MR = MC).

qs.q: Which credit guarantee scheme in Nigeria encourages commercial banks to lend to farmers by guaranteeing up to 75 percent of defaulted loans?
qs.e: ACGSF (managed by CBN) guarantees 75% of net defaults on agricultural loans advanced by commercial banks.

qs.q: What financial parameter measures the ratio of total farm assets to total farm liabilities?
qs.e: Solvency measures long-term business financial stability (Total Assets / Total Liabilities).

qs.q: What financial ratio measures the ability of a farm business to meet short-term cash obligations due within one year?
qs.e: Current Ratio (Current Assets / Current Liabilities) evaluates short-term enterprise liquidity.

qs.q: If a farm has Current Assets of ₦1,500,000 and Current Liabilities of ₦500,000, what is its Current Ratio?
qs.e: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = 1,500,000 / 500,000 = 3.0.

qs.q: What economic term describes a government policy that sets a minimum legal price above market equilibrium to protect farmer incomes?
qs.e: A price floor sets a legal minimum price above equilibrium, guaranteeing baseline producer prices.

qs.q: What legal policy sets a maximum legal price below market equilibrium to make basic food affordable to urban consumers?
qs.e: A price ceiling sets a maximum price limit below market equilibrium to protect consumers.

qs.q: What economic consequence frequently results when government enforces a strict price ceiling below equilibrium on food crops?
o: Food shortages and black market hoarding
qs.e: Setting price ceilings below equilibrium creates excess demand over supply, leading to shortages and informal black markets.

qs.q: Why is Stage III of the production function irrational for crop production?
o: Marginal physical product is negative, meaning total output declines with extra input
qs.e: In Stage III, marginal product is negative, so adding more input actually decreases total crop yield.

qs.q: What curve shows alternative maximum combinations of two crops that a farm can produce given fixed land and resources?
qs.e: The Production Possibility Curve (PPC) illustrates maximum output trade-offs between two enterprises sharing fixed resources.

qs.q: Which participatory extension approach involves farmers directly in designing, conducting, and evaluating field research on their own plots?
o: Participatory Rural Appraisal or Farmer Field School
qs.e: Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and PRA involve farmers directly in hands-on field experimentation and problem solving.

qs.q: What term describes the institutional bridge linking agricultural research institutes, extension agents, and practical farmers?
qs.e: REFILS facilitates two-way feedback between researchers, extension agents, input suppliers, and farmers.

qs.q: What role is played by Subject Matter Specialists (SMS) within the ADP extension organizational structure?
o: Providing specialized technical training to Village Extension Agents and diagnosing complex field problems
Distributing free land titles to corporate investors
Transporting harvested crops to export harbors
Collecting income taxes from rural market women
qs.e: Subject Matter Specialists bridge research centers and field staff, training agents on technical innovations.

qs.q: What term describes the formal rejection or discontinuance of an innovation after a period of initial adoption?
qs.e: Disenchantment discontinuance occurs when a farmer abandons a technology due to dissatisfaction or poor performance.

qs.q: What extension model uses universities to conduct agricultural research, train agents, and deliver extension directly to surrounding farm communities?
qs.e: The Land-Grant model (pioneered in the USA) integrates university research, teaching, and community extension outreach.

qs.q: What extension method uses organized radio listening clubs where farm groups listen to agricultural broadcasts and discuss action plans?
qs.e: Radio farm forums combine mass media broadcasts with localized group discussion and extension feedback.

qs.q: Which volatile fatty acid produced by rumen microbial fermentation serves as the primary precursor for glucose synthesis in ruminants?
qs.e: Propionate is absorbed through the rumen wall and converted into glucose via gluconeogenesis in the liver.

qs.q: Which volatile fatty acid produced in the rumen is the primary precursor for milk fat synthesis in dairy cows?
qs.e: Acetate is the major substrate for lipogenesis, providing building blocks for milk butterfat.

qs.q: Which anatomical structure in young suckling ruminants bypasses milk directly from the esophagus into the abomasum?
qs.e: The esophageal groove closes reflexively during suckling, directing milk past rumen and reticulum into the abomasum.

qs.q: Using Pearson Square, how many kilograms of Maize (10 percent CP) and Soybean meal (40 percent CP) are required to formulate 100 kg of a 16 percent CP pig ration?
o: 70 kg Maize and 30 kg Soybean meal
60 kg Maize and 40 kg Soybean meal
85 kg Maize and 15 kg Soybean meal
80 kg Maize and 20 kg Soybean meal
qs.e: Pearson square: Maize parts = |40 - 16| = 24; Soybean parts = |16 - 10| = 6. Total parts = 30. Maize % = (24/30)*100 = 80%. Soybean % = (6/30)*100 = 20%.

qs.q: What toxicity risk arises if ruminants ingest excessive urea without adequate soluble carbohydrates?
o: Bloat due to excessive lactic acid
qs.e: Excess urea produces rapid ammonia accumulation in the rumen exceeding microbial absorption, causing blood alkalosis.

qs.q: Which vitamin deficiency in poultry causes nutritional encephalomalacia (crazy chick disease)?
qs.e: Vitamin E deficiency causes lipid peroxidation in brain tissues, leading to ataxia and crazy chick disease.

qs.q: What parameter measures total feed energy minus energy losses in feces, urine, and gaseous products?
qs.e: Metabolizable Energy (ME) = Digestible Energy - (Urinary Energy + Gaseous Energy losses).

qs.q: What measure represents true energy available for maintenance and production after deducting heat increment?
qs.e: Net Energy (NE) = Metabolizable Energy - Heat Increment (heat dissipated during digestion and metabolism).

qs.q: What feed constituent is estimated in proximal analysis by subtracting moisture, crude protein, crude fat, crude fiber, and ash from 100?
qs.e: Nitrogen-Free Extract (NFE) represents soluble carbohydrates (starches and sugars) calculated by difference in proximate analysis.

qs.q: Which metabolic disease affects high-producing dairy cows in early lactation due to negative energy balance?
qs.e: Ketosis occurs when rapid fat mobilization produces excess ketone bodies in blood during early lactation.

qs.q: What term describes a sterile female calf born twin to a male calf in cattle?
qs.e: A free-martin is a sterile female calf co-twin to a male, masculinized by male anti-Müllerian hormone in utero.

qs.q: Which management practice uses hormones to synchronize estrus cycles across a group of breeding females?
qs.e: Estrus synchronization uses prostaglandins or progesterone devices so a herd comes into heat simultaneously.

qs.q: What term describes hormone treatment that induces female ovaries to release multiple ova during a single cycle?
qs.e: Superovulation uses follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) to induce development and release of multiple eggs for embryo transfer.

qs.q: What respiratory bacterial pathogen causes chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens, producing nasal discharge and coughing?
qs.e: Mycoplasma gallisepticum causes Chronic Respiratory Disease (CRD), leading to air sacculitis and rales.

qs.q: Which bacterial pathogen causes Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP), producing marbling of lung tissue?
qs.e: CBPP is caused by Mycoplasma mycoides, resulting in severe fibrinous pleuropneumonia and marbled lung hepatization.

qs.q: Which rickettsial pathogen transmitted by Amblyomma ticks causes Heartwater disease in ruminants?
qs.e: Ehrlichia ruminantium (formerly Cowdria ruminantium) causes Heartwater, leading to hydropericardium and nervous signs.

qs.q: What chemical additive can be sprayed on low-quality dry crop residues (straw) to break lignocellulose bonds and increase digestibility?
qs.e: Ammoniation via urea treatment hydrolyzes lignocellulose bonds in straw, boosting crude protein and intake.

qs.q: What toxic amino acid present in Leucaena leucocephala leaves causes hair loss and goitre in non-ruminants?
qs.e: Mimosine in Leucaena causes alopecia and thyroid dysfunction in non-ruminants unless degraded by specialized rumen bacteria.

qs.q: Which pasture legume is known as Siratro and is a drought-tolerant perennial climber with dark red flowers?
qs.e: Macroptilium atropurpureum (Siratro) is a deep-rooted pasture legume suitable for tropical pastures.

qs.q: What is the optimum temperature range for the fermentation of cocoa beans in sweat boxes?
qs.e: Fermentation of cocoa beans generates microbial heat, elevating box temperatures to 45-50 °C to kill embryos and develop flavor precursors.

qs.q: Which crop yields fibers extracted from the bark of stems through a water-soaking process known as retting?
qs.e: Jute (Corchorus capsularis) fibers are extracted from stem phloem tissues by retting in water.

qs.q: Which environmental factor triggers flowering in short-day plant species such as certain traditional rice varieties?
o: Day length shorter than a critical photoperiod
Total dark exposure for 48 consecutive hours
qs.e: Short-day plants flower when day length (photoperiod) falls below a specific threshold duration.

qs.q: What is the primary function of retting in jute fiber processing?
o: Drying seed capsules under intense heat
Coagulating latex into solid rubber sheets
Softening stem bark through microbial action to release fibers
Extracting vegetable oil from seed kernels
qs.e: Retting uses water microbes to dissolve pectins and gums binding phloem fibers to jute stems.

qs.q: Crops cultivated to suppress weed growth through rapid canopy formation and root exudates are called:
qs.e: Smother crops grow vigorously, blocking light and suppressing weed seed germination.

qs.q: Which classification groups crops based on photoperiodic floral induction response?
qs.e: Crops are categorized into short-day, long-day, and day-neutral based on response to photoperiod.

qs.q: Which practice subjects moist seeds to cold temperatures to break physiological embryo dormancy?
qs.e: Stratification chills moist seeds at low temperatures (2-5 °C) to break internal physiological dormancy.

qs.q: Which condition is required for successful union between scion and rootstock during grafting?
o: Complete removal of all stem bark
Total exposure of scion to dry air
Close alignment of vascular cambium layers
Applying heavy nitrogen fertilizer directly to union
qs.e: Vascular cambium layers of scion and stock must align tightly to form continuous vascular connections.

qs.q: Which plant hormone synthetic analog is commonly applied to stem cuttings to stimulate adventitious root formation?
qs.e: Auxins such as Indole-3-butyric acid (IBA) promote adventitious root initiation on stem cuttings.

qs.q: Which grafting method is widely used when top-working mature unproductive citrus trees with superior scions?
qs.e: Cleft or bark grafting allows inserting scions into large truncated limbs of mature trees (top-working).

qs.q: Which practice involves cutting back the main stem of an old orchard tree to graft new desirable scions?
qs.e: Top-working replaces the canopy of mature trees by grafting scions of improved cultivars onto severed scaffold limbs.

qs.q: Which plant propagation method induces adventitious shoots by mounding soil around pruned stem bases?
qs.e: Stooling (mound layering) cuts parent plants back near ground level and mounds soil around emerging shoots to induce roots.

qs.q: Which technique ensures complete contact between scion and rootstock cambium in whip and tongue grafting?
o: Leaving a wide open air gap between stock and scion
Soaking grafting joint in cold concentrated acid
Covering joint with dry coarse sand
Interlocking tongue cuts and wrapping securely with grafting tape
qs.e: Matching tongue cuts provides mechanical support and maximizes cambial contact, sealed with tape to prevent drying.

qs.q: What is the recommended storage temperature for long-term preservation of crop seed germplasm in genebanks?
qs.e: Orthodox seeds are safely stored long-term at -18 °C with low seed moisture content (5-7%).

qs.q: Which term describes seeds that cannot survive drying or freezing temperatures and must be planted fresh?
qs.e: Recalcitrant seeds (e.g. cocoa, rubber, mango) lose viability rapidly if dried below high moisture limits.

qs.q: If a maize farmer plants at a spacing of 0.75 m between rows and 0.25 m within rows, what is the theoretical plant population per hectare for single-seed stands?
qs.e: Area per plant = 0.75 m * 0.25 m = 0.1875 m². Plant population = 10,000 m² / 0.1875 m² = 53,333 plants.

qs.q: Which practice involves removing bark rings around tree branches to induce flower bud formation or fruit enlargement?
qs.e: Girdling removes a outer bark ring, blocking phloem sugar transport downward and accumulating carbohydrates above the ring.

qs.q: Which mealybug insect vector transmits the cocoa swollen shoot virus in West Africa?
qs.e: Planococcoides njalensis (mealybug) secretes honeydew and transmits cocoa swollen shoot virus (CSSV).

qs.q: What term describes the minimum pest population density that causes economic damage justifying chemical spray costs?
qs.e: Economic Injury Level (EIL) is the lowest pest population density that will cause economic damage exceeding control costs.

qs.q: Which pest insect damages rice plants by cutting young tillers at the base, creating 'dead hearts'?
qs.e: Maliarpha separatella (African white stem borer) attacks rice stems, causing dead-heart symptoms.

qs.q: What insect pest is known as the larger grain borer, capable of tunneling through wooden storage structures and dried cassava chips?
qs.e: Prostephanus truncatus (larger grain borer) is a highly destructive pest of stored corn and dried root chips.

qs.q: Which pest causes silvering and scarring on onion leaves by rasping epidermal tissues?
qs.e: Thrips tabaci (onion thrips) rasp leaf surfaces and lap exuded sap, producing silvery leaf streaks.

qs.q: Which insect pest attacks sweet potato tubers in the field and storage, creating tunnels filled with bitter excrement?
qs.e: Cylas formicarius (sweet potato weevil) bores into stems and tubers, producing toxic bitter sesquiterpenes.

qs.q: Which bacterial pathogen causes soft rot in stored yam tubers and vegetables?
qs.e: Pectobacterium carotovorum (formerly Erwinia carotovora) secretes pectolytic enzymes that break down cell walls into soft slimy rot.

qs.q: Which fungal disease produces sunken dark lesions with pinkish spore masses on mangoes and papayas?
qs.e: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides causes anthracnose, characterized by dark necrotic lesions on leaves and fruit.

qs.q: Which disease of citrus trees causes gum exudation from bark cracks near the soil line?
qs.e: Phytophthora citrophthora causes citrus gummosis, producing bark cracking and profuse gum secretion.

qs.q: Which viral disease of citrus is transmitted by citrus aphids and causes stem pitting and decline?
qs.e: Citrus tristeza virus (CTV) causes quick decline and stem pitting on susceptible rootstocks like sour orange.

qs.q: Which foliar fungal disease of plantain produces dark streaks on leaves leading to extensive leaf necrosis?
qs.e: Mycosphaerella fijiensis causes Black Sigatoka disease, severely reducing photosynthetic leaf area in plantain.

qs.q: Which disease of oil palm seedlings causes yellowing and drying of spear leaves in nurseries?
o: Freckle disease or Cercospora leaf spot
qs.e: Cercospora elaeidis causes oil palm freckle, producing brown necrotic spots on nursery fronds.

qs.q: Which bacterial disease of cassava causes internal brown streaking of tubers and stem dieback?
qs.e: Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis causes cassava bacterial blight with vascular stem staining.

qs.q: Which viral disease affects sugarcane, causing light green streaks on leaves and stunted stalk growth?
qs.e: Sugarcane mosaic virus causes chlorotic mottling and yield loss, transmitted by aphids.

qs.q: What selective post-emergence herbicide is widely used in rice fields to control broadleaf weeds and sedges?
qs.e: Propanil is a contact herbicide used in rice; rice plants produce acylamidase enzymes that detoxify propanil.

qs.q: What feature allows Striga seeds to remain dormant in farmlands for up to 20 years until host crops are planted?
o: Thick fleshy fruit pulp protecting seeds
Requirement for host root exudate strigolactones to trigger germination
qs.e: Striga seeds require chemical signals (strigolactones) exuded by host crop roots to stimulate germination.

qs.q: Which type of chemical weathering occurs when water reacts directly with mineral compounds to form new soluble minerals?
qs.e: Hydrolysis is a chemical weathering reaction in which hydrogen ions from water replace mineral cations, producing new chemical compounds.

qs.q: If a moist soil sample weighs 150 grams and weighs 120 grams after oven-drying at 105 degrees Celsius, what is its percentage moisture content on a dry basis?
qs.e: Mass of water = 150 g - 120 g = 30 g. Moisture content on dry basis = (30 / 120) * 100 = 25%.

qs.q: What is the term for the parent rock material from which soil is formed through weathering processes?
qs.e: Regolith refers to the loose mantle of weathered rock material covering solid bedrock from which soil horizons develop.

qs.q: If a soil sample has a total volume of 100 cubic centimetres and a dry mass of 130 grams, what is its bulk density?
qs.e: Bulk density = Dry soil mass / Total volume = 130 g / 100 cm³ = 1.30 g/cm³.

qs.q: Which factor of soil formation is considered a passive factor according to Jenny's state factor equation?
qs.e: Parent material and topography are passive factors of soil formation, while climate and organisms are active factors.

qs.q: What type of soil clay mineral exhibits high swelling when wet and severe shrinking when dry?
qs.e: Montmorillonite is an expanding 2:1 lattice clay mineral that swells significantly upon hydration and shrinks on drying.

qs.q: What percentage total porosity does a soil possess if its bulk density is 1.30 g/cm³ and its particle density is 2.60 g/cm³?
qs.e: Porosity = [1 - (Bulk Density / Particle Density)] * 100 = [1 - (1.30 / 2.60)] * 100 = 50%.

qs.q: Which biological soil organism is primarily responsible for decomposing woody plant matter containing lignin?
qs.e: Fungi possess specialized enzymes (such as laccase and peroxidase) capable of breaking down complex lignin molecules.

qs.q: Which micro-nutrient is required in trace amounts for nitrogenase enzyme activity during biological nitrogen fixation?
qs.e: Molybdenum is a component of the nitrogenase enzyme complex necessary for symbiotic and non-symbiotic nitrogen fixation.

qs.q: How many kilograms of a 15-15-15 NPK compound fertilizer are required to supply 30 kg of phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) to a field?
qs.e: Mass of fertilizer = Required P2O5 / Percentage P2O5 = 30 kg / 0.15 = 200 kg.

qs.q: Which micro-nutrient deficiency causes 'hollow heart' in root crops and distorted apical growth in plants?
qs.e: Boron is crucial for cell division and sugar translocation; deficiency causes internal tissue breakdown like hollow heart.

qs.q: Which process converts inorganic soil mineral nitrogen into organic forms incorporated into microbial biomass?
qs.e: Immobilization occurs when microorganisms absorb mineral nitrogen (NH4+ or NO3-) to build cellular proteins, rendering it temporarily unavailable to plants.

qs.q: How many kilograms of Single Superphosphate (18 percent P2O5) are needed to provide 45 kg of P2O5?
qs.e: Mass of SSP required = 45 kg / 0.18 = 250 kg.

qs.q: Which micro-nutrient deficiency causes 'little leaf' disease and shortened internodes in maize plants?
qs.e: Zinc deficiency reduces auxin synthesis, leading to stunted stem growth and small, clustered leaves ('little leaf').

qs.q: How many kilograms of Muriate of Potash (60 percent K2O) are required to supply 30 kg of K2O to a cocoa farm?
qs.e: Weight of MOP needed = 30 kg / 0.60 = 50 kg.

qs.q: What is the primary cause of nitrogen loss when urea is surface-broadcast on warm, alkaline, moist soils without incorporation?
qs.e: Surface-applied urea hydrolyzes into ammonium carbonate, which breaks down into gaseous ammonia (NH3) that volatilizes into air.

qs.q: Which type of irrigation relies on raising the underground water table so moisture moves upward into the root zone by capillarity?
qs.e: Sub-irrigation applies water below the root zone, raising the water table so water moves upward by capillary action.

qs.q: What pressure potential value (in bars) is conventionally associated with soil moisture at field capacity?
qs.e: Field capacity corresponds to a matric potential of approximately -0.33 bar (-33 kPa).

qs.q: What device measures actual evapotranspiration of crops in controlled field lysimeter studies?
qs.e: A lysimeter measures water balance parameters (precipitation, drainage, evapotranspiration) for a soil-plant system.

qs.q: What is the primary cause of physiological drought in crops growing in saline soils?
o: Complete absence of water molecules in soil pores
Excessive transpiration through thick leaf cuticles
Destruction of plant xylem vessels by salt crystals
High osmotic pressure of soil solution preventing water absorption
qs.e: High salt concentration lowers soil water potential (high osmotic pressure), making it difficult for roots to extract water.

qs.q: What component in a disc harrow allows adjusting the angle of disc gangs relative to the direction of travel?
qs.e: Adjusting disc gang angles changes cutting aggressiveness and soil pulverization depth.

qs.q: Which tillage machine utilizes mole plugs attached to subsoiler shanks to form unlined underground drainage channels?
qs.e: Mole ploughs drag bullet-shaped torpedoes through clay subsoils, creating unlined subterranean drainage channels.

qs.q: What calculation computes the area of a trapezoidal farmland plot with parallel bases of 120 m and 80 m, and a perpendicular distance of 50 m?
If a whole circle bearing of a line is 225 degrees, what is its corresponding quadrantal bearing?
qs.e: 225° lies in SW quadrant (between 180° and 270°). Quadrantal bearing = 225° - 180° = S 45° W.

qs.q: What straight line sight instrument is used on a plane table to align sight lines toward target ranging poles?
qs.e: An alidade is a straightedge rule with sighting vanes used on plane tables to draw sightlines.

qs.q: Which mechanical instrument is used on finished survey maps to measure irregular enclosed areas by tracing boundaries?
qs.e: A planimeter traces irregular map perimeters to integrate and calculate enclosed surface area directly.

qs.q: What formula calculates the magnetic declination angle between True North and Magnetic North?
o: Magnetic Declination = True Bearing + Whole Circle Bearing
Magnetic Declination = Back Bearing / Fore Bearing
Magnetic Declination = True Bearing - Magnetic Bearing
qs.e: Magnetic declination represents the angular difference between True Geographic North and Magnetic North.

qs.q: What term describes non-pesticidal chemical additives mixed into formulations to enhance active ingredient toxicity?
qs.e: Synergists (e.g., piperonyl butoxide) inhibit detoxification enzymes in target pests, boosting pesticide potency.

qs.q: Which chemical class includes systemic neonicotinoid insecticides that act as agonists on insect nicotinic acetylcholine receptors?
qs.e: Neonicotinoids (e.g. imidacloprid) act on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in insect central nervous systems.

qs.q: Which agrochemical class includes glyphosate that inhibits the EPSP synthase enzyme in the shikimate pathway?
qs.e: Glyphosate is an organophosphonate compound inhibiting 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate (EPSP) synthase.

qs.q: Which marine/brackish water fish species is cultivated in coastal West African brackish water enclosures?
qs.e: Mugil cephalus (grey mullet) is euryhaline, thriving in brackish coastal lagoons and estuaries.

qs.q: What technique produces all-male tilapia fingerlings by feeding male sex hormones (17-alpha methyltestosterone) to fry?
qs.e: Feeding 17-alpha methyltestosterone to newly hatched tilapia fry reverses female phenotypes into all-male populations.

qs.q: What term describes fish species that migrate from marine oceans into freshwater rivers to spawn?
qs.e: Anadromous fish (e.g. salmon) live in marine waters and migrate into freshwater rivers to breed.

qs.q: What science determines standing tree age by counting annual growth rings in wood core samples?
qs.e: Dendrochronology analyzes annual tree ring patterns to date tree age and past climate events.

qs.q: Which parasitic mite species infests adult bees and brood in hives, causing colony collapse disorder?
qs.e: Varroa destructor is an external parasitic mite that feeds on fat body tissues of bees and transmits viruses.

qs.q: Which enzyme joins cut DNA fragments together by forming phosphodiester bonds during recombinant DNA cloning?
qs.e: DNA ligase seals nicks in double-stranded DNA by catalyzing phosphodiester bond formation.

qs.q: If a farmer applies 100 kg of fertilizer and yields 3,000 kg of maize, and applying 120 kg yields 3,400 kg, what is the marginal physical product of the extra 20 kg of fertilizer?
o: 400 kg of maize total or 20 kg maize per kg fertilizer
qs.e: Change in output = 3,400 - 3,000 = 400 kg maize. Marginal physical product = 400 kg / 20 kg fertilizer = 20 kg maize/kg fertilizer.

qs.q: Which farm production function region represents the economically rational zone of input utilization?
o: Stage III or negative return stage
qs.e: Stage II (where MPP is positive but declining) is the rational production zone where profit maximization occurs.

qs.q: Why is Stage I of a classical production function considered economically irrational for farm managers?
o: Marginal physical product is increasing, meaning fixed inputs are underutilized
qs.e: In Stage I, average physical product increases with variable input, meaning fixed resources are underused; adding input yields increasing average returns.

qs.q: What curve shows all combinations of two inputs that can produce the same total level of crop output?
qs.e: An isoquant (equal-product curve) depicts all input combinations generating a constant output level.

qs.q: What line represents all combinations of two variable inputs that a farmer can purchase with a fixed budget?
qs.e: An iso-cost line shows all input combinations achievable given fixed input prices and budget.

qs.q: What index evaluates the yield advantage of intercropping over sole cropping on the same land area?
qs.e: Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) evaluates land area needed under monoculture to equal intercropped yields (LER > 1.0 indicates yield advantage).

qs.q: What evaluation tool measures changes in farmer knowledge, attitudes, skills, and aspirations resulting from an extension program?
qs.e: KASA measures changes in Knowledge, Attitudes, Skills, and Aspirations of extension target beneficiaries.

qs.q: Using Pearson Square, to formulate a 20 percent CP broiler starter diet using Sorghum (8 percent CP) and Fishmeal (60 percent CP), what percentage of Fishmeal is needed?
qs.e: Parts: Sorghum = |60 - 20| = 40; Fishmeal = |20 - 8| = 12. Total parts = 52. Fishmeal % = (12/52)*100 = 23.08%.

qs.q: What term describes the phenomenon where seeds germinate while still attached to the parent plant fruit?
qs.e: Vivipary is precocious seed germination while the seed remains attached to the parent fruit (e.g. in mangroves).

qs.q: What is the term for seed development without fertilization where seeds are genetically identical to the female parent?
qs.e: Apomixis is asexual seed formation bypassing meiosis and syngamy, producing clonal seeds.

qs.q: What is the recommended seed rate per hectare for maize when planting single seeds at 0.75 m x 0.25 m spacing assuming seed mass of 250 g per 1,000 seeds?
qs.e: Plant population = 53,333 stands/ha. Total seed mass = 53,333 * (250 g / 1000) = 13,333 g = 13.3 kg/ha.

qs.q: Which chemical group of herbicides acts by inhibiting the acetolactate synthase (ALS) enzyme in susceptible weed species?
qs.e: Sulfonylurea herbicides block ALS enzyme activity, stopping branched-chain amino acid synthesis in targeted weeds.

qs.q: What is the particle density of a soil sample if a soil solid volume of 50 cubic centimetres has a dry mass of 132.5 grams?
qs.e: Particle density = Mass of solids / Volume of solids = 132.5 / 50 = 2.65 g/cm³.

qs.q: Which soil order is characterized by highly weathered, reddish tropical soils rich in iron and aluminium oxides?
qs.e: Oxisols (or Ferralsols) are intensely weathered tropical soils dominated by iron and aluminium oxide clays.

qs.q: Which soil thermal property describes the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of dry soil by 1 degree Celsius?
qs.e: Specific heat capacity is the quantity of heat required to increase the temperature of a unit mass of soil by 1 °C.

qs.q: Which term describes a sequence of soils developed from similar parent material under similar climate but varying in relief and drainage?
qs.e: A soil catena is a topographic sequence of soils along a slope that differ primarily due to drainage and elevation differences.

qs.q: What ratio of Nitrogen to Carbon in organic residues generally promotes rapid microbial decomposition without temporary nitrogen immobilization?
qs.e: Organic material with a C:N ratio below 30:1 decomposes rapidly without causing microbes to scavenge soil mineral nitrogen.

qs.q: Which micro-nutrient is essential for lignin synthesis and disease resistance in cereal crop cell walls?
qs.e: Copper is involved in polyphenol oxidase activity and lignification of plant stem tissue, enhancing mechanical strength.

qs.q: Which micro-nutrient plays an essential role in photosynthesis by participating in the photolysis of water in Photosystem II?
qs.e: Manganese ions form part of the oxygen-evolving complex required for water splitting (photolysis) during photosynthesis.

qs.q: Which water quality parameter measures the relative concentration of sodium ions to calcium and magnesium ions in irrigation water?
qs.e: Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR) assesses the potential for irrigation water to cause sodium hazard and soil structural deterioration.

qs.q: Which chemical fungicide class includes triadimefon and propiconazole that inhibit ergosterol biosynthesis in fungal membranes?
qs.e: Triazole fungicides block C-14 demethylation during fungal ergosterol synthesis.

qs.q: What molecular marker technique uses short random primers to amplify unknown DNA fragments across crop genomes?
qs.e: RAPD uses single short arbitrary primers in PCR to generate polymorphic genomic DNA band patterns.

qs.q: What line on a production isoquant map joins points where the marginal rate of technical substitution equals input price ratios?
qs.e: The expansion path connects cost-minimizing input combinations as enterprise output expands.

qs.q: What measure expresses the percentage change in agricultural output resulting from a one percent change in variable input?
qs.e: Production elasticity = % change in output / % change in input = MPP / APP.

qs.q: If sole maize yields 4 tonnes/ha and sole cowpea yields 1.5 tonnes/ha, while intercropped maize yields 3 tonnes/ha and intercropped cowpea yields 1.0 tonne/ha, what is the Land Equivalent Ratio?
qs.e: LER = (3.0 / 4.0) + (1.0 / 1.5) = 0.75 + 0.67 = 1.42. (An LER of 1.42 indicates a 42% land-use advantage).

qs.q: A feed ration mixes 60 kg of maize (9% crude protein) with 40 kg of soybean meal (44% crude protein). What is the crude protein percentage of the mixture?
A feed ration mixes 70 kg of maize (9% crude protein) with 30 kg of soybean meal (44% crude protein). What is the crude protein percentage of the mixture?
A feed ration mixes 50 kg of maize (9% crude protein) with 50 kg of soybean meal (44% crude protein). What is the crude protein percentage of the mixture?
A feed ration mixes 65 kg of maize (8% crude protein) with 35 kg of soybean meal (42% crude protein). What is the crude protein percentage of the mixture?
A feed ration mixes 55 kg of maize (10% crude protein) with 45 kg of soybean meal (38% crude protein). What is the crude protein percentage of the mixture?
A maize enterprise records total revenue of N1,500,000 and total variable costs of N900,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N1,500,000 - N900,000 = N600,000.

qs.q: A maize enterprise records total revenue of N2,400,000 and total variable costs of N1,500,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N2,400,000 - N1,500,000 = N900,000.

qs.q: A maize enterprise records total revenue of N800,000 and total variable costs of N350,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N800,000 - N350,000 = N450,000.

qs.q: A maize enterprise records total revenue of N1,900,000 and total variable costs of N1,100,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N1,900,000 - N1,100,000 = N800,000.

qs.q: A maize enterprise records total revenue of N1,200,000 and total variable costs of N480,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N1,200,000 - N480,000 = N720,000.

qs.q: A maize enterprise records total revenue of N3,200,000 and total variable costs of N2,100,000. Calculate the gross margin.
qs.e: Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total Variable Costs = N3,200,000 - N2,100,000 = N1,100,000.

qs.q: A poultry enterprise has a gross margin of N700,000 and total fixed costs of N200,000. Determine its net profit.
qs.e: Net Profit = Gross Margin - Fixed Costs = N700,000 - N200,000 = N500,000.

qs.q: A poultry enterprise has a gross margin of N900,000 and total fixed costs of N350,000. Determine its net profit.
qs.e: Net Profit = Gross Margin - Fixed Costs = N900,000 - N350,000 = N550,000.

qs.q: A poultry enterprise has a gross margin of N550,000 and total fixed costs of N150,000. Determine its net profit.
qs.e: Net Profit = Gross Margin - Fixed Costs = N550,000 - N150,000 = N400,000.

qs.q: A poultry enterprise has a gross margin of N1,250,000 and total fixed costs of N480,000. Determine its net profit.
qs.e: Net Profit = Gross Margin - Fixed Costs = N1,250,000 - N480,000 = N770,000.

qs.q: A farmer applies 2 bags of a 46% nitrogen fertilizer, each bag weighing 50 kg. How many kg of pure nitrogen are applied in total?
qs.e: Pure N = 2 x 50 kg x 46/100 = 46 kg.

qs.q: A farmer applies 3 bags of a 46% nitrogen fertilizer, each bag weighing 50 kg. How many kg of pure nitrogen are applied in total?
qs.e: Pure N = 3 x 50 kg x 46/100 = 69 kg.

qs.q: A farmer applies 5 bags of a 20% nitrogen fertilizer, each bag weighing 25 kg. How many kg of pure nitrogen are applied in total?
qs.e: Pure N = 5 x 25 kg x 20/100 = 25 kg.

qs.q: A farmer applies 4 bags of a 15% nitrogen fertilizer, each bag weighing 50 kg. How many kg of pure nitrogen are applied in total?
qs.e: Pure N = 4 x 50 kg x 15/100 = 30 kg.

qs.q: A farmer applies 6 bags of a 12% nitrogen fertilizer, each bag weighing 50 kg. How many kg of pure nitrogen are applied in total?
qs.e: Pure N = 6 x 50 kg x 12/100 = 36 kg.

qs.q: A batch of broilers consumes 120 kg of feed and records a total weight gain of 50 kg. Calculate the feed conversion ratio.
qs.e: FCR = feed consumed / weight gained = 120 / 50 = 2.4.

qs.q: A batch of broilers consumes 96 kg of feed and records a total weight gain of 32 kg. Calculate the feed conversion ratio.
qs.e: FCR = feed consumed / weight gained = 96 / 32 = 3.0.

qs.q: A batch of broilers consumes 180 kg of feed and records a total weight gain of 60 kg. Calculate the feed conversion ratio.
qs.e: FCR = feed consumed / weight gained = 180 / 60 = 3.0.

qs.q: A batch of broilers consumes 75 kg of feed and records a total weight gain of 25 kg. Calculate the feed conversion ratio.
qs.e: FCR = feed consumed / weight gained = 75 / 25 = 3.0.

qs.q: A flock of 500 layers produces 410 eggs on a given day. What is the percentage hen-day production?
qs.e: Hen-day production = (eggs / number of hens) x 100 = (410/500) x 100 = 82.0 percent.

qs.q: A flock of 800 layers produces 640 eggs on a given day. What is the percentage hen-day production?
qs.e: Hen-day production = (eggs / number of hens) x 100 = (640/800) x 100 = 80.0 percent.

qs.q: A flock of 250 layers produces 195 eggs on a given day. What is the percentage hen-day production?
qs.e: Hen-day production = (eggs / number of hens) x 100 = (195/250) x 100 = 78.0 percent.

qs.q: A flock of 1200 layers produces 900 eggs on a given day. What is the percentage hen-day production?
qs.e: Hen-day production = (eggs / number of hens) x 100 = (900/1200) x 100 = 75.0 percent.

qs.q: A survey line rises 25 m over a horizontal distance of 500 m. Express the gradient as a percentage.
qs.e: Gradient (%) = vertical rise / horizontal distance x 100 = (25/500) x 100 = 5.0 percent.

qs.q: A survey line rises 15 m over a horizontal distance of 300 m. Express the gradient as a percentage.
qs.e: Gradient (%) = vertical rise / horizontal distance x 100 = (15/300) x 100 = 5.0 percent.

qs.q: A survey line rises 40 m over a horizontal distance of 800 m. Express the gradient as a percentage.
qs.e: Gradient (%) = vertical rise / horizontal distance x 100 = (40/800) x 100 = 5.0 percent.

qs.q: A survey line rises 8 m over a horizontal distance of 200 m. Express the gradient as a percentage.
qs.e: Gradient (%) = vertical rise / horizontal distance x 100 = (8/200) x 100 = 4.0 percent.

qs.q: A stock agrochemical is diluted at 5 ml per 100 litres of water. How much stock chemical is needed for 100 litres of spray solution?
qs.e: Chemical required = (100 / 100) x 5 ml = 5 ml.

qs.q: A stock agrochemical is diluted at 2 ml per 200 litres of water. How much stock chemical is needed for 800 litres of spray solution?
qs.e: Chemical required = (800 / 200) x 2 ml = 8 ml.

qs.q: A stock agrochemical is diluted at 10 ml per 400 litres of water. How much stock chemical is needed for 800 litres of spray solution?
qs.e: Chemical required = (800 / 400) x 10 ml = 20 ml.

qs.q: A stock agrochemical is diluted at 8 ml per 300 litres of water. How much stock chemical is needed for 900 litres of spray solution?
qs.e: Chemical required = (900 / 300) x 8 ml = 24 ml.

qs.q: A stock agrochemical is diluted at 4 ml per 500 litres of water. How much stock chemical is needed for 2500 litres of spray solution?
qs.e: Chemical required = (2500 / 500) x 4 ml = 20 ml.

qs.q: A paddock of 10 hectares carries 20 cattle. What is the stocking rate in animals per hectare?
qs.e: Stocking rate = number of animals / area = 20 / 10 = 2.0 animals per hectare.

qs.q: A paddock of 25 hectares carries 50 cattle. What is the stocking rate in animals per hectare?
qs.e: Stocking rate = number of animals / area = 50 / 25 = 2.0 animals per hectare.

qs.q: A paddock of 8 hectares carries 16 cattle. What is the stocking rate in animals per hectare?
qs.e: Stocking rate = number of animals / area = 16 / 8 = 2.0 animals per hectare.

qs.q: A paddock of 40 hectares carries 80 cattle. What is the stocking rate in animals per hectare?
qs.e: Stocking rate = number of animals / area = 80 / 40 = 2.0 animals per hectare.

qs.q: Explain why a waterlogged soil loses nitrogen through denitrification even when organic matter is abundant.
o: Aerobic bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen directly
Nitrates leach upward by capillary action
Anaerobic bacteria convert nitrates to nitrogen gas
qs.e: In waterlogged (anaerobic) conditions, denitrifying bacteria reduce nitrates back to gaseous nitrogen, which escapes to the atmosphere.

qs.q: A crop shows interveinal chlorosis on older leaves with leaf margins curling upward. Which nutrient deficiency is most consistent?
qs.e: Magnesium is mobile in the plant; its deficiency shows first on older leaves as interveinal chlorosis because magnesium is central in chlorophyll.

qs.q: In farm surveying, which instrument combination is best for measuring both horizontal and vertical angles precisely?
qs.e: The theodolite measures both horizontal and vertical angles accurately, unlike the compass (bearing only), chain (distance only) or Abney level (slope only).

qs.q: Which biological control agent is classically used against the cassava mealybug in West Africa?
qs.e: Epidinocarsis lopezi, a parasitoid wasp, was introduced successfully to control Phenacoccus manihoti, the cassava mealybug.

qs.q: Why is crop rotation effective against soil-borne pathogens such as bacterial wilt?
o: Rotation increases soil pH above pathogen tolerance
Tillage during rotation fumigates the soil
A break in host continuity starves the pathogen
qs.e: Most soil-borne pathogens are host-specific; rotating to non-host crops breaks their life cycle, starving the pathogen population.

qs.q: Which breeding technique produces a single cross hybrid maize variety?
o: Crossing an inbred line with its parent
qs.e: A single cross hybrid results from crossing two genetically unrelated inbred lines, exploiting heterosis for vigour.

qs.q: In apiculture, why is a queen excluder installed between the brood chamber and the honey super?
o: It prevents the queen from laying eggs in honey combs
It kills varroa mites entering the super
It separates drones from worker bees
qs.e: A queen excluder is a grid sized to let worker bees pass but block the larger queen, keeping eggs out of harvested honey combs.

qs.q: A fish pond stocked at 2 fingerlings per square metre shows stunted growth at harvest. What is the most likely management cause?
o: Overstocking relative to natural feed supply
Excess dissolved oxygen in pond water
qs.e: At high stocking density, natural food and dissolved oxygen become limiting, causing competition and stunting.

qs.q: Which soil structure type has the greatest risk of crusting after heavy rain, reducing seedling emergence?
qs.e: Massive structure lacks aggregates, so rain disperses surface particles into a sealing crust that blocks seedling emergence.

qs.q: Why does zero-grazing (cut-and-carry) dairy farming often raise milk yield per cow compared to extensive grazing?
o: Cows exercise more on open range
Fed concentrates and forage are controlled and balanced
qs.e: Under zero-grazing, intake of quality forage and concentrate is measured and balanced to production needs, while energy is not wasted roaming.

qs.q: According to the first account of creation in Genesis, on which day did God create light?
qs.e: In Genesis chapter one, God created light on the first day of creation when He said, 'Let there be light.'

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, who was the first son born to Adam and Eve?
qs.e: Genesis records that Cain was the firstborn son of Adam and Eve, followed by his brother Abel.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham was instructed by God to leave his native land of
qs.e: God called Abraham to leave Haran and journey to the land of Canaan which He promised to give to his descendants.

qs.q: In the Old Testament narrative, which patriarch was given the new name Israel after wrestling at Peniel?
qs.e: Jacob was renamed Israel by God after he wrestled with a divine messenger at Peniel until daybreak.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, God revealed His divine name to Moses at the burning bush as
qs.e: At Mount Horeb, God revealed His holy name to Moses as 'I AM WHO I AM' when commissioning him to free Israel.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus delivered the Sermon on the Mount primarily to teach His followers about
o: the values and principles of the Kingdom of God
the political downfall of the Roman empire
the rebuild of the physical Jerusalem temple
the ceremonial dietary laws of Moses
qs.e: The Sermon on the Mount expounds the moral, ethical, and spiritual standards required of citizens of God's Kingdom.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, who was the first Christian martyr stoned to death for his testimony?
qs.e: Stephen, one of the seven chosen deacons, became the first recorded Christian martyr after testifying before the Sanhedrin.

qs.q: According to the second account of creation in Genesis, God formed woman from
o: a rib taken from the man while he slept
a branch of the olive tree
qs.e: In Genesis chapter two, God caused a deep sleep to fall upon man and created woman from one of his ribs.

qs.q: In the story of Noah and the Flood in Genesis, the sign of God's covenant never again to destroy the earth with water was the
qs.e: God set the rainbow in the clouds as a sign of His covenant with Noah and every living creature.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Joseph was sold by his brothers into slavery to a traveling caravan of
qs.e: Joseph's brothers sold him to Ishmaelite traders heading to Egypt for twenty pieces of silver.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, the final plague that persuaded Pharaoh to let the Israelites leave Egypt was the
