o: death of all firstborn males in Egypt
plague of severe hail and fire
qs.e: The tenth plague brought the death of all firstborn sons and cattle in Egypt, prompting Pharaoh to release Israel.

qs.q: According to the Book of Judges, which female leader and prophetess judged Israel under the palm tree?
qs.e: Deborah was a prophetess and judge who held court under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, King Saul was rejected by God as king primarily because he
o: offered unauthorized sacrifice and spared Agag
refused to build a royal palace
married foreign women who worshipped idols
qs.e: Saul's disobedience at Gilgal and failure to completely execute God's judgment on Amalek led to his rejection.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount
qs.e: Elijah confronted 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel to demonstrate that Yahweh is the true God.

qs.q: In the Book of Amos, the prophet condemned the wealthy people of Samaria primarily for
o: refusing to trade with neighbor nations
oppressing the poor and trampling on the needy
neglecting to train their youth for military battle
qs.e: Amos denounced Samaria's elite for luxury, dishonesty, bribery, and severe exploitation of the poor.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Luke, the angel who announced the birth of Jesus to Mary was
qs.e: Gabriel was sent by God to Nazareth to inform Mary that she would conceive Jesus through the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, the Magi brought three gifts to the infant Jesus, which were
qs.e: The wise men from the east presented gold, frankincense, and myrrh to the young child Jesus in Bethlehem.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the Holy Spirit descended upon the believers on the Day of Pentecost in the form of
o: a bright cloud and thunderous lightning
tongues as of fire and a rushing wind
a gentle white dove flying from heaven
a flaming pillar standing over the upper room
qs.e: Acts records that divided tongues as of fire rested on each believer accompanied by the sound of a violent wind.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Romans, justification is described as being received through
o: strict adherence to Mosaic ceremonial rituals
faith in Jesus Christ rather than works of the law
membership in the earthly Jewish commonwealth
qs.e: Paul emphasizes that justification is a gift of God's grace appropriated by faith in Jesus Christ.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham showed supreme faith when he was commanded to sacrifice his son Isaac on Mount
qs.e: Abraham demonstrated ultimate trust in God by obeying the command to offer Isaac on Mount Moriah.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Pharaoh promoted Joseph to governor after Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams as predicting
o: a military invasion by the neighboring Syrian kingdom
seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine
a sudden flood of the River Nile destroying crops
three years of plague followed by ten years of peace
qs.e: Joseph correctly interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of cows and grain heads as seven years of plenty and seven of famine.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, the Passover lamb was required to be
o: a female sheep two years old
a male one year old without any blemish
any healthy goat from the flock
an ox dedicated to God at the altar
qs.e: The Lord instructed that each Passover lamb must be a male without defect, one year of age.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, Samuel warned the Israelites requesting a king that a monarch would
o: abolish all priestly sacrifices at Shiloh
take their sons, daughters, fields, and a tenth of their produce
force the nation into permanent foreign exile
demand the destruction of all tribal boundary markers
qs.e: Samuel outlined the heavy rights of a king, including conscription, heavy taxation, and forced labor.

qs.q: According to the Second Book of Samuel, when Prophet Nathan confronted King David over his sin with Bathsheba, Nathan used the parable of
o: a vineyard owner whose tenants refused to pay rent
a rich man who stole a poor man's single beloved ewe lamb
a shepherd who left ninety-nine sheep to find one
a king who invited guests to a royal wedding feast
qs.e: Nathan used the moving story of the rich man taking the poor man's lamb to bring David to repentance.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, King Solomon requested from God at Gibeon
o: an understanding heart to judge God's people wisely
long life and victory over all surrounding enemies
the destruction of all foreign idol temples in Canaan
qs.e: Solomon humbly asked God for wisdom and discernment to govern Israel justly.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, King Rehoboam caused the division of the kingdom because he
o: built pagan altars in the city of Dan
refused to pay tribute to the Egyptian king
rejected the counsel of the elders and increased the burden on the people
surrendered Jerusalem to the Philistine army
qs.e: Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders to lighten the workload, causing ten tribes to rebel under Jeroboam.

qs.q: In the Book of Hosea, God commanded Hosea to marry an unfaithful woman named Gomer in order to symbolize
o: the tragic end of the royal dynasty of Jehu
the political alliance between Israel and Assyria
Israel's unfaithfulness to God through idol worship
the legal process of divorce in ancient Israel
qs.e: Hosea's marriage to Gomer served as a living prophetic illustration of Israel's spiritual adultery.

qs.q: According to the Book of Nehemiah, Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem primarily to
o: translate the Law into the Aramaic language
crown a new descendant of David as king
rebuild the broken walls of the city
establish a new military fortress against Moab
qs.e: Nehemiah was deeply moved by reports of Jerusalem's ruined walls and obtained royal permission to rebuild them.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Mark, when Jesus calmed the storm on the Sea of Galilee, He demonstrated His
o: skill as a seasoned Mediterranean sailor
authority over nature and divine power
desire to avoid preaching to crowds
qs.e: By commanding the wind and waves to be still, Jesus revealed His sovereign power over creation.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke, the elder brother reacted to the prodigal son's return with
o: joy and immediate embrace of his brother
anger and refusal to join the celebration
eager assistance in preparing the feast
qs.e: The elder brother became angry and resented the merciful welcome given to his repentant younger brother.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, during the Last Supper, the bread broken by Jesus symbolized His
qs.e: Jesus broke the bread and gave it to His disciples, stating that it represented His body given for them.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Ananias and Sapphira died suddenly because they
o: refused to attend the apostles' daily teaching
stole money directly from the church treasury
lied to the Holy Spirit about the full price of their sold land
worshipped Roman deities secretly in their house
qs.e: Ananias and Sapphira held back part of the proceeds while pretending to give the total amount, lying to God.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, the conversion of Cornelius at Caesarea was historically significant because it demonstrated that
o: Roman soldiers were required to resign military duty
Jerusalem was no longer the administrative center
the Gospel and salvation were extended to Gentiles as well as Jews
the apostles must write written scriptures immediately
qs.e: The outpouring of the Holy Spirit on Cornelius' household confirmed God's acceptance of Gentile believers.

qs.q: According to Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, the greatest spiritual virtue that endures forever is
qs.e: Paul concludes his discourse on spiritual gifts by declaring that faith, hope, and love remain, but love is greatest.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God's covenant with Abraham involved the physical sign of circumcision, which served as
o: a temporary practice that ceased upon entry into Egypt
a requirement for entering into civil administration in ancient Canaan
a permanent ritual token of the eternal covenant between God and Abraham's descendants
a substitute for animal sacrifices performed at the altar
qs.e: Circumcision was instituted by God in Genesis seventeen as the enduring covenant sign for Abraham's lineage.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, Moses fled to the land of Midian after he
o: refused to pay taxes to the royal Egyptian palace
destroyed an Egyptian idol in the city of Memphis
killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew worker
led an unarmed protest against Pharaoh's workload
qs.e: Moses fled Pharaoh's wrath to Midian after killing an Egyptian overseer mistreating a Hebrew.

qs.q: According to the Book of Judges, Gideon reduced his army from thirty-two thousand men down to three hundred based on
o: their ability to handle heavy iron swords
their age and physical height in battle ranks
how the men drank water at the spring of Harod
whether they owned horses and chariot equipment
qs.e: God instructed Gideon to separate the men who lapped water directly with their tongues from those who knelt.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, Naboth refused to sell his vineyard to King Ahab primarily because
o: Ahab offered a price far below market value
he planned to sell it to foreign merchants
it was the inheritance of his ancestors which Mosaic law forbade transferring
he disliked King Ahab's religious court policies
qs.e: Naboth stood firm on God's law regarding ancestral land inheritance, refusing to forfeit his patrimony.

qs.q: According to the Book of Isaiah, the vision of the prophet in the temple included seraphim calling holy, after which Isaiah responded to God's call by saying
o: I am too young to speak to Israel
Lord, send my older brother instead
Wait until I consult my household
qs.e: Upon hearing God's inquiry 'Whom shall I send?', Isaiah willingly responded with total submission.

qs.q: In the Book of Jeremiah, the prophet used the image of a potter reworking spoiled clay to illustrate that
o: artisans in Israel should use finer clay
the temple vessel production was corrupt
God has absolute authority to reshape and restore nations that repent
qs.e: Jeremiah's visit to the potter's house demonstrated God's sovereign right to remold nations according to their response.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught that anyone who is angry with a brother without cause is in danger of
o: paying a fine to the city magistrates
judgment, comparing internal hatred to murder
qs.e: Jesus deepened the commandment against murder by condemning malicious anger and internal hatred.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, when Jesus healed the ten lepers, the only person who returned to give thanks was
qs.e: Of the ten cleansed lepers, only the Samaritan foreigner returned to glorify God and thank Jesus.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Sower, the seeds that fell among thorns represent people who
o: understand the message fully and teach others
immediately reject the truth with open hostility
endure trials steadfastly until the final harvest
hear the word, but worldly cares and riches choke it so it yields no fruit
qs.e: Jesus explained that thorny soil represents hearts where anxiety and wealth choke spiritual growth.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Philip preached the Gospel in Samaria and later baptized an official from Ethiopia who was reading from the Book of
qs.e: The Ethiopian eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah's passage regarding the suffering servant when Philip met him.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Galatians, the Law served as a tutor or guardian until Christ came, meaning that
o: the Law was flawed and created by human leaders
the ceremonial law replaces faith in Christ
believers must keep every rabbinic addition strictly
the Law exposed sin and directed humanity toward justification by faith
qs.e: Paul explains that the Mosaic Law functioned as a custodian to point out transgression until Christ brought faith.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Jeroboam established golden calves at Dan and Bethel primarily to
o: honor the Mosaic tradition of the golden altar of incense
compete with the architectural beauty of the Phoenician temples
fulfil a vow he made while exiled in the land of Egypt
prevent the northern tribes from traveling to Jerusalem for worship and defecting to Judah
qs.e: Jeroboam instituted idol worship at Dan and Bethel to stop northern Israelites from visiting Jerusalem's temple.

qs.q: In the Book of Ezekiel, the dramatic vision of the valley of dry bones coming back to life symbolized
o: the literal resurrection of physical bodies at the end of time
the destruction of the pagan temples of Babylon
the military victory of Judah over Edomite forces
the complete spiritual and national restoration of the exiled house of Israel
qs.e: Ezekiel's vision of dry bones receiving breath depicted God's promise to revive and restore exiled Israel.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the Jerusalem Council decided that Gentile Christians were not bound to follow circumcision, but must abstain from
o: paying taxes to pagan Roman authorities
things offered to idols, blood, strangled meat, and sexual immorality
entering any Jewish synagogue on the Sabbath day
qs.e: Acts fifteen records that Gentiles were freed from circumcision but instructed to avoid idolatry, blood, strangled meat, and immorality.

qs.q: In Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, Paul compares the Christian church community to a human body in order to emphasize that
o: spiritual gifts should only be exercised by designated elders
the head of the church must be an earthly bishop residing in Rome
physical health is guaranteed to every faithful Christian
every member has a unique essential function and all must work in mutual harmony
qs.e: Paul uses the human body metaphor to teach that diverse gifts are essential and inter-dependent within the Church.

qs.q: According to the Book of Job, Job maintained his moral integrity throughout severe suffering, demonstrating that
o: righteousness always guarantees immediate earthly wealth
human beings can demand answers from God in court
suffering is always a direct punishment for personal wickedness
true faith and reverence for God are not dependent on material prosperity or temporal comfort
qs.e: Job's steadfast faith proved Satan wrong by showing that genuine worship is rooted in God Himself, not material blessings.

qs.q: In the story of creation in Genesis, God rested from all His work of creation on the
qs.e: On the seventh day, God ended His work of creation and blessed it as a day of rest.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, which patriarch was spared from the wickedness of the world by building an ark?
qs.e: Noah found favor in God's eyes and built an ark to preserve his family and animals from the flood.

qs.q: In the Old Testament narrative, the mother of Isaac was
qs.e: Sarah was Abraham's wife who gave birth to Isaac in her old age as God had promised.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, who was appointed to be the spokesman for Moses before Pharaoh?
qs.e: Aaron, the brother of Moses, was appointed by God to serve as Moses' spokesman before Pharaoh.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, who was the young boy who ministered under Eli the priest at Shiloh?
qs.e: Samuel was dedicated to God by his mother Hannah and served under Eli at the tabernacle in Shiloh.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus was born in the town of
qs.e: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in accordance with the prophecy of Micah.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Mark, Jesus was baptized in the River Jordan by
qs.e: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the River Jordan, at which point the Holy Spirit descended like a dove.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Jacob bought the birthright of his twin brother Esau in exchange for
qs.e: Esau traded his birthright to Jacob when he returned famished from hunting for a meal of red lentil stew.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Potiphar's wife falsely accused Joseph because Joseph refused to
qs.e: Joseph rejected her immoral advances out of moral integrity and obedience to God, leading to his false imprisonment.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, water flowed from the rock to quench Israel's thirst when Moses struck the rock at
qs.e: At Rephidim (Massah and Meribah), God commanded Moses to strike the rock with his staff to produce water.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Samson's great physical strength was tied to his Nazirite vow, which strictly forbade him from
qs.e: Samson's Nazirite vow stipulated that no razor should come upon his head, symbolizing his dedication to God.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, David defeated the Philistine giant Goliath using
o: a sling and five smooth stones
a heavy iron sword and spear
qs.e: David relied on the name of the Lord and struck Goliath in the forehead with a stone from his sling.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, Prophet Elisha healed Naaman, the commander of the Syrian army, of leprosy by instructing him to
o: wash seven times in the River Jordan
drink water from the well of Bethlehem
fast for forty days in the wilderness
qs.e: Elisha told Naaman to dip seven times in the Jordan River, resulting in his complete physical cleansing.

qs.q: According to the Book of Proverbs, the foundational starting point for true knowledge and wisdom is
qs.e: Proverbs states that 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who was the first person to pass by the wounded traveler without helping?
qs.e: A priest saw the wounded man stripped and beaten on the Jericho road, but passed by on the other side.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to John, the first miracle performed by Jesus was turning water into wine at
qs.e: At a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee, Jesus performed His first miracle by changing water into fine wine.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, Jesus warned His disciples against greed using the parable of the man who
o: hid his single talent in the ground out of fear
built bigger barns for his abundant harvest but died that night
refused to forgive his fellow servant a small debt
sold his field to buy a pearl of great price
qs.e: The Parable of the Rich Fool exposes the vanity of accumulating earthly riches while being spiritually bankrupt.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Saul was traveling to Damascus when he encountered Jesus in order to
o: arrest and bring Christians back to Jerusalem
preach in the synagogues of Syria
study law under the Damascus scholars
qs.e: Saul obtained letters from the high priest to arrest any followers of the Way found in Damascus.

qs.q: In Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, the resurrection of Jesus Christ is described as the central foundation of Christian faith because
o: it proves that apostles have secular administrative authority
without the resurrection, preaching and faith are useless and in vain
it guarantees immediate earthly political victory over Rome
it replaces the need for Christian baptism
qs.e: Paul asserts that if Christ has not been raised, Christian faith is futile and believers remain in their sins.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God entered into a formal covenant with Noah after the flood, promising that
o: Israel would inherit the land of Canaan forever
never again would all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood
humanity would no longer experience physical death
the sun and moon would never cease to shine
qs.e: God established a covenant with Noah and creation, pledging never to destroy the earth with a flood again.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Joseph revealed his true identity to his brothers when they returned to buy grain because
o: Pharaoh ordered Joseph to return to Canaan immediately
they brought his full brother Benjamin with them as requested
the famine ended earlier than expected
his brothers threatened to attack the Egyptian royal palace
qs.e: Joseph broke down weeping and revealed himself after seeing their genuine concern for Benjamin and Jacob.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, God gave the Ten Commandments to Moses on tablets of stone at Mount
qs.e: The Decalogue was delivered to Moses at Mount Sinai (Horeb) amidst thunder, lightning, and smoke.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, King Saul disobeyed God's explicit instruction regarding Amalek by sparing
o: the city walls and pagan temples
King Agag and the best of the livestock
the iron chariots and bronze weapons
the royal palace treasury and advisers
qs.e: Saul spared King Agag and the finest sheep and cattle under the guise of offering sacrifices, disobeying God.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah proved that Yahweh was the true God on Mount Carmel when God answered his prayer by
o: sending rain immediately before the sacrifice
sending fire from heaven that consumed the sacrifice, wood, and water
causing a sudden earthquake that destroyed Baal's altar
sending an angel who spoke with a loud trumpet sound
qs.e: Fire fell from heaven and consumed Elijah's sacrifice, the wood, stones, dust, and licked up the water in the trench.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, Elisha's servant Gehazi was struck with leprosy because he
o: refused to wash in the Jordan River
secretly ran after Naaman to demand money and garments for personal gain
stole sacred items from the temple in Samaria
disobeyed Elisha's order to heal the Shunammite child
qs.e: Gehazi greedily pursued Naaman for silver and clothing, lying to both Naaman and Elisha, incurring Naaman's leprosy.

qs.q: According to the Book of Amos, true religious worship requires
o: multitudes of formal animal sacrifices and burnt offerings
building magnificent golden altars in major cities
justice to roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream
fasting twice every week with loud lamentation
qs.e: Amos declared that God despises hypocritical festivals and demands social justice and moral righteousness instead.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, the young Jesus was found by His parents in the temple at Jerusalem after three days, where He was
o: learning carpentry from the temple craftsmen
organizing an armed rebellion against Roman soldiers
sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions
writing copies of the Mosaic law on parchment
qs.e: At twelve years old, Jesus amazed the teachers in the Jerusalem temple with His understanding and answers.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, during His temptation in the wilderness, Jesus responded to Satan's suggestions by
o: calling twelve legions of angels to defend Him
performing dramatic miracles to prove His messianic role
quoting scriptures written in the Book of Deuteronomy
remaining completely silent throughout forty days
qs.e: Jesus repelled every temptation of the devil by declaring 'It is written' and quoting Deuteronomy.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sower, the seeds that fell on rocky ground represent people who
o: reject the gospel message instantly with hatred
produce a hundredfold harvest immediately upon hearing
receive the word with joy but fall away quickly when trouble or persecution arises
are choked by the deceitfulness of wealth and worldly ambitions
qs.e: Jesus taught that rocky soil represents shallow hearts that lack deep root and wither under trial.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus fed five thousand men with five loaves of bread and
qs.e: Jesus multiplied five barley loaves and two small fish to feed five thousand men besides women and children.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Peter and John healed a man lame from birth who was sitting at the temple gate called
qs.e: Peter commanded the lame man at the Beautiful Gate to walk in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Saul's sight was restored after his Damascus encounter when a disciple named
qs.e: Ananias of Damascus laid hands on Saul as commanded by God, causing scales to fall from Saul's eyes.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Romans, believers are urged to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, which means
o: offering animal sacrifices at Jerusalem's altar
withdrawing completely from all civil society
dedicating their lives entirely to holy, acceptable service to God
seeking physical martyrdom in times of persecution
qs.e: Paul exhorts Christians in Romans twelve to offer their total lives as a holy and living sacrifice pleasing to God.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Ephesians, Christian believers are saved by grace through faith, and this salvation is
o: earned through meticulous keeping of the law
a reward reserved exclusively for biological Israelites
a free gift of God so that no one can boast
dependent on individual financial contributions to the church
qs.e: Ephesians states that salvation is God's unearned gift of grace through faith, not a result of human works.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Jacob deceived his aging father Isaac to steal Esau's blessing by
o: claiming Esau had died while hunting in the open field
bribing the household servants to forge Isaac's written testament
wearing Esau's garments and putting goat skins on his hands and neck
presenting a fake decree signed by Abraham
qs.e: With Rebekah's guidance, Jacob covered his smooth skin with goat hair and wore Esau's clothes to deceive Isaac.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, the golden calf built by Aaron while Moses was on Mount Sinai demonstrated Israel's
o: attempt to initiate animal sacrifice before Moses returned
desire to build a grand monument for Egyptian rulers
quick relapse into idolatry and breaking of the covenant
fear of military invasion from surrounding Canaanite tribes
qs.e: The construction of the golden calf violated the commandment against graven images and broken covenant trust.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, King Solomon's heart was turned away from Yahweh in his old age primarily because
o: he refused to offer annual sacrifices at the temple
he spent all national taxes on military fortifications
his foreign wives led him to worship foreign deities such as Ashtoreth and Molech
he appointed non-Levite priests to minister in Jerusalem
qs.e: Solomon's political marriages to foreign women led to syncretism and idolatry, provoking God's anger.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, King Josiah initiated major religious reforms throughout Judah after
o: defeating the Syrian army at Samaria
receiving a prophetic vision from Isaiah
finding the Book of the Law during temple repairs
qs.e: High Priest Hilkiah discovered the Book of the Law in the temple, prompting Josiah to tear his clothes and eliminate idols.

qs.q: According to the Book of Nehemiah, when Sanballat and Tobiah opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, Nehemiah responded by
o: signing a peace treaty with the leaders of Samaria
paying heavy tribute money to buy temporary peace
abandoning the construction project until the king intervened
praying to God while positioning armed guards day and night
qs.e: Nehemiah combined persistent prayer with practical security, arming the builders with swords, spears, and bows.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, during the trial of Jesus, Pontius Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas because
o: the Jewish council demanded a joint trial by two rulers
Pilate lacked legal authority to sentence anyone to death
Herod was visiting Jerusalem specifically to conduct trials
Jesus was a Galilean under Herod's political jurisdiction
qs.e: Learning that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction in Galilee, Pilate sent Him to Herod who was in Jerusalem.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to John, when Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead at Bethany, Lazarus had been in the tomb for
qs.e: Martha pointed out that Lazarus had been dead four days, demonstrating the magnitude of Jesus' resurrection power.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Talents in Matthew, the master condemned the servant who received one talent because he
o: spent the money on personal luxury
lost the money through bad commercial investments
stole his fellow servant's share of the profit
buried his talent in the ground out of fear and slothfulness
qs.e: The wicked, lazy servant hid his master's money in the earth rather than putting it to productive use.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Peter was released from prison in Jerusalem when
o: the Roman governor granted an amnesty decree
the church paid a ransom to King Herod Agrippa
a sudden violent earthquake tore down the prison fortress
an angel of the Lord struck off his chains and opened the iron gate
qs.e: While the church prayed earnest prayers, an angel miraculously freed Peter from double chains and guarded prison doors.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Romans, Christians are instructed to submit to civil governing authorities because
o: governing laws replace the spiritual authority of Christ
rulers possess divine exemption from moral accountability
rebelling against the state destroys individual church property
governing authorities are instituted by God to maintain order and punish wrongdoing
qs.e: Paul teaches in Romans thirteen that civil authorities act as ministers of God to preserve civil order and restrain evil.

qs.q: According to Paul's First Letter to the Thessalonians, believers who have died before Christ's return will
o: forfeit their eternal inheritance in heaven
remain permanently unconscious in the grave
be reincarnated into new earthly lives
rise first when the Lord descends with a shout and trumpet of God
qs.e: Paul reassures believers that at Christ's Second Coming, the dead in Christ will rise first before the living are caught up.

qs.q: According to the Book of Deuteronomy, the Shema formula recited by Israel declares
o: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one
qs.e: The foundational declaration of monotheism in Israel begins with 'Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.'

qs.q: In the Book of Jeremiah, the prophet proclaimed a New Covenant that differs from the Sinai covenant because God will
o: restrict salvation strictly to the tribe of Judah
require double animal sacrifices at Jerusalem
rebuild the stone temple with pure gold
write His laws directly on human hearts and minds
qs.e: Jeremiah prophesied that the New Covenant would feature internal spiritual transformation with laws written on hearts.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Luke, on the road to Emmaus, the resurrected Jesus explained scriptures to two disciples by showing that
o: Gentiles must adopt Jewish circumcision traditions
the Roman empire would fall within their lifetime
the temple in Jerusalem must be rebuilt immediately
the Christ had to suffer these things and enter into His glory
qs.e: Jesus interpreted all scriptures concerning Himself, demonstrating that Messiah's suffering preceded His glory.

qs.q: In Paul's Second Letter to the Corinthians, Paul describes believers as ambassadors for Christ who carry the message of
qs.e: Paul explains that God entrusted Christians with the ministry of reconciliation, calling humanity to be reconciled to God.

qs.q: According to the Letter of James, faith without accompanying good works is described as being
o: sufficient for salvation as long as it is sincere
acceptable to God provided one recites prayers daily
dead in itself and incapable of saving anyone
qs.e: James asserts that genuine saving faith naturally produces good works, declaring that faith without works is dead.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God created human beings in His own image on the
qs.e: On the sixth day of creation, God made land animals and created mankind in His image and likeness.

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, Abraham's wife Sarah gave birth to a son named
qs.e: Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age as God had promised to Abraham.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, Moses was saved from Pharaoh's decree by being placed in a basket in the River
qs.e: Moses' mother placed him in a papyrus basket among the reeds along the bank of the Nile River.

qs.q: In the Old Testament story, who succeeded Moses as the leader of Israel to lead them into Canaan?
qs.e: Joshua son of Nun was appointed by God to succeed Moses and lead Israel across Jordan.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, the first anointed king of Israel was
qs.e: Saul from the tribe of Benjamin was anointed by Prophet Samuel as Israel's first king.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, the angel Gabriel announced the birth of John the Baptist to the priest named
qs.e: Zechariah was serving in the temple when Gabriel announced that Elizabeth would bear a son named John.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the home town of the apostle Paul was
qs.e: Paul was born in Tarsus of Cilicia, a prominent Roman city.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Jacob had a vision of a ladder reaching to heaven while sleeping at
qs.e: At Bethel, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending.

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, Joseph's brothers became jealous of him primarily because Jacob gave Joseph a
qs.e: Jacob loved Joseph more than his brothers and gave him an ornate coat of many colors, sparking envy.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, during the battle against Amalek, Israel prevailed as long as Moses kept his
qs.e: Aaron and Hur held up Moses' hands so that Israel would defeat Amalek at Rephidim.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, which judge defeated the Midianites using only three hundred men with trumpets and pitchers?
qs.e: Gideon led three hundred men carrying trumpets, empty pitchers, and torches to rout the Midianite camp.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, David and Jonathan established a deep covenant friendship characterized by
qs.e: Jonathan loved David as his own soul and protected David from Saul's murderous jealousy.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah was fed during the drought at the brook Cherith by
qs.e: God directed ravens to bring Elijah bread and meat morning and evening by the brook Cherith.

qs.q: According to the Second Book of Kings, Prophet Elisha multiplied the poor widow's jar of oil to help her
o: buy a new vineyard in Jericho
pay off her deceased husband's debts
qs.e: Elisha performed the miracle of multiplying oil so the widow could sell it and pay her creditor.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, the Beatitude 'Blessed are the peacemakers' promises that they shall be called
qs.e: In Matthew chapter five, Jesus declares that peacemakers will be recognized as children of God.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Lost Sheep in Luke, the shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep in the wilderness to
o: go search for the one lost sheep until he finds it
lead them to a new green pasture
sell them at the local market
qs.e: The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to seek the single lost sheep, illustrating God's joy over one repenting sinner.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, when Jesus cleansed ten lepers, how many returned to give thanks to God?
qs.e: Only one Samaritan leper returned to glorify God and thank Jesus after realizing he was cleansed.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the seven deacons were selected by the early church primarily to oversee
o: the daily distribution of food to widows
the collection of taxes for Jerusalem
qs.e: The Seven were appointed to ensure Hellenistic widows were not neglected in the daily table ministry.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Galatians, the fruit of the Spirit includes love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
qs.e: Paul contrasts fleshly works with spiritual fruit: gentleness and self-control round out the character of believers.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God made a covenant with Abraham promising that through his lineage
o: the Egyptian empire would be ruled by Hebrews
all nations of the earth would be blessed
no member of his family would ever suffer
the physical world would never experience winter
qs.e: God promised Abraham that in him and his seed all families of the earth would be blessed.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Joseph was cast into prison after Potiphar's wife falsely accused him of
qs.e: Potiphar's wife lied about Joseph after he repeatedly rejected her immoral advances, causing his imprisonment.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, God guided the Israelites through the wilderness during the day by a pillar of cloud and at night by a pillar of
qs.e: Exodus records that God went before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Deborah accompanied Barak into battle against the Canaanite commander Sisera on condition that
o: Barak would give all plunder to the altar
the glory of victory over Sisera would go to a woman
no Canaanite prisoners would be spared
the battle would take place on the Sabbath
qs.e: Deborah prophesied that because Barak hesitated, the Lord would hand Sisera over to a woman (Jael).

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, King Saul sought guidance from a medium at Endor because
o: Samuel advised him to consult female seers
the Lord refused to answer him by dreams, Urim, or prophets
he wanted to learn foreign military tactics
he was looking for lost royal horses
qs.e: Terrified of the Philistine army and rejected by God, Saul desperately resorted to consulting the necromancer at Endor.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Samuel, King David desired to build a temple for God, but God told him through Nathan that
o: no temple should ever be built in Jerusalem
his son would build the house because David was a man of war
only Levites could make architectural plans
the ark must remain permanently in Shiloh
qs.e: God deferred the temple construction to David's son Solomon, promising instead to establish David's royal throne forever.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah raised the son of the widow of Zarephath from death by
o: anointing his head with consecrated oil
washing the boy in the Jordan River
stretching himself upon the child three times and praying to God
touching his feet with his prophetic cloak
qs.e: Elijah stretched himself upon the deceased child three times and cried out to God, who restored the boy's life.

qs.q: In the Book of Isaiah, the prophet describes the coming Suffering Servant as one who would be
o: wealthier than Solomon and more powerful than Moses
crowned king over all foreign earthly monarchies
pierced for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities
exiled to Babylon without any hope of return
qs.e: Isaiah fifty-three portrays Messiah taking upon Himself human transgressions and bearing our griefs.

qs.q: According to the Book of Ezra, King Cyrus of Persia issued a royal decree permitting Jewish exiles to
o: conquer the neighboring land of Edom
establish a new military kingdom in Babylon
return to Jerusalem and rebuild the house of God
abolish the feast of the Passover
qs.e: Cyrus issued an edict allowing the Jewish exiles to return to Judah and rebuild the Jerusalem temple.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Parable of the Wise and Foolish Builders, the wise man built his house upon
o: the hill, to avoid river floods during winter
the sand, representing quick financial investment
the rock, representing one who hears Jesus' words and puts them into practice
the clay, to save construction costs
qs.e: Jesus explained that building on rock represents hearing and obeying His teachings, enduring life's storms.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Wheat and Tares in Matthew, the master instructed his servants not to pull up the tares immediately lest they
o: cause the farm workers to strike
destroy the fertility of the farm soil
uproot the wheat along with them before harvest time
qs.e: The master ordered both to grow together until harvest to prevent accidental destruction of the good wheat.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, Jesus healed a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years when she
o: washed seven times in the Pool of Siloam
offered a sacrifice at the Jerusalem temple
touched the fringe of His garment in faith
recited the Mosaic law before the crowd
qs.e: The woman believed she would be healed if she merely touched Jesus' garment, and power went out from Him to heal her.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Barnabas earned his nickname 'Son of Encouragement' primarily because he
o: preached longer sermons than other disciples
wrote letters of praise to Roman governors
sold a field he owned and brought the money to the apostles
built a house of hospitality in Jerusalem
qs.e: Barnabas demonstrated generosity and encouragement by selling land and presenting the full proceeds for church ministry.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Peter received a vision in Joppa of a sheet descending from heaven containing various animals to teach him that
o: all wild animals in Israel must be preserved
Jewish believers must strictly keep Mosaic dietary restrictions
God has shown that no human being should be called common or unclean
the apostles should stop traveling across coastal towns
qs.e: The divine vision prepared Peter to visit Gentile Cornelius, breaking down traditional Jewish-Gentile barriers.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Romans, all human beings have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, but are justified freely by His
o: personal moral perfection and human merit
grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus
monetary gifts given to religious institutions
qs.e: Romans three teaches that universal human sinfulness is answered by God's free grace through Christ's redemption.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God tested Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering, but provided a substitute in the form of
o: a golden vessel placed on the altar
a spotless white lamb from the valley
a ram caught in a thicket by its horns
an olive branch falling from heaven
qs.e: When Abraham showed obedience, the angel stopped him and God provided a ram caught in the bushes for the sacrifice.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, the waters of the Red Sea parted when Moses
o: blew a silver trumpet three times
cast salt into the river waters
stretched out his hand over the sea with his staff
offered a burnt sacrifice on the shore
qs.e: God sent a strong east wind to divide the waters after Moses stretched out his hand over the sea.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah confronted King Ahab after Jezebel plotted the murder of Naboth in order to
o: banish Naboth's family to foreign lands
build a pagan altar to Ashtoreth in Jezreel
seize Naboth's vineyard for royal vegetable gardens
force Naboth into royal army service
qs.e: Jezebel arranged false witnesses to stone Naboth so Ahab could illegally confiscate his ancestral vineyard.

qs.q: In the Book of Amos, the prophet rejected the title of professional prophet when questioned by Amaziah the priest of Bethel, stating he was
o: a Levite priest from the temple of Shiloh
a royal scribe from the city of Jerusalem
a herdsman and dresser of sycamore fig trees
a merchant trading spices across Gilead
qs.e: Amos clarified that he was not a career prophet, but a layman called by God while tending livestock and fig trees.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, during the Transfiguration on the mountain, Jesus appeared in radiant glory alongside
qs.e: Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared conversing with the transfigured Christ.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, the Samaritan showed genuine neighborly love by
o: offering sacrifices at Mount Gerizim for the man's recovery
reporting the robber attack immediately to Roman guards
building a new shelter along the dangerous Jericho road
bandaging the wounded man, pouring oil and wine, and paying the innkeeper
qs.e: The Samaritan provided immediate first aid, transportation, lodging, and funds for the victim's full recovery.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Luke, Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus to the chief priests in exchange for
o: a piece of land in Bethany
a prominent seat in the Sanhedrin
qs.e: Judas agreed to deliver Jesus to the religious authorities for thirty silver coins.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Stephen's defence speech before the Sanhedrin recounted Israel's history to demonstrate that
o: the Sanhedrin had no legal authority under Rome
the temple in Jerusalem was built by angels
Gentiles should be forced to observe Mosaic law
Israel had consistently resisted the Holy Spirit and rejected God's messengers
qs.e: Stephen reviewed patriarchal and prophetic history to show Israel's repeated rebellion against God's anointed messengers.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul and Silas were miraculously freed from the prison in Philippi when
o: an angel blinded the prison guards
the Philippian jailer unlocked their chains secretly
Roman soldiers mutinied against the city magistrates
a great earthquake shook the foundations and opened all prison doors
qs.e: While Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns at midnight, an earthquake opened prison doors and unfastened chains.

qs.q: In Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, Christian freedom is limited by the principle of love, meaning that believers should avoid actions that
o: cause a weaker brother or sister in faith to stumble
qs.e: Paul teaches that Christian liberty must be voluntarily restrained out of love for the spiritual welfare of others.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Philippians, Christians are exhorted to imitate the humility of Christ, who
o: built an earthly palace in Capernaum
demanded royal honors while walking on earth
refused to submit to Roman taxation authorities
emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient unto death
qs.e: Philippians two highlights Christ's voluntary self-emptying (kenosis) and obedience as the ultimate model of humility.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God's covenant with Noah established the sanctity of human life by declaring that
o: cities of refuge must be built across every continent
human beings may consume meat with its lifeblood intact
the earth would never again produce thorns and thistles
whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed
qs.e: God affirmed the sacred value of human life created in His image by instituting capital consequences for murder.

qs.q: In the Book of Isaiah, the prophet declared to King Ahaz the sign of Immanuel, prophesying that
o: the throne of David would move to Babylon
Judah would defeat Assyria without losing a single soldier
the temple would stand untouched for one thousand years
a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel
qs.e: Isaiah seven predicts the birth of Immanuel ('God with us') as a sign of divine deliverance and presence.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Parable of the Sheep and Goats, final judgment is based on how people treated
o: scholars who memorized the Mosaic legal traditions
religious leaders who held administrative power
wealthy patrons who funded temple projects
the least of Christ's brothers and sisters in distress
qs.e: The King judges nations based on compassionate action toward the hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked, sick, and imprisoned.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Paul's address at the Areopagus in Athens used an altar inscribed 'To the Unknown God' to teach that
o: the resurrection of Christ was a metaphorical concept
Greek philosophy was superior to Jewish prophetic revelation
idolatry was acceptable if done with sincere intentions
God who made the world does not live in temples made by human hands
qs.e: Paul proclaimed the Creator God who gives life to all and calls everyone to repent through the resurrected Christ.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Galatians, justification by faith means that neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but rather
o: membership in the historic Levite priesthood
faith working through love and a new creation
qs.e: Paul summarizes his theology by asserting that outward ritual marks are meaningless compared to faith expressing itself through love.

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, God destroyed the sinful cities of Sodom and Gomorrah with
qs.e: Genesis nineteen records that God rained brimstone and fire from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, which son of Jacob was sold into Egypt by his brothers?
qs.e: Joseph was sold into Egyptian slavery by his brothers because of their jealousy.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, Moses was called by God through a burning bush at Mount
qs.e: Moses encountered the burning bush at Mount Horeb (the mountain of God).

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, the prophet who anointed both Saul and David as kings was
qs.e: Samuel was the prophet chosen by God to anoint Saul and later David over Israel.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, who was the wise king of Israel who built the first temple in Jerusalem?
qs.e: King Solomon constructed the magnificent first temple in Jerusalem to house the Ark of the Covenant.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus raised which friend from the dead after four days?
qs.e: Jesus raised Lazarus of Bethany from the dead four days after his burial.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, the apostle who preached the famous sermon on the Day of Pentecost was
qs.e: Peter stood up with the Eleven on Pentecost and preached to the crowd, resulting in three thousand converts.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt because she
o: stole golden idols from the city
qs.e: Disobeying the angelic command, Lot's wife looked back toward Sodom as it burned and became a pillar of salt.

qs.q: In the story of Moses in Exodus, the first plague visited upon Egypt was turning the water of the Nile into
qs.e: Moses struck the Nile with his rod, and all the water in the river turned into blood.

qs.q: According to the Book of Joshua, the walls of Jericho fell down flat after Israel marched around the city for seven days and
o: blew trumpets and shouted with a great shout
struck the walls with heavy iron rams
offered sacrifices at the city gates
dug tunnels under the city wall
qs.e: On the seventh day after seven circuits, the priests blew horns, the people shouted, and Jericho's walls collapsed.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, David spared King Saul's life in the cave of En-gedi by only cutting off a corner of Saul's
qs.e: David secretly cut off a corner of Saul's robe to prove he had no intention of harming the Lord's anointed.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah was taken up to heaven in a
o: whirlwind with a chariot of fire
qs.e: A chariot and horses of fire appeared, and Elijah ascended into heaven in a whirlwind as Elisha watched.

qs.q: In the Book of Psalms, Psalm twenty-three opens with the famous declaration that
o: God is our refuge and strength
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want
The earth is the Lord's and its fullness
Blessed is the man who walks not in counsel of ungodly
qs.e: Psalm 23 is David's psalm of trust celebrating God's shepherd care and provision.

qs.q: According to the Book of Jonah, the prophet Jonah was swallowed by a great fish when he tried to flee to
qs.e: Jonah ran away from God's command to preach to Nineveh by boarding a ship bound for Tarshish.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus taught His disciples the Lord's Prayer as a model for praying with
o: loud public shouting on street corners
sincerity and humility rather than vain repetitions
qs.e: Jesus instructed His followers to pray simply, quietly, and sincerely without empty babbling.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Sower, the seeds that fell on good soil represent people who
o: fall away as soon as persecution begins
hear the word, accept it, and produce a fruitful harvest
choke under the pressure of worldly riches
reject the gospel with immediate contempt
qs.e: Good soil symbolizes noble hearts that hear, retain, and productively practice God's word.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Mark, who was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry the cross of Jesus to Golgotha?
qs.e: The soldiers pressed Simon of Cyrene into service to carry Jesus' cross on the path to Golgotha.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the disciple Barnabas brought Saul to Antioch to help teach the growing church of
qs.e: Barnabas retrieved Saul from Tarsus, and together they taught the believers in Antioch for a full year.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Romans, paul teaches that nothing can separate believers from the love of God in Christ Jesus, including
o: tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, or danger
holding high political office in Rome
qs.e: Romans eight concludes triumphantly that no hardship or created thing can separate us from God's love.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Jacob wrestled with a divine man at Peniel and refused to let him go until he was
qs.e: Jacob declared, 'I will not let you go unless you bless me,' leading to his new name Israel.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, God provided the Israelites in the wilderness with manna to eat, which appeared every morning as
o: fine flake-like frost on the ground
qs.e: Manna lay around the camp like white coriander seed, tasting like wafers made with honey.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, young Samuel responded to God's night call in the tabernacle by saying
o: Here am I, send my brother
Lord, why have you awakened me
I am ready to lead Israel
qs.e: Guided by Eli, Samuel answered God's call with 'Speak, for your servant hears.'

qs.q: In the Second Book of Samuel, King David brought the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem with great joy, dancing before the Lord clad in a
qs.e: David danced before the Lord with all his might wearing a simple linen ephod, demonstrating humility.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, King Solomon demonstrated exceptional wisdom when deciding between two women claiming the same living baby by suggesting to
o: give the child to the royal palace nurses
divide the living child in two with a sword
cast lots before the Ark of the Covenant
qs.e: Solomon proposed cutting the child in two, exposing the true mother who begged to spare the baby's life.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, Elisha cursed a group of youths who mocked his baldness near Bethel, resulting in two female bears coming out of the woods to
o: chase the youths back to Jericho
qs.e: Scripture records that two bears emerged from the forest and mauled forty-two disrespectful youths.

qs.q: According to the Book of Jeremiah, the prophet was imprisoned in a muddy cistern by royal officials because he prophesied that
o: Egypt would conquer the city of Samaria
King Nebuchadnezzar would convert to Yahweh
Jerusalem would fall to the Babylonian army
the temple would never suffer damage
qs.e: Jeremiah was cast into Malchiah's muddy dungeon for faithfully warning that Jerusalem would fall to Babylon.

qs.q: In the Book of Daniel, three Hebrew men Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were thrown into a blazing fiery furnace because they refused to
o: serve in the Babylonian royal army
pay tribute money to the Babylonian treasury
bow down and worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
eat meat from the king's royal table
qs.e: The three men stood firm in faith, refusing idol worship despite the threat of the fiery furnace.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus declared 'You are the salt of the earth', warning that if salt loses its taste it is good for nothing except to be
o: burned in the temple altar fire
thrown out and trampled underfoot by men
qs.e: Tasteless salt loses its preserving value and is cast out to be walked upon.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, Jesus compared the Kingdom of God to a small seed that grows into a large tree so that
o: wild animals can hide under its shadow
birds of the air come and nest in its branches
no weeds can grow around its trunk
qs.e: The tiny mustard seed grows into a expansive tree, illustrating the miraculous expansion of God's Kingdom.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Luke, when Jesus raised the widow's son at Nain, He was moved with compassion because the deceased was
o: a young child of a Roman official
a prominent ruler of the local synagogue
the only son of his widowed mother
qs.e: Jesus saw the grieving widow losing her only son and commanded the young man to arise.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to John, Thomas declared his belief in the resurrected Jesus after Jesus invited him to
o: read the prophetic scroll of Isaiah
watch Him perform a new nature miracle
see and touch the nail marks in His hands and side
eat a meal of broiled fish on the shore
qs.e: Thomas confessed 'My Lord and my God!' after Jesus offered physical proof of His resurrection.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Philip led the Ethiopian eunuch to faith by explaining how the prophecy of Isaiah was fulfilled in
qs.e: Beginning with Isaiah fifty-three, Philip proclaimed the good news of Jesus to the Ethiopian traveler.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Tabitha (Dorcas) of Joppa was remembered by the believers for her devotion to
o: writing letters to churches across Judea
building stone meeting houses for apostles
good works and acts of charity making garments for widows
singing psalms during daily prayer hours
qs.e: Dorcas was beloved for her selfless charity and making clothes for poor widows before Peter raised her.

qs.q: According to Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude; love does not insist on
qs.e: Paul's hymn to love in 1 Corinthians 13 highlights selflessness: love does not demand its own way.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Joseph tested his brothers when they came to Egypt by placing his personal silver cup into the sack of
qs.e: Joseph had his steward hide his silver cup in Benjamin's bag to test whether the brothers would defend Benjamin.

qs.q: In the Book of Numbers, Moses lifted up a bronze serpent on a pole in the wilderness so that anyone bitten by poisonous snakes would live upon
o: washing in the waters of Meribah
offering animal sacrifices at the tabernacle
looking at the bronze serpent in faith
qs.e: God instructed Moses to make a bronze serpent; whoever looked upon it after being bitten survived.

qs.q: According to the Book of Joshua, Rahab the harlot of Jericho was spared when the city was destroyed because she
o: guided Joshua's army through secret mountain paths
refused to worship the king of Jericho
hid the Israelite spies and bound a scarlet cord in her window
stole the idol images from Jericho's temple
qs.e: Rahab hid Joshua's spies and marked her house with a scarlet rope, preserving her household.

qs.q: In the First Book of Samuel, Prophet Samuel confronted King Saul after the battle against Amalek, declaring that to obey is better than
o: sacrifice, and to heed than the fat of rams
qs.e: Samuel uttered the timeless truth: obedience to God's word is far superior to ritual sacrifices.

qs.q: According to the Second Book of Kings, Prophet Elisha performed a miracle for the sons of the prophets by making a lost iron axe head
o: multiply into ten sharp axe heads
float on top of the water when he threw a stick in
qs.e: When an axe head fell into the Jordan, Elisha threw a stick into the water and the iron floated to the surface.

qs.q: In the Book of Micah, the prophet summarized what the Lord requires of humanity: to do justice, to love kindness, and to
o: offer daily burnt sacrifices at Jerusalem
build stone monuments in every village
qs.e: Micah six outlines true religion: doing justice, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, the king handed the servant over to the jailers because he
o: stole money directly from the royal treasury
refused to work in the king's vineyard
refused to forgive his fellow servant a tiny debt after his own immense debt was canceled
qs.e: The king was furious because the servant received great mercy but refused to show small mercy to a peer.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, Jesus commended the poor widow who cast two small copper coins into the temple treasury because she
o: hoped to receive immediate public praise
gave more monetary value than all the wealthy donors combined
wished to buy special favor from the high priest
gave out of her poverty all she had to live on
qs.e: Jesus noted that while others gave out of surplus, the poor widow gave sacrificially her whole livelihood.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the believers in Antioch were first called
qs.e: Acts eleven records that the disciples were first called Christians in the Syrian city of Antioch.

qs.q: In Paul's Second Letter to the Corinthians, Paul speaks of a 'thorn in the flesh' given to him to keep him from becoming conceited, to which God responded
o: You must return to Tarsus to rest
I will remove this affliction instantly from your body
You must fast for thirty days to receive healing
My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness
qs.e: God answered Paul's prayer regarding his thorn by assuring him that divine grace is perfected in human weakness.

qs.q: In his Letter to the Galatians, Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit. Which trio is listed among the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians chapter five?
qs.e: Galatians chapter five lists the fruit of the Spirit as love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Envy, strife, sorcery, jealousy and wrath appear among the works of the flesh, not the fruit.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God established the covenant of circumcision with Abraham when Abraham was ninety-nine years old, specifying that every male child must be circumcised on the
qs.e: Genesis seventeen commands that every male infant throughout generations be circumcised on the eighth day.

qs.q: In the Book of Habakkuk, amidst national distress and impending Babylonian invasion, the prophet declared the central principle that
o: human power can alter divine decrees
the righteous shall live by his faith
qs.e: Habakkuk two states the foundational spiritual principle quoted in the New Testament: 'the righteous shall live by faith.'

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to John, Jesus declared 'I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep', contrasting Himself with the hired hand who
o: leads the sheep into greener pastures daily
guards the sheep fold with iron weapons
flees when he sees the wolf coming because he does not care for the sheep
qs.e: Jesus contrasts the selfless love of the Good Shepherd with a mercenary hired hand who abandons the flock in danger.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, when the apostles were brought before the Sanhedrin and commanded to stop preaching in Jesus' name, Peter answered
o: We demand financial compensation for our church
We will cease preaching until political conditions improve
We appeal directly to Caesar in Rome
We must obey God rather than human beings
qs.e: Peter and the apostles boldly declared that divine mandate supersedes human prohibition: 'We must obey God rather than men.'

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Romans, the Law is holy, righteous, and good, but it cannot justify sinners because it is weakened by
o: lack of enforcement by Jewish kings
the sinful nature of fallen humanity
qs.e: Romans eight explains that what the Law was powerless to do because it was weakened by human flesh, God accomplished through Christ.

qs.q: According to the story of creation in Genesis, God made the sun, moon, and stars on the
qs.e: Genesis one records that God created heavenly lights on the fourth day to separate day from night.

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, Abraham was seventy-five years old when God commanded him to leave
qs.e: Abraham departed from Haran at seventy-five years of age as the Lord had commanded him.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, who was the sister of Moses and Aaron who led the women in victory songs?
qs.e: Miriam the prophetess took a timbrel and led the Israelite women in singing praise after crossing the Red Sea.

qs.q: In the Old Testament narrative, which Israelite king was famous for asking God for wisdom rather than riches?
qs.e: Solomon asked God for an understanding mind to judge Israel wisely, pleasing the Lord.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah pronounced a severe drought upon Israel during the reign of King
qs.e: Elijah confronted King Ahab, declaring that there would be neither dew nor rain except at his word.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, Jesus was presented in the temple at Jerusalem forty days after His birth where He was praised by
qs.e: Righteous Simeon and the prophetess Anna gave thanks to God upon seeing the infant Savior in the temple.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, who was the Roman centurion in Caesarea whose conversion marked the opening of the Gospel to Gentiles?
qs.e: Cornelius was a God-fearing centurion who invited Peter to preach the Gospel to his household.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Esau sold his birthright to Jacob because he was famished after returning from
qs.e: Esau came from the field exhausted and traded his birthright for a single meal of lentil stew.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Pharaoh gave Joseph an Egyptian name, Zaphenath-paneah, and gave him in marriage
o: Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On
the daughter of Potiphar the captain of guard
a princess from the royal house of Pharaoh
a maiden from the Hebrew tribe of Levi
qs.e: Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, daughter of the priest of On, as his wife upon his promotion to governor.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, Moses was instructed to place blood from the Passover lamb on the
o: two doorposts and lintel of each house
threshold and floor of the entrance
altar of burnt offering in the camp
qs.e: The blood applied to the doorposts and lintel served as a sign for the Lord to pass over Israelite homes.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Samson destroyed the wheat fields of the Philistines by tying torches between the tails of three hundred
qs.e: Samson caught three hundred foxes, tied them tail to tail with torches, and released them into Philistine grain fields.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, King Saul grew jealous of David when Israelite women sang that Saul killed thousands, but David killed
qs.e: The women sang 'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands,' igniting Saul's bitter jealousy.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, Naaman was angry with Elisha at first because Elisha
o: did not come out personally but sent a messenger telling him to wash in Jordan
demanded a heavy price in gold and silver
insisted Naaman offer sacrifices in Jerusalem
told him his leprosy was incurable
qs.e: Naaman expected Elisha to perform a dramatic ritual in person rather than sending a simple message.

qs.q: According to the Book of Proverbs, a gentle answer turns away wrath, but harsh words stir up
qs.e: Proverbs 15 teaches that soft speech defuses conflict, whereas harsh words provoke anger.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke, the younger son decided to return home after he spent all his money and was reduced to
o: working as a slave in a copper mine
feeding pigs and longing to eat their pods
rowing merchant boats on the sea
qs.e: In desperate famine, the prodigal son hired himself out to feed swine and realized his father's servants fared better.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to John, at the wedding in Cana, Mary instructed the servants regarding Jesus by saying
o: Bring out the old wine first
qs.e: Mary demonstrated faith in Jesus by instructing the servants to obey whatever command He gave.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, when Jesus entered Jericho, a short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Him named
qs.e: Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore fig tree so he could see Jesus over the pressing crowd.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the sorcerer in Samaria who tried to purchase the gift of the Holy Spirit with money was
qs.e: Simon the sorcerer offered money to Peter to buy apostolic authority, receiving severe rebuke.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Romans, paul explains that Abraham was justified before he was circumcised, proving that righteousness is by
o: faith and not outward legal ritual
qs.e: Paul uses Abraham's timing of justification in Genesis to prove faith precedes physical ritual marks.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, the city of Babel became famous because God confused the language of humanity there to stop them from
o: building a tower that would reach to heaven
offering pagan sacrifices to false gods
qs.e: God scattered humanity at Babel by confusing their speech to curb human pride and self-exaltation.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Joseph's brothers brought Benjamin with them to Egypt on their second trip because Joseph insisted that
o: Benjamin must be sold into slavery as punishment
they could not buy grain or see his face without Benjamin
Jacob must move to Egypt immediately
qs.e: Joseph demanded Benjamin's presence to test his brothers' honesty regarding their family situation.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, the Tabernacle constructed in the wilderness was built according to the exact pattern shown to Moses on Mount
qs.e: God repeatedly instructed Moses to make the sanctuary precisely according to the divine blueprint revealed on Mount Sinai.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Jephthah made a rash vow to God before fighting the Ammonites, promising to offer as a burnt offering whatever
o: first born male animal was found in his flock
first came out of the doors of his house to meet him upon return
portion of gold plunder was captured in battle
qs.e: Jephthah vowed to offer whatever greeted him first upon returning victorious, which proved to be his only daughter.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, Prophet Samuel confronted Saul after he spared Agag, declaring that rebellion is like the sin of
o: divination, and presumption is like iniquity and idolatry
qs.e: 1 Samuel 15 likens rebellion against God's direct command to the severe sin of witchcraft and idolatry.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Samuel, David showed great kindness to Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth by restoring his land and allowing him to
o: command a division of the Israelite army
eat regularly at the royal king's table
build a new house in Bethlehem
serve as high priest at Shiloh
qs.e: Out of covenant love for Jonathan, David restored Saul's family estate to Mephibosheth and seated him at the king's table.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah fled into the wilderness to Mount Horeb after Jezebel threatened his life, where God spoke to him in a
o: thunderous roar from a dark cloud
still small voice after wind, earthquake, and fire
loud trumpet blast from the sky
qs.e: God manifested His presence to weary Elijah not in violent elements, but in a gentle, quiet whisper.

qs.q: In the Book of Amos, the prophet saw five visions of judgment, including a plumb line, which represented God measuring Israel for
o: architectural expansion of Samaria's city walls
imminent destruction because of their moral collapse
equal distribution of land among tribes
qs.e: The vision of the plumb line demonstrated that Israel failed God's standard of righteousness and faced inevitable judgment.

qs.q: According to the Book of Nehemiah, when Sanballat and Tobiah sent messages inviting Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono, Nehemiah replied
o: I appeal to King Artaxerxes for protection
I will meet you if you lay down your weapons
I am doing a great work and cannot come down
I am sending my army to fight you
qs.e: Nehemiah recognized their deceitful trap and refused to interrupt the vital work of rebuilding Jerusalem's wall.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His followers to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them so that they may be
o: honored by all secular earthly kings
children of their Father who is in heaven

qs.q: In the Book of Hosea, God commanded Hosea to take an unfaithful wife Gomer to illustrate Israel's spiritual adultery, declaring that despite Israel's idolatry, God would allure her into the wilderness and speak
qs.e: Hosea 2 portrays God's restoring love drawing unfaithful Israel back into intimate covenant fellowship.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Parable of the Sheep and Goats, the King will welcome the righteous into His Kingdom because when He was hungry they gave Him food, when thirsty they gave Him drink, and when a stranger they
qs.e: Matthew 25 bases judgment on practical mercy extended to suffering human beings.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Paul's address to the Ephesian elders at Miletus warned them to care for the church of God obtained with His own blood, reminding them of Jesus' words that 'It is more blessed to give than to'
qs.e: Paul cited an unrecorded saying of Jesus highlighting the superior joy of generosity.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Galatians, justification is received by faith in Christ alone, and those who attempt to be justified by keeping the Mosaic Law have fallen away from
qs.e: Galatians 5 warns that returning to legalistic works for salvation forfeits grace.

qs.q: In the Book of Genesis, God created dry land and gathered the waters on the
qs.e: Genesis one states that God formed dry land and seas on the third day.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham had his first son Ishmael by Sarah's Egyptian maid named
qs.e: Hagar bore Ishmael to Abraham before Isaac was born.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, God split the waters of the Red Sea so Israel could cross on dry ground using His servant
qs.e: Moses stretched out his hand with staff to divide the Red Sea.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, David killed Goliath using a sling and a smooth
qs.e: David struck Goliath in the forehead with a single smooth stone.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, King Solomon built the temple of God in the capital city of
qs.e: Solomon built the First Temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, Jesus delivered the Sermon on the Mount sitting on a
qs.e: Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down to teach His disciples.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, the Holy Spirit descended on believers gathered in Jerusalem on the Day of
qs.e: Pentecost marked the baptism of the Holy Spirit on the early church.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God placed Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden to work it and
qs.e: Genesis two records mankind's original stewardship task to cultivate and guard Eden.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Potiphar promoted Joseph to oversee his house because the Lord was with Joseph and made him
qs.e: God's blessing on Joseph brought total success to Potiphar's estate.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, God provided manna every morning in the wilderness, which melted when the sun grew
qs.e: Manna had to be gathered early because it melted under the hot sun.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Gideon destroyed his father's altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah pole beside it at
qs.e: Gideon acted at night out of fear of his family and townspeople.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, Saul attempted to kill David with a spear because he feared David, for the Lord was with David but had departed from
qs.e: Saul's dread stemmed from knowing God had abandoned him and favored David.

qs.q: In the Second Book of Kings, Prophet Elisha multiplied twenty barley loaves brought by a man from Baal-shalishah to feed a hundred men with food left
qs.e: Elisha's miracle presaged Christ's feeding miracles, leaving surplus food.

qs.q: According to the Book of Proverbs, the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is
qs.e: Proverbs 9 equates knowing God with genuine spiritual understanding.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke, the returning son confessed 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your'
qs.e: The prodigal son's repentance expressed deep humility regarding his lost sonship.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Mark, Jesus healed blind Bartimaeus near Jericho after Bartimaeus cried out 'Son of David, have mercy on'
qs.e: Bartimaeus persisted in faith, calling on Jesus' messianic mercy.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Luke, Jesus was crucified at the place called the Skull between two
qs.e: Jesus was numbered with transgressors, dying between two thieves.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Barnabas took John Mark and sailed to Cyprus, while Paul chose
qs.e: Acts 15 records Paul teaming with Silas for his Second Journey.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Romans, paul asserts that the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the
qs.e: Romans 1 emphasizes universal gospel accessibility for all humanity.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, Jacob had a vision at Bethel of a ladder reaching to heaven, promising to give God a tenth of everything if God would
o: make him king over all Canaanite cities
keep him in safety and give him bread to eat and clothing to wear
grant him golden riches in Haran
qs.e: Jacob vowed a tithe at Bethel in response to God's covenant protection promise.

qs.q: In the story of Joseph in Egypt, Joseph forgave his brothers after testing their loyalty to Benjamin, telling them 'Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve'
qs.e: Joseph viewed his suffering through divine providence aimed at saving lives.

qs.q: According to the Book of Exodus, God led Israel through the Red Sea on dry land, while Pharaoh's pursuing army was drowned when Moses stretched his staff over the sea, prompting Moses and Israel to sing a song of
o: praise to the LORD who triumphed gloriously
qs.e: Exodus 15 contains the Song of Moses praising God's glorious victory.

qs.q: In the Book of Judges, Samson destroyed the Philistine grain fields by tying torches between the tails of three hundred foxes because his father-in-law gave Samson's wife to his
qs.e: Samson took revenge after his Timnite wife was given away to his best man.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Samuel, David refused to kill King Saul in the wilderness of Ziph when Abishai urged him to spear Saul, saying 'Who can put out his hand against the LORD's anointed and be'
