qs.e: David revered God's anointed office, refusing vigilante violence against Saul.

qs.q: In the First Book of Kings, King Solomon split the judgment between two women claiming one baby by proposing to cut the child in two, exposing the true mother who begged 'Oh, my lord, give her the living child, and by no means'
qs.e: The real mother's protective love revealed her identity to wise Solomon.

qs.q: According to the Second Book of Kings, Elisha healed Naaman's leprosy by ordering him to dip seven times in the Jordan, but Gehazi was struck with Naaman's leprosy because he secretly accepted from Naaman silver and
qs.e: Gehazi's greed and lies brought Naaman's skin curse upon himself and his lineage.

qs.q: In the Book of Hosea, God commanded Hosea 'Go, take to yourself a wife of whoredom', using Hosea's marriage to unfaithful Gomer to picture Israel's unfaithfulness in turning to
qs.e: Hosea's marriage symbolized Israel's spiritual adultery through idol worship.

qs.q: According to the Book of Nehemiah, Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem's walls despite ridicule from Sanballat and Tobiah by organizing workers so that each worked with one hand and held a weapon with the
qs.e: Nehemiah's builders combined vigilant defense with diligent manual labor.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught 'You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is'
qs.e: Jesus replaced legalistic retaliation with non-violent Christian love.

qs.q: According to the Parable of the Good Samaritan, a priest and a Levite saw a beaten traveler and passed by, but a Samaritan bound his wounds, set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and gave the innkeeper two
qs.e: The Samaritan paid two days' wages (denarii) to guarantee full lodging and medical care.

qs.q: In the Gospel according to Mark, Jesus calmed a violent windstorm on the Sea of Galilee by saying 'Peace! Be still!', after which the disciples feared greatly and said 'Who then is this, that even the wind and sea'
qs.e: Jesus' miracle over creation filled the disciples with reverent awe.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Stephen's defense speech before the Sanhedrin accused the religious leaders of stiff-necked resistance, saying 'You always resist the'
qs.e: Stephen condemned the council's historical pattern of resisting God's Spirit.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns in the Philippian prison at midnight, causing an earthquake that opened prison doors and led to the jailer's confession 'Sirs, what must I do to be'
qs.e: The jailer's dramatic question received Paul's immortal gospel promise of faith in Christ.

qs.q: According to Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, love is patient and kind, does not envy or boast, is not arrogant, and never
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13 concludes that true divine love is eternal and permanent.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God tested Abraham by telling him to offer Isaac on Mount Moriah, but when Abraham stretched out his hand with the knife, the angel of the Lord called from heaven saying 'Do not lay your hand on the boy', and Abraham saw a ram caught by its horns in a
qs.e: God provided a ram in the thicket as a substitute sacrifice for Isaac.

qs.q: In the Book of Exodus, during the wilderness journey, Moses struck the rock at Massah and Meribah with his staff as God commanded, causing water to pour out for the thirsty people who had grumbled against
qs.e: Moses struck Horeb's rock to provide water despite Israel's rebellious complaining.

qs.q: According to the First Book of Kings, Prophet Elijah proved that Yahweh was God when fire fell from heaven on Carmel and consumed the sacrifice, wood, stones, dust, and water, causing all the people to fall on their faces and cry 'The LORD, he is God; the LORD, he is'
qs.e: Israel fell prostrate and acknowledged Yahweh as the sole living God.

qs.q: In the Book of Isaiah, the prophet declared the famous prophecy of Messiah's virgin birth: 'Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name'
qs.e: Isaiah 7 predicts Immanuel ('God with us') as the divine messianic sign.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Matthew, in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His followers 'You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden. Nor do people light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a'
qs.e: Jesus exhorted Christians to let their good works shine visibly before others.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke, when the younger son returned home, his compassionate father saw him from afar, ran, embraced him, and kissed him, ordering servants to put on him a robe, a ring, and sandals, and kill the fattened
qs.e: The father celebrated his lost son's return with a feast featuring the fattened calf.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to Luke, when Jesus was brought before Pontius Pilate, Pilate stated three times to the chief priests and crowds that he found no guilt in
qs.e: Pilate repeatedly declared Jesus innocent before bowing to mob pressure.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, after Stephen was stoned to death, devout men buried him and made great lamentation, while Saul began ravaging the church, entering house after house and dragging off men and women to
qs.e: Saul fiercely persecuted early believers, imprisoning Christian families in Jerusalem.

qs.q: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul preached in Athens at the Areopagus, introducing God as the Creator who made the world and does not dwell in temples made by hands, calling all people everywhere to repent because God will judge the world by the man He raised from the
qs.e: Paul anchored universal divine judgment in Christ's historical resurrection.

qs.q: In Paul's Letter to the Galatians, paul writes that if righteousness were through the Mosaic Law, then Christ died for no
qs.e: Galatians 2 asserts that legalistic justification renders Christ's death pointless.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Romans, Christians should present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, not being conformed to this world, but being transformed by the renewal of their
qs.e: Romans 12 commands mind transformation to discern and live God's will.

qs.q: According to the Book of Genesis, God made a covenant with Abraham in Genesis fifteen, promising that his descendants would be strangers in a foreign land for four hundred years, but God would judge that nation and bring them out with great
qs.e: God foretold the Egyptian bondage and the Exodus deliverance with great plunder.

qs.q: In the Book of Jeremiah, God warned Judah against trusting in deceptive words of false prophets who proclaimed peace when there was no peace, comparing false prophets to those who heal the wound of God's people
qs.e: Jeremiah 6 denounced superficial spiritual remedies that ignored deep moral decay.

qs.q: According to the Gospel according to John, Jesus declared 'I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live', spoken to Martha before raising
qs.e: Jesus proclaimed His resurrection power directly to Martha before bringing Lazarus out of the tomb.

qs.q: In the Acts of the Apostles, when Paul defended his ministry before King Agrippa, Agrippa remarked 'In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?', to which Paul replied 'Whether short or long, I would to God that not only you but also all who hear me this day might become such as I am—except for these'
qs.e: Paul expressed passionate desire for everyone's salvation while humbly mentioning his physical chains.

qs.q: According to Paul's Letter to the Ephesians, by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may
qs.e: Ephesians 2 states salvation is purely God's gracious gift, eliminating human self-glory.

qs.q: What was the primary message of John the Baptist when he preached in the wilderness of Judea?
o: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
Build new synagogues for public prayer
Refuse to pay taxes to the Roman authorities
Offer animal sacrifices in Jerusalem daily
qs.e: John the Baptist preached repentance and prepared the way for Jesus, proclaiming that the kingdom of heaven was at hand.

qs.q: Which king of Israel requested wisdom from God rather than wealth or long life?
qs.e: King Solomon prayed for an understanding heart to govern God's people, and God granted him extraordinary wisdom.

qs.q: What was the occupation of Amos before God called him to prophesy to the northern kingdom of Israel?
o: Herdsman and dresser of sycamore trees
qs.e: Amos explicitly stated that he was not a professional prophet or a prophet's son, but a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.

qs.q: Who was the first Christian martyr stoned to death for his courageous defense of the faith?
qs.e: Stephen was one of the seven chosen deacons and became the first Christian martyr after testifying before the Sanhedrin.

qs.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who was the first person to pass by the injured traveler on the road to Jericho?
qs.e: A priest was the first person who saw the wounded man and passed by on the other side of the road.

qs.q: Which prophet confronted King Ahab after Jezebel arranged the judicial murder of Naboth for his vineyard?
qs.e: Elijah confronted Ahab in Naboth's vineyard and pronounced divine judgment upon Ahab and Jezebel for their wicked act.

qs.q: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles before Pentecost?
qs.e: Matthias was selected after prayer and casting lots to fill the apostolic office vacated by Judas Iscariot.

qs.q: According to Paul's teaching in his letter to the Galatians, what is the primary purpose of the Mosaic Law prior to Christ?
o: To act as a guardian or tutor until Christ came
To serve as an eternal requirement for justification
To replace faith in God's promises to Abraham
To grant total immunity from moral failure
qs.e: Paul explained that the Law was our guardian or tutor to lead us to Christ so that we might be justified by faith.

qs.q: What sign did Judas Iscariot use to identify Jesus to the chief priests and elders in the Garden of Gethsemane?
o: Calling Jesus by his full title
qs.e: Judas arranged a signal with the armed crowd, saying that the one he kissed was the man they should arrest.

qs.q: Which Persian monarch issued the decree permitting the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple?
qs.e: King Cyrus of Persia was prompted by the Lord to issue a decree allowing the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.

qs.q: What immediate political decision by King Rehoboam caused the ten northern tribes of Israel to break away?
o: Rejecting the advice of the elders and increasing forced labor
Moving the national capital from Shechem to Jerusalem
Abolishing all taxation across the northern territories
Forcing the Israelites to worship foreign idols in Samaria
qs.e: Rehoboam rejected the counsel of the older advisors and declared he would make their burden heavier, prompting Jeroboam and the northern tribes to secede.

qs.q: In the book of Proverbs, what is stated as the beginning of knowledge and wisdom?
qs.e: Proverbs declares that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom, whereas fools despise wisdom and instruction.

qs.q: Which major prophet experienced a vision of God's glory by the Chebar canal during the Babylonian exile?
qs.e: Ezekiel was among the exiles by the River Chebar when the heavens opened and he saw visions of the glory of the Lord.

qs.q: How did God respond when Moses expressed hesitation at the burning bush regarding his speaking abilities?
o: Sent Joshua immediately to take his place as leader
Appointed his brother Aaron to serve as his spokesman
Granted Moses an instant complete silence from speech
Commanded Jethro to address Pharaoh on his behalf
qs.e: God reassured Moses and designated Aaron the Levite, Moses' brother, to serve as his spokesman before the people and Pharaoh.

qs.q: What key lesson does the narrative of Joseph forgiving his brothers in Egypt illustrate regarding divine providence?
o: Human betrayal permanently cancels God's covenant promises
God turns human evil intentions into good for preservation of life
Reconciliation requires severe financial compensation first
Forgiveness should only be extended if offenders pay restitution
qs.e: Joseph told his brothers that while they intended evil against him, God intended it for good to accomplish the saving of many lives.

qs.q: What was the central issue debated at the Council of Jerusalem recorded in the Acts of the Apostles?
o: Which gospel account should be declared official Scripture
Whether Gentile converts must be circumcised and follow the Law of Moses
How the financial relief funds for Judea should be distributed
Whether Peter or Paul should be head of the entire church
qs.e: The Jerusalem Council addressed whether Gentile believers needed to be circumcised and required to keep the Law of Moses for salvation.

qs.q: Which judge of Israel delivered the nation from Midianite oppression with a chosen force of only three hundred men?
qs.e: Gideon reduced his army from thirty thousand to three hundred men based on how they drank water, demonstrating that victory comes from God.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what guideline did Jesus give regarding acts of charity and almsgiving?
o: Blow trumpets in the synagogues to inspire public praise
Perform them in secret so that God who sees in secret will reward you
Publish all donations to ensure organizational transparency
Limit charitable giving exclusively to immediate family members
qs.e: Jesus instructed that when giving to the needy, it should be done in secret without seeking public praise from people.

qs.q: What was the immediate physical result when Peter commanded the lame beggar at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple to walk?
o: The man was required to wash in the pool of Siloam first
The man's feet and ankles instantly received strength and he leaped up
The man received partial healing that took three days to complete
The man was told to present himself to the priests for examination
qs.e: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, Peter took him by the right hand, and instantly the man's feet and ankles became strong.

qs.q: In Isaiah's Temple vision, what action was taken by one of the seraphim to purge the prophet's guilt and sin?
o: Touched his lips with a burning coal taken from the altar
Anointed his head with sacred oil from a golden flask
Washed his feet with pure water from the sanctuary basin
Placed a clean linen turban upon his head before God
qs.e: A seraph flew to Isaiah with a live coal taken with tongs from the altar and touched his mouth, declaring his guilt was taken away.

qs.q: In Jeremiah's Temple Sermon, what false belief held by the people of Judah did the prophet strongly denounce?
o: The assumption that offering sacrifices was entirely forbidden during national crises
The superstitious trust that the presence of God's Temple guaranteed security regardless of their sinful conduct
The conviction that Babylon would never expand its empire beyond Mesopotamia
The doctrine that the Davidic royal line would end with King Josiah
qs.e: Jeremiah warned the people not to trust in deceptive words, repeatedly chanting 'The temple of the Lord', while practicing injustice and idolatry.

qs.q: Which minor prophet used his unfaithful marriage to Gomer as a dramatic allegory of God's unyielding love for faithless Israel?
qs.e: Hosea was instructed by God to marry Gomer to symbolize Israel's spiritual adultery and God's persistent redeeming love.

qs.q: According to the book of Micah, what does the Lord require of human beings beyond outward religious rituals?
o: To observe strict fasts every week and offer gold offerings
To do justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with God
To enforce political domination over neighboring nations
To build magnificent sanctuaries throughout the countryside
qs.e: Micah summarized true religion by declaring that God requires humanity to do justice, love mercy/kindness, and walk humbly with God.

qs.q: In the book of Job, how did God answer Job when speaking out of the whirlwind?
o: By providing a itemized list of every private sin Job had committed
By pointing to His divine sovereignty and wisdom in creating and sustaining the complex cosmos
By explaining that Satan had personally requested permission to test Job's integrity
By commanding Job's three friends to immediately offer a compensation fine to Job
qs.e: God addressed Job from the whirlwind, emphasizing His divine power and incomprehensible wisdom in creation rather than explaining the explicit reason for suffering.

qs.q: In Ecclesiastes, what is the ultimate conclusion reached regarding human duty after contemplating the vanity of worldly pursuits?
o: Pursue human philosophy and intellectual fame
Fear God and keep His commandments
Accumulate material wealth for future generations
Avoid all social interaction and retire to isolation
qs.e: Ecclesiastes concludes that after everything has been heard, the end of the matter is to fear God and keep His commandments.

qs.q: According to Paul's epistle to the Romans, how is a person justified before God?
o: By virtue of ancestral lineage descending directly from Abraham
By meticulous obedience to both ceremonial and moral commandments
By grace through faith in Jesus Christ, apart from the works of the Law
By performing public works of philanthropy in the community
qs.e: Paul taught that righteousness comes from God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe, justified freely by His grace.

qs.q: In Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, what core metaphor does he use to illustrate unity and diversity among believers?
o: A commercial fleet trading in foreign harbors
A military battalion commanded by a single general
The human body composed of many interdependent members
An agricultural vineyard pruned by different laborers
qs.e: Paul compared the church to a human body, which is one unit made up of many parts, each exercising distinct spiritual gifts for the common good.

qs.q: What significance did the tearing of the Temple curtain from top to bottom at Jesus' death symbolize?
o: The end of all Jewish civil laws regarding land ownership
The physical destruction of Jerusalem by foreign armies within a week
Unrestricted direct access to God's presence for all believers through Christ
The immediate conversion of the Roman centurion and his soldiers
qs.e: The tearing of the veil signified that the barrier between God and humanity was removed, giving believers direct access through Christ.

qs.q: What was the main charge brought against Jesus before the Jewish Sanhedrin presided over by Caiaphas?
o: Inciting an armed rebellion in Galilee
Refusing to pay taxes to the Roman Emperor
Blasphemy for claiming to be the Son of God
Violating the architectural purity of the Temple
qs.e: The High Priest declared Jesus guilty of blasphemy when Jesus affirmed His identity as the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One.

qs.q: Which leaders guided the rebuilding of the second Temple in Jerusalem after the return from Babylonian captivity?
o: Zerubbabel and Jeshua the high priest
qs.e: Zerubbabel the governor and Jeshua (Joshua) the high priest led the returning exiles in rebuilding the altar and laying the temple foundation.

qs.q: Under whose leadership were the broken walls of Jerusalem successfully restored in fifty-two days despite fierce opposition?
qs.e: Nehemiah organized the citizens of Jerusalem to rebuild the ruined city walls in fifty-two days while defending against hostile neighbors.

qs.q: What was the primary spiritual cause for the division of the united kingdom of Israel after Solomon's death?
o: Jeroboam's military invasion of Jerusalem with Egyptian backing
Rehoboam's refusal to worship at the sanctuary in Shiloh
Solomon's heart turned away from the Lord to worship foreign gods introduced by his foreign wives
The complete loss of the Ark of the Covenant during a Philistine attack
qs.e: Scripture records that Solomon's idolatry and worship of foreign deities provoked God's judgment to tear the kingdom away from his line.

qs.q: What religious monuments did Jeroboam I erect at Dan and Bethel, and for what purpose?
o: Bronze altars, to offer sacrifices exclusively for the tribe of Ephraim
Stone pillars, to commemorate the covenant made at Mount Sinai
Golden calves, to prevent his subjects from traveling to Jerusalem to worship
Wooden poles, to honor the Phoenician goddess Asherah
qs.e: Jeroboam set up two golden calves at Dan and Bethel so the northern Israelites would not return to Jerusalem for worship and switch allegiance.

qs.q: How did God demonstrate His supreme authority over Baal during Elijah's contest on Mount Carmel?
o: By striking King Ahab with temporary blindness on the mountain peak
By causing an earthquake that swallowed the 450 prophets of Baal instantly
By sending fire from heaven that consumed the sacrifice, wood, stones, and water
By turning the waters of the Mediterranean Sea into blood for three days
qs.e: Fire fell from the Lord and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, the soil, and licked up the water in the trench around Elijah's altar.

qs.q: Which prophet declared that God would make a New Covenant with Israel, writing His law directly upon their hearts?
qs.e: Jeremiah prophesied that God would make a new covenant with the house of Israel, putting His law in their minds and writing it on their hearts.

qs.q: What symbolic action did Jeremiah perform at God's command to demonstrate that fields would again be bought in Judah after the exile?
o: Buried a linen waistcloth by the Euphrates River
Broke an earthenware flask at the Valley of Ben-Hinnom
Purchased a field at Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel
Made a wooden yoke and wore it around his neck
qs.e: Jeremiah bought the field at Anathoth for seventeen shekels of silver while imprisoned, symbolizing future restoration and land ownership in Judah.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the Valley of Dry Bones, what did the reassembly and reanimation of the dry bones represent?
o: The military defeat of the Babylonian army by the Persian empire
The literal resurrection of the ancient patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
The corporate restoration and spiritual revival of the entire house of Israel
The total destruction of Gentile nations surrounding Jerusalem
qs.e: God revealed that the dry bones represented the whole house of Israel, promising to bring them out of their graves and return them to their land.

qs.q: Which minor prophet condemned the luxurious, complacent lifestyle of the upper class in Samaria who trampled upon the poor?
qs.e: Amos delivered stern warnings to those who were at ease in Samaria, lying on ivory beds while oppressing the poor and needy.

qs.q: Which minor prophet prophesied that the ruler of Israel whose origins are from of old would be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah?
qs.e: Micah foretold that out of Bethlehem Ephrathah would come a ruler over Israel whose origins are from of old, from ancient times.

qs.q: In the book of Job, who was the youngest speaker who waited until the three older friends finished speaking before offering his perspective?
qs.e: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite waited to speak because the others were older than he, expressing zeal for God's righteousness.

qs.q: According to Paul's teaching in First Corinthians chapter thirteen, what is the greatest of all spiritual virtues?
qs.e: Paul concluded his discourse on spiritual gifts by stating that three things remain: faith, hope, and love, but the greatest of these is love.

qs.q: What was the main argument presented by Paul in his letter to the Galatians regarding circumcision?
o: Circumcision grants physical health benefits that spiritual grace cannot provide
Circumcision is strictly required for all Jewish believers but optional for Gentile believers
Uncircumcision is a sin that must be repented of before receiving baptism
Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything; what counts is a new creation in Christ
qs.e: Paul emphasized to the Galatians that in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value; the only thing that counts is faith expressing itself through love.

qs.q: What took place during the agony of Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane prior to his arrest?
o: Jesus transformed bread and wine into His physical body before the twelve apostles
Jesus preached a sermon on resurrection to an assembled crowd of Galilean disciples
Jesus wrote a formal letter of defense to be delivered directly to Pontius Pilate
Jesus prayed fervently in anguish, submitting His will to the Father while His disciples slept
qs.e: In Gethsemane, Jesus experienced deep anguish, praying that the cup might pass from Him if possible, yet submitting entirely to the Father's will.

qs.q: In the account of the crucifixion, what phrase did the Roman centurion utter upon witnessing how Jesus died?
o: This prisoner deserved the sentence passed by Caesar
This man was an innocent political rebel
Surely this man was a prophet of Galilee
Truly this man was the Son of God
qs.e: When the centurion standing in front of Jesus saw how He died, he declared that truly this man was the Son of God.

qs.q: What strategy did Sanballat and Tobiah attempt to use to halt Nehemiah's work on the walls of Jerusalem?
o: Destroying the water supply of Jerusalem by diverting the Gihon spring
Offering lucrative trade deals in exchange for dismantling the gates
Appealing directly to the High Priest to excommunicate Nehemiah from the Temple
Using ridicule, threats of armed attack, and deceptive invitations to meetings
qs.e: Opponents tried mocking the wall, threatening military attacks, and sending treacherous invitations to compromise Nehemiah's work.

qs.q: Which king of Israel instituted non-Levitical priests and made two golden calves to consolidate his political rule?
qs.e: Jeroboam I established a counter-worship system with golden calves at Bethel and Dan, appointing non-Levitical priests to solidify his kingdom.

qs.q: In the book of Hosea, what were the names of Hosea's three children that served as prophetic signs to Israel?
qs.e: Hosea's children Jezreel (God sows/scatters), Lo-Ruhamah (not pitied), and Lo-Ammi (not my people) symbolized God's coming judgments upon unfaithful Israel.

qs.q: Which passage in the Major Prophets depicts the Servant of the Lord as being pierced for our transgressions and led like a lamb to the slaughter?
o: The Interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar's Statue in Daniel
The Vision of the Holy Temple in Ezekiel
The Fourth Servant Song in Isaiah
qs.e: Isaiah's prophecy of the Suffering Servant describes Him bearing our griefs, pierced for our transgressions, and led like a lamb to slaughter.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, how does civil authority relate to God's divine order?
o: Civil authorities are only valid when ruled directly by ordained Christian elders
Civil authorities are inherently demonic structures that Christians must always overthrow
Civil authorities hold no legitimate power over human conduct under any circumstances
Civil authorities are instituted by God as servants to maintain order and punish wrongdoing
qs.e: Paul taught in Romans that governing authorities are established by God to execute justice, reward good conduct, and punish evil.

qs.q: During the passion narrative, who was forced by Roman soldiers to carry the cross of Jesus to Golgotha?
qs.e: Simon, a native of Cyrene in North Africa, was compelled by the Roman soldiers to carry the cross behind Jesus.

qs.q: What primary creation account detail distinguishes humanity from all other created living beings?
o: Humanity was created in the image and likeness of God
Humanity was created before plants and animals
Humanity was made without any physical earthly body
Humanity was granted authority over angels in heaven
qs.e: Scripture states that God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created male and female, granting them dominion.

qs.q: Which patriarch was instructed by God to leave his native country, relatives, and father's house for an unknown land?
qs.e: God called Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans and Haran to go to the land that He would show him, promising to make him a great nation.

qs.q: How did God appear to Moses when commissioning him to lead Israel out of Egyptian bondage?
o: In a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush that was not consumed
In a thunderous cloud resting upon the peak of Mount Sinai
In a quiet whisper inside the inner chamber of the tabernacle
In a dream while Moses was sleeping in Pharaoh's palace
qs.e: The angel of the Lord appeared to Moses in a flame of fire from within a bush at Mount Horeb, and the bush burned without being consumed.

qs.q: What was the name of the female judge and prophetess who led Israel to victory over Sisera?
qs.e: Deborah was a prophetess and judge who held court under the Palm of Deborah and instructed Barak to assemble Israelite forces.

qs.q: Which king of Judah was anointed as a youth by Samuel after God rejected Saul from reigning?
qs.e: Samuel visited Jesse of Bethlehem and anointed David, the youngest son who was tending sheep, as God's chosen king.

qs.q: At what event did the Holy Spirit descend upon Jesus in physical form like a dove while a voice spoke from heaven?
o: The baptism of Jesus by John in the Jordan River
The transfiguration of Jesus on the high mountain
The presentation of Jesus in the Jerusalem Temple
The temptation of Jesus in the Judean wilderness
qs.e: When Jesus was baptized by John in the Jordan, the heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and God declared His divine sonship.

qs.q: Where did Jesus deliver the core moral teachings known as the Beatitudes to his disciples?
o: On a mountain during the Sermon on the Mount
In the Temple outer courtyard in Jerusalem
Beside the Well of Jacob in Samaria
qs.e: Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down to teach His disciples the Beatitudes and moral principles of God's kingdom.

qs.q: What nature miracle demonstrated Jesus' authority over atmospheric elements while sailing across Lake Galilee?
o: Calming the raging storm and stilling the wind and waves
Dividing the waters of the lake so disciples walked on dry ground
Turning the lake water into pure wine during a festival
Causing a sudden eclipse of the sun over the lake
qs.e: When a fierce windstorm arose on the lake, Jesus rebuked the wind and said to the sea, Peace! Be still! and there was a great calm.

qs.q: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, how did the father respond upon seeing his returning younger son from a distance?
o: Ran to him with compassion, embraced him, and held a feast
Required him to serve as a hired servant for seven years first
Refused to let him enter the family house until he paid his debts
Reprimanded him publicly before the entire village elders
qs.e: While the younger son was still a long way off, his father saw him, felt compassion, ran and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

qs.q: What miraculous sign accompanied the arrival of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost in Jerusalem?
o: Believers heard a sound like a mighty rushing wind and spoke in other tongues
The Temple building shook and its altar was split into two pieces
A pillar of cloud descended and covered the upper room for seven days
An army of angels appeared singing praises above Mount Zion
qs.e: On Pentecost, a sound like a violent rushing wind filled the house, tongues as of fire appeared, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: What vision did Peter see while praying on the rooftop in Joppa prior to visiting Cornelius?
o: A large sheet descending from heaven containing all kinds of four-footed animals
A golden altar with incense rising to the throne of God
A chariot of fire carrying a prophet into the clouds
A glowing ladder reaching from earth to the heavenly gates
qs.e: Peter saw a sheet lowered from heaven filled with four-footed animals, reptiles, and birds, symbolizing that God cleansed the Gentiles.

qs.q: Who was the Ethiopian eunuch reading when Philip approached his chariot on the desert road to Gaza?
qs.e: The Ethiopian treasurer was reading from Isaiah regarding the lamb led to the slaughter when Philip joined him to preach Jesus.

qs.q: What dramatic event led to the conversion of Saul on the road leading to Damascus?
o: An earthquake split the road and trapped his horses in a chasm
A bright light from heaven flashed around him and Jesus spoke to him
A prophet from Jerusalem met him and read a scroll of judgment
He had an angelic dream while resting at an inn at noon
qs.e: As Saul approached Damascus, a light from heaven shone around him, he fell to the ground, and heard the voice of Jesus asking why he persecuted Him.

qs.q: What advice did Jethro give to Moses regarding the administration of justice among the Israelites?
o: Abolish all lower courts and handle every single dispute personally
Delegate minor cases to capable, God-fearing men over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens
Require each tribe to govern itself without any central legal oversight
Appoint Egyptian military officers to enforce imperial decrees
qs.e: Jethro advised Moses to select trustworthy men who fear God to judge small matters, reserving only major cases for Moses.

qs.q: Which king of Israel established Samaria as the capital of the northern kingdom?
qs.e: Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built a city there, making Samaria the royal capital of the northern kingdom.

qs.q: What dramatic act did Elisha perform to demonstrate that Naaman the Syrian commander was healed of leprosy?
o: Anointed Naaman's forehead with consecrated oil from Shiloh
Instructed Naaman to dip seven times in the Jordan River
Placed his hands directly over Naaman's skin for three hours
Offered a burnt offering on the altar at Bethel on Naaman's behalf
qs.e: Elisha sent a messenger telling Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan, and Naaman's flesh was restored like that of a young boy.

qs.q: Which major prophet witnessed the destruction of Jerusalem and wrote a book of funeral dirges lamenting its fall?
qs.e: Jeremiah witnessed the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem and composed the book of Lamentations, mourning the ruin of Zion.

qs.q: Which minor prophet preached a message of divine repentance to the pagan city of Nineveh?
qs.e: Jonah was commissioned by God to go to Nineveh, and when he preached, the people and king of Nineveh repented in sackcloth.

qs.q: What main topic is addressed in the wisdom book of Proverbs regarding interpersonal relationships?
o: Enforcing military conscription across all administrative districts
Avoiding malicious gossip, lying lips, and hasty anger
Establishing royal diplomatic marriages with neighboring empires
Calculating interest rates on foreign commercial loans
qs.e: Proverbs repeatedly warns against gossip, deceitful speech, uncontrolled anger, and slander to foster healthy human relationships.

qs.q: According to Paul's epistle to the Ephesians, how are believers saved from sin?
o: By strictly maintaining moral purity without making any mistakes
By grace through faith, and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God
By inheriting the physical bloodline of ancient Hebrew patriarchs
By offering financial contributions to the temple treasury in Jerusalem
qs.e: Paul affirmed that it is by grace you have been saved through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Philippians, what attitude did he encourage believers to emulate regarding Christ Jesus?
o: Pride in their academic and legal qualifications before society
Humility, taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient unto death
Seeking political office to control judicial decisions in Rome
Demanding financial compensation for missionary endeavors
qs.e: Paul urged believers to have the mindset of Christ, who humbled Himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient to death on a cross.

qs.q: What key event took place during the Last Supper before Jesus was betrayed?
o: Jesus appointed Peter as the political ruler over Judea
Jesus instituted the Holy Communion with bread and the cup representing his body and blood
Jesus called down fire from heaven to consume the chief priests
Jesus wrote the book of Revelation on a parchment scroll
qs.e: At the Last Supper, Jesus took bread and wine, giving thanks and declaring them to be His body given and His blood shed for the new covenant.

qs.q: What was the response of Pontius Pilate when the crowd insisted that Jesus be crucified?
o: He ordered his soldiers to immediately arrest the chief priests
He washed his hands in water, declaring himself innocent of Jesus' blood
He released Jesus and condemned Barabbas to crucifixion instead
He resigned his position as Roman governor of Judea on the spot
qs.e: Pilate took water and washed his hands before the crowd, claiming he was innocent of the righteous man's blood, yet handed Jesus over to be crucified.

qs.q: Which prophet encouraged the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple, warning that neglecting God's house caused economic failure?
qs.e: Haggai rebuked the returned exiles for living in paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins, urging them to rebuild the Temple.

qs.q: What religious reform did Ezra carry out among the returned Jewish community in Jerusalem?
o: Re-established the monarchy by crowning a descendant of David as king
Confronted intermarriage with foreign pagan women and renewed covenant obedience to the Law
Abolished the daily morning and evening burnt sacrifices at the altar
Forbade the public reading of the Torah in synagogues
qs.e: Ezra taught the Law of Moses to the people and led a spiritual reform addressing unfaithful intermarriages with surrounding pagan nations.

qs.q: Why did Rehoboam's young advisors give him foolish counsel regarding the citizens' petition?
o: They were paid by Egyptian merchants to disrupt Israelite trade
They secretly plotted to install Jeroboam as the sole king of Judah
They lacked wisdom and sought to assert harsh royal dominance over the northern tribes
They believed the northern tribes were preparing an immediate invasion
qs.e: Rehoboam's young peers advised him to show harsh power rather than gentle servant leadership, leading directly to the rupture of the kingdom.

qs.q: What altar did Jeroboam build in Bethel to rival Jerusalem, and what prophetic warning was given against it?
o: An altar to Baal, which Elijah consumed with fire during his ministry
An altar of unhewn stone, which Solomon's son blessed during his coronation
An altar for a golden calf, which a man of God from Judah prophesied would be split apart
An altar of bronze, which Nebuchadnezzar carried off to Babylon
qs.e: Jeroboam built the calf altar at Bethel, and a man of God from Judah cried out against it, predicting that Josiah would defile it.

qs.q: What message did the prophet Hosea convey through God's instruction to rename his son Lo-Ammi?
o: That the tribe of Judah would relocate to Egypt for safety
That God would grant military victory over the Assyrian empire
That the unfaithful people of Israel were temporarily disowned as God's people
That the priesthood would be transferred from Levi to Benjamin
qs.e: Lo-Ammi means 'not my people', signifying that Israel's covenant relationship with God was fractured by their persistent idolatry.

qs.q: In the book of Habakkuk, what fundamental truth is revealed regarding how the righteous shall live during times of crisis?
o: The righteous shall live by military alliances with Egypt
The righteous shall live by accumulating stockpiles of grain
The righteous shall live by his faith
The righteous shall live by fleeing into wilderness caves
qs.e: Habakkuk declared that while the proud soul is not upright, the righteous person shall live by his faithfulness and trust in God.

qs.q: In Isaiah's prophecy of the Messiah, what title is given to the child born to us in chapter nine?
o: King of Babylon, Master of Wisdom, Ruler of Egypt, Great Judge
Supreme Monarch, Conqueror of Nations, Lord of War, High Priest
Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace
Lion of Judah, Archangel of Heaven, Commander of Chariots, Prophet
qs.e: Isaiah prophesied that the child born to us would be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

qs.q: What symbolic vision did Ezekiel see depicting God's departing glory from Jerusalem?
o: A dark cloud completely covering the Dead Sea region for forty days
A consuming fire burning down the palace of King Zedekiah
The chariot-throne of God lifting up from the Temple threshold and moving east of the city
An iron wall erected between the prophet and the city walls
qs.e: Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord rise from above the cherubim, move to the threshold of the Temple, and depart east over the Mount of Olives.

qs.q: In the book of Proverbs, how is the Virtuous Woman described in terms of her character and industry?
o: She seeks political power in the city gates over the elders
She spends her days in idle leisure while servants perform all duties
She works willingly with her hands, cares for her household, and speaks with wisdom and kindness
She hoarding wealth exclusively for her personal adornment
qs.e: The virtuous woman in Proverbs is praised for her diligence, charitable spirit, trustworthy character, and wise, kind instruction.

qs.q: What central question about human suffering forms the core debate of the book of Job?
o: Whether animal sacrifices can permanently wash away ancestral guilt
Whether military power is superior to philosophical knowledge
Whether a person can love and worship God blamelessly without expecting material reward
Whether the Temple in Jerusalem should be built of cedar or stone
qs.e: Job addresses why the righteous suffer and whether genuine faith exists independent of earthly prosperity and blessings.

qs.q: What ethical requirement regarding neighborly love did Paul state in Romans as the fulfillment of the Law?
o: Love applies only to fellow Hebrew citizens who keep the Sabbath
Love requires enforcing religious conformity across all public institutions
Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law
Love eliminates the need for civil laws and tax collection
qs.e: Paul taught that all moral commandments are summed up in loving one's neighbor as oneself, because love does no harm to a neighbor.

qs.q: Which major prophet was commanded by God to buy a linen loincloth, hide it in a rock crevice, and later retrieve it ruined?
qs.e: Jeremiah hid his linen waistcloth at the Euphrates; when retrieved, it was ruined, symbolizing how Judah became useless through pride.

qs.q: In the book of Ezekiel, what was the role of the prophet described as a watchman over the house of Israel?
o: To record tax records for the Babylonian governor in exile
To command the military guards defending the city gates of Jerusalem
To hear God's word and warn the wicked to turn from their evil ways or share guilt for their blood
To perform ritual cleansings for priests in the sanctuary
qs.e: God appointed Ezekiel as a watchman; if he warned the wicked and they refused to repent, their blood was on their own heads.

qs.q: Which minor prophet announced that God hates divorce and spiritual unfaithfulness in covenant relationships?
qs.e: Malachi declared that God hates divorce and unfaithfulness to the wife of one's youth, calling the nation to covenant integrity.

qs.q: Which minor prophet declared that God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh, causing sons and daughters to prophesy?
qs.e: Joel foretold the outpouring of God's Spirit on all people, a prophecy cited by Peter on the day of Pentecost.

qs.q: In the book of Ecclesiastes, what observation is made regarding time and human events in chapter three?
o: Physical hard labor guarantees permanent earthly happiness
Human history is completely random without any divine oversight or purpose
Future events are predetermined solely by planetary positions
There is an appointed time for everything, and a season for every activity under heaven
qs.e: Ecclesiastes affirms that to everything there is a season, a time for every purpose under heaven, reflecting God's sovereign timing.

qs.q: What profound truth did Paul teach in First Corinthians chapter fifteen regarding the Christian resurrection hope?
o: Only ordained church leaders will experience bodily resurrection at the last day
Resurrection applies only to the soul, whereas the physical body is permanently discarded
The resurrection took place in secret prior to the crucifixion of Jesus
If Christ has not been raised, our preaching is useless and your faith is futile
qs.e: Paul emphasized that Christ's physical resurrection is foundational to Christian faith; without it, believers remain in their sins.

qs.q: In the letter to the Romans, how does Paul describe the spiritual adoption of believers into God's family?
o: Adoption requires complete legal naturalization under Roman civil law
Believers are adopted automatically by purchasing church membership certificates
Adoption is restricted exclusively to descendants of the twelve patriarchs
Believers receive the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry, Abba, Father
qs.e: Paul wrote that believers received the Spirit of adoption, testifying with our spirit that we are children of God and co-heirs with Christ.

qs.q: What sign appeared in the sky and what miraculous events occurred at the moment Jesus yielded up his spirit on the cross?
o: An angel appeared and carried the body of Jesus directly into heaven
A bright rainbow spanned across Jerusalem while heavy rain cleansed the city
Fire descended from heaven and consumed the wooden cross completely
Darkness covered the land, the curtain was torn, the earth shook, and rocks split
qs.e: At Jesus' death, darkness fell over the land, the sanctuary curtain tore in two, the earth quaked, and rocks split open.

qs.q: Who went to Pontius Pilate to request the body of Jesus for burial in his own new tomb?
qs.e: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the Council who was secretly a disciple, asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in his tomb.

qs.q: What obstacle did Zerubbabel face while rebuilding the Temple after returning from Babylon?
o: The complete refusal of Cyrus to grant financial authorization
A severe drought that made it impossible to transport timber from Lebanon
A rebellion among his own priests who refused to offer morning sacrifices
Local opposition from neighboring peoples who sent letters to Persian kings to halt construction
qs.e: Adversaries in Samaria opposed the rebuilding project, hiring counselors to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus.

qs.q: How did Jeroboam's religious system lead northern Israel into long-term national apostasy?
o: It required the sacrifice of royal children to foreign deities every year
It forced all citizens to adopt Egyptian pharaonic worship rituals
It abolished all religious festivals and prohibited prayer across the nation
It made syncretistic calf-worship the official state religion, causing subsequent kings to walk in the sin of Jeroboam
qs.e: Jeroboam's calf shrines established a corrupt state religion that misled Israel for generations, known in Scripture as the sin of Jeroboam.

qs.q: Which Old Testament passage is cited by Peter during Pentecost to explain the phenomenon of speaking in tongues?
o: The proclamation of Isaiah regarding the child named Immanuel
The vision of Ezekiel regarding the valley of dry bones
The promise of Jeremiah regarding the new covenant written on hearts
The prophecy of Joel regarding the outpouring of the Holy Spirit
qs.e: Peter quoted Joel's prophecy that in the last days God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh, explaining the Pentecost manifestation.

qs.q: In Paul's defense before King Agrippa recorded in Acts, what central Christian doctrine did Paul claim was the hope of Israel?
o: The total abolition of the Mosaic ceremonial law
The political liberation of Judea from Roman taxation
The military conquest of surrounding Mediterranean kingdoms
The resurrection of the dead through Jesus Christ
qs.e: Paul asserted before Agrippa that he stood on trial for the hope of the promise made by God to the fathers: the resurrection of the dead.

qs.q: Which minor prophet contains a dramatic prophecy of the Day of the Lord coming with darkness, fire, and cosmic judgment?
qs.e: Zephaniah vividly proclaimed the great Day of the Lord as a day of wrath, distress, anguish, darkness, and cosmic inspection.

qs.q: In the book of Job, what was the final outcome for Job after he prayed for his three friends?
o: Job's three friends were condemned to perpetual exile in Chaldea
Job was appointed as governor over the land of Uz by divine decree
Job was taken to heaven without experiencing physical death
The Lord restored Job's prosperity and gave him double what he had before
qs.e: After Job prayed for his friends, the Lord restored his fortunes and granted him double the wealth, along with seven sons and three daughters.

qs.q: Which prophet confronted King David with the parable of the poor man's single ewe lamb after David sinned with Bathsheba?
qs.e: Nathan the prophet used the story of the rich man who stole a poor man's beloved ewe lamb to convict King David of his sin.

qs.q: Which disciple betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver?
qs.e: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.

qs.q: What was the name of the garden where Jesus prayed in agony before his arrest?
qs.e: Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane on the Mount of Olives to pray prior to His arrest.

qs.q: Who was the high priest who presided over the Jewish Sanhedrin trial of Jesus?
qs.e: Caiaphas was the high priest that year who questioned Jesus and declared Him guilty of blasphemy before the council.

qs.q: What sign of covenant did God set in the clouds after the flood during Noah's time?
qs.e: God established His covenant with Noah and every living creature, setting the rainbow in the sky as a sign.

qs.q: Which patriarch wrestled with a man until daybreak and had his name changed to Israel?
qs.e: Jacob wrestled with the divine messenger at Peniel, and his name was changed to Israel because he strived with God and prevailed.

qs.q: Who was the young shepherd boy who defeated the Philistine champion Goliath using a sling and stone?
qs.e: David, trusting in the name of the Lord of hosts, struck down the Philistine giant Goliath with a single sling stone.

qs.q: What city was captured by King David and established as the political and religious capital of Israel?
qs.e: David captured the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, making it the City of David and the capital of his kingdom.

qs.q: What did Solomon construct in Jerusalem that fulfilled his father David's deep desire?
o: The high places at Dan and Bethel
qs.e: Solomon constructed the magnificent Temple of the Lord on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, fulfilling David's goal.

qs.q: Who was the queen of the northern kingdom whose idolatry and persecution of God's prophets brought severe judgment?
qs.e: Jezebel, the Phoenician wife of King Ahab, introduced Baal worship and ordered the killing of the Lord's prophets.

qs.q: Which major prophet was called while still a youth and told not to be afraid because God was with him?
qs.e: God called Jeremiah as a youth, telling him that before he was formed in the womb God knew him and appointed him to the nations.

qs.q: In the vision of Ezekiel, what was the primary purpose of the watchman standing upon the wall?
o: To sound the trumpet warning to the people when danger or sword approaches
To collect tolls from foreign merchants entering city gates
To record daily meteorological changes over Judea
To light ceremonial lamps at sunset every evening
qs.e: The watchman's duty was to blow the trumpet and warn the citizens; if they heeded the warning, their lives were saved.

qs.q: Which minor prophet was commanded to go to the city of Nineveh but initially boarded a ship to Tarshish instead?
qs.e: Jonah attempted to flee from the presence of the Lord by boarding a ship bound for Tarshish instead of obeying God's command.

qs.q: What is the central theme of the minor prophetic book of Amos?
o: A passionate call for social justice and moral righteousness among God's people
A detailed manual for military conquest of neighboring states
A philosophical debate on the physical nature of angels
A architectural blueprint for rebuilding the temple walls
qs.e: Amos denounced religious hypocrisy accompanied by social oppression, demanding that justice roll down like waters.

qs.q: According to Proverbs, how does a wise person respond to soft speech during a heated argument?
o: A soft answer indicates weakness that should be exploited immediately
A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger
A soft answer should be met with louder shouting to win the dispute
A soft answer has no impact on human emotions
qs.e: Proverbs teaches that a gentle, soft answer diffuses anger and turns away wrath, whereas harsh words fuel conflict.

qs.q: What message does the author of Ecclesiastes emphasize regarding youth and aging?
o: Spend all youthful energies accumulating earthly fame and pleasure
Remember your Creator in the days of your youth before the difficult days come
Ignore spiritual devotion until old age arrives
Physical strength during youth guarantees immunity from hardship
qs.e: Ecclesiastes urges the young to remember their Creator during youth before the years draw near when they will find no pleasure in them.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Galatians, what fruit is produced in the life of a believer led by the Spirit?
o: Wealth, physical dominance, political authority, social prestige, intellect
Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control
Strict ceremonial perfection, public praise, financial prosperity, long life
Immunity from legal trials, flawless memory, military victory, worldly status
qs.e: Paul listed the fruit of the Spirit as love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

qs.q: In First Corinthians, how does Paul describe the Lord's Supper tradition handed down to the church?
o: It is a private family banquet reserved exclusively for wealthy citizens
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes
It replaces all civil laws and obligations toward local government
It grants physical immortality to anyone who tastes the bread
qs.e: Paul explained that participating in the Lord's Supper proclaims Christ's sacrificial death until His glorious return.

qs.q: What key issue led to the appointment of the seven deacons in the early church at Jerusalem?
o: The apostles needed bodyguards to protect them from Roman soldiers
Hellenistic widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food
The church needed financial accountants to manage real estate sales
Gentile believers were demanding separate worship services
qs.e: The seven men full of faith and the Spirit were appointed to ensure fair food distribution to Hellenistic widows without neglecting prayer.

qs.q: Where were the disciples of Jesus first called Christians?
qs.e: Acts records that it was in the city of Syrian Antioch that the believers were first called Christians.

qs.q: What significant statement did Stephen make right before he died as he prayed for his executioners?
o: May the fire of heaven consume this Sanhedrin immediately
Lord, do not hold this sin against them
I appeal my sentence to Caesar in Rome
My death will bring military destruction upon Jerusalem
qs.e: As Stephen was being stoned, he fell on his knees and cried out with a loud voice asking God not to hold the sin against them.

qs.q: How did God deliver Peter from King Herod Agrippa's prison on the night before his scheduled trial?
o: Earthquakes tore down the jail walls and freed all prisoners
An angel appeared, broke his chains, opened the iron gates, and led him out
Christian soldiers stormed the prison and rescued Peter by force
Herod changed his mind and issued a royal pardon at midnight
qs.e: An angel of the Lord struck Peter on the side, his chains fell off, and the angel guided him past guards and through iron gates.

qs.q: What vision led Paul and his companions to cross over into Macedonia during his second missionary journey?
o: A pillar of fire guiding their ship toward the Aegean coast
A vision of a man of Macedonia standing and begging him, Come over to Macedonia and help us
A letter from the Roman governor inviting them to preach in Philippi
A dream of an angel holding a golden crown above Europe
qs.e: During the night Paul had a vision of a Macedonian man pleading for help, which Paul interpreted as God's call to preach there.

qs.q: What sermon did Paul deliver at the Areopagus in Athens regarding the Unknown God?
o: Condemned Greek literature and demanded all philosophy books be burned
Proclaimed that the God who made the world does not live in temples made by hands and calls all people to repent
Urged the Athenian philosophers to adopt Hebrew circumcision laws
Claimed that Roman emperors were divine representatives of God
qs.e: Paul addressed the Areopagus, identifying the Unknown God as the Creator of heaven and earth who raised Jesus from the dead.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, how does the grace of God through Christ free believers from sin's power?
o: Grace eliminates all moral distinctions between righteousness and wickedness
Believers were buried with Christ through baptism into death so they might walk in newness of life
Believers are exempt from physical suffering and social trials
Grace allows believers to continue sinning without any spiritual consequence
qs.e: Paul taught that we were buried with Christ through baptism so that just as Christ was raised, we too may walk in newness of life.

qs.q: In Paul's second letter to the Corinthians, how is the ministry of reconciliation defined?
o: Reconciliation requires political agreements between church elders and Roman authorities
God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting people's sins against them, and entrusting us with the message
Reconciliation is achieved by offering formal animal sacrifices at Mount Zion
Reconciliation applies only to individuals who have never committed any moral failure
qs.e: Paul declared that God reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry and message of reconciliation.

qs.q: What was the outcome of the trial of Jesus before Pontius Pilate when Pilate offered to release a prisoner according to custom?
o: Pilate overruled the crowd and set both Jesus and Barabbas free
The crowd overwhelmingly voted to release Jesus and punish Barabbas
The crowd demanded the release of Barabbas and insisted that Jesus be crucified
The Sanhedrin requested that both prisoners be kept in custody until Passover ended
qs.e: The crowd, persuaded by the chief priests and elders, asked for Barabbas the insurrectionist to be released and Jesus to be crucified.

qs.q: What supernatural event accompanied the resurrection of Jesus on the first day of the week?
o: The Temple of Solomon collapsed completely in Jerusalem
A column of fire descended on the tomb and consumed the Roman soldiers
A severe earthquake occurred as an angel of the Lord rolled back the stone from the tomb
A trumpet sounded across the whole Mediterranean region for three hours
qs.e: There was a violent earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it.

qs.q: Who was the governor of Persia who allowed Nehemiah to travel to Jerusalem to rebuild its city walls?
qs.e: Nehemiah served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, who granted him official letters and permission to rebuild Jerusalem.

qs.q: What solemn pledge did the returned exiles make in the covenant signed under Nehemiah and Ezra?
o: To refuse to pay taxes to the Persian imperial administration
To build a massive army and conquer surrounding territories
To keep God's law, avoid intermarriage with pagan neighbors, observe the Sabbath, and support the Temple
To move the sanctuary from Jerusalem to Mount Gerizim
qs.e: The people entered into a binding agreement to walk in God's Law, refrain from intermarriage, keep Sabbath, and provide for God's house.

qs.q: How did Jeroboam's institution of golden calves affect the priesthood in the northern kingdom?
o: He doubled the salaries of Levitical priests to secure their loyalty
He required high priests to be consecrated exclusively by the king of Judah
He rejected the Levites and appointed priests from all sorts of people who were not of Levi's line
He limited the priesthood exclusively to the sons of Aaron
qs.e: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron and Levites, appointing his own priests for the high places.

qs.q: What prophecy did the man of God from Judah deliver against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel?
o: That fire from heaven would consume Jeroboam and his royal family instantly
That the altar would be transported to Egypt by foreign invaders
That a child named Josiah would be born to the house of David who would burn human bones upon the altar
That the altar would be rebuilt out of gold by the king of Babylon
qs.e: The prophet cried against the altar, announcing that a son named Josiah would be born to David's house and burn priests' bones on it.

qs.q: What did Elisha request from Elijah before the senior prophet was taken away in a whirlwind?
o: A guarantee that Elisha would never suffer persecution
Elijah's gold ring and royal staff
A double portion of Elijah's spirit
An appointment as chief advisor to King Ahab
qs.e: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, which was granted when Elisha witnessed Elijah taken up in a chariot of fire.

qs.q: What miraculous sign occurred when Elisha's dead bones touched a deceased man thrown into his tomb?
o: The man's body turned into pure gold
The tomb filled with sweet fragrant perfume
The dead man came back to life and stood up on his feet
An angelic choir sang praises inside the burial cave
qs.e: When the corpse touched the bones of Elisha, the man revived and stood up on his feet, demonstrating God's power through Elisha.

qs.q: Which major prophet was told by God to go down to the potter's house to learn a lesson about divine sovereignty over nations?
qs.e: Jeremiah watched the potter reshape a marred clay vessel, learning that God has sovereign authority to shape and reshape nations.

qs.q: In Isaiah's prophecy, what is the significance of the title Immanuel given to the promised child?
qs.e: The prophet Isaiah declared that the virgin would conceive and bear a son and call his name Immanuel, meaning 'God with us'.

qs.q: What message did Ezekiel convey through the symbolic action of eating a scroll filled with lamentations and mourning?
o: The prophetic ministry would bring great material riches to Ezekiel
God's judgment would cause severe physical famine across Babylonia
The prophet must fully absorb and digest God's word before preaching it to a rebellious house
The Mosaic scroll was to be hidden in a cave near the Dead Sea
qs.e: Ezekiel ate the scroll as commanded, finding it sweet as honey, symbolizing internalizing God's message for His rebellious people.

qs.q: Which minor prophet declared that God desires steadfast love and mercy rather than sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings?
qs.e: Hosea delivered God's message: 'For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.'

qs.q: In the book of Micah, what judgment is pronounced upon greedy leaders who covet fields and seize houses by force?
o: They will be rewarded with expansion of their commercial estates
Their descendants will rule over Jerusalem for ten generations
God plans disaster against such a family, and they will be stripped of their ill-gotten possessions
They will receive divine immunity from foreign invasion
qs.e: Micah condemned those who plot evil on their beds and seize fields, declaring that God was planning disaster against them.

qs.q: What main topic is explored in the wisdom book of Proverbs regarding the tongue and speech?
o: Silent meditation replaces all vocal communication in worship
Speech has no lasting impact on human destiny or divine judgment
Flattery and deceitful speech are effective tools for spiritual growth
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit
qs.e: Proverbs emphasizes that death and life are in the power of the tongue, warning against careless, destructive, or deceitful words.

qs.q: In the book of Job, what was Job's physical and emotional reaction when his friends sat with him in silence for seven days?
o: Job fled into the desert of Midian to escape their presence
Job immediately renounced his faith in God and joined his friends in pagan rituals
Job demanded that his friends pay him financial compensation for his lost livestock
Job eventually broke his silence and cursed the day of his birth while maintaining he had not sinned against God
qs.e: After seven days of silent grief, Job spoke and cursed the day he was born, expressing deep anguish while seeking understanding from God.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, what is the relationship between believers and the Law of Moses?
o: The Law applies only to Gentile Christians living in Rome
Believers must keep every ceremonial ritual of the Law to retain salvation
The Law was an evil institution created by human rulers to enslave humanity
Believers died to the Law through the body of Christ so that they might belong to another, to Him who was raised
qs.e: Paul explained that believers died to the Law through Christ so that we might serve in the new way of the Spirit.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Ephesians, what spiritual armor is believers instructed to put on against spiritual forces of evil?
o: Ceremonial robes, golden crowns, silver incense burners, phylacteries, special garments
Physical chainmail, iron helmets, bronze spears, wooden shields, catapults, and chariots
Academic degrees, political alliances, commercial wealth, physical strength, legal protection
The belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shoes of peace, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, sword of the Spirit
qs.e: Paul exhorted Christians to take up the full armor of God: truth, righteousness, gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and God's word.

qs.q: What took place during the Resurrection appearances of Jesus to his disciples behind locked doors?
o: Jesus informed them that Thomas was excluded permanently from apostolic ministry
Jesus rebuked them severely and departed to heaven without speaking a word
Jesus commanded them to immediately organize an armed resistance against Rome
Jesus appeared among them, showed his hands and side, said 'Peace be with you', and breathed on them the Holy Spirit
qs.e: Jesus came and stood among the disciples despite locked doors, imparted His peace, showed His wounds, and breathed on them the Spirit.

qs.q: What was the reaction of the chief priests when Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver to the Temple?
o: They distributed the silver to the poor widows of Jerusalem
They accepted the silver joyfully and added it to the high priest's personal fund
They returned the money to Judas and demanded he bring Jesus back alive
They refused to put the money into the Temple treasury because it was blood money, and bought the Potter's Field
qs.e: The chief priests declared it unlawful to put blood money into the treasury, so they used it to purchase the Potter's Field as a burial place for foreigners.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah respond when Sanballat and Geshem invited him to meet at the plain of Ono?
o: He ordered his men to attack the plain of Ono with archers
He accepted immediately and took fifty armed guards to negotiate a truce
He sent Ezra the scribe to represent him at the conference
He declined, stating he was doing a great work and could not leave it to come down
qs.e: Nehemiah recognized their treacherous intent and replied four times that he was doing a great work and could not come down.

qs.q: Which major prophet saw the vision of God's holy throne with four living creatures, each having four faces and four wings?
qs.e: Ezekiel's opening vision by the Chebar canal featured four living creatures accompanying the divine throne-chariot of God.

qs.q: In the book of Hosea, what is the spiritual symbolic meaning of the name Lo-Ruhamah given to Hosea's daughter?
o: Exile in Babylon, predicting the fall of Judah
God is my strength, symbolizing military deliverance from Syria
Prince of peace, foretelling the birth of a righteous king
No mercy / not pitied, showing that God would no longer show mercy to the rebellious house of Israel
qs.e: God instructed Hosea to name his daughter Lo-Ruhamah to signify that God would no longer show mercy to the house of Israel.

qs.q: Which passage in the New Testament contains Paul's hymn celebrating Christ's self-emptying (kenosis) and exalted name?
qs.e: Philippians chapter two features the famous Christ-hymn describing Jesus emptying Himself, taking human form, dying on the cross, and being exalted.

qs.q: During the reign of which king of Judah was the Book of the Law rediscovered in the Temple during repairs?
qs.e: Hilkiah the high priest found the Book of the Law in the Temple during repairs under King Josiah, sparking a major national spiritual reformation.

qs.q: Which judge of Israel made a rash vow before battle that resulted in sacrificing his only daughter upon returning victorious?
qs.e: Jephthah vowed that whatever came out of his house to meet him after defeating the Ammonites would be offered as a burnt offering, which turned out to be his daughter.

qs.q: In the parable of the Sower, what does the seed sown on good soil represent?
o: Those who hear the word, accept it, and produce a fruitful harvest
Those who hear the word but immediately forget it due to worldly worries
Those who accept the word with joy but fall away during persecution
Those who reject the preacher and refuse to listen
qs.e: The seed on good soil represents those with noble and good hearts who hear the word, retain it, and by persevering produce a crop.

qs.q: Which miracle of Jesus involved feeding five thousand men with five barley loaves and two small fish?
qs.e: Jesus multiplied five barley loaves and two fish provided by a young boy, feeding five thousand men besides women and children.

qs.q: Who was the mother of Samuel who prayed fervently at the sanctuary in Shiloh for a child?
qs.e: Hannah prayed in deep anguish at Shiloh, promising that if God gave her a son, she would dedicate him to the Lord for all his life.

qs.q: Which prophet rebuked King Saul for offering an unlawful sacrifice at Gilgal instead of waiting for the prophet?
qs.e: Samuel confronted Saul for failing to wait the seven days, declaring that to obey is better than sacrifice.

qs.q: What was the main topic taught by Jesus regarding worry and anxiety in the Sermon on the Mount?
o: Look at the birds of the air and lilies of the field; seek first God's kingdom and His righteousness
Stockpile grain and gold to ensure financial security against future famines
Rely on political treaties with Rome to preserve personal safety
Anxiety is a virtue that helps humans plan effectively for old age
qs.e: Jesus taught that God cares for birds and lilies and will care for people, instructing them to seek first God's kingdom.

qs.q: Who was the Roman governor who condemned Jesus to be crucified despite finding no guilt in him?
qs.e: Pontius Pilate served as the Roman procurator who reluctantly passed the death sentence of crucifixion upon Jesus.

qs.q: What happened to Saul on the road to Damascus that caused him to fall to the ground?
o: A bright light from heaven flashed around him and he heard the voice of Jesus
A fierce thunderstorm struck his horse and threw him into the mud
An armed group of Christians blocked his path and arrested him
A sudden earthquake destroyed the city walls of Damascus
qs.e: Saul was blinded by a sudden heavenly light and heard Jesus asking why he was persecuting Him.

qs.q: What was the principal charge brought against Stephen by false witnesses before the Sanhedrin?
o: That he spoke blasphemous words against the holy place and the Law of Moses
That he stole money from the Temple treasury to give to Gentiles
That he led an armed revolt against the Roman garrison in Jerusalem
That he refused to give food to Hebrew widows in the daily distribution
qs.e: False witnesses testified that Stephen never stopped speaking against the Temple and the Law.

qs.q: Which Christian believer in Damascus was instructed by God in a vision to visit Saul and lay hands on him to restore his sight?
qs.e: Ananias of Damascus obeyed the Lord's command, went to the house on Straight Street, laid hands on Saul, and restored his sight.

qs.q: What vision did Cornelius the Roman centurion in Caesarea see that prompted him to send for Peter?
o: An angel of God appeared to him telling him that his prayers and alms had ascended as a memorial before God
A sheet descended from heaven filled with clean and unclean animals
A chariot of fire appeared above his military barracks
A voice spoke from a burning bush instructing him to move to Jerusalem
qs.e: An angel appeared to Cornelius, acknowledging his prayers and charitable gifts, and directed him to send men to Joppa for Peter.

qs.q: How did King Herod Agrippa I die after accepting divine praise from the people of Tyre and Sidon?
o: An angel of the Lord struck him down because he did not give praise to God, and he was eaten by worms
He was slain in battle against the Persian empire
He drowned while attempting to cross the Sea of Galilee
He was assassinated by his own palace guards during a feast
qs.e: Because Herod did not give praise to God when acclaimed as a god, an angel struck him down and he was eaten by worms.

qs.q: What was the result of Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns at midnight in the Philippian jail?
o: A violent earthquake shook the prison foundations, opening all doors and loosening everyone's chains
The Roman governor sent an urgent letter ordering their immediate release
The jailer called Roman soldiers to execute them before daybreak
An angel carried them through the prison roof to safety
qs.e: As Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns, a great earthquake shook the jail, doors flew open, and chains unfastened.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, how does a person receive the gift of salvation?
o: By performing seventy ritual washings in the Jordan River
If you confess with your mouth Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead
By proving flawless ancestral descent from King David
By purchasing indulgence letters from the Jerusalem apostles
qs.e: Paul affirmed that confessing Jesus as Lord and believing in God's resurrection of Jesus leads to righteousness and salvation.

qs.q: What does Paul teach in First Corinthians regarding the nature of Christian love in chapter thirteen?
o: Love requires physical military defense of national borders
Love is patient, love is kind, it does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud
Love applies only to people of the same ethnic and religious background
Love is inferior to spiritual gifts like speaking in tongues
qs.e: Paul described love as patient, kind, humble, forgiving, enduring all things, and exceeding all spiritual gifts.

qs.q: Which Old Testament patriarch was willing to offer his son Isaac as a sacrifice on Mount Moriah in obedience to God?
qs.e: Abraham demonstrated supreme faith when tested by God, offering up his son Isaac until God provided a ram caught in a thicket.

qs.q: How did Joseph interpret Pharaoh's two dreams regarding seven fat cows and seven lean cows?
o: Seven years of foreign military invasion followed by seven years of peace
Seven years of great abundance across Egypt followed by seven years of severe famine
Seven royal sons born to Pharaoh followed by seven years of mourning
Seven years of plagues on the Nile followed by seven years of prosperity
qs.e: Joseph explained that both dreams revealed seven years of great plenty throughout Egypt followed by seven years of famine.

qs.q: What plague finally compelled Pharaoh to let the children of Israel depart from Egypt?
o: The plague of locusts that devoured all vegetation
The death of the firstborn in every Egyptian household during Passover
The turning of the Nile River waters into blood
The severe hail and fire that destroyed livestock
qs.e: At midnight the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, prompting Pharaoh to urgently command Israel to leave.

qs.q: Which judge of Israel delivered the people from Philistine oppression through his supernatural physical strength?
qs.e: Samson was endowed with extraordinary physical strength through his Nazirite vow, repeatedly defeating Philistine forces.

qs.q: What severe punishment did King Saul incur when he spared Agag the king of the Amalekites and the best livestock?
o: Saul was struck with leprosy like Naaman the Syrian
God rejected Saul from being king over Israel because he disobeyed the voice of the Lord
Saul's kingdom was immediately surrendered to the Philistines
Saul was forced to serve as a high priest at Shiloh
qs.e: Samuel informed Saul that because he rejected the word of the Lord, God rejected him from being king over Israel.

qs.q: What was the response of the northern tribes when Rehoboam declared his finger would be thicker than his father's waist?
o: We pledge eternal allegiance to the house of David
What share do we have in David? To your tents, O Israel!
Let us build a joint capital city at Jericho
We demand that Rehoboam be crowned emperor of Syria
qs.e: The northern tribes shouted 'What share have we in David?' and returned to their tents, establishing Jeroboam as king.

qs.q: What sin did Jeroboam commit that became a recurring curse for all subsequent kings of northern Israel?
o: Surrendering the Temple treasures to the king of Babylon
Setting up golden calves at Dan and Bethel and appointing non-Levitical priests
Abolishing the celebration of the Passover throughout Israel
Moving the capital from Shechem to Jerusalem
qs.e: Jeroboam's golden calf sanctuaries and illegitimate priesthood established a pattern of idolatry known as the sin of Jeroboam.

qs.q: How did Elijah demonstrate God's provision for the widow of Zarephath during the three-year drought?
o: He provided her with ten bags of silver from King Ahab's treasury
Her jar of flour was not spent and her jug of oil did not fail until rain returned
He brought bread and meat to her house via ravens every morning
He turned her house into a royal palace for prophets
