qs.e: Elijah promised that the jar of flour would not be exhausted and the jug of oil would not run dry, sustaining her family.

qs.q: What judgment was pronounced upon King Ahab and Queen Jezebel by Elijah after the murder of Naboth?
o: Ahab would be captured and imprisoned in Babylon for twenty years
Dogs would lick Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's blood, and Jezebel would be devoured by dogs by the wall of Jezreel
Jezebel would be struck with blindness and banished to Midian
Their royal palace would be converted into a sanctuary for Levites
qs.e: Elijah prophesied that dogs would lick Ahab's blood in Jezreel and Jezebel would be eaten by dogs beside the wall.

qs.q: Which major prophet was commissioned by God in the Temple when he heard the voice saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
qs.e: Isaiah heard the Lord asking whom to send, and he responded: 'Here am I! Send me.'

qs.q: In the book of Jeremiah, what object lesson was illustrated when God commanded the prophet to break a potter's earthenware jar?
o: The Babylonian empire would be completely destroyed within three days
God would break the city of Jerusalem and its people beyond repair because of their persistent idolatry
The Levitical priesthood would be replaced by angelic messengers
The Temple vessels would be duplicated in gold by Persian craftsmen
qs.e: Jeremiah smashed the potter's jar at the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, symbolizing how God would shatter Jerusalem for its sins.

qs.q: Which minor prophet used the locust plague as a vivid picture of the coming Day of the Lord?
qs.e: Joel described a catastrophic locust invasion as a harbinger of the great and awesome Day of the Lord calling for national repentance.

qs.q: What central declaration did the minor prophet Habakkuk make when questioning God about why the wicked Babylonians were used to discipline Judah?
o: The law of Moses is no longer relevant for God's covenant people
Judah will defeat Babylon using chariot armies
The Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before Him
Idolatry in Babylon is superior to religious life in Jerusalem
qs.e: Habakkuk concluded his dialogue by affirming God's sovereignty: 'The Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before Him.'

qs.q: In the book of Proverbs, what contrast is drawn between the path of the righteous and the path of the wicked?
o: The wicked always accumulate greater spiritual wisdom than the righteous
The righteous experience no physical death, while the wicked die young
The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn shining brighter until full day, but the way of the wicked is like deep darkness
The path of the righteous leads to material poverty, while the wicked prosper
qs.e: Proverbs contrasts the righteous path, which shines brighter and brighter, with the way of the wicked where they stumble in darkness.

qs.q: What was the response of Job's wife when Job lost his children, wealth, and health?
o: Flee to the land of Egypt for safety
Offer animal sacrifices to heal your body
Praise the Lord for His righteous judgment
qs.e: Job's wife, overwhelmed by tragedy, told him to curse God and die, but Job refused to sin with his lips.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Colossians, what role does Jesus Christ hold in creation and the church?
o: He is a minor political reformer who modified Roman civic codes
He is one of several created angelic beings sent to guide humanity
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation, and the head of the body, the church
He is a prophet exclusive to the geographical region of Judea
qs.e: Paul proclaimed Christ as the image of the invisible God, Creator of all things in heaven and earth, and head of the church.

qs.q: In First Thessalonians, what comfort does Paul offer believers regarding those who have died in Christ before his return?
o: Deceased believers reincarnate into new human bodies on earth
Those who die before Christ's return have lost all spiritual inheritance forever
The dead in Christ will rise first, then we who are alive will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord
Only those who survived Roman persecution will participate in the resurrection
qs.e: Paul reassured believers that at the Lord's coming, the dead in Christ will rise first, followed by living believers caught up together.

qs.q: What was the main topic discussed by Jesus with Nicodemus when Nicodemus came to him by night?
o: The architectural layout of the second Temple in Jerusalem
The political steps required to overthrow Pontius Pilate
Unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God
The exact financial budget required for synagogal administration
qs.e: Jesus told Nicodemus that no one can see or enter the kingdom of God unless they are born again of water and the Spirit.

qs.q: What took place when Jesus cleansed the Temple in Jerusalem during Passover?
o: He burned down the outer courtyard to rebuild it with marble
He appointed Roman soldiers to guard the inner sanctuary altars
He drove out those who sold animals, overturned the tables of money changers, and called it a house of prayer
He permitted international currency trade inside the Holy of Holies
qs.e: Jesus made a whip of cords, drove out sellers and sheep, overturned money changers' tables, and declared His Father's house a house of prayer.

qs.q: Which king of Persia issued the second decree reconfirming Cyrus' decree to complete the Temple construction under Haggai and Zechariah?
qs.e: King Darius searched the royal archives, located Cyrus' original decree, and ordered local officials to fund and complete the Temple.

qs.q: What symbolic vision did Jeremiah see regarding an almond branch and a boiling pot facing away from the north?
o: The almond branch symbolized the house of David, and the pot symbolized Egyptian trade
The almond branch represented a fertile harvest, and the pot represented endless peace
The almond branch showed God watching over His word, and the boiling pot represented disaster pouring from the north
The almond branch represented the Levites, and the pot represented the altar sacrifices
qs.e: God showed Jeremiah an almond rod (watching) and a boiling pot tilting from the north, signifying coming invasion from Babylon.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the divine chariot, what four faces were on each of the four living creatures?
o: The face of a king, a priest, a warrior, and a prophet
The face of a horse, a leopard, a bear, and a dragon
The face of a man, a lion, an ox, and an eagle
The face of a dove, a ram, a goat, and a fish
qs.e: Ezekiel recorded that each creature had four faces: the face of a human, a lion on the right, an ox on the left, and an eagle.

qs.q: Which minor prophet proclaimed that God would restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem and gather all nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat?
qs.e: Joel prophesied that God would gather all nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment while restoring his covenant people.

qs.q: Which minor prophet delivered a severe message of doom exclusively against the ancient nation of Edom for their violence against Jacob?
qs.e: Obadiah's single-chapter vision pronounced divine destruction upon Edom for standing aloof and gloating when Judah was destroyed.

qs.q: What primary theme is presented in the book of Proverbs regarding financial integrity and wealth?
o: Charging exorbitant interest on loans to widows is commendable
Wealth acquired through deceit grants permanent spiritual security
Poverty is proof of divine malediction in every circumstance
Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice
qs.e: Proverbs repeatedly highlights that honest modest gains with righteousness are far better than great riches gained unrighteously.

qs.q: In the book of Job, what was Elihu's unique perspective regarding why God allows suffering?
o: Suffering is caused exclusively by human ancestral curses
Suffering is always proof of secret unrepented wicked deeds
God is indifferent to human suffering and does not intervene
God uses suffering to discipline, instruct, and refine humans to turn them back from pride and the pit
qs.e: Elihu argued that God speaks through dreams and suffering to discipline people, rescue them from pride, and redeem their lives.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, how does the Holy Spirit assist believers during prayer?
o: The Spirit limits intercession to ordained apostles only
The Spirit provides written litanies to recite in synagogue services
The Spirit eliminates the need for personal prayer entirely
The Spirit helps us in our weakness, interceding for us with wordless groans according to God's will
qs.e: Paul wrote that we do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Galatians, what warning does he give regarding spiritual sowing and reaping?
o: Physical financial investments guarantee eternal spiritual salvation
Sowing evil produces spiritual rewards if one belongs to the church
Reaping depends entirely on human astrological signs
Do not be deceived: God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows
qs.e: Paul warned that whoever sows to please their flesh reaps destruction, but whoever sows to please the Spirit reaps eternal life.

qs.q: What took place during the walk to Emmaus when Jesus appeared to two disciples after his resurrection?
o: He commanded them to move permanently to Galilee
He revealed Himself immediately as a political leader who would conquer Rome
He vanished before speaking a single word to them
He explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself, and was recognized in the breaking of bread
qs.e: Jesus walked with them, interpreted the Scriptures regarding Messiah's suffering and glory, and was recognized when He broke bread.

qs.q: What testimony did John the Baptist give when he saw Jesus coming toward him at the Jordan River?
o: Behold, a priest from the tribe of Levi!
Behold, the king who will overthrow Caesar!
Behold, a prophet greater than Moses who will rebuild Jerusalem!
Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
qs.e: John the Baptist declared Jesus to be the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, testifying to His divine identity.

qs.q: What spiritual revival took place under Ezra when the Book of the Law was read aloud from morning until midday?
o: The Levites refused to translate the Hebrew text into Aramaic
The citizens rejected the law and returned to Babylonian exile
The Persian governor suspended all religious gatherings in Jerusalem
The people wept, repented, confessed their sins, and celebrated the Feast of Booths with great joy
qs.e: When Ezra read the Law, the Levites explained it, the people repented, confessed sin, and joyfully celebrated the Feast of Booths.

qs.q: Which king of Judah was struck with leprosy by God after arrogantly entering the Temple to burn incense on the altar?
qs.e: King Uzziah became proud and entered the sanctuary to burn incense—a duty reserved for priests—and was struck with leprosy.

qs.q: In the book of Hosea, what is the meaning of the name Jezreel given to Hosea's firstborn son?
o: The priests of Bethel will be exalted above Aaron
God will rebuild the walls of Samaria with gold
The house of David will rule over Assyria
God will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel and bring an end to the kingdom of Israel
qs.e: God named the boy Jezreel to signify coming judgment on the dynasty of Jehu for the violent massacres committed at Jezreel.

qs.q: Which major prophet was cast into a muddy cistern by royal officials during the siege of Jerusalem for preaching submission to Babylon?
qs.e: Jeremiah was thrown into the muddy cistern of Malkijah where he sank in the mire, until Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian rescued him.

qs.q: In Paul's second letter to the Corinthians, what thorn in the flesh did Paul plead with the Lord three times to remove?
o: A legal warrant issued against him by the Roman Senate
A severe financial debt owed to the Philippian church
A physical blindness that prevented him from traveling by ship
A messenger of Satan to torment him, to keep him from becoming conceited; the Lord replied, 'My grace is sufficient for you'
qs.e: Paul spoke of his thorn in the flesh, revealing God's response: 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.'

qs.q: Which Old Testament king brought back the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem with dancing, shouting, and sounding of trumpets?
qs.e: David brought up the Ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David with great rejoicing and dancing before the Lord.

qs.q: What sign did Judas use to betray Jesus to the soldiers sent by the chief priests?
o: He greeted Jesus with a kiss
He pointed at Jesus with a wooden staff
He handed Jesus a lamp in the dark
He called out Jesus' full title loudly
qs.e: Judas told the armed guards that the man he kissed was Jesus, using the friendly greeting as a signal for arrest.

qs.q: What was the name of the place outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified?
qs.e: Jesus was led out to Golgotha, which means the Place of the Skull, where he was crucified between two criminals.

qs.q: Who was the high priest when Jesus was interrogated before the Sanhedrin?
qs.e: Caiaphas was the high priest who questioned Jesus and tore his robes when Jesus affirmed his identity as Messiah.

qs.q: What food did God send from heaven to feed the Israelites in the wilderness every morning?
qs.e: God rained down manna from heaven every morning to sustain the Israelites during their wilderness journey.

qs.q: Who was the younger brother of Esau who obtained Isaac's blessing through Rebekah's plan?
qs.e: Jacob, with his mother Rebekah's guidance, covered his hands with goatskins to receive Isaac's patriarchal blessing.

qs.q: Which prophet anointed both Saul and David as kings over Israel?
qs.e: Samuel was the prophet and judge whom God instructed to anoint Saul first, and later David at Bethlehem.

qs.q: What was the outcome of Solomon's judgment between the two mothers claiming the same baby?
o: The real mother revealed herself by pleading for the baby's life rather than letting it be divided
Both mothers agreed to divide the living child in half
Solomon gave the baby to the local priest to raise
Solomon banished both women from Jerusalem
qs.e: When Solomon ordered the child cut in two, the true mother's compassion overflowed and she begged to give the baby to the other woman.

qs.q: Which queen of Israel introduced Phoenician Baal worship and arranged Naboth's execution?
qs.e: Jezebel manipulated royal seals and hired scoundrels to falsely accuse Naboth, securing his vineyard for King Ahab.

qs.q: Which major prophet was told that God knew him before he was formed in his mother's womb?
qs.e: God called Jeremiah before his birth, commissioning him as a prophet to the nations despite his youth.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the valley, what brought life back to the dry bones?
o: The breath of the Spirit entering them when the prophet prophesied to the wind
A great rainstorm washing over the valley floor
The priests placing holy oil on the skeletal frames
An army of angels touching each bone with golden rods
qs.e: When Ezekiel prophesied to the breath, spirit entered the dry bones and they came to life, standing up as a vast army.

qs.q: Which minor prophet was commanded by God to marry Gomer as a symbol of divine love?
qs.e: Hosea's marriage to Gomer illustrated God's unshakeable love for Israel despite their persistent spiritual unfaithfulness.

qs.q: What central message did Amos proclaim to the wealthy rulers in Samaria?
o: Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream
Increase animal sacrifices at Bethel to guarantee military prosperity
Build stone defense towers along the Syrian frontier
Form economic trade treaties with Egypt and Assyria
qs.e: Amos condemned empty religious performance while trampling the poor, declaring that God demands justice and righteousness.

qs.q: What does Proverbs state regarding a person who trusts in their own heart?
o: He who trusts in his own heart is a fool, but he who walks wisely will be delivered
He who trusts in his own heart will rule over many cities
He who trusts in his own heart never experiences error
He who trusts in his own heart is superior to all teachers
qs.e: Proverbs cautions that relying solely on self-confidence without divine guidance is foolishness.

qs.q: What observation does Ecclesiastes make regarding human toil under the sun?
o: Hard labor guarantees permanent earthly happiness and peace
All is vanity and a striving after wind, apart from fearing God
Physical wealth preserves a person from physical death
Wisdom removes all mystery from daily human life
qs.e: Ecclesiastes reflects that worldly achievements without reference to God are temporary vanity and chasing after wind.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Galatians, how does a person become a true child of Abraham?
o: By strictly observing the dietary laws of the Torah
Through faith in Jesus Christ, regardless of circumcision or ethnicity
By proving physical descent from the tribe of Judah
By residing in the geographical territory of Canaan
qs.e: Paul explained that those who have faith are children of Abraham, inheriting the covenant promise through Christ.

qs.q: In First Corinthians chapter twelve, how does Paul describe spiritual gifts given to believers?
o: Gifts given exclusively to Apostles for personal prestige
Different gifts given by the same Spirit for the common good of the entire church body
Gifts meant to rank believers into spiritual social classes
Gifts that replace the need for love and humility
qs.e: Paul taught that there are varieties of gifts but the same Spirit, distributed to each individual for the building up of the church.

qs.q: Why were seven men of honest report chosen by the early church in Acts chapter six?
o: To serve as armed guards for the apostles during trials
To oversee the daily distribution of food to widows so apostles could focus on prayer and word
To collect taxes for the Roman imperial treasury
To record historical records of early church sermons
qs.e: The seven deacons were appointed to administer food care fairly to Hellenistic widows without disrupting apostolic ministry.

qs.q: In what city did Paul deliver his address at the Areopagus regarding the Unknown God?
qs.e: Paul spoke at the Areopagus in Athens, engaging Greek philosophers by referencing an altar dedicated to an Unknown God.

qs.q: What key task was assigned to Zerubbabel upon the initial return of Jewish exiles from Babylon?
o: To establish a new naval fleet on the Mediterranean Sea
To rebuild the altar of God and lay the foundation of the second Temple
To rewrite the administrative codes of Persia
qs.e: Zerubbabel led the first returnees in rebuilding the altar and laying the foundation for the Temple in Jerusalem.

qs.q: How did Stephen pray for those stoning him at his execution?
o: May justice strike down these accusers immediately
Lord, do not hold this sin against them
Remember my good deeds and punish this council
I appeal to the Roman governor for vindication
qs.e: Following the example of Jesus, Stephen knelt down and prayed that God would not charge his killers with the sin.

qs.q: What happened when Peter visited the home of Cornelius in Caesarea to preach the gospel?
o: Cornelius refused to listen and had Peter arrested by Roman soldiers
The Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the word, and they spoke in tongues and praised God
Peter required all male household members to be circumcised first
An earthquake shook the house and destroyed the outer wall
qs.e: While Peter was speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon the Gentile listeners, convincing Jewish believers that God accepted Gentiles.

qs.q: What call did Paul receive in a night vision that led him to cross into Europe?
o: An angel showing him a vision of the Roman Senate
A man of Macedonia standing and pleading, Come over to Macedonia and help us
A prophet from Jerusalem handing him a broken staff
A voice commanding him to return immediately to Tarsus
qs.e: The Macedonian vision prompted Paul and his team to travel across the Aegean Sea to preach in Philippi and Europe.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Romans, how is justification described in relation to works?
o: Justification is earned by accumulating meritorious deeds over a lifetime
A person is justified by faith apart from the works of the law
Justification requires physical lineage from Aaron's priestly line
Justification is awarded only to civil rulers who keep peace
qs.e: Paul argued in Romans that salvation is a free gift received by faith in Christ, not earned through legalistic works.

qs.q: According to Second Corinthians chapter five, what new identity does a person receive in Christ?
o: A person receives immunity from physical sickness and earthly trial
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away, behold, the new has come
A person becomes a temporal monarch over civil nations
A person is freed from obeying any civil laws or paying taxes
qs.e: Paul affirmed that in Christ a believer is transformed into a new creation with a renewed spirit and ministry.

qs.q: What choice was given to the crowd by Pilate during the trial of Jesus?
o: To crown Jesus king or exile him to Rome
To release either Jesus or Barabbas the murderer
To rebuild the Temple or pay a Roman tribute fine
To release Peter or release Caiaphas
qs.e: Pilate offered to release one prisoner for Passover, and the crowd chose Barabbas over Jesus.

qs.q: What sign occurred in the Jerusalem Temple at the exact moment Jesus died on the cross?
o: The Ark of the Covenant vanished from the sanctuary
The golden altar was split into three equal parts
The curtain of the Temple was torn in two from top to bottom
The outer court walls collapsed completely into the valley
qs.e: The tearing of the Temple curtain signified that access to God's holy presence was opened to all through Jesus' death.

qs.q: Who was the Persian monarch who authorized Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem's walls?
qs.e: King Artaxerxes granted Nehemiah official permission, letters of passage, and timber to restore Jerusalem.

qs.q: What covenant commitment did the exiles make under Ezra and Nehemiah regarding intermarriage?
o: They required foreign spouses to pay an annual tax to the Temple
They encouraged intermarriage to expand commercial trade networks
They agreed to put away foreign pagan wives and walk faithfully in God's Law
They abolished all family records across the twelve tribes
qs.e: The community repented of foreign idolatrous intermarriages to protect the spiritual purity of God's covenant people.

qs.q: Why did Jeroboam place golden calves at Bethel and Dan?
o: To honor Egyptian gods who helped him escape Pharaoh
To fulfill a prophecy given by Samuel to his father
To keep the northern Israelites from traveling to Jerusalem to worship in Judah
To replace animal sacrifices with incense offerings
qs.e: Jeroboam feared his subjects would return allegiance to the house of David if they kept worshiping in Jerusalem.

qs.q: What prophecy was spoken against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel by the man of God from Judah?
o: Fire from heaven would turn the gold into liquid silver
The altar would be carried off to Nineveh by Assyrian soldiers
A son named Josiah would be born to David's house and burn human bones upon the altar
The altar would remain the holy sanctuary of Israel forever
qs.e: The prophet predicted that a Davidic king named Josiah would defile Jeroboam's idolatrous altar centuries later.

qs.q: What request did Elisha make of Elijah before Elijah was taken up into heaven?
o: Protect me from the persecution of Jezebel
Grant me your golden cloak and silver staff
Let a double portion of your spirit be upon me
Make me chief prophet over the court of Samaria
qs.e: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's prophetic spirit, which was granted when he saw Elijah ascending.

qs.q: What miracle occurred when a dead body was thrown into Elisha's burial cave?
o: The body turned into pure white marble
The burial cave filled with heavenly light and music
As soon as the body touched Elisha's bones, the man revived and stood on his feet
The tomb door sealed itself permanently
qs.e: Even after death, God demonstrated power through Elisha's remains as the dead man returned to life upon contact.

qs.q: Which major prophet was commanded to go down to the potter's house to observe clay being molded?
qs.e: Jeremiah watched the potter rework spoiled clay, illustrating God's power to shape and reform nations.

qs.q: What principal blessing does Paul highlight in his letter to the Ephesians regarding spiritual inheritance in Christ?
o: Believers are exempt from physical death and earthly labor
Believers receive guaranteed political appointments in Rome
Believers are blessed with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ
Believers receive material gold mines in Asia Minor
qs.e: Paul praised God who blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.

qs.q: What does the title Immanuel mean in Isaiah's prophecy regarding the child born of a virgin?
qs.e: Immanuel translates directly as 'God with us', signifying divine presence among His people.

qs.q: What did Ezekiel's eating of the scroll taste like in his mouth?
qs.e: Ezekiel recorded that when he ate the scroll of God's words, it tasted sweet as honey in his mouth.

qs.q: Which minor prophet declared that God requires steadfast love rather than sacrifice?
qs.e: Hosea proclaimed that God desires heart love and true knowledge of Himself over mere ritual sacrifices.

qs.q: In Micah chapter six, what three things does the Lord require of human beings?
o: To conquer neighboring cities, build altars, and rule harshly
To offer animal sacrifices, fast weekly, and pay tithes
To do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with God
To live in desert isolation, wear sackcloth, and avoid people
qs.e: Micah summarized true religion: doing justice, loving mercy/kindness, and walking humbly with God.

qs.q: What key lesson does Proverbs teach regarding the power of the tongue?
o: Flattery is the best method to gain true friendship
Words have no impact on moral character or human destiny
Silent people are always lacking in understanding
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit
qs.e: Proverbs warns that speech carries life-or-death power, urging self-control and truthful words.

qs.q: How did Job respond after seven days of silent grief with his three friends?
o: He cursed his friends and ordered them to leave
He immediately renounced God and left the land of Uz
He demanded money from his friends to rebuild his herds
He opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth while maintaining his innocence before God
qs.e: Job gave voice to intense grief by cursing his birth day, yet he did not blaspheme or abandon God.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, what did Christ accomplish regarding the Law?
o: Christ made animal sacrifices compulsory for all nations
Christ abolished all moral boundaries and self-discipline
Christ required all Gentiles to move to Judea
Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes
qs.e: Paul taught that Christ fulfilled the Law, providing righteousness by faith to all who believe.

qs.q: In Ephesians chapter six, what piece of armor represents God's word?
qs.e: Paul identified the sword of the Spirit as the word of God, the primary offensive weapon against spiritual deception.

qs.q: How did Jesus reveal himself to Mary Magdalene near the tomb on resurrection morning?
o: He spoke to her from a cloud above Mount Olivet
He appeared as a shining angel with golden wings
He wrote her name on a stone near the garden tomb
He called her by name, Mary, and she recognized him, saying Rabboni!
qs.e: Mary recognized Jesus when he spoke her name, responding in joyful recognition.

qs.q: Why did the chief priests refuse to put Judas' return money into the Temple treasury?
o: Because the silver was damaged and unfit for temple use
Because the coins were struck by Roman authorities
Because Judas had touched the coins with unwashed hands
Because it was blood money, so they bought the Potter's Field for burying strangers
qs.e: The priests deemed silver paid for betrayal as blood money, purchasing a burial ground for foreigners.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah respond when opposition leaders tried to intimidate him into fleeing to the Temple?
o: He paid a bribe to Sanballat to end the conflict
He immediately fled into the sanctuary and locked the inner doors
He resigned his position and returned to Susa
Should a man such as I run away? I will not go in to save my life!
qs.e: Nehemiah refused to show cowardice or violate Temple rules, discerning that the invitation was a trap.

qs.q: Which major prophet experienced the vision of the divine chariot-throne with wheels full of eyes?
qs.e: Ezekiel described complex wheels within wheels full of eyes accompanying God's mobile glory.

qs.q: What does the symbolic name Lo-Ammi mean in the book of Hosea?
o: House of bread, predicting a season of abundance
God is merciful, promising immediate military conquest
City of joy, foretelling Jerusalem's economic growth
Not my people, showing Israel's broken covenant status due to idolatry
qs.e: Lo-Ammi translates to 'not my people', warning Israel of covenant rupture if unfaithfulness continued.

qs.q: In Philippians chapter two, what example of humility is set before believers?
o: Peter gave up his fishing boats to move to Rome
Solomon surrendered his wealth to neighboring kings
Moses refused to lead Israel out of Midian
Christ emptied himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient unto death on a cross
qs.e: Paul held up Jesus' self-emptying and supreme obedience as the ultimate model of Christian humility.

qs.q: During whose reign was the Book of the Law found in the Temple by Hilkiah?
qs.e: The discovery of the Law during Josiah's Temple restoration sparked sweeping national reforms.

qs.q: Which judge made a vow that resulted in devoting his daughter after victory over Ammon?
qs.e: Jephthah's rash vow before battle led to sacrificing his only daughter upon returning home.

qs.q: What does the seed sown on rocky ground represent in the parable of the Sower?
o: Those who receive the word with joy but fall away when trouble or persecution arises
Those who reject the word outright with anger
Those whose faith produces a hundredfold yield
Those who use wealth to buy church offices
qs.e: Rocky ground represents shallow soil where roots cannot grow deep, so initial joy vanishes under persecution.

qs.q: How many men were fed by Jesus using five loaves and two fish?
o: Five thousand men besides women and children
qs.e: The miracle of multiplying five loaves and two fish satisfied five thousand men plus women and children.

qs.q: Who was the mother of Samuel who brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh?
qs.e: Hannah fulfilled her vow by bringing young Samuel to Eli at Shiloh to serve the Lord for life.

qs.q: Which judge delivered Israel from Moabite oppression by using a double-edged dagger against King Eglon?
qs.e: Ehud the Benjamite used a concealed dagger to slay Eglon king of Moab, freeing Israel from bondage.

qs.q: What did Jesus teach about loving one's enemies in the Sermon on the Mount?
o: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you
An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth is the supreme rule
Hate your enemies and destroy their possessions
Avoid enemies by moving to another country
qs.e: Jesus commanded his followers to love their enemies and pray for persecutors, reflecting God's love.

qs.q: Who was the governor of Judea who authorized the execution of Jesus under pressure from the chief priests?
qs.e: Pontius Pilate surrendered to public pressure and sentenced Jesus to be crucified despite finding no crime in him.

qs.q: Where was Saul traveling when a heavenly light flashed around him and Jesus spoke to him?
qs.e: Saul was near Damascus on his persecuting mission when he encountered the resurrected Jesus.

qs.q: What charge was brought against Stephen by false witnesses before the high priest?
o: Speaking blasphemous words against the holy place and the Law
Stealing vessels from the Temple treasury
Refusing to pay taxes to Caesar
qs.e: Stephen was falsely accused of speaking against the Temple and the Law of Moses.

qs.q: Who was sent by God to lay hands on Saul in Damascus so he could regain his sight?
qs.e: Ananias obeyed God's direction, visited Saul on Straight Street, and restored his sight.

qs.q: What led Cornelius to send men to Joppa to invite Peter to his house?
o: An angel of God appeared to him in a vision instructing him to send for Peter
A letter from the Roman governor in Jerusalem
A commercial trade agreement between Joppa and Caesarea
A request from local Jewish elders
qs.e: An angel assured Cornelius that his prayers were heard and instructed him to call Peter from Joppa.

qs.q: What judgment befell Herod Agrippa I when he failed to give praise to God at Caesarea?
o: An angel of the Lord struck him down and he was eaten by worms
He was deposed by the Roman Emperor
He lost his speech for seven years
His army was defeated by Syria
qs.e: Herod accepted divine honors from the crowd, so an angel struck him down and he died.

qs.q: What happened while Paul and Silas were singing hymns in the Philippian prison at midnight?
o: A violent earthquake opened prison doors and unfastened all chains
The Roman governor sent a messenger releasing them
The jailer joined them in singing without incident
An angel flew them out through the prison window
qs.e: God sent an earthquake that opened prison doors, leading to the conversion of the Philippian jailer.

qs.q: How does Paul explain salvation in his letter to the Romans chapter ten?
o: Salvation requires complete perfection in keeping all ceremonial laws
If you confess with your mouth Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him, you will be saved
Salvation is reserved exclusively for native citizens of Israel
Salvation is achieved by military service for the empire
qs.e: Paul declared that vocal confession of Jesus' lordship and heart belief in his resurrection brings salvation.

qs.q: What feature of love is emphasized in First Corinthians chapter thirteen?
o: Love seeks its own advantage in every negotiation
Love never fails, and it is greater than faith and hope
Love demands immediate public retribution for wrongs
Love is valid only when accompanied by material gifts
qs.e: Paul concluded that love endures forever and is the greatest virtue among faith, hope, and love.

qs.q: Which patriarch was willing to sacrifice his son Isaac on Mount Moriah?
qs.e: Abraham demonstrated faith by offering Isaac, stopping only when God provided a ram caught in a thicket.

qs.q: What was Joseph's interpretation of Pharaoh's dreams of seven fat and seven lean cows?
o: Seven years of war followed by seven years of peace
Seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine
Seven royal sons followed by seven daughters
Seven plagues on the Nile followed by prosperity
qs.e: Joseph explained that Egypt would experience seven prosperous years followed by seven severe famine years.

qs.q: What event during Passover caused Pharaoh to finally demand that Israel leave Egypt?
o: The turning of the Nile into blood
The death of the firstborn in every Egyptian home
The plague of dark clouds across the land
The destruction of Egyptian crops by locusts
qs.e: The fatal plague on Egyptian firstborn sons forced Pharaoh to release the Israelites.

qs.q: Which judge defeated a vast Midianite army using only three hundred men armed with trumpets and torches?
qs.e: Gideon's small force of three hundred routed the Midianite camp using trumpets, smashed jars, and burning torches.

qs.q: Why was Saul rejected as king over Israel by the Lord?
o: Because he refused to pay taxes to Samuel
Because he disobeyed God's command regarding Amalek by sparing King Agag and livestock
Because he moved the sanctuary from Shiloh to Hebron
Because he lost the Ark of the Covenant to the Philistines
qs.e: Saul's selective obedience and failure to destroy all Amalekite property led to his rejection as king.

qs.q: What was the outcry of the northern tribes when Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders?
o: We pledge total loyalty to Rehoboam forever
What share do we have in David? To your tents, O Israel!
Let us make Jerusalem a neutral city
We demand that Egypt rule over Judah
qs.e: The ten northern tribes rejected Davidic leadership, declaring independence under Jeroboam.

qs.q: What idolatrous centers did Jeroboam establish in the northern kingdom to prevent worship in Jerusalem?
o: Baal temples at Samaria and Jezreel
Golden calf altars at Dan and Bethel
Stone pillars at Shiloh and Shechem
Bronze serpents at Gilgal and Jericho
qs.e: Jeroboam set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel to stop Israelites from traveling south to Jerusalem.

qs.q: How did God supply food to the widow of Zarephath through Elijah during the famine?
o: Ravens brought bread and meat to her doorstep daily
Her jar of flour was not used up and her jug of oil did not run dry
Elijah gave her gold coins to purchase food in Sidon
Manna fell inside her house every morning
qs.e: God miraculously multiplied the widow's flour and oil throughout the severe drought.

qs.q: What prophecy did Elijah give concerning Jezebel's death after Naboth's murder?
o: Jezebel will die peacefully in her royal palace
Dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel
Jezebel will be taken into exile in Babylon
Jezebel will drown in the Mediterranean Sea
qs.e: Elijah foretold that Jezebel would suffer a violent death and be devoured by dogs in Jezreel.

qs.q: What was Isaiah's response when he heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send?
o: I am too young to speak
Wait until I finish my work in Jerusalem
qs.e: After his lips were cleansed with an altar coal, Isaiah eagerly volunteered for divine service.

qs.q: What lesson was signified when Jeremiah smashed the potter's earthenware flask at Ben-Hinnom?
o: The Babylonian army would collapse within three days
God would break Jerusalem and its people beyond repair for their sins
The Levites would receive new golden vessels
The walls of Jerusalem would expand outward
qs.e: Breaking the clay flask symbolized irreversible destruction coming upon Jerusalem for persistent idolatry.

qs.q: Which minor prophet used a severe locust plague to warn of the coming Day of the Lord?
qs.e: Joel saw the swarming locust invasion as a sign of God's impending judgment, calling for heartfelt repentance.

qs.q: What declaration did Habakkuk make regarding the righteous living in troublesome times?
o: The righteous shall live by forming military alliances
The righteous shall live by accumulating gold
The righteous shall live by his faith
The righteous shall live by escaping into desert caves
qs.e: Habakkuk stated that while the proud fail, the righteous will endure by remaining faithful to God.

qs.q: In Proverbs, how is the path of the righteous described in comparison to the path of the wicked?
o: The wicked path is always filled with permanent joy
Both paths lead to the same identical outcome
The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn shining brighter, while the wicked stumble in darkness
The righteous path guarantees physical worldly fame
qs.e: Proverbs contrasts the growing light of the righteous path with the dangerous darkness of wicked living.

qs.q: What was Job's reply when his wife told him to curse God and die?
o: Let us leave the land of Uz immediately
I will curse God as you suggest
Shall we accept good from God and not accept trouble?
I will demand compensation from my friends
qs.e: Job maintained integrity, asking if humanity should receive only blessings from God without accepting hardship.

qs.q: How does Paul describe Christ in Colossians chapter one?
o: He is a minor regional teacher in Judea
He is an angelic messenger created during the Exodus
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation, and head of the church
He is a temporal king who rules by physical sword
qs.e: Paul exalted Christ as supreme over all creation and sovereign head of the church body.

qs.q: What encouragement does Paul give in First Thessalonians regarding believers who have died?
o: Physical death permanently ends all spiritual hope
Deceased believers lose all inheritance in the kingdom
At the Lord's coming, the dead in Christ will rise first, then living believers will be caught up together
Only apostles will be resurrected at the final trumpet
qs.e: Paul comforted Thessalonian Christians with the assurance of resurrection for all who die in Christ.

qs.q: What did Jesus explain to Nicodemus regarding entering the kingdom of God?
o: Only high priests and Pharisee elders can enter
Entrance requires paying tax to the Jerusalem sanctuary
No one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit
Entrance is based on physical strength and ancestry
qs.e: Jesus revealed that spiritual rebirth through water and the Holy Spirit is essential for entering God's kingdom.

qs.q: What action did Jesus take when he found money changers and sellers in the Temple?
o: He joined them in trading currency for Passover
He collected a portion of their profits for the poor
He drove them out, overturned their tables, and declared it a house of prayer
He praised them for providing convenience to travelers
qs.e: Jesus cleansed the Temple outer court, condemning commercial exploitation of God's house of prayer.

qs.q: Which Persian ruler authorized the search of royal archives that allowed Temple rebuilding to resume?
qs.e: Darius confirmed Cyrus' original decree, ordering local officials to assist the Jews in completing the Temple.

qs.q: What was signified by the boiling pot tilting away from the north in Jeremiah's vision?
o: A peace treaty signed with northern Syria
Abundant rain coming from northern mountains
Disaster tilting from the north against all who live in the land
The return of lost Israelite tribes from captivity
qs.e: The boiling pot represented Babylonian armies pouring out judgment against Judah from the north.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision by the Chebar canal, what were the four faces on each creature?
qs.e: Each living creature had four distinct faces symbolizing God's sovereign creation.

qs.q: Which minor prophet spoke of all nations gathered for judgment in the Valley of Jehoshaphat?
qs.e: Joel prophesied divine judgment upon hostile surrounding nations in the Valley of Jehoshaphat.

qs.q: Which minor prophet wrote a single-chapter book pronouncing total doom on Edom for pride and violence against Judah?
qs.e: Obadiah's prophecy focuses exclusively on judgment against Edom for taking pleasure in Judah's fall.

qs.q: What principle does Proverbs teach regarding honest wealth versus unjust gain?
o: Poverty is proof of criminal behavior in every person
Deceitful wealth grants long-term peace to families
Honest gain is inferior to quick speculative riches
Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice
qs.e: Proverbs emphasizes that moral integrity with modest income is far better than unrighteous wealth.

qs.q: What was Elihu's argument in Job regarding why God sends hardship?
o: Hardship is caused exclusively by human planetary alignment
Hardship is always proof that a person committed murder in secret
God has no knowledge or interest in human pain
God uses suffering to instruct, correct, and save humans from pride and destruction
qs.e: Elihu presented suffering as a redemptive discipline used by God to rescue human souls from ruin.

qs.q: How does Paul describe the Holy Spirit's role in Christian prayer in Romans chapter eight?
o: The Spirit restricts intercession to ordained ministers
The Spirit provides set written litanies for daily recitation
The Spirit eliminates the need for human prayer completely
The Spirit intercedes for believers with groanings too deep for words according to God's will
qs.e: Paul taught that the Holy Spirit helps our weakness and intercedes in harmony with God's will.

qs.q: What law of spiritual harvest is stated in Galatians chapter six?
o: Physical financial giving guarantees immediate worldly fame
Sowing wickedness brings spiritual rewards if one attends worship
Harvest depends entirely on political treaties
A man reaps whatever he sows; sowing to the Spirit brings eternal life
qs.e: Paul warned that actions have consequences: sowing to the flesh brings destruction, while sowing to the Spirit brings life.

qs.q: What did Jesus do during his appearance to disciples in the upper room after resurrection?
o: He ascended to heaven immediately without speaking
He commanded them to organize an army to capture Jerusalem
He condemned Thomas and cast him out of the company
He showed them his hands and feet, ate fish before them, and opened their minds to understand Scriptures
qs.e: Jesus proved his physical resurrection by showing wounds, eating food, and explaining fulfilled Scripture.

qs.q: What was John the Baptist's testimony when he saw Jesus approaching at the Jordan?
o: Behold, a priest from the tribe of Levi!
Behold, a king who will drive out Roman soldiers!
Behold, a builder who will expand Jerusalem's walls!
Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
qs.e: John identified Jesus as the sacrificial Lamb of God who removes human sin.

qs.q: How did the exiles respond when Ezra read the Book of the Law publicly in Jerusalem?
o: They demanded that Persian officers stop the reading
They refused to listen and returned to Babylon
They tore up the scroll and burned it in a brazier
They wept, repented, confessed their sins, and celebrated with great joy
qs.e: Reading the Law led to national repentance, covenant renewal, and joyful celebration of the Feast of Booths.

qs.q: Which king of Judah was struck with leprosy for usurping the priests' duty of burning incense in the Temple?
qs.e: King Uzziah's pride led him to perform priestly incense duties, resulting in immediate leprosy on his forehead.

qs.q: What was the prophetic significance of naming Hosea's son Jezreel?
o: Judah would surrender its territory to Edom
God would grant permanent military victory over Assyria
The temple in Samaria would be rebuilt with gold
God would avenge the bloodshed of Jezreel on the house of Jehu and end northern Israel's monarchy
qs.e: Jezreel's name foretold divine retribution on Jehu's line for violent massacres at Jezreel.

qs.q: Which prophet was thrown into a muddy cistern by princes during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem?
qs.e: Jeremiah was cast into Malkijah's mire-filled cistern for advocating surrender to Babylon, but was rescued by Ebed-Melech.

qs.q: What response did Paul receive when he prayed three times for his thorn in the flesh to be removed?
o: Your thorn is punishment for preaching to Gentiles
Your prayer is granted and you will never suffer again
You must travel to Jerusalem to receive healing from apostles
My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness
qs.e: God answered Paul that divine grace is sufficient, showing strength through human weakness.

qs.q: Which king danced with all his might before the Lord as the Ark of the Covenant entered Jerusalem?
qs.e: King David expressed exuberant worship, dancing before the Lord as the Ark entered Jerusalem.

qs.q: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, what reaction did the older brother have when the younger son was welcomed back with a celebration?
o: He became angry and refused to go in to join the celebration
He threw a larger party for his own personal friends
He left the farm permanently to move to Egypt
He paid the father's debts using his own inheritance
qs.e: The elder brother was resentful and complained that he had served faithfully without receiving a young goat to celebrate with friends.

qs.q: What was the name of the Pharisee member of the Sanhedrin who came to Jesus by night to inquire about his teachings?
qs.e: Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews, visited Jesus by night, acknowledging Him as a teacher come from God.

qs.q: Which apostle was a tax collector in Capernaum before being called by Jesus to follow him?
qs.e: Matthew was sitting at the tax collector's booth when Jesus called him to leave his booth and follow Him.

qs.q: Who was the mother of John the Baptist and cousin of Mary the mother of Jesus?
qs.e: Elizabeth, wife of Zechariah, was advanced in years when she miraculously conceived John the Baptist.

qs.q: What sign did God give to Noah that He would never again destroy all flesh with a global flood?
o: A rainbow set in the clouds
A golden altar built on Mount Ararat
A pillar of fire standing in the ocean
A voice speaking from a whirlwind every year
qs.e: The rainbow in the clouds was instituted as the perpetual sign of God's covenant with Noah and all creation.

qs.q: Which son of Jacob was sold into slavery by his brothers for twenty pieces of silver?
qs.e: Joseph's jealous brothers sold him to Midianite/Ishmaelites merchants who carried him down to Egypt.

qs.q: What sea did the Israelites cross on dry ground when Moses stretched out his staff over the waters?
qs.e: Moses stretched out his hand, God drove back the sea with a strong east wind, and Israel walked through on dry land.

qs.q: What was the name of the female judge who rendered decisions under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel?
qs.e: Deborah the prophetess held court under the Palm of Deborah, leading Israel alongside Barak against Canaanite forces.

qs.q: Who was the giant Philistine warrior from Gath defeated by young David with a sling?
qs.e: Goliath mocked Israel's armies until David struck him in the forehead with a sling stone.

qs.q: Which king of Israel built the city of Samaria on a hill bought from Shemer?
qs.e: Omri purchased the hill of Samaria and fortified it, establishing Samaria as Israel's northern capital.

qs.q: What dramatic event took place on Mount Carmel when Elijah confronted 450 prophets of Baal?
o: Fire fell from heaven and consumed Elijah's sacrifice, wood, stones, and water in the trench
An earthquake swallowed the prophets of Baal and their altars
A heavy rainstorm extinguished all altars on the mountain before prayer
King Ahab repented immediately and destroyed Samaria's idols
qs.e: God answered Elijah's prayer with fire from heaven, demonstrating that the Lord alone is God.

qs.q: Which major prophet was commanded by God to marry an adulterous woman named Gomer?
qs.e: Hosea's marriage to unfaithful Gomer depicted God's redeeming love toward idolatrous Israel.

qs.q: What call vision did Isaiah receive in the Temple during the year King Uzziah died?
o: He saw the Lord sitting on a high throne with seraphim crying, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts
He saw a valley filled with dry bones coming together
He saw four living creatures holding golden trumpets
He saw a linen loincloth hidden near a river rock
qs.e: Isaiah saw God's throne in glory and was cleansed by a live coal before accepting his prophetic mission.

qs.q: Which minor prophet delivered a message of severe judgment against social injustice in Samaria while working as a shepherd?
qs.e: Amos, a herdsman from Tekoa, rebuked Samaria's wealthy elite for trampling upon the poor.

qs.q: What key concept is taught in the book of Proverbs regarding the acquisition of wealth?
o: Accumulating wealth by any means brings divine favor
Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death
Poverty is required of all who seek wisdom
Financial investments should be placed only in foreign trade
qs.e: Proverbs emphasizes that moral integrity and honest gain outweigh dishonest riches.

qs.q: In the book of Ecclesiastes, what is described as the sum of human wisdom after evaluating life under the sun?
o: Pursue worldly fame and intellectual accolades above all else
Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man
Isolate oneself from society to avoid all earthly trouble
Rely on physical strength to dominate daily events
qs.e: Ecclesiastes concludes that reverent obedience to God is humanity's ultimate purpose and duty.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Galatians, what is the primary purpose of faith in Christ regarding salvation?
o: Faith requires physical descent from the twelve tribes of Israel
Faith justifies a person freely by grace, making circumcision and legalistic works unnecessary for salvation
Faith serves as an addition to strict ceremonial observance of the Torah
Faith grants temporal political immunity from Roman tax laws
qs.e: Paul insisted that justification comes by faith in Jesus Christ, not by works of the Law.

qs.q: What analogy does Paul use in First Corinthians chapter twelve to describe the church community?
o: A army divided into competitive military platoons
One body with many diverse parts, each necessary for the healthy functioning of the whole
A business corporation managed by financial directors
A vineyard where lower branches are discarded without care
qs.e: Paul likened the church to a human body where every member exercises distinct gifts for mutual benefit.

qs.q: Who was the first Gentile convert to Christianity, along with his household, following Peter's sermon in Caesarea?
qs.e: Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion, received the Holy Spirit along with his family when Peter preached Christ.

qs.q: What defense did Stephen give before the Sanhedrin prior to his martyrdom?
o: He argued that Roman legal codes granted him total immunity from religious trial
He reviewed Israel's history, showing how their ancestors repeatedly resisted God's messengers and rejected the Righteous One
He offered to pay a fine to the high priest to dismiss the charges
He denied ever preaching about Jesus of Nazareth in Jerusalem
qs.e: Stephen outlined Israel's history from Abraham to Solomon, confronting the council for rejecting Christ.

qs.q: What took place when Philip preached the gospel in Samaria recorded in Acts chapter eight?
o: The Samaritan citizens drove Philip out of the city with stones
Unclean spirits came out with loud cries, many paralytics were healed, and there was great joy in the city
Simon the sorcerer was appointed as leader of the Samaritan church
The Roman garrison placed Samaria under martial law
qs.e: Philip's ministry in Samaria brought miraculous healings, deliverance, and widespread joy.

qs.q: How did Paul escape from Damascus when hostile plotters guarded the city gates day and night?
o: He disguised himself as a Roman officer and marched out at noon
Believers lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall at night
An angel made him invisible as he walked through the main gate
He paid a bribe to the governor appointed by King Aretas
qs.e: Paul's disciples lowered him in a large basket through a wall opening to bypass hostile watchers at the gates.

qs.q: What central declaration did Paul make in his Areopagus speech in Athens regarding God's relationship to humanity?
o: God resides inside idols crafted by skilled gold and silver artisans
God made from one man every nation of mankind and is not far from each one of us, for in Him we live and move and have our being
God requires animal sacrifices at Mount Zion before hearing Gentile prayers
God grants salvation only to those proficient in Greek philosophy
qs.e: Paul proclaimed God as Creator and Sustainer who calls all people everywhere to repent.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Romans, how is the believer's freedom from sin explained in chapter six?
o: Believers can continue in sin freely because grace will abound even more
Count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus, no longer letting sin reign in your mortal body
Freedom from sin is achieved through physical asceticism in desert caves
Sin is an illusion that has no real existence in human behavior
qs.e: Paul asserted that union with Christ in death and resurrection frees believers from sin's mastery.

qs.q: According to Second Corinthians chapter four, why do believers hold spiritual treasure in jars of clay?
o: Because physical earthly bodies are permanent and indestructible
To show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us
To hide spiritual truth from ordinary citizens in society
To prove that apostles possess greater physical endurance than others
qs.e: Paul noted that human weakness (jars of clay) highlights God's glorious power working within believers.

qs.q: What reaction did Pontius Pilate exhibit during the trial of Jesus when the chief priests pressed for a death sentence?
o: He converted to Christianity and resigned his governor post
He immediately ordered the arrest of Caiaphas for treason against Rome
He took water, washed his hands before the crowd, and declared himself innocent of Jesus' blood
He commanded his soldiers to disperse the crowd with swords
qs.e: Pilate washed his hands symbolically, releasing Barabbas and handing Jesus over to be crucified.

qs.q: What miraculous sign occurred at Golgotha when Jesus breathed his last on the cross?
o: The sun shone seven times brighter than normal across Judea
Fire descended from heaven and consumed the Roman garrison
The curtain of the Temple was torn in two, the earth quaked, and rocks split
The city walls of Jerusalem collapsed into the valley
qs.e: Darkness fell, the Temple curtain ripped from top to bottom, and an earthquake accompanied Jesus' death.

qs.q: Under whose supervision were the walls of Jerusalem rebuilt in fifty-two days despite threats from Sanballat?
qs.e: Nehemiah organized families to build sections of the wall while holding weapons to defend against enemies.

qs.q: What spiritual reform did Ezra lead upon arriving in Jerusalem from Babylon?
o: He abolished morning and evening sacrifices at the altar
He established a new monarchy by crowning a governor
He taught the Law of Moses publicly and called the people to repent of foreign pagan marriages
He forbade the translation of Hebrew Scriptures into Aramaic
qs.e: Ezra instructed the community in God's Law, restoring covenant fidelity and purity.

qs.q: What was the political cause of the rupture of the united kingdom of Israel under Rehoboam?
o: The Philistines captured the northern territories during a siege
Jeroboam invaded Jerusalem with an Egyptian army
Rehoboam rejected the moderate advice of the elders and threatened harsher taxation and forced labor
The Levites organized a revolt against Solomon's tax officers
qs.e: Rehoboam's harsh response to the people's petition caused ten northern tribes to secede under Jeroboam.

qs.q: What idolatrous worship did Jeroboam establish at Dan and Bethel, and why?
o: Sun pillars, to honor Egyptian pharaohs
Stone altars for Baal, to form an alliance with Phoenicia
Golden calves, to keep northern Israelites from traveling to Jerusalem to worship
Incense altars for Moloch, to secure military victory
qs.e: Jeroboam set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel to maintain political control over northern tribes.

qs.q: How did God answer Elijah's prayer on Mount Carmel during the contest with Baal's prophets?
o: An earthquake shook Mount Carmel and split the mountain peak
A massive rainstorm washed away the Baal prophets' altars before noon
Fire from heaven fell and consumed the burnt offering, wood, stones, soil, and water in the trench
Angels appeared and drove King Ahab away from the summit
qs.e: God sent fire from heaven consuming the entire altar, proving to Israel that the Lord is God.

qs.q: What miracle did Elisha perform for the Shunammite woman whose son died of a severe headache?
o: He instructed her to wash the child in the Pool of Siloam three times
He anointed the dead child's forehead with Jordan water from a flask
He lay upon the child, mouth to mouth and eyes to eyes, and the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes
He offered a burnt sacrifice at Bethel on behalf of the family
qs.e: Elisha prayed fervently and stretched himself upon the boy until divine life returned to the child.

qs.q: Which major prophet was commanded by God to buy a potter's clay jar and smash it at the Valley of Ben-Hinnom?
qs.e: Jeremiah shattered the earthenware jar as a sign that God would smash Jerusalem for its persistent idolatry.

qs.q: In Isaiah's prophecy, what attributes are ascribed to the Suffering Servant who bears human transgressions?
o: He was a wealthy monarch who bought peace from neighboring states
He was a mighty general who conquered foreign empires by physical sword
He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities, and by his wounds we are healed
He was an angel who visited Jerusalem without taking human form
qs.e: Isaiah depicted the Servant as bearing our griefs and carrying our sorrows through his sacrificial death.

qs.q: What symbolic action did Ezekiel perform by lying on his left side for 390 days and right side for 40 days?
o: Protesting against the corrupt priesthood in the exile camp
Demonstrating physical paralysis caused by Babylonian imprisonment
Bearing the iniquity of the house of Israel for 390 years and Judah for 40 years symbolically
Calculating the precise calendar years until Cyrus' decree
qs.e: Ezekiel acted out the duration of punishment for Israel's and Judah's covenant unfaithfulness.

qs.q: Which minor prophet used his unfaithful wife Gomer as a living object lesson of God's redeeming covenant love?
qs.e: Hosea bought back unfaithful Gomer, illustrating God's unyielding love for faithless Israel.

qs.q: Which minor prophet foretold that the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his Temple, like a refiner's fire?
qs.e: Malachi prophesied the sudden coming of the Lord to purify the sons of Levi like gold and silver.

qs.q: What warning is given in Proverbs regarding hasty anger and uncontrolled temper?
o: Hasty speech guarantees immediate victory in disputes
Anger is a virtue that demonstrates strong leadership ability
Uncontrolled temper has no effect on human relationships
A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, but a man of understanding remains calm
qs.e: Proverbs repeatedly counsels against hasty anger, praising self-control and slow-to-anger wisdom.

qs.q: In the book of Job, how did God challenge Job's perspective when speaking out of the whirlwind?
o: Depart from the land of Uz and live in the desert
List every secret sin you committed during your youth in Uz
Pay a compensation fine to your three friends at the altar
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare if you have understanding!
qs.e: God questioned Job regarding the majesty and mystery of creation, bringing Job to humble trust.

qs.q: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, how does a believer experience transformation of mind?
o: Perform seventy ceremonial washings every Sabbath
Conform outward habits to surrounding secular society for safety
Rely on human philosophy and academic degrees alone
Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind through God's word
qs.e: Paul urged Christians to present their bodies as living sacrifices and be transformed by renewed minds.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Ephesians, how is the relationship between Christ and the church compared to marriage?
o: Church members are forbidden from entering marital relationships
Marriage is a temporary civil contract without spiritual significance
Wives rule over husbands through financial authority
Husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her
qs.e: Paul portrayed Christian marriage as a reflection of Christ's sacrificial love for the church.

qs.q: What took place on the road to Emmaus when Jesus walked with two discouraged disciples after his resurrection?
o: He revealed himself as a military conqueror who would destroy Rome
He rebuked them harshly and vanished into the desert
He commanded them to return to fishing on Lake Galilee
He interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself, and their hearts burned within them
qs.e: Jesus opened the Old Testament Scriptures to them, revealing how the Messiah had to suffer and enter glory.

qs.q: What was the response of Thomas when he saw the resurrected Jesus and touched his wounds?
o: You are a prophet sent from Galilee!
Truly this is a spirit without flesh and bones!
I still do not believe unless I see another sign!
qs.e: Thomas confessed Jesus' full divinity and lordship upon seeing His hands and pierced side.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah respond when Sanballat sent an open letter accusing him of plotting rebellion?
o: He marched his army to attack Samaria
He immediately surrendered the governorship to Sanballat
He paid silver coins to Sanballat to withdraw the letter
He denied the false charges, stating they were invented in Sanballat's own mind, and prayed for strength
qs.e: Nehemiah exposed the false rumors, prayed for God to strengthen his hands, and continued wall construction.

qs.q: Which king of Judah instituting sweeping spiritual reforms after finding the Book of the Law in the Temple?
qs.e: Josiah restored Passover, tore down pagan shrines, and renewed the covenant after Hilkiah found the Law.

qs.q: What was the name of the prophet who confronted King David after he committed adultery with Bathsheba?
qs.e: Nathan used the parable of the rich man and the ewe lamb to convict David, saying 'You are the man!'

qs.q: In the book of Ezekiel, what was represented by the vision of two sticks joined together in the prophet's hand?
o: The division of the Levitical priesthood into two guilds
The destruction of the two golden calves at Bethel and Dan
The military alliance between Babylonia and Egypt
The future reunion of the northern kingdom Israel and southern kingdom Judah into one nation
qs.e: Joining the two sticks symbolized God reuniting Israel and Judah under one Davidic shepherd.

qs.q: Which minor prophet proclaimed that the vision is for an appointed time, though it tarries, wait for it?
qs.e: Habakkuk was told to record the vision clearly, trusting that divine promises will surely come to pass.

qs.q: Which judge made a rash vow before battle against the Ammonites that affected his only daughter?
qs.e: Jephthah's vow led to devoting his daughter upon returning victorious from defeating Ammon.

qs.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who was the second person to pass by the wounded man without helping?
qs.e: The Levite arrived second, looked at the wounded man, and also passed by on the other side.

qs.q: What miracle did Jesus perform at the wedding in Cana of Galilee?
qs.e: Jesus turned six stone jars of water into choice wine at his mother's request, demonstrating his glory.

qs.q: Who was the high priest who raised Samuel in the sanctuary at Shiloh?
qs.e: Eli served as priest and judge at Shiloh, mentoring young Samuel in divine service.

qs.q: Which judge defeated Sisera's Canaanite army with the help of Barak?
qs.e: Deborah guided Barak to assemble troops at Mount Tabor, routing Sisera's army.

qs.q: What instruction did Jesus give regarding fasts in the Sermon on the Mount?
o: Anoint your head and wash your face so your fasting is seen by God in secret
Disfigure your face so everyone knows you are fasting
Blow trumpets in public streets before starting a fast
Fast only on Roman civil holidays
qs.e: Jesus warned against hypocritical public displays, teaching that fasting should be done unto God in secret.

qs.q: Who was the Roman governor who handed Jesus over to be crucified after washing his hands?
qs.e: Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified to satisfy the crowd.

qs.q: What city was Saul heading toward when he was blinded by a light from heaven?
qs.e: Saul was on the road approaching Damascus when the resurrected Christ confronted him.

qs.q: What speech did Stephen make before the Sanhedrin prior to his martyrdom?
o: A historical review of Israel's resistance to God's prophets culminating in the rejection of Jesus
A request for financial mercy from the high priest
A defense of Roman legal authority in Judea
A refusal to preach to Hellenistic widows
qs.e: Stephen reviewed salvation history, calling out the council for resisting the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: Who visited Saul in Damascus, placed hands on him, and restored his sight?
qs.e: Ananias was sent by God to heal Saul's blindness and welcome him into fellowship.

qs.q: What vision did Cornelius receive that led him to send messengers to Joppa?
o: An angel of God appearing and instructing him to send for Simon Peter
A sheet filled with animals descending from heaven
A pillar of cloud hovering above his house
A dream of an angel holding a golden scroll
qs.e: An angel directed Cornelius to call Peter from Joppa to hear the gospel message.

qs.q: What happened to King Herod Agrippa I after he accepted divine praise from the crowd at Caesarea?
o: An angel of the Lord struck him and he was eaten by worms and died
He was deposed by Caesar and exiled to Gaul
He lost his eyesight for ten years
His palace was destroyed by an earthquake
qs.e: Herod failed to give glory to God, so divine judgment struck him down instantly.

qs.q: How were Paul and Silas freed from their chains in the Philippian prison?
o: A great earthquake shook the prison foundations, opening all doors
The jailer received a bribe and unlocked their cells
Roman guards released them by governor decree at midnight
An angel made them invisible to the guards
qs.e: God sent a severe earthquake while they sang, opening prison doors and unfastening chains.

qs.q: How does Paul summarize salvation in Romans chapter ten?
o: Observe every detail of Mosaic ceremonial law perfectly
Confess with your mouth Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him
Prove descent from Abraham's physical bloodline
Pay tithes to the Jerusalem apostles
qs.e: Paul affirmed that vocal confession of Jesus' lordship and heart belief brings salvation.

qs.q: What attribute of love is highlighted in First Corinthians chapter thirteen?
o: Love seeks personal advantage in every situation
Love is patient, kind, does not envy, and never fails
Love demands public praise for every good deed
Love is valid only when accompanied by material gifts
qs.e: Paul defined love as patient, humble, selfless, enduring all things, and exceeding all gifts.

qs.q: Which patriarch offered his son Isaac on Mount Moriah in obedience to God?
qs.e: Abraham displayed deep trust in God when tested with offering his son Isaac.

qs.q: What was Joseph's interpretation of Pharaoh's dreams of cows and ears of grain?
o: Seven years of war followed by seven years of peace
Seven years of prosperity followed by seven years of severe famine
Seven royal sons followed by seven daughters
Seven plagues on Egypt followed by blessing
qs.e: Joseph explained that Egypt would experience seven abundant years followed by seven famine years.

qs.q: What event caused Pharaoh to finally allow the Israelites to depart from Egypt?
o: The turning of the Nile River into blood
The death of all Egyptian firstborn males during Passover night
The plague of dark clouds across the land
The destruction of Egyptian crops by swarms of locusts
qs.e: The fatal midnight plague on Egypt's firstborn compelled Pharaoh to let Israel go.

qs.q: Which judge routed a Midianite army with three hundred men holding trumpets and torches?
qs.e: Gideon's small force routed the Midianites using trumpets, smashed jars, and torches.

qs.q: Why was Saul rejected from being king over Israel?
o: He refused to build a palace in Jerusalem
He disobeyed God's command regarding Amalek by sparing Agag and best livestock
He lost the Ark of the Covenant to Philistines
He taxed the northern tribes excessively
qs.e: Saul's willful disobedience in sparing Amalekite property cost him his royal crown.

qs.q: What was the outcry of the ten northern tribes when Rehoboam threatened harsher treatment?
o: We pledge allegiance to Rehoboam forever
What share do we have in David? To your tents, O Israel!
Let us make Shechem the joint capital
qs.e: The ten tribes rejected Davidic rule, shouting 'To your tents, O Israel!' and crowning Jeroboam.

qs.q: What worship centers did Jeroboam institute to keep northern Israelites from Jerusalem?
o: Baal temples at Samaria and Jezreel
Golden calf shrines at Dan and Bethel
Stone pillars at Gilgal and Jericho
Incense altars at Hebron and Shiloh
qs.e: Jeroboam set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel to preserve his political power.

qs.q: How did God preserve the widow of Zarephath through Elijah during the drought?
o: Ravens brought her food every morning and evening
Her flour jar was not spent and her oil jug did not run dry
Elijah provided gold from the king's treasury
Manna fell inside her house daily
qs.e: God multiplied the widow's flour and oil throughout the three-year famine.

qs.q: What judgment was prophesied by Elijah against Jezebel for the murder of Naboth?
o: She will die peacefully in her sleep at Samaria
Dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel
She will be exiled to Babylon for twenty years
She will drown in the Jordan River
qs.e: Elijah foretold that Jezebel would meet a violent end and be eaten by dogs in Jezreel.

qs.q: What did Isaiah say when he heard the Lord ask, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
o: I am too young to speak
Wait until I consult my family
qs.e: Cleansed by an altar coal, Isaiah responded eagerly to God's divine call.

qs.q: What lesson was illustrated when Jeremiah smashed a potter's jar at Ben-Hinnom?
o: The Babylonian army would collapse within three days
God would break Jerusalem beyond repair for its persistent idolatry
The Temple vessels would be duplicated in silver
The city walls would expand outward
qs.e: Smashed pottery symbolized irreversible destruction coming upon Jerusalem for unrepented sin.

qs.q: Which minor prophet depicted a locust plague as a warning of the Day of the Lord?
qs.e: Joel used the swarming locust invasion to call the nation to urgent repentance.

qs.q: What truth did Habakkuk affirm regarding how the righteous live in difficult times?
o: The righteous shall live by forming foreign alliances
The righteous shall live by accumulating riches
The righteous shall live by his faith
The righteous shall live by hiding in caves
qs.e: Habakkuk declared that the righteous person endures through steadfast faith in God.

qs.q: In Proverbs, how is the path of the righteous contrasted with the way of the wicked?
o: The wicked path is always filled with divine blessing
Both paths lead to identical outcomes in this life
The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn shining brighter, while the wicked stumble in darkness
The righteous path guarantees worldly prestige
qs.e: Proverbs contrasts growing light on the righteous path with dangerous stumble-filled darkness.

qs.q: What was Job's response when his wife advised him to curse God and die?
o: Let us move to Egypt immediately
I will curse God as you say
Shall we accept good from God and not accept trouble?
I will demand money from my friends
qs.e: Job maintained integrity, asking if humanity should accept only good from God and not hardship.

qs.q: How is Christ described in Colossians chapter one?
o: He is a minor regional teacher in Galilee
He is an angel created during the Exodus
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation, and head of the church
He is a king who rules by physical sword
qs.e: Paul exalted Christ as supreme over creation and sovereign head of the church.

qs.q: What encouragement does Paul give in First Thessalonians regarding deceased believers?
o: Physical death permanently ends all spiritual hope
Deceased believers lose all inheritance in the kingdom
At the Lord's coming, the dead in Christ will rise first, then living believers will be caught up together
Only apostles will be resurrected at the last day
qs.e: Paul comforted believers with the assurance of resurrection for all who die in Christ.

qs.q: What did Jesus teach Nicodemus about entering the kingdom of God?
o: Only high priests and Pharisee elders can enter
Entrance requires paying tax to the sanctuary
No one can enter the kingdom of God unless born of water and the Spirit
Entrance depends on physical strength and ancestry
qs.e: Jesus taught that spiritual rebirth through water and the Holy Spirit is required for entry.

qs.q: What action did Jesus take against sellers and money changers in the Temple?
o: He joined them in trading currency for Passover
He collected a portion of their money for charity
He drove them out, overturned their tables, and declared it a house of prayer
He praised them for serving travelers
qs.e: Jesus cleansed the Temple, condemning commercial degradation of God's house.

qs.q: Which Persian king confirmed Cyrus' decree, allowing Temple rebuilding in Jerusalem to finish?
qs.e: King Darius reconfirmed Cyrus' decree, ordering local officers to support Temple completion.

qs.q: What was represented by the boiling pot tilting away from the north in Jeremiah's vision?
o: A peace treaty signed with Syria
Abundant rain coming from northern mountains
Disaster pouring from the north against all who live in the land
The return of lost Israelite tribes from captivity
qs.e: The boiling pot represented coming Babylonian invasion pouring down from the north.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision by the Chebar canal, what four faces were on each living creature?
qs.e: Each creature possessed four faces reflecting divine majesty across creation.

qs.q: Which minor prophet spoke of all nations gathered for divine judgment in the Valley of Jehoshaphat?
qs.e: Joel prophesied divine judgment upon hostile surrounding nations in Jehoshaphat Valley.

qs.q: Which minor prophet wrote a single-chapter vision pronouncing doom on Edom for gloating over Judah?
qs.e: Obadiah focused exclusively on judgment against Edom for taking pleasure in Judah's ruin.

qs.q: What principle does Proverbs teach regarding honest gain versus deceitful wealth?
o: Poverty is proof of criminal behavior in every person
Deceitful wealth grants permanent peace to families
Honest gain is inferior to quick speculative riches
Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice
qs.e: Proverbs stresses that moral integrity with modest income is superior to dishonest wealth.

qs.q: What was Elihu's perspective in Job regarding why God permits human suffering?
o: Hardship is caused by planetary alignment
Hardship is always proof that a person committed secret murder
God has no knowledge or interest in human pain
God uses suffering to instruct, discipline, and rescue humans from pride and death
qs.e: Elihu presented suffering as a redemptive discipline used by God to save souls from ruin.

qs.q: How does Paul describe the Holy Spirit's role in prayer in Romans chapter eight?
o: The Spirit restricts intercession to ordained ministers
The Spirit provides written litanies for daily recitation
The Spirit eliminates the need for human prayer completely
The Spirit intercedes for believers with groanings too deep for words according to God's will
qs.e: Paul taught that the Holy Spirit assists our weakness and intercedes according to God's will.
